properties.description: A summit accessed via a scramble off of the south side of I-90. Cross country navigation experience and navigation required.
properties.title: Duke of Kent

properties.description: Take a short loop from the Coal Mines Trail through the pine forest.
properties.title: Roslyn Urban Forest - Slag Pile Loop

properties.description: Several hiking trails exist in the Lookout Mountain Forest Preserve, part of the Whatcom County Park system, including a 2.2-mile loop with a one mile viewpoint spur trail, a quick waterfall trail, and lower loop trail. Alternatively, head up and up to Lookout Mountain on an eight mile service road.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lookout Mountain Forest Preserve

properties.description: Despite its name, Dead Horse Lake is a beautiful location. Take a short hike in from the trailhead to big skies, rolling hills, and a peaceful lakeshore.
properties.title: Dead Horse Lake

properties.description: Visit several charming lakes just south of Mount Rainier National Park using a pleasant little trail. Granite Lake is a beautiful place for a dip, while Bertha May and Cora Lake offer good fishing.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Bertha May and Granite Lakes

properties.description: This hike is short but stunning with Mount Rainier keeping watch over a wildflower-filled sub-alpine meadow. You'll see iconic views of Mount Rainier, butterflies fluttering between colorful blooms, and if the sky is clear, a view of the Cascades all the way to Mount Baker.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Sunrise Nature

properties.description: Located just minutes off the freeway, Pomona Grange Park provides easy access to Friday Creek with excellent salmon viewing sites in the fall or a place to cool off during the heat of summer. With a wide, flat trail and room for a picnic, the park is an excellent place to stop with family and friends of all ages.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Pomona Grange Park

properties.description: Take a short hike to a pleasant waterfall tucked away on the northeast corner of Larrabee State Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Larrabee State Park - Chuckanut Falls

properties.description: Maple Creek Park is a 73-acre Whatcom County Park sitting just outside the town of Maple Falls. It contains a section of the developing Bay to Baker Trail, as well as a 1.4 mile-long loop trail. Along the loop are several junctions, none of them marked. To keep on the main loop, the hike is best done counterclockwise.
properties.title: Maple Creek Loop Trail

properties.description: One of just three remaining lookouts on the Gifford Pinchot National Forest, Burley Mountain Lookout was built in 1934 and is still active today. This route utilizes nature trails, a forest road, and a short hiking trail to access this unique site just south of Highway 12.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Burley Mountain

properties.description: Whether you need a day hike for the whole family or the perfect trail to round out your first visit to Olympic National Park, Hurricane Hill is the answer. You can even use this trail as the jumpoff (or ending point) to a variety of longer hikes out of the Elwha River Valley.
properties.title: Hurricane Hill

properties.description: Accessible via two separate trailheads, the Domerie Peak trail offers a ridgeline traverse with views of Cle Elum Lake and the surrounding peaks of the Teanaway.
properties.title: Domerie Peak

properties.description: Set beneath two of Washington’s tallest peaks, Colchuck Lake is an alpine gem. It is a larger cousin to the nearby fabled Enchantment Lakes and offers many of the same payoffs – including groves of larches on its far shore – but can be reached with less than half the effort.
properties.title: Colchuck Lake

properties.description: This long day hike is 16+ miles and goes through all manner of terrain. There’s a fair amount of elevation gain as well, but in return you get to see three sites of WTA’s past work, a hidden waterfall, and get a heck of a workout. Visit at the right time and you might also get a heck of a flower show with very few other people.
properties.title: Yacolt Burn / Silver Star Loop

properties.description: The Little Creek Trail is a 0.4-mile section of trail in Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park. Visitors in the fall will find and abundance of mushrooms and fiery fall colors. You can reach the trail by taking the Military Road Trail from the Red Town Trailhead.
properties.title: Little Creek Trail

properties.description: Looking for a great day at the beach with the dog? Double Bluff is the place to be! Time it just right and at low tide you could walk for miles!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Double Bluff

properties.description: Crowell Ridge is visible from many valley roads but hikers rarely tread on it. Rough roads, steep trail, and sheer distance from city centers keeps this ridgeline lonely, but the expansive views to be had from the summit are worth the work.
properties.title: Crowell Ridge

properties.description: Talapus Lake is a popular hiking trail during the summer. In the winter the road to the trailhead may be inaccessible to cars, so you will have to start with a road walk before getting to the actual trail, adding some extra miles to a snowshoe route to the lake.
properties.title: Talapus Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: This neighborhood park is named for the Pacific Tree Frogs that live here and drum up a loud chorus during mating season.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Frog Holler Forest

properties.description: This hike is across the Washington border in Idaho, but provides a lovely outing near the historic town of Wallace.
properties.title: Slate Creek Trail

properties.description: A popular destination for whitewater rafters and kayakers, Kanasket-Palmer State Park is 320 acres of forest surrounding the Green River. Visitors can hike through the trees, go rafting or kayaking on the river, view wildlife, fish for trout, wade in the pools, and camp in tents, RVs, or yurts to take advantage of everything the park has to offer.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Kanaskat-Palmer State Park

properties.description: Take a tour of an active research and conservation campus as you hike past current conservation plots, a native and endangered plant nursery, and enjoy rare remnants of Whidbey Island prairie.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Pacific Rim Institute

properties.description: The trail at Point No Point gives you both a glimpse into the past, as well as a bit of a workout and great views. With 3 acres in the Point No Point County Park and one hiking trail, the Point No Point lighthouse makes a great destination for visitors young and old.
properties.title: Point No Point Park

properties.description: Woodinville has struck gold with this park. Tucked away in the wine country, Gold Creek offers a multitude of hiking experiences on well-maintained trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Gold Creek County Park

properties.description: Just adjacent to the Boeing campus in Everett, Narbeck Wetland Sanctuary is a great place for a short nature walk in town or a leg-stretcher after work. In fact, you may completely forget you're near an busy part of town when you're in the heart of the sanctuary.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Narbeck Wetland Sanctuary

properties.description: A rolling snowshoe route departing from the Marble Mountain Sno-Park near Mount St. Helens.
properties.title: Pine Marten Trail

properties.description: Make a steep ascent through flowerfilled slopes to views of high mountain peaks and pillow lavas that originated on the bottom of the Pacific Ocean.
properties.title: Klahhane Ridge

properties.description: With a trailhead accessible year round, Cow Heaven and views of the Skagit and Sauk River Valleys along with the majestic North Cascades are a promising paradise despite the challenge of a zigzag ascent spent mostly within the shelter of the forest.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cow Heaven

properties.description: This year-round hike offers great views of the Columbia River Gorge along with enchanting stands of oak, cascading waterfalls, dramatic basalt outcroppings, and profuse wildflowers in the spring. Often sunny here while raining in Vancouver, it is a great place to hike while waiting for snow to melt at higher elevations.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Coyote Wall - The Labyrinth Loop

properties.description: This breathtaking loop offers an undulating ridge walk on the Pacific Crest Trail, a jaunt through the West Fork Pasayten River Valley — one of the priority areas in WTA's Lost Trails Found campaign — and views from the highest fire lookout in the state.
properties.title: Seven Pass Loop (Pasayten)

properties.description: This short, flat paved trail takes curious hikers less than 100 yards to the Potters Pond Fishing and Observation Platform. From here, enjoy watching a wide variety of birds and fish play and dive in the skies and water.   Keep an eye out for the resident pair of bald eagles, or raptors flying the thermals above the cliffs near Bayley Lake just south of the pond.
properties.title: Potters Pond Fishing and Observation Platform

properties.description: This nature preserve represents the best of Washington all in one 86-acre parcel on the edge of Whidbey Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Admiralty Inlet Natural Area Preserve

properties.description: Take a loop hike any time of the year on the Rotary Dominion Meadows Trail. It is good for strollers and wheelchairs, and in the winter, it can be used for snowshoeing and cross-country skiing.
properties.title: Rotary Dominion Meadows Trail

properties.description: Cutthroat Pass is a stunner no matter which way you access it. This way, you'll enjoy a wider, more well-maintained trail, and you're more likely to share it with Pacific Crest Trail thru-hikers.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cutthroat Pass via the Pacific Crest Trail

properties.description: The Tillicum Trail offers a tranquil hike through a mature forest with wild strawberries, huckleberries, wildflowers and a babbling stream.
properties.title: Tillicum Trail

properties.description: The route up Tonga Ridge is not clearly marked for winter travel. Visitors to this area should have a route planned, a map, snow travel and avalanche travel skills.
properties.title: Tonga Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: Home to elves, gnomes, and fairies, this trail in Point Roberts is one of the most whimsical in the state.
properties.title: Enchanted Forest Trail

properties.description: A short trail connects the Table Mountain road to Naneum Meadows and adventures beyond.
properties.title: Naneum Meadows

properties.description: The trail to Sunset Park and Golden Lakes is a section of the longer 93-mile Wonderland Trail that can also be hiked as an out-and-back beginning at Mowich Lake.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Sunset Park and Golden Lakes

properties.description: An easy, short loop hike out of the Lone Fir campground. The first bit is paved before giving way to a dirt trail that follows Early Winters Creek. After a creek crossing (log bridge) it loops back to the campground.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Lone Fir Loop

properties.description: Beaver Peak is the unofficial name for the easy-to-reach peak located three miles north of Silverton.
properties.title: Beaver Peak

properties.description: The Mill Pond Historic Site is a fascinating and beautiful location to explore, with accessible trails, historical features, and an evolving landscape healing after removal of a dam.
properties.title: Mill Pond Historic Site Trails

properties.description: A nice trip through a quiet forest that features trees, moss, and ferns on a steep hillside above a babbling creek.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Diobsud Creek

properties.description: The Tarbell trail is a 24.75 mile multi-use loop that connects recreation sites and scenic viewpoints in the Yacolt Burn Recreation area.
properties.title: Yacolt Burn State Forest - Tarbell Trail

properties.description: Accessible by boat or by foot only via a sandy tombolo at low tide, McMicken Island Marine State Park has over a quarter-mile of shoreline to explore — and the hike over (if you choose to take it) is incredibly scenic in its own right.
properties.title: McMicken Island Marine State Park

properties.description: This pleasant loop or out-and-back meanders through shrub-steppe and dry ponderosa communities. Spring is great for flowers; autumn, brilliant with aspen groves; and in winter, a snowshoe is in order. Bring binoculars if you have them, as birding opportunities are good year-round.
properties.title: Lynn’s Trail

properties.description: The Annette Lake Sno-Park offers visitors access to multiple winter outdoor activities, along with a large plowed parking lot, toilet and educational resources.
properties.title: Annette Lake Sno-Park

properties.description: The river level Pinnacles Trail which was an old ranch road follows the John Day River below beautiful and colorful basalt cliffs and pinnacles through sagebrush flats and scenic views of the rolling hills.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Cottonwood Canyon State Park

properties.description: Although it can get crowded on the weekends, there is plenty of room for seclusion on either a day hike or an overnight stay.  Some of the best views and meadows within the Mt. Adams Wilderness.
properties.title: Adams Creek Meadows

properties.description: This is a remote and rugged trail that has not been maintained for decades. From the Upper Suiattle River Trail, this route fords the Suiattle River to eventually arrive at Buck Creek Pass.
properties.title: Upper Suiattle River

properties.description: Walk through Seattle's historically Black neighborhood along this section of the Redlining Heritage Trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redlining Heritage Trail - Central District

properties.description: Tiptop is a summit in Chelan county. During the summer, the summit can be driven to via the forest service road, but the area also makes a great snowshoeing destination in the winter months.
properties.title: Tiptop

properties.description: Nestled in a quiet basin only a stone’s throw from Snoqualmie Pass, pristine Mirror Lake is a destination to be enjoyed by the whole family. Rarely can you find such lovely sites with so little effort, but here, a short trek will take you through forests, across delicate streams and past brightly colored wildflowers. Humming with butterflies, birds, bees and babbling streams, this trail is not to be missed.
properties.title: Mirror and Cottonwood Lakes

properties.description: Short, easy trail to the Stillaguamish River and the site of the railroad town of Robe and great views of the Stilliguamish River as it races by. The trail switchbacks through a forest of alder down to a forest of big leaf maple draped with lush mosses,  liverwort and licorice fern. The forest floor is thick with fern and colorful salmonberry.  Watch the kids!  The Stilliguamish runs swift and deep here, especially during periods of high water flow.  It is not recommended to continue on to the old railroad tunnels due to trail washout, slope slump and rockfall.
properties.title: Old Robe Canyon

properties.description: On the Oregon side of the Columbia River Gorge, Nesmith Point Trail provides hikers with a relatively low-elevation trail that generally melts out in spring, offering a great early season hike for those hoping to get outside.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Nesmith Point

properties.description: Climb through dense old-growth forest to a barren cinder plateau that bursts with wildflowers and unobstructed views.
properties.title: Ape Canyon

properties.description: This easily-accessed trail just off I-90 in north Idaho leads to two alpine lakes.
properties.title: Stevens Lake

properties.description: This loop hike is about the journey through beautiful vegetation including some old forests — with the added bonus of two sweet, small lakes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Twin Lakes and Mount Pickett

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Stevens Peak

properties.description: Ford a river, climb through forest and end at two lakes in the heart of a wilderness area -- Cougar Lake is a gorgeous respite for hikers in the William O. Douglas wilderness.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Cougar Lakes
Durr Road and North Yakima Skyline

properties.description: A beautiful multi-day hike through ponderosa pines to a high altitude basin. Enjoy lakes, waterfalls, larches, and solitude with the possibility of a top out of 9,060 foot Mount Maude.
properties.title: Ice Creek - Ice Lakes

properties.description: Despite not having the flashy title of “Mountain” or “Peak,” Duncan Hill climbs high above the Entiat River, providing panoramic views of Mount Fernow and Mount Maude, along with sights of Glacier Peak and Mount Rainier.
properties.title: Duncan Hill

properties.description: Old Pass Hill is located between Old Blewett Pass and Blewett Pass. The route offers beautiful panoramas of the Teanaway peaks Tronsen Ridge, but even with a decent snow pack, the slide alder that grows on disused logging roads can add difficulty to a trip to the summit.
properties.title: Old Pass Hill

properties.description: Hike through an old burn zone to reach an idyllic meadow high in the Entiat Mountains.
properties.title: Cow Creek Meadows

properties.description: Just outside the little town of Eastsound on Orcas Island is a sweet little beach that offers some nice rambling; the perfect place to walk off a meal, or simply take in low tide and the lovely animals that come with it.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Crescent Beach Preserve

properties.description: This 22.5-mile rail trail follows the abandoned Burlington Northern grade connecting the towns of Sedro Woolley and Concrete, and can be accessed from three trailheads off of the North Cascades Highway.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cascade Trail

properties.description: A Big Valley hike has a lot to offer: a river, shady groves and grassy fields with mountain views.
properties.title: Big Valley

properties.description: Big Gulch includes a system of forested trails in Mukilteo.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Big Gulch

properties.description: Hike down the south side of Squak Mountain, connecting with the May Valley Loop Trail or the Perimeter Loop Trail.
properties.title: Bullitt Gorge

properties.description: A rocky trail under the powerlines.
properties.title: Preston Powerline Trail

properties.description: On a stretch of Washington coast known for its beach-driving, Griffiths-Priday State Park is a welcome respite for walkers. The natural spit features low sand dunes that are protected as a wildlife refuge bordered by Conner Creek on one side and the Copalis River on the other.
properties.title: Griffiths-Priday State Park - Copalis River Spit

properties.description: Climb to really excellent views of Rainier, Adams and Mount St. Helens via an exposed ridgeline before traversing east through hillside wildflowers, and ending at junction with the Loowit Trail in the center of the Plains of Abraham.
properties.title: Windy Ridge and Plains of Abraham

properties.description: A climb in the North Cascades. Climbing gear, routefinding experience and expertise required.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Snowfield Peak

properties.description: In the aftermath of the 2017 Jolly Mountain fire, this forest walk to a wonderful viewpoint has become a study in the effects of fire. Even so, the spring flowers are a beautiful contrast and the vista includes Mount Rainier.
properties.title: Yellow Hill

properties.description: To get panoramic views of the North Cascades without fighting the crowds at Cascade Pass or Hidden Lake Lookout, look no further than Lookout Mountain, an arduous climb that often gets overlooked by hikers heading to North Cascades National Park. From the fire lookout on the summit, enjoy 360-degree views of Mount Baker, Mount Shuksan, and a panoply of other North Cascades giants.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Lookout Mountain Lookout

properties.description: Stunning section of the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT).  Starts high and stays high, going from Hart's Pass to Windy Pass to Holman Pass.
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) - Hart's Pass to Holman Pass

properties.description: This section hike is a great way to get a taste of the Pacific Crest Trail over the course of a week or long weekend.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) - Bridge of the Gods to Road 23

properties.description: An extension of the Lily Lake trail that leads to the Lily Lake Campsite. It's pretty uphill, but worth the view once you get there. You can get to this trail by several means: The Lily Lake/Lizard Lake Trailhead, Larry Reid/Max's Shortcut/Lily Lake route, or from the Oyster Dome trail from the West.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: North Butte

properties.description: Walking along this old railroad bed offers insight into the history, ecology, and biology of the Chehalis River Surge Plain. Surge plains are rare, and the interpretive trail along this route helps highlight the important part they play in a healthy ecosystem.
properties.title: Preacher's Slough to Blue Slough

properties.description: Visit a multi-use trail to a summit that boasts coastal scenery, forests, rocky bluffs, tidepools, and a hearty climb to a 1,166-foot viewpoint over the Strait of Juan de Fuca
properties.title: Striped Peak

properties.description: One of several trails in the network at Riverside State Park.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Trail 210

properties.description: A 20-acre park in the middle of Bellevue.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bellevue Downtown Park

properties.description: Ruston Way runs along the Tacoma Waterfront from Jack Hyde Park to Point Defiance Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ruston Way

properties.description: This garden comprises 22 acres of native forest intermingled with numerous other plant species, most notably rhododendrons.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Rhododendron Species Botanical Garden

properties.description: The climb up the North Fork Trail to the Pacific Crest Trail is steep and often buggy, but vast meadows of wildflowers and alpine heaven are the well-earned reward.
properties.title: Glacier Peak Meadows

properties.description: A delightful wooded neighborhood park for an easy dip into nature.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Juanita Woodlands Park

properties.description: Hike from the Artist Point parking area to the Heather Meadows Visitor Center and back. With 1,100 feet of elevation gain, you'll have a great thigh workout. Combine Wild Goose with many of the other short trails in the area to make a full day of exploration, or use the Wild Goose trail to access Swift Creek or Lake Ann.
properties.title: Wild Goose

properties.description: Low-lying with impressive trees bordering each side of it, this trail is a nice option year-round. The Doug-fir, bigleaf maple, and hemlock forest canopy in this narrow valley shades hikers in the heat of summer, and in winter the elevation means it's unlikely to have heavy snow to navigate. And since much of it's a former railroad grade, the trail is easy enough for hikers of all types.
properties.title: Dry Creek

properties.description: This easily attainable series of lakes provides a good place for kids and adults alike to splash their feet in the sandy bottom and cool water on warm summer days.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Deer and Sand Lake

properties.description: Bayshore Preserve is a 74-acre spread of land on the Bayshore Peninsula which pokes into Oakland Bay. A former golf course, WTA is working on improving the informal trails here so hikers can enjoy an area that is undergoing restoration efforts.
properties.title: Bayshore Preserve

properties.description: Climb through rich, old growth forest to miles of some of the finest ridge walking available in Washington, where alpine meadows and jaw-dropping views abound.
properties.title: West Cady Ridge to Benchmark Mountain

properties.description: Get a great workout and some incredible views on this steep, dry trail in the Teanaway.
properties.title: Iron Peak

properties.description: Lots of access points to this network of trails right in the heart of Mukilteo makes for great hiking for all ages.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Japanese Gulch

properties.description: This trail provides access for kayakers to the Sultan River at the gorge below the dam.
properties.title: Sultan Gorge

properties.description: Hike a green, forested trail for a mile or so along tiny Lyon Creek in Mountlake Terrace. In season, enjoy a variety of wildflowers or, later in the year, some fall colors. Be alert for squirrels and for a variety of birds. As a hike, it's very easy and relaxing. For a more dynamic experience, put on your trail runners and jog the entire way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Terrace Creek Park

properties.description: With a road washout 5 miles from the actual trailhead, this relatively short hike has been extended into a fairly substantial dayhike. But the peak, just outside of Randle, does offer commanding views of the Cowlitz River valley, and a bushwhacking exploration for more adventurous hikers.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Pompey Peak

properties.description: Hike a short but steep trail up to the Pacific Crest Trail and points beyond.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Fog City

properties.description: The trail to Boardman Lake is one of the most accessible hikes along the Mountain Loop Highway, offering old-growth forest and a two-for-one lakeside opportunity. If you are willing to hike a mile or so in with marginal elevation gain, you can find yourself marveling at peaceful azure waters deep in the verdant backcountry of the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.
properties.title: Boardman Lake

properties.description: This short, sweet little loop near the Ohanapecosh Visitors Center make a great visit for a leg stretch or a history hike with little ones. You can't get into the hot springs (and you probably wouldn't want to) but you can still have a nice short hike here.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Ohanapecosh Hot Springs

properties.description: An infrequently-maintained trail in the William O Douglas wilderness.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Indian Creek

properties.description: Julia Butler Hansen was the first woman to serve on the Cathlamet City Council and to head an appropriations subcommittee in the Washington Legislature. This wildlife refuge is an excellent way to honor and experience what Butler Hansen held dear: protecting our nations natural resources.
properties.title: Julia Butler Hansen National Wildlife Refuge for the Columbian White-Tailed Deer

properties.description: Previously known as the Barnes Point Nature Trail, this is a magical flat forest loop hike near the Storm King Ranger Station, Marymere Falls and Lake Crescent through a mix of old growth and second growth forest full of ferns and moss that Olympic National Park is known for.
properties.title: Moments in Time Interpretive Trail

properties.description: The highest summit in the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness, Oval Peak does indeed look ovoid when viewed from some directions. With talus as far as the eye can see, scrambling this peak can be frustrating, but reaching the top rewards climbers with views of the craggy peaks surrounding it, including Star, Courtney, and Gray Peaks.
properties.title: Oval Peak

properties.description: The trail around Wynoochee Lake is a pleasant stroll through second growth forest with a lush understory.  As with many “lakeshore” trails, the trail is not actually near the lakeshore.  While the lake is generally out of sight, it does allow the possibility of a hike/canoe biathlon, if you can find a partner with a canoe.  Wynoochee Lake is smaller and calmer than some of the lakes in Washington, making this a nice option.
properties.title: Wynoochee Lake

properties.description: In 2016, the Friends of Badger Mountain bought 195 acres of land on Candy Mountain overlooking the Tri Cities area. The trail here, built by more than 240 volunteers and officially opened in June of 2017 nicely complements the trail network at Badger Mountain across the road. Between the two preserves, Friends of Badger Mountain has provided some of the best close-in hiking options in the Tri-Cities area.
properties.title: Candy Mountain Trail

properties.description: This extremely short paved and boardwalk trail is a nice, quick stop to make while traveling the Mountain Loop Highway. Interpretive signs along the way explain the history of the area.
properties.title: Gold Basin Mill Pond Interpretive Trail

properties.description: A shorter, less challenging outing near the popular Amabilis Mountain. Be sure to share the trail with skiers.
properties.title: Cabin Creek Snowshoe

properties.description: Lakeview Ranch is a wild and expansive former ranch set among the Channeled Scablands of Eastern Washington. Now a part of the Bureau of Land Management, the recreation area offers a network of old farm roads that are perfect for exploring seasonal lakes, sagebrush flats, and coulees between basalt cliffs and mesas.
properties.title: Lakeview Ranch

properties.description: The furthest northwest tip of the contiguous United State, Cape Flattery provides a dramatic backdrop to a surprisingly accessible hike. It's managed by the Makah Tribe, who provide permits for parking here in Neah Bay. Be sure to pick one up before your hike. It's good for the year, and you can also use it for Shi Shi Beach.
properties.title: Cape Flattery

properties.description: This short loop out of Longmire makes for a great, quick way to get some elevation gain, some forest views, and a fantastic vista of Mount Rainier, all in less than five miles!
properties.title: Rampart Ridge Loop

properties.description: Elip Creek is a wild and challenging hike for those seeking an alternate approach to the Skyline Trail. It also makes a fine 21-mile loop by connecting to the Three Lakes and Big Creek trails, a route that climbs to subalpine meadows where picturesque tarns lie in solitude beneath tree studded ridges.
properties.title: Elip Creek

properties.description: The Salt Creek Recreation Area just outside of Port Angeles has several small trails in and around the camping area for folks to explore, and connects hikers to the nearby Striped Peak trail.
properties.title: Salt Creek Recreation Area

properties.description: For a flat riparian ramble or a great workout to a scenic summit, Snow Mountain Ranch is a walking wonderland just outside of Yakima.
properties.title: Snow Mountain Ranch and Cowiche Mountain

properties.description: These quiet little lakes tucked on the south side of Mount Townsend make a delightful respite from the hordes that are trucking up Townsend. And, like Townsend, there are several ways to access them.
properties.title: Silver Lakes

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Fifes Ridge

properties.description: Stretch your legs on this easy jaunt between two peaceful mountain lakes or use the trail for access to fly fishing locations along the west side of Fish Lake.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Fish Lake

properties.description: Trail closed: The Tahoma Creek Trail is washed out, difficult to navigate and travels through a hazardous area.
properties.title: Tahoma Creek

properties.description: Great day hike through old growth with the final 1000 feet on the west slope rock of Red Mountain. When dry, this roughly 40 degree incline is mostly a walk-up with hands needed here and there. Amazing 360 degree view from the summit.
properties.title: Red Mountain (Commonwealth Basin)

properties.description: Crossing through the stunning Alpine Lakes Wilderness, this section is a must-do for serious Washington backpackers. This 75-mile section leads through some of the most beautiful, remote and varied surroundings along the PCT.
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) Section J - Snoqualmie Pass to Stevens Pass

properties.description: An easy hike along Icicle Gorge.
properties.title: Jack Pine Trail

properties.description: A steep trail climbing to a small lake. What this trail lacks in views and photo ops it makes up for in the excellent workout.
properties.title: Wagonwheel Lake

properties.description: This short, paved interpretive trail provides scenic vistas of surrounding peaks, as well as a look into how fire helped shape the landscape. In the fall, the western larches turn to gold.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sherman Overlook

properties.description: A year-round hike, Trail 131 is the main snowshoe access trail to Bald Knob Campground and connecting trails.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 131

properties.description: Try this trail for riverside Ponderosas and a low-key walk.
properties.title: Peshastin Mill Trail

properties.description: Hike through a stunning canyon in a state park rich in history from the Ice Age Floods.
properties.title: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park - Park Lake Side Canyon

properties.description: This hard-to-follow route in the WIlliam O Douglas wilderness links the Rattlesnake Trail to Mount Aix, but it requires stamina and route-finding to get there.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Hindoo

properties.description: It doesn’t get better than Stuart Island if you want to combine a quaint little hiking trip with sea kayaking, camping and wildlife watching.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Turn Point Lighthouse

properties.description: Accessible from both Packwood Lake and the Clear Fork trailhead, Lost Lake is a medium-sized, scenic little mountain lake ringed with trees and nestled in a small bowl below the former Lost Lake lookout site, a good spot for overnighting or taking a long day hike.
properties.title: Lost Lake

properties.description: St. Andrews Lake is a lovely high country lake along the Wonderland Trail that can be reached via the Westside Road.
properties.title: St. Andrews Park - St. Andrews Lake

properties.description: Start at Edmond's Marina Beach Park and head through the marina and out along the edge of the water to your choice of two beaches.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Edmonds Marine Walkway

properties.description: Tucked in the heart of the Indian Heaven Wilderness. The short and sweet Lemei Lake trail takes you through open meadow to a calm lake ringed with lush evergreens and grasses.
properties.title: Lemei Lake

properties.description: See first-hand the effects of wildland fire and the forest recovery while hiking up to the sparsely forested ridge and views.This trail provides options for loops hikes and off-trail exploration up peaks or up to a mine site.  The old miner's cabin and other wood structures are long gone, but in a few places find the rusted metal remnants of the mining activity.
properties.title: Bernhardt Mine

properties.description: Enjoy watching for birds from an easy-to-reach viewing blind along Tarlatt Slough.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Tarlatt Slough

properties.description: Boulder Lake is a brilliant, azure gem set deep within a stunning cirque of metamorphic cliffs, but to reach it you will need perseverance.
properties.title: Boulder Lake

properties.description: Blyth Park lies along the Sammamish River in the City of Bothell. Hiking trails extend from this more developed area out through the woods and along the river. Some trails are more developed while others are impromptu social trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Blyth Park

properties.description: This trail is located in the Umatilla National Forest in Oregon, but is close enough for a day hike from Washington. The route is a thru-hike in the Blue Mountains.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Umatilla Rim Trail

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Mowich River

properties.description: Extend your hike on Squak Mountain by connecting the May Valley Trail with the Chybinski Trail via the Perimeter Loop Trail.
properties.title: Perimeter Loop Trail

properties.description: With commanding views of the Puget Sound and Olympic Mountains, this 347-acre park also has opportunities for bird watching, clamming and crabbing, and offers 3.5 miles of hiking trails in old-growth forest and along a stretch of unspoiled saltwater shoreline.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: South Whidbey State Park

properties.description: After a long day at the office, the Bay to Baker Trail offers a convenient dose of nature right in the heart of Bellingham.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Bay to Baker Trail

properties.description: Tinkham Discovery Trail is a 0.5-mile family-friendly nature path — wheelchair- and stroller-accessible — that starts in Tinkham Campground. Note that only registered campers can access this hike; there is no day-use parking at the trailhead.
properties.title: Tinkham Discovery

properties.description: Venture beyond the Nordic trails to enter this hiker-only Natural Area Preserve, home to numerous wildlife species and old growth trees with outstanding views of the Spokane Valley and neighboring Idaho.
properties.title: Ragged Ridge

properties.description: Hike to an old fire lookout with in-your-face views of Mount Rainier and a sapphire blue lake below. Tolmie Peak and Eunice Lake pack a one-two punch when it comes to scenery, but stopping at the picturesque lake is a perfectly acceptable destination as well.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Tolmie Peak Lookout - Eunice Lake

properties.description: Just north of Lake Boren, this trail connects Coal Creek Parkway to the Crosstown Trail just across from 129th Ave. SE. Over its short course, this trail passes through the green spaces between the residential areas of the town of Newcastle.
properties.title: China Creek - Newcastle

properties.description: This nature preserve has a network of trails that wind through the trees and out to bluffs above Puget Sound.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: West Port Madison Nature Preserve

properties.description: This route is a groomed snowmobile trail in the winter that connects directly to the previously-private property of Bear Creek Lodge. The lodge area was purchased by Washington State Parks in 2023.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 170

properties.description: This short interpretive takes you through a homestead from the 1800s. Relics from the past along the way include an old barn, the home that the Kestner and Higley families occupied, and various outbuildings and equipment they used.
properties.title: Kestner Homestead - Maple Glade

properties.description: This group of small lakes in the Alpine Wilderness sits along the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) between Mac Peak and Surprise Mountain. It's a great rest stop for a multi-day backpacking trip along the PCT, a campsite for an overnight trip, or even a destination for a long day hike.
properties.title: Deception Lakes

properties.description: Enjoy a short hike to one of the best beaches in Kitsap County.
properties.title: Anderson Point

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: McAlester Trail

properties.description: Part of a series of lowland loop trails from the Tradition Plateau trailhead area of Tiger Mountain.
properties.title: Adventure Trail

properties.description: This is a fantastic trip -- amble along a river before making a steep climb to breathtaking ridge walks and astounding views of the craggy Cascades.
properties.title: Mount David

properties.description: This primitive trail forms a partial loop, connecting the High Divide trail just above Heart Lake with Appleton Pass.
properties.title: Cat Basin Primitive

properties.description: Take a wide forest road with beautiful views up to a short trail through a burn area to meet up with the Sasse Mountain trail. (Or, drive your high-clearance vehicle to the trail directly for a short 3-mile roundtrip hike.)
properties.title: Little Salmon La Sac

properties.description: Hikers who venture to the summit of Kamiak Butte are rewarded with a rolling patchwork of green and yellow fields in every direction, and bright blue skies overhead.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Kamiak Butte

properties.description: From the top, you’ll marvel at vistas of icy peaks including Mounts Baker, Shuksan and Sefrit. Big alpine meadows with plenty of huckleberries in the fall!
properties.title: Goat Mountain

properties.description: The Constance Pass Trail climbs from the Dosewallips River, over the pass and on to the border between Olympic National Park and the Buckhorn Wilderness in Olympic National Forest, where it continues on with a new name, the Home Lake Trail.
properties.title: Constance Pass

properties.description: Ascend from a creek gorge on the east side of Squak Mountain to the Thrush Gap, the saddle between Squak’s central and southeast peaks. Immerse yourself in relatively preserved mountain rainforest, finding solitude alongside abundances of old growth, wildflowers, mushrooms, and fauna, enjoying occasional glimpses of the surrounding mountains and lowlands.
properties.title: Phils Trail - Thrush Gap Loop

properties.description: The 3.5 mile Steam Donkey Loop Trail is an especially good choice in spring, with lots of creeklets, views of the Dosewallips River and silent forest. There is a strong chance that you will see wildlife in winter and spring. An elk herd resides in the area, and with the estuary so close, the area is rife with bird-life. As an added bonus for fall hikers, you can search for and pick chanterelle mushrooms.
properties.title: Dosewallips State Park - Steam Donkey Trail

properties.description: This short hike offers access to a stunning Goat Rocks summit, but you'll work for it. With more than 1000 feet of elevation gain in the last 0.9 mile push to the top, you'll be gasping for breath...and that's before the view renders you speechless.
properties.title: Bear Creek Mountain

properties.description: This sweet little trail on the Kitsap Peninsula makes a wonderful winter hike when the high country is snowed in.
properties.title: Big Tree Trail

properties.description: Hike a short section of the Pacific Crest Trail in southwest Washington. It takes hikers through an experimental forest all the way up to a high point at Big Huckleberry Mountain (though the views aren't much from the top, you'll enjoy some peek-a-boos from the forest on the way up.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Panther Creek Experimental Forest

properties.description: There are two ways to attain Fourth of July Pass - from Thunder Creek or from Panther Creek. Both offer wonderful opportunities to travel along burbling, blue-green creeks, but access via Thunder Creek is truly stunning. Make it an out-and-back or stash a second car for a traverse.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Fourth of July Pass via Thunder Creek

properties.description: A class 3 or 4 scramble to the summit of a peak near Alpental. Climbing gear and expertise recommended.
properties.title: Guye Peak

properties.description: Evans Creek Preserve features a WTA-built trail system in an ecologically diverse enclave. Wetlands, meadows, and hillside forest can be found in this 179-acre farmstead-turned-suburban nature preserve that will thrill both the hiker and the birdwatcher. Not only that, this gem has ADA-accessible trails and is reachable by public transportation.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Evans Creek Preserve

properties.description: Whether you’re an expert or a first-timer, Hurricane Ridge in Olympic National Park is one of the most spectacular places to snowshoe in Washington state—and on clear days you’ll be treated to bird’s-eye views of Mount Olympus in all her winter splendor.
properties.title: Hurricane Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: Thanks to an extensive planning process in this popular area, this formerly user-created trail has been re-routed and improved to make it enjoyable for hikers and mountain bikers, and sustainable for the land it is on.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Coyote Wall

properties.description: Take this remote, flower-filled trail up the north side of Mount Adams to the rocky alpine terrain of giant glaciers.
properties.title: Killen Creek to High Camp

properties.description: This small park just outside of downtown Kingston is indeed a quiet place. The trails here delve into the forest and loop around the edge of the park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: A Quiet Place Park

properties.description: Tucked away atop Chuckanut Mountain is shallow Lost Lake. The south trail to the lake leads through a recovering forest of bigleaf maple, alder, Douglas fir, and western hemlock, meandering 4.5 miles to a riparian hideout, providing waterfalls, old growth, fall color, and year-round hiking to those who make the journey.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Larrabee State Park - South Lost Lake Trail

properties.description: Providing access to the gorgeous views along the High Divide, Welcome Pass is a nice option for those looking for a workout. Count the 66 switchbacks from the trailhead to the pass at 5,200 feet.
properties.title: Welcome Pass

properties.description: While mostly used by mountain bikers, the over-20-mile trail system is open to hikers and equestrians as well.
properties.title: Number Two Canyon Trails

properties.description: This arboretum is located in northern Everett and is free and open to the public. From the arboretum entrance visitors will connect to a series of looping and intersecting paths that go past the different themed areas: a fern garden, a maple grove, a rock garden, and many others.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Evergreen Arboretum and Gardens

properties.description: Great trail which has many views, and rarely is crowded. May encounter dirtbikers on trail.
properties.title: North Ridge

properties.description: Hike a small piece of the new San Juan Islands National Monument! This section of BLM land is one of 75 sections throughout the islands (most are on uninhabited islands) and the site of the Cattle Point Lighthouse. This lighthouse was erected in 1935, but a navigational lantern has stood here since 1888.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Cattle Point Lighthouse

properties.description: You don't have to drive far to hike in the forest — start in Fairhaven Park and explore the several miles worth of trail in the Hundred Acre Wood.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Fairhaven Park and Hundred Acre Wood

properties.description: Add a little more to a loop around Hugo Peak by tacking on Windy Ridge on this dog-friendly hike in the foothills of Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Pack Forest - Hugo Peak Loop and Windy Ridge

properties.description: The eastern part of the Grand Ridge trail can be accessed from Deer Park as a day hike and has a charm all of its own -- forest with avalanche lilies in spring, wildflower meadows and great views of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Mount Baker, Glacier Peak, the Cascades, and the Olympic mountains.
properties.title: Deer Park to Maiden Peak

properties.description: The Halliday trail is certainly no holiday, but tackling this steep, infrequently maintained trail means you will get quite the workout, and have the opportunity to experience the varying terrain and environments of the Colville National Forest.
properties.title: Halliday

properties.description: A 1.5 mile connector trail winding up the East Ridge of Squak Mountain. Accesses the Summit Trail and the East Side Trail.
properties.title: East Ridge Trail

properties.description: With amenities aplenty, Squaxin Park (formerly Priest Point Park) serves a wide community of users. Take a picnic and explore its many nature trails, let your kids play on the playground, or simply relax and enjoy the surroundings.
properties.title: Squaxin Park (Priest Point)

properties.description: The Glacier Peak climbing route combines long distances of non-technical trails on the lower mountain with technical terrain on the upper mountain.
properties.title: Glacier Peak

properties.description: Take a short hike to a cattail fringed lake and beyond through a blackened forest to grand views of the Sawtooth Range.  It's a four-season hike boasting beauty in all seasons, pristine snow, spring and summer flowers, and some fall colors.
properties.title: Sawtooth View via Aspen Lake

properties.description: Home to a small trail system and made accessible thanks to Taylor Shellfish and Green Diamond, in partnership with a local nonprofit and Department of Natural Resources, Kennedy Creek is a nice walk where, in fall, you can experience spawning salmon up close.
properties.title: Kennedy Creek Natural Area Preserve

properties.description: Climb on an old sheep driveway. It's a steep trek past a junction with the County Line Trail to meadows, where the faint, sometimes invisible trail can be followed up to a 6200-foot pass.
properties.title: Scatter Creek

properties.description: This family-friendly classic hike has perhaps the most photo ops per mile than any other hike in the Gorge. You can check out a natural rock arch, see a variety of terrain, take in sweeping views of the Columbia River, and enjoy early-spring wildflower displays.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Catherine Creek - Natural Arch

properties.description: Explore the iconic Wonderland Trail along the southwestern slopes of Mount Rainier. Enjoy stunning views of the mountain as well as the surrounding peaks, ridges and creeks.
properties.title: Longmire to South Puyallup River

properties.description: This is one of the best places to go if you're looking for wildlife and a little leg-stretchers. McLane Creek's boardwalk provides an intimate glimpse into nature, whether it's swimming families of news, spawning salmon, or laughing ducks. As always, please refrain from feeding the wildlife.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - McLane Creek

properties.description: Found on the shores of Puget Sound is the marine and camping Penrose Point State Park. The park consists of 237 acres and nearly two miles of shoreline, including Mayo Cove and Carr Inlet.
properties.title: Penrose Point State Park

properties.description: This local park features two trails that take visitors out-and-back through the forest.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Harper Hill Park

properties.description: The Palouse to Cascades Trail in Iron Horse State Park provides access to notable North Bend hikes, views of mountains and waterfalls, and a journey back into Washington’s history. Take in the wildlife and cross soaring bridges as you make a level traverse from Rattlesnake Lake to Change and Hall Creeks 5.5 miles to the east.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Rattlesnake Lake

properties.description: Moritani Preserve is a relatively new park located on a historic 8.5-acre former strawberry farm.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Moritani Preserve

properties.description: This trail is unmaintained and has no trailhead of its own, but rather is reached by using the Ingalls Creek Trail and the rarely used or maintained Etienne Creek Trail.
properties.title: Falls Creek

properties.description: A trail that climbs out of the Stehekin River valley and into the Glacier Peak wilderness.
properties.title: Company Creek

properties.description: Although this trail is short, take time to savor the broad views across the Mount St. Helens volcanic blast zone while interpretive signs help you contemplate the forces that created it.
properties.title: Winds of Change

properties.description: The North Creek trail offers a quiet urban oasis that links the cities of Mill Creek, Bothell, and Everett. It's a wide, shaded path that leads from McCollum Park in Everett to the city center.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: North Creek Trail

properties.description: Get ready for a butt-kicker! You’ll be climbing over 1,200 feet in a mile, but it’s a great entry point to a larger trail network that can take you to Garland Peak, Rock Creek, Basalt Peak and more.
properties.title: Basalt Pass

properties.description: Ollalie Creek Camp offers a walk through old growth woodland, colorful blooms and berries to an isolated creekside campsite perfect for solitude or connecting to the stunning Cowlitz Divide and iconic Indian Bar.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Ollalie Creek Camp

properties.description: Just 3 miles west of Blewett Pass, Cairn Hill is one of two popular summits in the area. Despite its relatively low elevation in comparison to the surrounding peaks of Diamond Head and the Teanaway, Cairn Hill affords hikers who venture up it beautiful panoramas of the surrounding peaks.
properties.title: Cairn Hill

properties.description: The short section of the Wonderland between Longmire and the Cougar Rock Campground makes for a lovely snowshoe in the wintertime.
properties.title: Longmire to Cougar Rock Campground

properties.description: The Sterling Munro Boardwalk is an accessible trail in North Cascades National Park.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Sterling Munro

properties.description: Horsethief Butte, one part of the expansive Columbia Hills State Historical Park, is composed of hexagonal columns of Wanapum basalt flows that were scoured by the Ice Age floods some 10,000 years ago. Rock climbers are attracted to the sheer cliff faces but hikers and scramblers will find a marked route to the summit.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Columbia Hills State Park - Horsethief Butte

properties.description: A valley walk along Foggy Dew Creek with two large waterfalls, followed by a steep climb into beautiful Merchant's Basin, culminating in expansive views of the Sawtooth and Entiat ranges from the top of Angel's Staircase.
properties.title: Foggy Dew Creek

properties.description: This is a loop hike created in April 2013 to provide for a new hiking experience while preserving some areas of the natural area for wildlife.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Natural Area - Nimbus Knob Loop

properties.description: This natural area is a green oasis within the boundaries of Spokane Valley, and the Deep Ravine loop is a showcase of the valley's geology.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Natural Area - Deep Ravine Loop Trail

properties.description: A well-graded trail leading from Deer Park to the Three Forks campground.
properties.title: Three Forks

properties.description: The White River gets its name from the glacial flour pouring down from the heights of the Dakobed Range via Foam, Lightning, and Thunder Creeks. The milky blue-white color is a result of suspended rock particles that have been ground down from the peaks over millennia.
properties.title: White River

properties.description: Heading to Surprise Lake in the winter can be rewarding, but be sure you know your avalanche warning signs before heading up.
properties.title: Surprise Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: Lose yourself in the land around Billy Clapp Lake. Walk lakeside, or head into the grasslands around it, and look for wildlife.
properties.title: Billy Clapp Lake

properties.description: Hike a gently-graded trail for miles up the Eagle Creek valley. It's a beautiful walk, though quite exposed in some places; those with small children or a fear of heights may want to skip this one.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Eagle Creek

properties.description: Hike up to the summit of Mount Howard, or take the gondola to the top.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Mount Howard (Oregon)

properties.description: Hike through a tunnel of rhododendron blooms and second-growth forest to views of the Olympic Peninsula interior and a carpet of wildflowers. Hike this route in the early summer and you may be lucky enough to see Deer Park with no cars, since the road to Deer Park often doesn't open until late in the season.
properties.title: Deer Ridge

properties.description: Detour off the Lingering Trail and amble through forest to junctions with the Preston Trail or the Bootleg Trail.
properties.title: Dwight's Way

properties.description: High Hut is the highlight of the Mount Tahoma Trail System. From the warmth of a cozy alpine hut, enjoy some of the best views in the southern Cascades.
properties.title: High Hut

properties.description: This park outside the city of Bellingham has 65 miles of trails and is popular with hikers and mountain bikers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Galbraith Mountain

properties.description: A deep-forest experience without the drive. Whipple Creek Park is a 300-acre green oasis in the midst of farmlands to the west of the Clark County Fairgrounds.
properties.title: Whipple Creek Park

properties.description: This is one of the most popular hikes along the US 2 corridor, and it's easy to understand why: a historic and active fire lookout, an enclave for mountain goats, miles of flower-blooming meadows, jaw-slacking views of Lake Wenatchee, Glacier Peak, and hundreds of other peaks. It's amazing there aren't more hikers sunning themselves on this Nason Ridge summit. And being on one of the area's first high peaks to shed its winter snows, Alpine Lookout makes for an excellent early summer adventure.
properties.title: Alpine Lookout

properties.description: The Chilliwack River Trail is an important part of the Copper Ridge Loop and is also part of the traverse between Hannegan Pass and Ross Lake via a connection with the Little Beaver Trail.
properties.title: Chilliwack River

properties.description: There is no doubt that Chelan Summit Trail is a long and challenging hike but once you reach the summit it will have been worth every step.  You will get to experience flower filled meadows, rugged peaks, high alpine lakes, golden larches, and the North Cascades at your door step.
properties.title: Chelan Summit

properties.description: Cross Noisy Creek on this difficult trail through Colville National Forest.
properties.title: Noisy Creek

properties.description: This wildlife refuge near Port Angeles is co-managed by the Jamestown S'kallam Tribe and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
properties.title: Dungeness National Wildlife Refuge - Dungeness Spit

properties.description: Despite its name, Swamp Lake is a lovely little destination in the William O. Douglas wilderness near Mount Rainier. It's popular with fishermen and backpackers, though it can be extremely buggy in early summer.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Swamp Lake

properties.description: While Evans Lake may be less well-known than many of the other lakes nestled within the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, it nevertheless offers a pleasant backcountry experience.
properties.title: Evans Lake

properties.description: When looking for solitude or a quiet, cool creek to ramble along, look no further than Canyon Creek. This trail’s gentle tread and easy grade were cut long ago for horse-pack trains. Along this old supply route to the mines there are numerous babbling brooks, and other natural wonders to keep you entertained. Once this river trail could be followed all the way to Chancellor and then into the Pasayten Wilderness or towards Harts Pass. Alas, wash outs now close the trail five miles in at Mill Creek.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Canyon Creek

properties.description: A beautiful waterfall flows out of Lake Serene and cascades below the rugged east wall of Mount Index at the end of a trail on the west side of Bridal Veil Creek. Take time to see and enjoy a stunning view of Bridal Veil Falls and climb flights of steps paralleling the falls.
properties.title: Bridal Veil Falls

properties.description: A more than 30 mile hike on the west side of Lake Chelan, from Holden Village to High Bridge at the north end of Stehekin.
properties.title: Holden Village to High Bridge

properties.description: Easy trails wander through 410 acres of ponderosa pine forest jutting out into a bend of the "Long Lake" section of the Spokane River. Established as key wildlife habitat along the river, it's a nice little spot right outside Spokane for bird-watching. Keep your eyes peeled for nesting osprey.
properties.title: McLellan Conservation Area

properties.description: Connect between the Mount Rainier area and Snoqualmie Pass along the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT). Travel over rolling hills through forests and clear cut areas with views of Mt. Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) - Chinook Pass to Snoqualmie Pass

properties.description: Enjoy a paved, forested trail through the Maple Valley region, even if you're living carless. This area is serviced by bus routes (143, 168, 912).  The trail has off shoots to Lake Wilderness, The Lake Wilderness Arboretum, and the Maple Valley Community Center, as well as others.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Green to Cedar River Trail

properties.description: Named for its proximity to Hauser Lake, this hike doesn't actually offer any lake access or views. Instead, it's a good place to stretch one's legs and perhaps see some wildlife.
properties.title: Hauser Lake Conservation Area

properties.description: A barrier-free trail that uses part of the Mount Si trail to give just about anyone a taste of the Mount Si Natural Resource Conservation Area. It can be used to add variety to your Mount Si hike, or as an easy leg stretch after a picnic in the recreation area. This trail manages to feature a variety of wildflowers, ferns, moss-laden trees, and two bridges in its short duration.
properties.title: Creekside Loop

properties.description: Trail 140 represents the only “bottom to top” trail experience for Mount Spokane’s summit, but is frequently enjoyed in smaller sections to create loops of various distances. Upper Trail 140 in its entirety is only accessible for part of the year since its upper reaches cross into the alpine ski concession, but this is the only summer multi-use trail that leads to the top of the park’s namesake peak.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Upper Trail 140

properties.description: The northeast segment of the Timberline Trail provides the highest point on the trail and exposed moon-like landscapes; the most rugged of the sections of the circumnavigation.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Timberline Trail - Elk Cove To Gnarl Ridge Junction

properties.description: The Ravensdale Retreat Natural Area is a 145-acre park in historic Ravensdale, south of the Issaquah Alps. The natural area borders Rock Creek to the south, below Ravensdale Ridge. It's primarily intended for foot traffic, but you may see an occasional equestrian rider. Mountain bikes are discouraged but not disallowed; the nearby Black Diamond Natural Area has trails that are specifically designed with proper tread and pitch on turns for bikes. While there are several trails across the natural area, this entry describes a lollipop loop to catch the highlights.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ravensdale Retreat Natural Area

properties.description: Visitors to the North Fork Loop Trail will see several different forests and enjoy views of the lush Cispus Valley. The trail is adjacent to the North Fork of the Cispus River, and departs from the North Fork campground, making it a great option for people staying there.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: North Fork Loop

properties.description: The Icicle Gorge Trail, one of the most popular trails in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, is a wonderful way to explore the natural beauty of the Icicle Creek Valley. The interpretive loop trail has a gentle grade and scenic views of Icicle Creek, Icicle Gorge, and the surrounding forest that are ideal for families, trail runners, beginner hikers, bird enthusiasts, and those looking to take a nice long walk on a well-defined path.
properties.title: Icicle Gorge Nature Loop

properties.description: The Blue Lakes High Route ascends a steep, cairn-dotted trail to a high pass with a beautiful view across to Johnson Mountain and down to a sometimes frozen Blue Lake in a rocky basin below.
properties.title: Blue Lake High

properties.description: Hike a trail that WTA is helping restore. The Ridley Creek trail provides access to scenic Mazama Park and views of Mount Baker.
properties.title: Mazama Park via Ridley Creek

properties.description: The Lower Big Quilcene Trail begins just outside the Buckhorn Wilderness and follows the lower Big Quilcene River along a mostly non-technical tread for approximately 6.5 miles. The moss-lined route starts on an old road bed through younger forest and then winds past large old-growth cedars. In spring and summer, blooming rhododendrons add vibrant color to your journey. This trail is also a great choice during the fall and winter months because the trees provide shelter from precipitation.
properties.title: Lower Big Quilcene River

properties.description: A connector trail that goes from the west side of the 25-mile Tarbell Trail Loop to the east side and one of the latest of the Department of National Resources (DNR) trail projects in the historic Yacolt Burn State Forest of southwest Washington.
properties.title: Yacolt Burn State Forest - Appaloosa Trail

properties.description: The Shedroof Cutoff Trail serves as a short feeder trail to the Shedroof Divide Trail in the Salmo Priest Wilderness.
properties.title: Shedroof Cutoff

properties.description: Just a short jaunt from the cabin at Indian Henry's Hunting Grounds is Mirror Lakes, a beautiful little tarn that — in the right weather — reflects Rainier's west-facing slopes beautifully.
properties.title: Mirror Lakes

properties.description: Gem Lake is nestled at the foot of Wright Mountain and is about two miles beyond the trail junction at Rock Creek trail #1013.1 that intersects with the Snow Lake trail starting at Alpental.  Beautiful colors surround the lake in autumn as do the many climbable peaks in the area.
properties.title: Gem Lake

properties.description: Frontier park is a 71-acre park situated between Puyallup and Graham.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Frontier Park Trail

properties.description: Hike the Hoh River to the Blue Glacier through lush rainforest. The biodiversity on this hike is seldom seen on such an accessible backpacking trip. Just be sure to check in with the ranger station before overnighting — while there are lots of campsites, it's a popular place, and you'll need to reserve in advance.
properties.title: Hoh River Trail to Blue Glacier

properties.description: A short and steep hike, somewhat challenging hike to a quiet mountain lake.
properties.title: Glacier Lake

properties.description: Providing miles of interconnected and gently graded trail, the Quinault National Recreation Trail System provides you with options to extend or shorten your trip into the Quinault Rainforest. The description provided follows Trail the Quinault Loop Trail 854, though it intersects with a few others at various points.
properties.title: Quinault National Recreation Trails

properties.description: This short connector trail is an alternative to the Tiger Mountain Trail for a short bit near the Tiger Mountain Trailhead on Issaquah-Hobart Road SE.
properties.title: Horse Bypass

properties.description: A gentle trail that hugs a river in a colorful valley recovering from a 2017 forest fire. Multiple river crossings, including at the trailhead, are the main challenges on this hike.
properties.title: Middle Fork Teanaway River

properties.description: The first section of the Toutle Trail begins at the Kalama Horse Camp, where ample parking and camping are available. The trail crosses a gully and follows alongside the Kalama River.
properties.title: Toutle Trail - Kalama Horse Camp to Red Rock Pass

properties.description: One of many trails in this area that create tons of fun loop options, the French Creek Trail is 14.4 miles long, and gains 3200 feet of elevation along its length. Due to diminishing funding, the trail is very brushy in sections, making it difficult to navigate. Hiking it end-to-end makes for a fun traverse through the heart of the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, and over county lines!
properties.title: French Creek

properties.description: The Tibbett's Marsh Trail runs through the northern reaches of Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Tibbett's Marsh

properties.description: Visitors to this small lake outside of Poulsbo will be able to walk through the forest and along the shore.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Island Lake Park

properties.description: The Skyline Trail is the main route for hiking out of Paradise, Mount Rainier’s south side hub and most popular destination, providing visitors a unique opportunity to experience the breathtaking beauty of Washington’s grandest mountain.
properties.title: Skyline Trail Loop

properties.description: One of many nice day hike options on Camano Island, Elger Bay Preserve has several interpretative trails featuring beautiful views across Elger Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Elger Bay Preserve

properties.description: Southeast of the Seattle Metro area, in scenic Maple Valley are the Big Bend and Landsburg Reach Natural Areas. These two greenspaces are located along the Cedar River. People walking, biking, or riding their horses along the Cedar River Trail pass through these two areas which are near the end of the long Cedar River Trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Big Bend/Landsburg Reach Natural Area

properties.description: Head to the site of a former fire lookout for expansive sunset views, then wait for darkness to enjoy a star-spangled night sky before heading back to camp.
properties.title: Nannie Peak Loop

properties.description: Just east of Vancouver, off the Evergreen Highway is a delightful little education center that houses a fish hatchery (complete with feeding pond), a small greenspace, and three little trails that are friendly to even the littlest hikers.
properties.title: Columbia Springs

properties.description: This is a road hike on Forest Service Road 5400 from the gate to the old lookout site on top of Slate Peak.
properties.title: Slate Peak

properties.description: Featuring loop trails ranging from a few hundred feet to 2.25 miles, Meadowbrook Farm makes a wonderful spot to stop in the Snoqualmie Valley. Bring your kids, or just yourself and come explore this sweet little parcel of land off Highway 202.
properties.title: Meadowbrook Farm

properties.description: This watershed hike offers water crossings, swaying bridges, beautiful views close to Bothell, and birds galore!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: North Creek Park Boardwalk

properties.description: This 1.3-mile trail is a lovely, somewhat flat walk through the Olympic rainforest to where it intersects Willaby Creek itself.
properties.title: Willaby Creek

properties.description: Popular in the winter as a beginner snowshoeing route, Kendall Peak Lakes is less-frequently visited in the summertime. But if you're OK with hiking a Forest Service road, then navigating a somewhat faint route to your destination, you can enjoy a short and sweet hike with good views of Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Kendall Peak Lakes

properties.description: Yudwasta Big Rock Park (previously Hoag Memorial) is a small park located just east of Mount Vernon.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Yudwasta Big Rock Park (Hoag Memorial)

properties.description: This hike is sometimes called Last Promontory; Absolute Last Promontory and starts out as a road walk on the CCC road; then climbs another road to a viewpoint east of the Green Mountain summit.  From here, the route is a very rough trail or scramble route directly up the ridge line to the summit.
properties.title: Green Mountain (I-90)

properties.description: Prefer to learn something while you walk? Check out the Willapa Art Trail, then hike up and down the hillside along Cutthroat Creek.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Cutthroat Climb

properties.description: Gold Run Pass is a great picture spot and awesome lunch rest area. Also, about a quarter mile from the pass there is a new trail over to Yellow Aster Butte.
properties.title: Tomyhoi Lake

properties.description: Just a few miles from the heart of downtown Vancouver is a quaint rural getaway, where the Frenchman’s Bar Trail connects Vancouver Lake Park to Frenchman’s Bar Regional Park. The wide, paved path provides the perfect urban getaway for hikers and dog walkers alike—it’s also a favorite among birders. On clear days, you’ll be treated to views of Mount Hood, Mount Adams and Mount St. Helens.
properties.title: Frenchman's Bar

properties.description: One of several rugged trails in the Dark Divide
properties.title: Langille Ridge Trail

properties.description: Sun drenched ridgelines, blooming trillium, and sparkling alpine waters define this fitting tribute to one of Washington’s greatest trail advocates.
properties.title: Ira Spring Trail - Mason Lake

properties.description: Enjoy a long ramble through the Port Gamble Forest full of second-growth Douglas firs and lots of ferns.
properties.title: Port Gamble Forest - Forbidden Forest Trail Loop

properties.description: Tucked into the Maple Ridge Neighborhood east of Maple Valley, this trail network is popular with mountain bikers but also offers hiking opportunities.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Henry's Ridge Open Space

properties.description: Hike to a former fire lookout site on the Olympic Peninsula. Fires are now patrolled by aircraft here, but the beautiful, rugged surroundings can still be reviewed by hikers from the lookout with a name that draws on a Chinook phrase that translates to "take care".
properties.title: Kloshe Nanitch

properties.description: With gentle terrain, easy river access and views of snow-laden peaks, this narrow river valley is an inviting snowshoe destination, especially for beginners.
properties.title: Salmon Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: This is a walk up an old mining and logging road that follows beautiful Trout Creek up to the old Sundown Mine.
properties.title: Trout Creek

properties.description: Enjoy easy walking, wide-open views and plenty of sunshine along the Columbia River shore near Priest Rapids Dam.
properties.title: Priest Rapids Shoreline Trail

properties.description: The High Divide Trail is popular because of its long ridge ramble through alpine meadows and its sweeping views of the North Cascades.
properties.title: High Divide Trail

properties.description: East Creek has long been unmaintained, but with the construction of a bridge over East Creek in summer of 2025, the Forest Service has resumed maintenance. It may take time for the trail to be returned to a totally hikable state, but at one time, the trail, at its full length, connected to the Pacific Crest Trail.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: East Creek

properties.description: Use the Pacific Crest Trail as an alternate approach to the Indian Racetrack via the Shortcut Trail.
