properties.title: Race Track Shortcut

properties.description: The Mercer Slough Nature Park is a 320-acre wetland populated with ferns, shrubs, flowers, several varieties of berries, distinctive wooden boardwalks and shaded pathways. Hike among the lush vegetation and wildlife, visit the Mercer Slough Environmental Education Center, tour the historic Winters House, pick blueberries at the seasonal Blueberry Farm, or canoe up the Slough Channel to experience the Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Mercer Slough Nature Park

properties.description: The Wildcat Trail on Green Mountain follows a multi-use trail on a steep, rocky ascent to the peak. Along the way, enjoy views of Hood Canal, the Olympics, and sometimes even downtown Seattle!
properties.title: Green Mountain State Forest - Wildcat Trail

properties.description: This innovative park in Edmonds is a delight for the senses of both blind and sighted visitors. The trail through the park was landscaped with trees and shrubs that provide a wide range of textures and fragrances as well as visual beauty.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Sierra Park

properties.description: The Domke Mountain trail was badly damaged by the Wolverine Fire in 2015. WTA crews have aided in fire recovery and a re-route of the trail. This steep hike along mountain summits will take you past wildflowers and beautiful views.
properties.title: Domke Mountain

properties.description: With a flat grade and plenty of benches and signs, this trail makes for a calming stroll through a beautiful area, no matter the occasion.
properties.title: Silver Falls Interpretive Trail

properties.description: This multi-use trail meanders through mature forest to connect with the Boundary Way trail to expansive views of the North Cascades and Mount Baker.
properties.title: Canyon Ridge

properties.description: Don’t be fooled by the name — the way to Easy Pass is anything but easy. But the reward for your efforts is an eastside gateway into the stunning North Cascades National Park. At the pass, you’re greeted by trickling streams of snowmelt and views of the peaks of Golden Horn and Mount Hardy to the east. Venturing further west, gaze into the Park, with awe-inspiring glacially carved river valleys, dark gray craggy massifs of Fisher Peak and Mount Logan dotted with snowfields or cloaked by glaciers, and a host of wildflowers.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Easy Pass

properties.description: Sheep Lake is a picturesque alpine lake guarded by jagged-edged ridges. It makes a good destination for children, especially if you let them swim, play in the meadows, or explore the small rock outcroppings. Sheep Lake is also a worthy destination for adults who want a pause from daily life to enjoy the outdoors. The campsites around the perimeter are ideal for base camping or for backpacking with children.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Sheep Lake

properties.description: The land encompassed by Dugualla State Park was acquired in 1992, when Washington State Parks bought the property to prevent it from being logged. It is now a quiet little state park at the north end of Oak Harbor.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Dugualla State Park

properties.description: An important route through urban King County, this 10-mile paved trail follows I-90 across Lake Washington, linking Seattle with Bellevue.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: I-90 Trail

properties.description: Incredible views and beautiful alpine lakes are your reward if you can ascend this steep trail in the North Cascades. At the top, you can choose between taking in sweeping panoramic views of North Cascades National Park and the Pickets Range, or relaxing near the lowest of the Thornton Lakes, both of which make a rewarding destination.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Thornton Lakes and Trappers Peak

properties.description: Fisk State Park is a large property on the southern bank of the Spokane River located about 30 miles northwest of downtown Spokane.
properties.title: Fisk State Park

properties.description: The Wood Trails area provides for a pleasant walk through a shady forest on a hillside with a native plant understory.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wood Trails

properties.description: Moulton Falls Trail is an out-and-back hike along the Lewis River. The trail crosses a picturesque footbridge and then follows the Lewis River with the river to the right and a mossy cliff to the left. The wide, hard-surfaced trail is mostly flat, making this a perfect year-round hike for people of all ages.
properties.title: Moulton Falls

properties.description: This patch of community forest on the north end of the Key Peninsula has a vast network of trails that are open to hikers, equestrians and mountain bikers. Take the Main Loop to explore the network, with many offshoot trails to extend and craft your own hike.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: 360 Trails

properties.description: Liberty, originally named Meaghersville, is a living ghost town. It was the center of a Washington State gold rush in the 1870s and has the look and feel often associated with the term ghost town. There is no formal trail through Liberty, but the open landscape makes it easy to navigate. Since it begins by the roadside, it’s a perfect exploration for all ages and abilities.
properties.title: Liberty Ghost Town

properties.description: A short loop hike to rock cliffs, with fantastic views out towards the Olympic Peninsula, and back toward other parts of Lopez.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Iceberg Point

properties.description: Indian Heaven trail provides access to one of the Gifford Pinchot National Forest's most popular areas. The Indian Heaven Wilderness is a high, forested plateau dotted with lakes and berry-filled meadows. Its a lovely location for a day hike or a backpacking trip. Some connect this trail with Cultus Creek trail and the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) to make a popular loop hike.
properties.title: Indian Heaven

properties.description: Route finding expertise is necessary to successfully complete this hike.
properties.title: Baldy Mountain

properties.description: A one mile trail in the Bumping River Valley connecting Road 1800 with Bumping Lake Trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Fish Lake

properties.description: A nice creekside hike within the Olympics with the option to check out Marymere Falls on the hike.  This hike has all types of old growth and lush vegetation.
properties.title: Barnes Creek

properties.description: The Hardy Ridge hike makes use of the old logging roads that wind through the backcountry or the park north of Highway 14. These routes are closed to vehicles but open to equestrians, mountain bikers and hikers. A WTA-built single-track trail traverses the ridge, offering a wide vista of the Columbia River Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Hardy Ridge

properties.description: The upper section of the CCC Road is just adjacent to the Middle Fork Road. Hiking this way, you'll avoid the somewhat confusing lower section, where DNR and private property bump up against each other. Here the trail is on National Forest land, so you'll need a Northwest Forest Pass, but the 3.4 miles to the Middle Fork Campground pass through uninterrupted quiet forest, creeks, and lovely views of the nearby peaks.
properties.title: CCC Road: Upper Trailhead

properties.description: Visit a popular water feature close to the trailhead, or get your feet wet and continue walking up the canyon along a rough road/railroad grade.
properties.title: Douglas Creek Canyon - South

properties.description: Shorter than the hike to Third Beach, the access to Second Beach is also a little more interesting, thanks to the ups and downs and a set of switchbacked stairs leading down to a coastline dotted with seastacks and a hole in the mainland that wind whistles through eerily.
properties.title: Second Beach

properties.description: An alternate approach to the Shedroof Divide, this trail offers a mostly-gentle climb through old-growth forest on its approach to the Salmo Priest Wilderness.
properties.title: Hughes Fork

properties.description: Spend a day strolling the rugged Olympic Coast to dramatic sea stacks and natural wonders.
properties.title: Rialto Beach and Hole-in-the-Wall

properties.description: This wide-open grassland offers roaming, but route-finding is necessary to enjoy your time on trail here.
properties.title: Goose Lake Plateau

properties.description: Lemah Meadow is a marshy clearing set at the foot of Lemah Mountain. Although the meadow lies along the Pacific Crest Trail, it is most easily reached by the Pete Lake Trail. A couple of scenic campsites make this a fun alternative to staying at the busy shores of Pete Lake.
properties.title: Lemah Meadow

properties.description: Fauntleroy Park, in West Seattle, is a few blocks southeast of the Vashon Island Ferry dock. The park offers some impressively tall trees, both conifers and deciduous trees. There is a good system of short trails, with boardwalks, rustic stairs and viewing platforms. Wildflowers are common in spring, and many wild birds make the park their home.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Fauntleroy Park

properties.description: The Fletcher Canyon Trail is a disproportionately difficult hike for being little more than two miles long. Perhaps because the route is steep and often muddy, obscured by blowdown, or faded entirely, it earns its ire and accolades. Individual accounts may be forgiven for their embellishments, especially those recalled fireside at the lodge tavern on a wet winter’s eve.
properties.title: Fletcher Canyon

properties.description: Explore an easy, gently graded trail to Falls Creek Falls just outside of Winthrop. The first waterfall is just a quarter-mile from the trailhead and is accessible via a paved trail.
properties.title: Falls Creek Falls (Winthrop)

properties.description: Located near South Seattle Community College, the Seattle Chinese Garden provides a peaceful retreat from the busyness of the city.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Seattle Chinese Garden

properties.description: Formerly known as the John Wayne Trail, this is a rail trail whose route crosses Washington, offering a nice short walk from a myriad of trailheads, or a fun, multi-day bikepacking adventure.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Army West

properties.description: This small, forested park in the city of Shoreline offers a network of trails that provide a pleasant diversion if you are in the neighborhood. The trails are accessible all year and are suitable for families.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: South Woods Park

properties.description: This hike is a flat 3.3 mile one-way blacktop trail that starts at The Port of Anacortes and ends at March Point near The Shell and Tesoro Refineries. The trail has great views of Mount Baker, Fidalgo Bay and lots of blue heron, especially when the tides are low.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Tommy Thompson Trail

properties.description: See history in your backyard. Tiger Mountain is full of historic trails, but the Bus Trail gets its name from an old bus that lies on its side along the trail. Kids will love exploring the area, and the Bus Trail can be used to make a huge variety of loops on the north side of Tiger Mountain.
properties.title: Bus Trail

properties.description: The Quilomene Wildlife Area is adjacent to the Whiskey Dick Wildlife Area, the Ginkgo Petrified Forest, and the popular climbing area of Vantage, including Frenchmans Coulee. Cross-country travel is possible here, and hikers can connect to the adjacent recreation areas to create miles-long loops and traverses, or just a simple out-and-back.
properties.title: Quilomene Wildlife Area

properties.description: Climb and climb to a high alpine parkland. Along the way, take in the gorgeous views, massive trees, and fluffy mosses that are signature to the Hurricane Ridge area of Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Heather Park

properties.description: From towering old-growth giants to placid lakes with craggy mountain views, this hike has everything you want in a trail. Put this one on your list of places to explore along Highway 2.
properties.title: Surprise and Glacier Lakes

properties.description: From its rocky and rutted beginnings, to the short last push to the top of a former fire lookout site, this trail boasts big rewards for very little effort. The west slope of Mount Adams is right there behind you as you head to the top of Council Bluff to face the mountain in full.
properties.title: Council Bluff

properties.description: Teanaway Butte is a prominent peak and former fire lookout site with stunning views of the Mount Stuart Range, the greater Teanaway area, and Mount Rainier. This hike is best enjoyed as a snowshoe adventure in winter, or a spring hike when other mountain trails are still buried in snow but wildflowers are already blooming in this area.
properties.title: Teanaway Butte

properties.description: With many miles of trails that are being improved by King County Parks, Ames Lake Forest is a good option for anyone looking to get away from crowds at Tolt-MacDonald. Keep in mind that this is a watershed though, and be certain to keep Leave No Trace principles in mind in this sensitive area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ames Lake Forest

properties.description: The Volcano View Trail completes a trifecta of great hikes for children near Mount St. Helens, offering hikers of every age a mile-long nature trail that curves around stumps, boulders and hemlocks.
properties.title: Volcano View Trail

properties.description: This section of Dishman Hills is a parcel that was owned by DNR and transferred to the Conservancy early in 2016.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Conservation Area - Glenrose

properties.description: Enjoy the solitude at two small lakes set in a forested basin adjacent to the crest of well-named Sawtooth Ridge.  Below the rocky crest and its scree slopes is a fringe of larch, golden in the fall. At the edge of this fringe and a few hundred feet above the lakes are two tarns, each in their own basin, accessible via cross-country travel.
properties.title: Martin Lakes

properties.description: A rugged, riverside trail that accesses the Olympic high country, at a price.
properties.title: Cameron Creek

properties.description: This state park has trails that wind through a forest of Ponderosa pine and Oregon white oak in the Simcoe Mountains near the Columbia River Gorge. Some trails take you up to meadows with wildflowers in the spring and views of Mount Hood in Oregon on a clear day.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Brooks Memorial State Park

properties.description: What was once a nice, short loop hike for families on the east side of Mount St. Helens National Volcanic monument has been lost to downed trees and heavy brush. Thankfully, the lake is still visible from an overlook partway up.
properties.title: Ryan Lake

properties.description: A long neglected trail connecting Buck Creek Pass to the rugged and wild upper Suiattle River.
properties.title: Triad Creek

properties.description: Heading right up the nose of the ridge it’s named after, Polallie will give you a workout. It’s steep, it’s rocky, and there are very few views. Head all the way to Diamond Lake for an overnight, go further into the Alpine Lakes wilderness, or call it quits whenever your glutes have had enough.
properties.title: Polallie Ridge

properties.description: A connector trail on the east side of Squak Mountain. Make loops of Summit Trail and Phil's Creek or East Ridge Trail with Old Griz.
properties.title: Old Griz

properties.description: A moderately challenging snowshoe route in Mount Rainier National Park with some avalanche danger in times of heavy snow.
properties.title: Rampart Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: Perched on a bluff overlooking majestic Puget Sound is the unique acreage of Ebey’s Landing. In addition to the Bluff Trail, visitors can experience the seaport town of Coupeville, observe working farms, and get their fill of wildlife viewing, all in a tiny National Park on Whidbey Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Ebey's Landing

properties.description: Floods in 2006 severely damaged the Glacier Basin trail, but after four years of work, WTA completed a new trail in Glacier Basin at Mount Rainier National Park in the summer of 2011. Since then, hikers of all stripes have had the pleasure of enjoying a brand-new route to one of the mountain's most iconic glaciers on an easy-to-hike trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Glacier Basin

properties.description: Popular year-round, but especially on sunny summer days, Gas Works Park is a popular greenspace with some old remains from an coal gasification plant. A rolling hill on the north side of Lake Union offers a great place to luxuriate in the sun and watch water traffic on the lake.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Gas Works Park

properties.description: Follow a network of nearly-level trails in this Edmonds park as you hike through vigorous second-growth mixed forest. Be alert for spring wildflowers or, seasonally, fall colors. Listen for many bird calls. Enjoy views across Goodhope Pond, a small lake that often hosts waterfowl.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Pine Ridge Park

properties.description: A scramble to Del Campo Peak from Gothic Basin. Class 3 or 4. Technical expertise required.
properties.title: Del Campo Peak

properties.description: Follow tumbling, churning, Van Trump Creek upstream past spectacular Bloucher Falls and Comet Falls, to an alpine meadow featuring views of Mount Rainier and easy wandering.  For an added treat, hike an extra mile for a stunning view of the barren Kautz Creek valley from Mildred Point.
properties.title: Van Trump Park

properties.description: Hike this easy leg stretcher while taking in the beautiful scenery of the North Cascades Highway. A good stop if you have a car full of restless children or you are  showing off the area to visiting relatives. The views from the top are a big payoff for such a short hike.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Thunder Knob

properties.description: Part of the scenic Pacific Northwest Trail, rugged 8-mile Swift Creek Trail accesses the Mount Baker Wilderness.
properties.title: Swift Creek

properties.description: Accessible only by water, this state park has primitive campgrounds, trails to explore and incredible views of the Puget Sound.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Stuart Island Marine State Park

properties.description: This is a burly day trip, but a great overnight destination for exploring the Sawtooth Range in the Olympic high country.
properties.title: Flapjack Lakes via North Fork Skokomish River

properties.description: There are two ways to reach Soda Peak Lake, a beautiful sub-alpine lake in an old growth forest. This approach is from the Trapper Creek trailhead to the east. It's a tough hike to a serene location, with plenty of secluded camps.
properties.title: Soda Peaks Lake

properties.description: A nice hike up a small canyon in a local community.
properties.title: Saddleback Trail

properties.description: The Sammamish River Trail is a 9.5-mile trail with one end at Marymoor Park in Redmond, passing through Woodinville, and the other end at Blythe Park in Bothell.  At Blyth Park, it connects with the Burke-Gilman Trail and continues another 18.8 miles ending at Golden Gardens in Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Sammamish River Trail

properties.description: A summit scramble in the Central Cascades. Gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Easter Peak

properties.description: Rising close to 4,000 feet out of the Cle Elum River Valley to meet the Yellow Hill Trail, the Jolly Mountain Trail presents a vigorous climb to a rambunctious ridgeline and perky panoramic summit with breathtaking mountain range views for miles of West Teanaway, the Enchantments, Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Glacier Peak, Mount Rainier and Mount Adams that you are likely to have all to yourself.
properties.title: Jolly Mountain

properties.description: This is a pleasant walk through the forest for nature lovers of all ages. There is a large, grassy area for picnics or play time and a resource center that provides educational opportunities. Getting here requires a five minute ferry ride on the Lummi Island Ferry.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Otto Preserve

properties.description: A 3-mile roundtrip trail to the Green Mountain (Camas) summit, through a mixed fir and maple forest. A moderate grade hike.
properties.title: Green Mountain (Camas)

properties.description: With a half-mile of sandy beach to explore, Pacific Beach State Park is great for a day at the beach with the family.
properties.title: Pacific Beach State Park

properties.description: This is a classic multi-day backpack ideal in larch season.
properties.title: Sawtooth Lakes Loop

properties.description: The Finch Arboretum is a 65-acre park found just minutes southwest of downtown Spokane. The site is an extensive botanical and tree garden with more than 2,000 labeled ornamental trees, shrubs, and flowers.
properties.title: Finch Arboretum

properties.description: How's this for a diverse urban hike? Begin in the eastern section of this Bellevue park and hike a series of trails for a satisfying loop through dark second-growth forest. Then, follow a connecting trail over to the western section of the park for a loop though the Bellevue Botanical Garden - both the formal gardens and some additional longer forest trails. Along the way brave a high, narrow trail bridge that crosses a deep ravine. Not enough? Multiple spur trails throughout the park invite further exploration.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wilburton Hill Park

properties.description: A scramble up a mountain just off I-90 near Snoqualmie Pass. Route finding and climbing experience required.
properties.title: Low Mountain

properties.description: Kautz Creek is a rewarding snowshoe trek for those willing to put in the effort. You’ll find sweeping views of the Tatoosh Range and Mount Rainier, but those come only after enduring four steadily uphill, largely view-free miles.
properties.title: Kautz Creek Snowshoe

properties.description: Navigate through a recently burned area to reach the top of Miners Ridge and enjoy views of the Stuart Range and Lake Wenatchee.
properties.title: Miners Ridge (Entiat)

properties.description: The Methow Community Trail runs along the Methow River valley between the towns of Mazama and Winthrop. It is a multi-use trail that provides countless connections to other trails like the Sun Mountain trail system and beyond.
properties.title: Methow Community Trail

properties.description: An off-road vehicle accessed trail in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, this route is closed from April to June.
properties.title: Louie Way

properties.description: This 13-acre Snohomish County park in Bothell offers about a mile of trails, all of them wide, paved and ADA accessible. The park has a lot of open grassy areas, other areas where the trails pass through forest, and it has a large playground area. Wherever possible, native vegetation has been replanted or maintained.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Miner's Corner

properties.description: Hike to a sweet, small, little-known lake near the trailhead for High Rock lookout.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Greenwood Lake

properties.description: While there is another park of the same name in Redmond, the Viewpoint Park in Bellevue serves as a natural buffer separating the neighborhoods from the businesses in the area. There are wooded trails to explore, including a trail leading to Bridle Trails State Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Viewpoint Park

properties.description: Branch off from the Batey Bould ORV Area to climb into the Colville National Forest. Enjoy the trees as you walk through the forest up to the top of Tacoma Peak, where you can get views of the Pend Oreille River Valley.
properties.title: Tacoma Peak Trail

properties.description: The small rocky bluff known as Little Si is a moderately-graded trail located in the North Bend area. Although relatively steep inclines bookend this hike, the route is perfect for beginners as well as hiking veterans with opportunities to cut away on the Boulder Garden Loop (at 0.3 miles and 0.5 miles).
properties.title: Little Si

properties.description: One of several Blue Lakes in Washington State, this Blue Lake lies about four and a half miles south of Mount Baker and requires less than a mile of hiking to reach it. Its translucent blue-green colors peek out beneath the shadows of a sheer rock wall partially encircling the lake, a reward for conquering the somewhat eroded and rooty trail that leads to it. Families, anglers, and hikers looking to experience a pretty subalpine lake will enjoy this short, yet memorable hike.
properties.title: Blue Lake

properties.description: Reaching the summit of Suntop can require considerable energy (a 16-mile hike), or it can be a simple 2-mile walk, depending on whether or not the 2 gates are open. Wide views of Mount Rainier and the White River valley below are worth it either way.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Suntop Lookout

properties.description: The route to Buck Mountain is a Class 3 and involves exposed scrambling. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Buck Mountain

properties.description: This trail connects Fort Ward Park Park to Blakely Harbor Park via a forested corridor.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Fort Ward to Blakely Harbor

properties.description: Start from Maritime Heritage Park in Bellingham and walk along Whatcom Creek to I-5, where you can continue to the eastern half of the Whatcom Creek Trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Whatcom Creek Trail - West

properties.description: This snowshoe route follows Forest Road 27 northwest from the Meadow Mountain Trailhead to Rat Trap Pass.
properties.title: Rat Trap Pass Snowshoe

properties.description: This trail winds through fire-ravaged terrain to a quiet lake in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest that borders Lake Chelan.
properties.title: Domke Lake

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Bullion Basin Snowshoe

properties.description: This long, meandering trail in the Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument makes for a lovely out-and-back, or as part of a big loop hike.
properties.title: Cinnamon Trail

properties.description: This short connector trail on Little Mountain Park helps visitors connect the Darvill Trail with the Ridge Trail, making for a direct route to the summit of this little park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Little Mountain Park - Up Quick

properties.description: Traverse Manastash Ridge over rugged eastern slope terrain between Quartz Mountain and Blowout Mountain. The distance covered is nearly 17 miles, so be prepared to spend a full day hiking one segment or stay overnight to complete the journey, which has ample trail to delight mountain vista aficionados, larch lovers, berry munchers, flower photographers, and campers alike.
properties.title: Manastash Ridge

properties.description: WTA has done some general trail maintenance in this beautiful neighborhood park. The site is extremely valuable from an ecological standpoint.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Moss Lake

properties.description: Walk up a wild and remote canyon on an old railroad grade.
properties.title: Douglas Creek Canyon - North

properties.description: Alpine lakes, high ridge traverses, wildflower-filled meadows, and a stroll along the Pasayten River await hikers who elect to visit the Buckskin Ridge Trail.
properties.title: Buckskin Ridge

properties.description: An easy hike up the Selah Creek canyon with views of both abundant wildlife and geological points of interest.
properties.title: Selah Cliffs Natural Area Preserve

properties.description: A fine trail for those willing to climb to get to great views in a remote part of the North Cascades National Park. Best done as a side trip off an overnight trip from Rainy Pass to Stehekin, or something similar.
properties.title: Goode Ridge

properties.description: A short boardwalk at Coldwater Lake, the Birth of a Lake trail is stroller and wheelchair friendly, and provides interesting information about the creation of this lake thanks to the 1980 eruption.
properties.title: Birth of a Lake Interpretive Trail

properties.description: Accessible from the Beverly Turnpike trail or from the Ingalls Creek trail, Fourth Creek is a hiker-only trail that connects Beverly Turnpike with the Ingalls Creek trail and allows hikers to create loops in the popular Teanaway area.
properties.title: Fourth Creek

properties.description: Heather Lake is a moderate day hike to an attractive lake just below the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT), particularly good for families. There are huckleberries in season and a dive into the lake will refresh hikers in the warmth of August.
properties.title: Heather Lake (near Lake Wenatchee)

properties.description: While it's possible to drive the the summit of Mount Constitution, you can also hike there. You'll begin and end at Mountain Lake and, along the way, you'll enjoy walking through forest as well as sweeping views of the San Juan Islands.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Moran State Park - Mount Constitution via Mountain Lake

properties.description: Enjoy a hike or glimpse some native species of bird along the Washougal Dike.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Captain William Clark Regional Park at Cottonwood Beach - Dike Trail

properties.description: The Chief Joseph Wildlife Area sits in the very southeast corner of Washington State. This trail follows Joseph Creek for a couple miles before ending in overgrowth.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Chief Joseph Wildlife Area - Joseph Canyon

properties.description: Perhaps you have hiked to each of the four named high points of the Anacortes Community Forest Lands (ACFL), or even combined two of these "summits" for a longer hike (e.g. Little Round Top and Sugar Cube, or Mount Erie and Sugarloaf.) So here's a thought: why not do a grand tour that reaches all four named summits in a single loop hike?
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Four Summit Loop

properties.description: A paved walkway follows an abandoned railroad grade trail along the Seattle Ship Canal with views of the water and extensive Ballard maritime industry.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: South Ship Canal Trail

properties.description: Once a railroad, this trail can visitors to travel between the towns of Chehalis and South Bend without having to drive! Do note though, the trail is in varying stages of development, so be sure you are prepared for pavement, gravel, dirt, or detours depending on your route.
properties.title: Willapa Hills Trail

properties.description: Snag views of Mount Stuart, the Enchantment range and much of the North Fork Teanaway Valley on this less-traveled trail in the Teanaway. Wildflowers, rivers, and a healthy workout all precede the views many seek at Medra Pass.
properties.title: Johnson Creek - Medra Pass

properties.description: This short trail in Olallie State Park heads to the base of 30-foot Weeks Falls.
properties.title: Olallie State Park - Weeks Falls

properties.description: As the oldest non-Native American settlement in the Pacific Northwest, Vancouver celebrates its long history more than most Washington cities. Experience many historic and scenic attractions in close proximity on this inviting urban loop.
properties.title: Vancouver Discovery Historic Loop

properties.description: If the tide is high, or you just want to see a different side of the Olympic Peninsula while you're visiting the coast, cross Highway 101 from the Kalaloch campground and take a peek into the deep Olympic forest.
properties.title: Kalaloch Creek Nature Trail

properties.description: The quintessential Seattle walk around the perimeter of a 50,000 thousand-year-old glacial lake, this trail is accessible to folks of all ages and abilities. It continues to be a preserve for hundreds of species of trees and plants, as well as numerous birds and waterfowl.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Green Lake

properties.description: If you only have a single day and really want to push yourself, then check out this winter route to Indian Racetrack, in the Indian Heaven Wilderness.
properties.title: McClellan Meadows to Indian Racetrack Snowshoe

properties.description: This small park near Olympia offers a nice meandering loop trail, as well as beaches and playgrounds for kids.
properties.title: Frye Cove County Park

properties.description: Built by a Trout Unlimited board member who wanted to give a newly wheelchair-bound friend a way to enjoy fishing and the outdoors, Friends Landing provides a delightful outing around Quigg Lake, which is stocked with a variety of fish, so it’s good for folks who want to bring a rod and relax, too.
properties.title: Friends Landing

properties.description: The O O Denny County Park has history, hiking and old-growth trees all within the city of Kirkland. See wildlife wandering through the trees, swimming in the creek and flying high in the sky.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: O. O. Denny Park

properties.description: A charming little escape on Budd Inlet, just north of the City of Olympia.
properties.title: Burfoot County Park

properties.description: Long Lake is a great option for those looking for a short hike to get back into the swing of things for the hiking season. It's relatively short and gains elevation steadily, so hikers can choose to make it an easy hike or bring a heavier pack for a bit more of a workout.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Long Lake

properties.description: This small pond next to Highway 12 and the Oak Creek Wildlife Area has a small trail circumnavigating it.
properties.title: Tims Ponds

properties.description: A delightful little waterfall tucked off of scenic Interstate 84, Starvation Creek State Park is also the jumping-off point for a handful of other popular hikes in the Columbia River Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Starvation Creek Falls

properties.description: Tyler Peak is located northwest of Mount Townsend. While this area can be windy, and views are obscured by fog, when it's clear, you'll enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding area.  Experience navigating off-trail and some climbing experience are necessary to summit Tyler Peak.
properties.title: Tyler Peak Trail

properties.description: Enjoy great views of Mount Adams from the site of a former fire lookout tower.
properties.title: Steamboat Mountain

properties.description: As you might expect from a former fire lookout, Sweetgrass Butte provides expansive views and carpets of wildflowers. The area provides a great respite from the hard hiking that much of the Methow Valley offers.
properties.title: Sweetgrass Butte

properties.description: This neighborhood park has a nice trail through the forest that is perfect for a dose of nature.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Renton Park

properties.description: Right in Olympia is this small forest near West Bay, where hikers can see all sorts of wildlife and might even be able to find shells and other artifacts from when the forest used to be part of the shore.
properties.title: West Bay Woods

properties.description: Spring is the perfect time to enjoy native flowers in bloom and a landscape alive with birdsong in this Pierce County Parks preserve.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Naches Trail Preserve

properties.description: These trails provide a multitude of multi-season hikes of varying difficultly. The reward is great views of the Columbia River and the geology of Wallula Gap from the east side of the river.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Wallula Gap - East

properties.description: This trail can be hiked on its own or joined with other area trails for a longer outing.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Forest to Sky Trail

properties.description: Climb up and up on the Wonderland Trail as you make your way along the southwest side of Mount Rainier. Enjoy sweeping views of the mountain and surrounding peaks.
properties.title: Longmire to Devil's Dream Camp

properties.description: The Naneum-Wilson trail features abundant wildflowers in spring as you traverse a large meadowed plateau recovering from a wildfire and studded with abundant creeks. With modest elevation gain, you will have expansive views of surrounding mountain ridges.
properties.title: Naneum-Wilson

properties.description: Sunrise (or sunset) offer a time of introspection. In Moran State Park, find this time to mull over life atop Sunrise Rock.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Moran State Park - Sunrise Rock

properties.description: This trail is a short, well-maintained descent to Beach 4 in the Kalaloch area of the Olympic coast. While there are many possible entry points to this stretch of PNW beach, this well-established interpretive trail provides a great location for a variety of visits: a quick stop at the viewpoint, day-use to explore the beach and tide pools or as a launch point for a multi-day adventure.
properties.title: Beach 4

properties.description: Enjoy an easy hike through a shady forest in an uncrowded corner of the state. Check out the progress of habitat restoration in the valley where Sullivan Creek was formerly dammed.
properties.title: Sullivan Creek and South Mill Pond

properties.description: Explore the far reaches of Taylor Mountain on this gently rolling trail.
properties.title: Knee Knocker Trail

properties.description: The trail up Huckleberry Mountain is a grind, but as with so many other hikes to high places on the Suiattle River Road, your efforts will be rewarded with spectacular views.
properties.title: Huckleberry Mountain

properties.description: The trail to Twin Lakes is actually an extremely rough forest road that is, in theory, driveable for high-clearance vehicles. If you elect to drive it, you'll have immediate access to the trails to Winchester Lookout, High Pass and Silesia Creek. If you park at the Yellow Aster Butte Trailhead (a popular option, which makes parking difficult on nice days), you have a 2.5 mile road walk to arrive at the lakes.
properties.title: Twin Lakes (North Cascades)

properties.description: This route on the north side of Sloan Peak is steep and challenging. Hikers with navigational skills can make it to the base of the peak -- climbing gear and expertise is needed to achieve the summit.
properties.title: Sloan Peak

properties.description: Pearrygin Lake State Park features miles of groomed trails, both on the state park land and on the adjoining Lloyd Ranch lands. There are miles of options here, from the far afield Crazy Eights and Southpark Loops, to the short loop near the West Campground.
properties.title: Pearrygin Lake Sno-Park - Lloyd Ranch

properties.description: This trail is located in the Salmo-Priest Wilderness area -- the first mile follows an old roadbed, then continues for two miles along an open ridge, with views of surrounding peaks.
properties.title: Salmo Divide

properties.description: The route to the top of Goat Island Mountain is not on true trail but is more of a scramble.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Goat Island Mountain

properties.description: Fish Park is a 40-acre park just north of downtown Poulsbo with a wonderful network of trails that run along the Liberty Bay Estuary.
properties.title: Poulsbo Fish Park

properties.description: While Mohawk Falls is on Forest Service land, there is no official trail to access this waterfall.
properties.title: Mohawk Falls and Mohawk Mine

properties.description: A short loop stroll along a small lake bordered by a small forest and many park amenities.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Five Mile Lake Park

properties.description: Dalles River is a short trail branching off of the Dalles Campground and meandering along the White River. It is known for the fallen 9.5-foot diameter Douglas fir at the trailhead, one of the largest trees in the Snoqualmie Ranger District.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Dalles River

properties.description: A relatively steep and rocky connector trail running between the Crystal Mountain resort area up through Bullion Basin to the Pacific Crest Trail with mountain and meadow views.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Bullion Basin

properties.description: Home to local middle and high school cross country runs, this trail is used by many locals for peaceful walks and jogs, and anyone interested in disc golf!
properties.title: Big Cross (Pasco)

properties.description: If ever there was a hike to satisfy all a hiker's desires, this one comes as close as any. A loop hike with many fabulous changing faces throughout the seasons, Heather-Maple Pass features ridgelines blanketed in wildflowers in summer, lakes ringed with golden larches in fall, and before the highway closes for the season, a dramatic place to experience early winter’s snows.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Heather - Maple Pass Loop

properties.description: Hike through a diverse forest to two alpine lakes that rest atop Manastash Ridge, one of Central Washington’s most notable geologic formations. The trail to Lost and Manastash Lakes is an underappreciated gem that will delight larch lovers, berry munchers, flower photographers, and campers alike.
properties.title: Manastash Lake

properties.description: Hike an easy mile to a spectacular cliff with a chance to see mountain goats, then continue through forest and meadows to views of Mount Adams, Mount Aix, Nelson Ridge and Mount Rainier.
properties.title: Gold Creek - Devils Slide

properties.description: This hiker-only trail makes for a quick way to sample the ecosystem on the east slope of the Olympic mountains. Plus, it's a decent starter backpacking trip for kids and makes for a nice day for birdwatchers.
properties.title: Elk Lakes

properties.description: The North Fork of Bridge Creek is a tucked-away gem of a hike in the North Cascades National Park. Accessible from both the Stehekin valley and Highway 20, many people blaze past this side trip on their way along the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT).   But if you choose to explore this branch, you'll be rewarded with stunning mountain valleys at the base of Mount Logan, one of many striking peaks in the North Cascades. Of course, you'll have to share the trail with brush, bugs, and maybe even bears to get there.
properties.title: North Fork Bridge Creek

properties.description: This quiet little forested walk near Acme offers lush greenery, plenty of wildlife to spot, and a nice, newly-maintained trail to enjoy a half-day hike.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Edfro Creek Preserve

properties.description: Moore Point is a starting point for hikers tackling the Lakeshore Trail, a popular spring backpacking trip. This trail is free from winter snow earlier than many thanks to its low elevation, and because of that, it can get quite full in the early season. Consider starting your hike midweek if you prefer to hike in solitude.
properties.title: Moore Point

properties.description: A scramble up a peak off the Mountain Loop Highway. Route finding gear and previous experience required.
properties.title: Bedal Peak

properties.description: A forest walk and a wetlands walk-two trails for the price of one! This wide, paved trail loops through meadows and shoreline.
properties.title: Seaquest State Park - Silver Lake

properties.description: Along a moderate trail into the glorious Alpine Lakes Wilderness Area, past burnt Ponderosa Pines, chattering mountain streams, plenteous wildflowers and tall mountain peaks, hikers will find beautiful Eightmile Lake and its rocky, tree lined shore.
properties.title: Eightmile Lake

properties.description: The Goat Creek trail ascends at a moderate pace from the Bumping River valley up to American Ridge and Goat Peak. The trail can be accessed via the Cougar Flat Campground.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Goat Creek

properties.description: Escape the crowds on this two-day backpacking adventure into the less-traveled areas on the north side of Mount St. Helens.
properties.title: Goat Creek Loop

properties.description: This short, easy, year-round trail meanders under the cool, protective trees of Squak Mountain State Park. It is a treat for kids with fun story boards along the way.
properties.title: Pretzel Tree Trail

properties.description: Heather Meadows is an area of Mount Baker with a variety of trails to explore with gorgeous views.
properties.title: Heather Meadows

properties.description: Take a day trip or camp at Lake Sylvia State Park to hike the Brownie Trail, one of 22(!) named multi-use trails in the Montesano City Forest.
properties.title: Lake Sylvia State Park - Brownie Trail

properties.description: With five miles of shoreline in South Puget Sound, the Woodard Bay Conservation Area includes forests, wetlands of freshwater, as well as historic and cultural resources that are a valuable diversion in the area.
properties.title: Woodard Bay Conservation Area

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Sauk Mountain Snowshoe

properties.description: About 1.5 miles long, this trail traverses east from the Mount Washington trail about 2.5 miles from the parking lot, and gains about 600 feet before connecting to the Olallie Trail.
properties.title: Great Wall Trail

properties.description: Enjoy a family hike at one of the new trail systems near Maple Valley and Covington.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cedar Creek Park

properties.description: This trail starts out at the Raven Roost high point at road’s end. This trail starts out with the views before you even set foot on trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Raven Roost

properties.description: Lacamas Lake Park is a diverse natural area with a surprisingly 'wild' feel for a park this close to town. Picnic by the lake, check out the Camas meadow in bloom, or explore the forest and creeks along the many trails. This hike describes a "lollipop" loop starting at the south end of the park, visiting the Lower Falls, then circling around through the park past Round Lake and returning along Lacamas Creek.
properties.title: Lacamas Park - Lacamas Creek

properties.description: Here's a nice little urban walk to keep in your back pocket if you need a flat paved path, or maybe you are in town for the Tulip Festival and need a bit of a leg stretcher.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Kulshan Trail

properties.description: A pleasant stroll for all ages- discover the history while enjoying a variety of avian wildlife on the southern terminus of the Columbia Plateau surveying the stark, scalloped Snake River country of southeast Washington.
properties.title: Columbia Plateau Trail - Snake River

properties.description: This is a short trail within the Blanchard Mountain trail system.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Caddis Fly

properties.description: This short walk through a neighborhood in Burien weaves between residents backyards and ends at a cliffy overlook of the Sound. Neighbors maintain the route and ask that visitors clean up after their pets and keep dogs on leash if you choose to visit.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Indian Trail

properties.description: This rugged trail in the Dark Divide is part of a large network of trails that offer miles of wandering in the forests between Mount St. Helens and Mount Adams.
properties.title: Dark Meadows

properties.description: This snowshoe route to Windy Pass and Mount Catherine is part of the Snoqualmie Nordic Center trail system.
properties.title: Windy Pass - Mount Catherine Snowshoe

properties.description: Take a short side trip from Waptus Pass to a small, shallow lake on Polallie Ridge.
properties.title: Escondido Lake

properties.description: There is one section of the Lake Wynoochee Lakeshore Trail that can be hiked year-round—a pleasant, interesting hike for all ages, at 6 miles round-trip and 800 feet of elevation gain. Its creeks have bridges; it has road access at both ends; it features flowers in spring and summer, autumn color in fall, and provides a pleasant winter outing in clear weather.
properties.title: Lake Wynoochee East Shore Trail

properties.description: Hiking the trail between the Narada Falls viewpoint and Reflection Lakes is pleasant enough. But you can extend the route into a loop featuring an unobstructed view of the Tatoosh Range from a rocky bluff, and an up-close experience of the awe-inspiring whitewater cascades of the Paradise River.
properties.title: Narada Falls to Reflection Lakes

properties.description: Hike the southernmost part of the Main Tiger Mountain Trail - the TMT - for a gentle introduction to the southern slopes of the Tigers. The trail is usable all year unless there has been significant lowland snow. In spring, enjoy blooms of trilliums and other wild flowers. In the fall, appreciate the colors of leaves that carpet parts of the trail.
properties.title: Tiger Mountain Trail South

properties.description: A half-mile jaunt from Shangri La to Tibbetts Marsh and West Tibbetts Creek Trails.
properties.title: Protector Trail

properties.description: This trail features plenty of variety, with destinations spaced perfectly for families or first-time backpackers. Beautiful hemlock forest, meadows dotted with wildflowers, gleaming lakes, mountain views, juicy berries and excellent camping are all available.  Wait until later in the hiking season though, as this area is known for its bugs.
properties.title: Anderson and Watson Lakes

properties.description: This trail begins at Crooked Creek Trail 3100 and ends at Smooth Ridge Trail 3105 (Moore Flat). It is maintained for foot and horse traffic since it is located within the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Packer's Trail

properties.description: Take your young hikers out on a half-mile trail through the swampy area north of Tradition Lake. It could even be their first hike! The trail is solidly-constructed, with good footing, no mud and it's almost all level. It's designed with the young visitors in mind. But hey, it's OK if you older folks enjoy it, too!
properties.title: Swamp Trail

properties.description: Located just south of Priest Lake in Idaho, this area offers 10 miles of trails that give visitors plenty of hiking and snowshoeing options. The trail system here starts from the Priest Lake Information Center just off Highway 57.
properties.title: Chipmunk Rapids National Recreation Trail

properties.description: Take an old prospector’s trail from valley to the heights of Copper Pass. Of course, the style of route is direct, with more up the fall line than switchbacks. Once there, enjoy the views west to the heart of the North Cascades and take time for exploration in all directions.
properties.title: Copper Pass via Twisp River

properties.description: This small neighborhood park features a loop trail that winds through the forest behind the playground.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Ruth Cohen Memorial Park

properties.description: This trail offers a nice wander through the woods to a low pass. While it's short on views, it offers an extended forested wander where you can creekhop to your heart's content.
properties.title: North Fork Tieton to Tieton Pass

properties.description: Scorpion Mountain offers a 360-degree view of the Central Cascades, and the huckleberries and blueberries make this a much underrated fall hike.
properties.title: Scorpion Mountain via Johnson Ridge

properties.description: Walk on a dike next to a usually quiet river through the outskirts of Kelso.
properties.title: Coweeman River Trail

properties.description: Discover the area that was the original source of Olympia's drinking water--a delightful little green wetland known as Watershed Park. With thirty structures on the 1.35 mile loop, you can be sure to have an intimate look at the workings of a wetland without getting damp yourself.
properties.title: Watershed Park

properties.description: Goat Flats is part of the route used to access Three Fingers Lookout.
properties.title: Goat Flats

properties.description: Take this 4-mile trek along an old forest road, to peek-a-boo views of the Teanaway ridges and quiet forest.
properties.title: Pipe Creek Loop Snowshoe

properties.description: A steep fisherman's trail to a secluded lake beneath Malachite Peak.
properties.title: Rock Lake

properties.description: The way to Melakwa Lake is like two different trails: first a wide gentle trail through old growth forest beneath an elevated and noisy Interstate freeway. And second, a rocky steep trail that follows a waterfall and a precipitous gorge upstream to get to a pair of clear alpine lakes flanked by rocky peaks.  Is it about the journey or the destination?  You decide.
properties.title: Melakwa Lake

properties.description: The Lacrosse Pass Trail runs up and over the ridge between the West Fork Dosewallips River valley and the Duckabush River Valley.
properties.title: LaCrosse Pass

properties.description: The Hidden Lake trail is one of the crown jewels of hiking in Washington State. No other trail offers so much as Hidden Lake Lookout: forest, wildflowers, a true alpine environment of stark granite well above treeline, breathtaking summit views of the heart of North Cascades National Park, and a fire lookout with a sweeping history almost as big as the mountainous landscape it gazes over.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Hidden Lake Lookout

properties.description: Looking for the perfect first hike for young kids?  Eaten too much bratwurst in Leavenworth and need a walk in the woods to settle your stomach? Want a moderate flat snowshoe with a beautiful winter destination? The short trail to Hidden Lake adjacent to Lake Wenatchee is the answer to all of these requests.
properties.title: Hidden Lake (Lake Wenatchee)

properties.description: Nestled deep within the heart of the Olympics, LaCrosse Basin is steeped in rich history as well as views that never relent.
properties.title: LaCrosse Basin

properties.description: A trail to a ridgetop in the Icicle Creek area.
properties.title: Jack Ridge

properties.description: The Boulder Garden Loop offers an opportunity to explore stone giants on a relatively untraveled path, despite its proximity to two of the busiest hiking thoroughfares in the Snoqualmie Pass region. It also is the access route to the Old Mount Si trail, for those who desire a less peopled approach to the Puget Sound region's most well-known hike.
properties.title: Boulder Garden Loop

properties.description: Salmon Creek Ravine Park in Burien, located a few blocks north of Seahurst Park, is a large, minimally developed park centered on the drainage of Salmon Creek and its small tributaries. The area is forested and has some very large maples and alders, interspersed with Douglas-fir, redcedar and madrone.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Salmon Creek Ravine Park

properties.description: Hike a broad, sunny trail on the north side of Tiger Mountain.
properties.title: Puget Power

properties.description: Bring your binoculars along on this hike through a birding hotspot, where 116 species have been seen, and watch for other wildlife — like deer — too.
properties.title: Washougal River Greenway Trail

properties.description: This trail takes hikers up close and personal with Cathedral Rock before dropping down to the shores of Deep Lake.
properties.title: Deep Lake

properties.description: A large, wooded park in the Capitol Hill neighborhood of Seattle. With a historic watertower, the Asian Art Museum and the Volunteer Park Conservatory here, there is plenty to see here on your walk.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Volunteer Park

properties.description: Press on past Pratt Lake to reach a measure of backcountry solitude at Windy Lake or Kaleetan Lake in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
properties.title: Kaleetan Lake

properties.description: Spencer Island is part of a larger area known as the Snohomish River Estuary and is a stop on the Washington State Great Birding Trail. The mix of saltwater from Possession Sound and fresh water from the Snohomish River create a unique ecosystem, making it one of the best birding spots in Puget Sound. On this walk, you don’t want to forget your binoculars!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Spencer Island

properties.description: A short trail leads to Sunset Pond in Bellingham, which allows hikers to connect to Squalicum Creek Trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Sunset Pond Park

properties.description: This short connector trail runs through the UW Bothell-Cascadia Community College campus, with views of a large reclaimed wetland area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: UW Bothell - Cascadia Community College Wetlands

properties.description: Enjoy an easy 1.2-mile loop near the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center. Pair it with the Hall of Mosses for a couple of nice, flat exploratory leg-stretchers in the Hoh. Both make for an interesting introduction to the area, and will be a hit with the kids!
properties.title: Spruce Nature Trail (Hoh)

properties.description: Not the easiest hike, but the reward is a hot springs if you are persistent.
properties.title: Sulphur Creek

properties.description: This is a lateral trail off the PCT north of Waptus Lake.
properties.title: Lake Vicente

properties.description: Summiting Hibox requires route finding experience and comfort with scrambling.
properties.title: Hibox Mountain

properties.description: This hike contains all of what a classic Rainier outing should – a quiet canopy of old-growth forest, high alpine meadows bursting with wildflowers in the summer, and in-your-face-views of glaciated Mount Tahoma (not to mention Mounts Adams, St. Helens, and even Hood on a crystal clear day).
properties.title: Eagle Peak Saddle

properties.description: Travel deep into the Goat Rocks Wilderness and enjoy stunning views of Mount Adams, Mount St. Helens, Jordan Basin, and Goat Lake.
properties.title: Goat Lake

properties.description: This approximately one mile trail provides a link between the East Hardy Ridge Trail and the Upper Hardy Creek Trail to providing multiple loop options in the backcountry of Beacon Rock State Park. With its majestic bridge across Hardy Creek, lush evergreen forest and enchanting stream crossings, it is a worthy destination in itself.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Bridge Trail

properties.description: A lengthy, pleasant hike through lodgepole pine and deciduous forest, past a lovely waterfall to Abernathy Pass.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Abernathy Pass via Cedar Creek

properties.description: Goat Peak is best tackled when this trail is snow-free. When snow is present, the route can pose extreme avalanche danger and requires route-finding expertise.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Goat Peak Snowshoe

properties.description: There are two routes up the north side of Silver Star Mountain that in good conditions can be combined to form a sort of loop. Along the way, hikers will be delighted with a diverse array of wildflowers, a natural arch, volcanic views and fine hiking. But some sections of Ed's Trail are very exposed, and require agility and flexibility to navigate.
properties.title: Silver Star Mountain - Ed's Trail

properties.description: Here's an ADA-accessible forested trail just over half a mile long in Beacon Rock State Park that takes you to a lookout point for Bonneville Dam and the Columbia Gorge. It can also connect you with the Hamilton Mountain Trail from the Beacon Rock Campground.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Hadley Trail

properties.description: Hike in to a small lake at the head of a valley with good campsites and many possibilities for exploration.  Along the way, see the difference between the 2018 Crescent Mountain Fire impacted forest and the old growth forest.
properties.title: North Lake

properties.description: See beautiful wildflower meadows on the way up to a panoramic view that includes many of the big peaks in both Washington and Oregon.
properties.title: Silver Star Mountain - Grouse Vista

properties.description: Take the trail less traveled by and visit some quiet lakes near Mount Rainier. Or, continue on to extensive views afforded by Noble Knob.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Greenwater Trail to Lost Lakes

properties.description: This 178-acre area just outside of Packwood has nearly 4 miles of trails for hikers to wander.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Skate Creek Park

properties.description: A scramble up Anaconda Peak in the Mount-Baker Snoqualmie National Forest. Climbing experience recommended.
properties.title: Anaconda Peak

properties.description: A very short trail in Cle Elum that offers a little history of the railroad through Washington state.
properties.title: South Cle Elum Yard

properties.description: Blue Stilly Park is located in Snohomish County along the Stillaguamish River. The small park has a baseball diamond, picnic areas, a fire pit and a nature trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Blue Stilly

properties.description: The trail to Third Beach provides plenty of suspense for hikers. It’s a 1.3 mile trek through high trees, sometimes shrouded in fog, giving the forest here a spooky aura. But popping out onto the coast at the log-choked mouth of a creek and seeing the grand Pacific Ocean provides the perfect payoff.
properties.title: Third Beach

properties.description: A very short access trail on Cougar Mountain from the Red Town Trailhead that offers a nice graveled path, and a small waterfall.
properties.title: Red Town Creek

properties.description: This sweet little hike on the south side of Mount St. Helens is a good destination for families seeking a short day hike, but it is also one access point for the round-the-mountain Loowit Trail, and a popular snowshoeing location, so it sees a fair amount of traffic year-round.
properties.title: June Lake

properties.description: The Batey-Bould Trail System is 40 miles of motorcycle tracks in the summer and snowmobile tracks in the winter, but it is also a lovely walk through the forest for hikers/snowshoers who go during the week and avoid the motorists.
properties.title: Batey-Bould

properties.description: A rambling trail that provides easy access from the Beckler River Road near Skykomish to the Pacific Crest Trail and Henry M. Jackson Wilderness through the Meadow Creek Valley to sweet little Pear Lake for an overnight.
properties.title: Pear Lake via Meadow Creek

properties.description: This short trail in the Hood Canal Ranger District on the east side of the Olympics takes hikers to a relatively unknown waterfall that delivers its reward -- a captivating 130-foot plunging waterfall -- in just under a mile.
properties.title: Murhut Falls

properties.description: The former Wayne Golf Course has now been converted into an urban green space, and provides an 89-acre open area for visitors to hike, picnic, play field games and enjoy nature.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wayne Golf Course

properties.description: An excellent hike for wildlife and wildflowers, the Scroggie Loop curves through open terrain, Ponderosa pines, and wetlands -- a wide variety of desert country just west of Spokane.
properties.title: Fishtrap Lake - Scroggie Loop

properties.description: Visit three looping routes on Mount St. Helens near the Marble Mountain Sno-Park. From here you'll enjoy quiet forest and views of Mount St. Helens, as well as a variety of difficulties of hike, from a casual stroll to a more sweat-inducing climb. It's hikers choice!
properties.title: Sasquatch Ski Loops

properties.description: A popular summer destination, Pilchuck requires more experience with routefinding and snow gear in the winter. Be sure to have both should you venture here when snow or ice are present.
properties.title: Mount Pilchuck - Winter

properties.description: A low-key stroll to riparian wild-life viewing along the Tucannon River.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Mouth of the Tucannon

properties.description: Climb most of the way up Center Mountain along this trail as you enter the Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Chancellor

properties.description: A summit of a mountain in the central Cascades, accessible from Holden Village or the Phelps Creek trailhead.
properties.title: Mount Maude

properties.description: Josephine is a beautiful lake 5.2 miles south of Stevens Pass on the Pacific Crest Trail. The trail winds thru the Stevens Pass Ski area, climbing for two miles to top of the hill, gaining 1000 feet along the way.
properties.title: Josephine Lake

properties.description: The 721 forested acres of Trillium Community Forest can be explored by the quiet, meandering trails provided for hiking, horseback riding, and mountain biking. Your path is lined with ferns and soaring stands of Douglas-fir trees.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Trillium Community Forest

properties.description: Robinswood Community Park has a 10-acre wooded area with about 2 miles of hiking trails. The rest of the park includes a small pond, big grassy fields, dog parks, and sports fields. The park is also home to the Robinswood House. It's easily accessible from the surrounding neighborhoods, which includes Bellevue College.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Robinswood Park

properties.description: Rainbow and Blazer Lakes sit along the Defiance Trail between Mason Lake and the Pratt Lake Trail junction. Blazer is reached on an abandoned trail that starts just west of the Rainbow outlet creek.
properties.title: Blazer Lake

properties.description: This short hike takes you to a delightful little waterfall; it's a good alternate to the longer, nearby Bells Mountain trail if you don't have the time or energy.
properties.title: Lucia Falls

properties.description: To see beautiful Williams Lake, set in a meadow basin with pockets of larch trees, a hiker must earn it. The shallow gradient trail takes 7 miles to gain 3600 feet and is mostly on a fire-scorched, sun-baked south facing slope where the sparse shade offers a welcome respite from the heat.
properties.title: Williams Creek

properties.description: Imagine a freeway through the woods with offramps to points of interest, a few rest areas, and meadow viewpoint.  With this in mind, you'll have a good understanding of the Martin Creek Trail. This trail is a connector route between popular lakes and part of the Sawtooth Lakes Loop (aka Golden Lakes Loop).
properties.title: Martin Creek

properties.description: The Worm Flows Climbing Route, from Marble Mountain Sno-Park, is the most direct route to the summit of Mount St. Helens during the winter season. Ice axe, crampons, and avalanche awareness are necessary when attempting to summit St. Helens in the winter. Skis with climbing skins or snowshoes with cleats are also highly recommended.
properties.title: Mount St. Helens - Worm Flows Route

properties.description: Maury Island Marine Park is located on the east side of Maury Island which is connected to Vashon Island. There is more than one mile of natural shoreline with stunning views of Mount Rainier and the Cascade Mountains. The park is a former gravel mine and contains rare stands of the Pacific Madrone tree. The accessible shoreline allows for scuba diving and an excellent beach walk to observe marine life with a salt marsh at the north end.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Maury Island Marine Park

properties.description: If you are bored at the thought of another hike up West Tiger #3, here is an option for a more ambitious hike. First, the route will take you to Poo Poo Point, a knoll on a shoulder of West Tiger Mountain, for the view and perhaps to see paragliders launching into the sky. Then, you'll continue via a sequence of short trails to reach and traverse all three numbered summits of West Tiger Mountain before returning to your trailhead.
properties.title: West Tiger Four-Summit Loop

properties.description: This one is a jewel. A railtrail with opportunities for biking, hiking, birding, wildlife, wildflowers, river views, salmon viewing, photography, waterfall, and history. If you want an urban trail this one has it all.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Similkameen Trail

properties.description: This short connector trail leads hikers from the Pacific Crest Trail to Waptus Pass.
properties.title: Waptus Burn

properties.description: Great views, a canyon beneath spectacular cliffs, buttresses and pinnacles of weathered basalt, wildflowers in the spring, color and wildlife in the autumn, and sunshine through most of the day in the winter make the Point 3582-Waterworks Canyon loop on Mount Cleman a great hike.
properties.title: Cleman Mountain - Waterworks Canyon Loop

properties.description: If your car can take the chassis-rattling drive to the Stacker Butte trailhead, you'll be rewarded with one of the most gratifying views-per-mile hikes in Washington. The Columbia Hills Natural Area Preserve boasts spreading views of the east side of the Columbia River Gorge, both in Washington and Oregon, and provides one of the only protected areas for houndstongue hawkweed and Idaho fescue grasslands. These protected plants need mininmal disturbance, so it's especially important to stay on trail and four-legged hiking companions have to stay home from this hike.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Columbia Hills State Park - Stacker Butte

properties.description: One of the hundreds of lakes in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Lake Kulla Kulla is visible from the top of Mount Defiance but not accessible via formal trails.
properties.title: Lake Kulla Kulla

properties.description: Hardscrabble Creek connects the Ingalls Creek drainage with the Wenatchee Mountain crest. Steep and difficult to follow, it has no trailhead, but rather begins at a junction with the Ingalls Creek trail, 8.5 miles from the Ingalls Creek Trailhead.
properties.title: Hardscrabble Creek

properties.description: The road to the Sheep Canyon trailhead has washed out and the trailhead is closed. The hike to the Sheep Canyon viewpoints now requires an extra 2.4 miles, and begins at the Blue Lake trailhead, found at the end of the drivable portion of Forest Road 8123.
properties.title: Sheep Canyon

properties.description: This old trail is no longer maintained by the Forest Service, and there's hardly any parking available at the trailhead, but if it's a quiet day, you might enjoy big old-growth on this little used trail.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Rocky Creek

properties.description: Hike into the heart of Colville's Salmo-Priest Wilderness — so remote that even grizzly bears have been spotted here. This is high country, with some of the most impressive old-growth stands this side of the Cascades.
properties.title: Salmo-Priest Loop

properties.description: South of Mt. St. Helens near Amboy, the Horseshoe Ridge Trail (#140) is an aptly named 7.3 mile trek off of well-traveled Siouxon Creek. Once easily accessed a mile from West Creek, attempts from the relocated main trailhead entail an 18.1 mile round trip.
properties.title: Horseshoe Ridge

properties.description: Nick’s Lagoon is a small greenspace managed by Kitsap County Parks. The lagoon sits in the nook of Seabeck Bay.
properties.title: Nick's Lagoon

properties.description: An unmaintained trail that climbs steeply up the shoulder of Humpback Mountain to an infrequently visited summit on a massive pile of boulders.
properties.title: Humpback Mountain

properties.description: Just east of Centralia, Seminary Hill offers hilltop wandering and views of Centralia, Chehalis and the Chehalis or Skookumchuck River Valley.
properties.title: Seminary Hill Natural Area

properties.description: Choral Peak is an off trail climb in the Entiat Range.
properties.title: Choral Peak

properties.description: Enjoy this short day hike with views of Chewelah and the surrounding valley and mountains.
properties.title: Quartzite Mountain

properties.description: This interpretive trail is a great one for visitors of all ages. Thanks to the boardwalk, it's great for all comers, including those with mobility issues. Educational signs found along the trail illustrate the purpose of our forests and the reason we need to preserve them.
properties.title: Shadow of The Sentinels

properties.description: Located on the outskirts of Colville, this trail is an ideal place to enjoy a rambling loop hike while peering down onto Main Street and the Colville Valley.
properties.title: Colville Mountain Loop Trail

properties.description: Though a short one, this hike around Historic Snoqualmie and the old railway is a very unique hike that's great for the whole family (and even wheelchairs and strollers!).
properties.title: Railroad Park and Centennial Log Pavilion

properties.description: Hike to a peak in a working and research forest near Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Pack Forest - Hugo Peak via Horse Trail

properties.description: Take a short hike near the campgrounds at Cape Disappointment State Park to gorgeous views of the mighty Pacific Ocean and the Columbia River.
properties.title: Cape Disappointment State Park - McKenzie Head

properties.description: This section of the Olympic Discovery Trail, from Blyn to Port Angeles, offers an appealing mix of forest, farms, rivers and waterfront views.
properties.title: Olympic Discovery Trail - East Central

properties.description: In addition to broad views, Shellrock Peak features some interesting rock formations for the geology buff. Constant elevation changes along the trail, lack of water, and the need for minor off-trail routefinding make solitude likely.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Shellrock Peak

properties.description: The Hidden Lakes are the jewels of the Pasayten Wilderness. Tucked high within the Wilderness, these lakes provide backpackers with opportunities to fish, swim, relax, and view wildlife and wildflowers.
properties.title: Hidden Lakes

properties.description: Most hikers enter the Goat Rocks Wilderness from the western side, but those who come in from the east find the wilderness just as beautiful and wild, and much less crowded. The Surprise Lake Trail is one of the few that enter from the east, and it is also one of the most gentle and scenic.
properties.title: Surprise Lake

properties.description: From mountain peak to Wild and Scenic River, this long loop takes in a range of terrain, wildlife and views.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Mount Misery Loop

properties.description: The longer, more scenic approach to Abercrombie Mountain, North Fork Silver Creek Trail is worth the extra effort involved for a hike to eastern Washington's second highest summit.
properties.title: North Fork Silver Creek Trail

properties.description: The Upper Dungeness River trail is an easy stroll along a roaring river and among towering trees. It’s great for all ages (as long as the trail is snow- and ice-free), and the shelter at Camp Handy is a welcome and dry lunch destination on rainy days.
