properties.title: Upper Dungeness River

properties.description: The trails in this park reveal the military history and natural wonder of this area. There are options for walking along the beach or through forested slopes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Fort Ward Park

properties.description: Horan offers two miles of graveled trails and 15 viewing stations where visitors can watch local wildlife and learn about the flora and fauna that surround them.
properties.title: Wenatchee Confluence State Park - Horan Natural Area

properties.description: Located on the western edge of West Seattle, Lincoln park offers 5 miles of trails, including a loop hike with bluff and beachfront views of Puget Sound, Vashon Island, and the Olympic Mountains.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lincoln Park

properties.description: Reflection Lakes are not just a popular photography stop. From the lakes, you can hike to a stunning cliffside view of the lakes and the Tatoosh range. From there, you have the option of returning the way you came or hiking in a loop around the largest of the lakes.
properties.title: High Lakes Loop

properties.description: With 12 named peaks along a route that starts and stays high, hikers can expect big views, no crowds and excellent stargazing.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Kettle Crest North

properties.description: This popular state park is nestled on a stretch of shoreline between the urban centers of Seattle and Tacoma, so unsurprisingly, it's a frequently-visited location. Share the beach, share the views, and enjoy the atmosphere here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Saltwater State Park

properties.description: Visit two waterfalls plunging to the Lewis River on this family friendly accessible trail.
properties.title: Curly Creek Falls

properties.description: View thousands of migrating waterfowl and other wildlife from an easy, accessible trail through a national wildlife refuge just outside of the Tri-Cities.
properties.title: McNary National Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: Camp Long is a hidden gem, a 68-acre enclave in West Seattle featuring old growth forest, wildlife, a variety of hiking trails, rock climbing, ropes courses, camping, and environmental education.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Camp Long

properties.description: Goat Peak offers expansive views into the William O. Douglas Wilderness and beyond. Once the site of a U.S. Forest Service lookout, Goat Peak’s 6,400-foot summit showcases such impressive gems as the Goat Rocks, Bumping Lake, Mount Rainier, Fife’s Peak, and the Stuart Range.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Goat Peak

properties.description: Grand Park provides one of the absolute best views of The Mountain from any of the trails in the park. Though longer than the access from Lake Eleanor, this route is more scenic, passing through the stark rocky landscape of Sunrise to flower-filled Berkeley Park and then climbing gradually through cool forest before getting to alpine meadows and majestic Grand Park itself.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Grand Park via Sunrise

properties.description: Quincy Lakes is an umbrella term for the area including Ancient Lakes and Dusty Lake.
properties.title: Quincy Lakes

properties.description: Follow a loop trail that samples what Mount Rainier has to offer: a popular waterfall, vast expanses of wildflowers, numerous snowmelt streams, a historic monument to the mountain’s first climbers, and of course views of Mount Rainier itself.
properties.title: Golden Gate Loop

properties.description: Hike down into a canyon starting at 1000 feet of elevation and descending. The trail is an old road that goes for several miles.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Chief Joseph Wildlife Area - Green Gulch

properties.description: The Tired Creek is a quiet, steep trail that departs the Pete Late trail 1.2 miles from the trailhead. It's less-traveled than the Pete Lake trail, so you'll get solitude, but also might have to contend with a little less maintenance than on other trails in the area.
properties.title: Tired Creek

properties.description: Accessible only by bridge or by boat, Harstine Island State Park is one of a few state parks available to explore on Harstine Island.
properties.title: Harstine Island State Park

properties.description: King Sisters Preserve is a short, flat walk that runs parallel to San Juan Valley Road on San Juan Island. It is easy and non-technical, and is a nice place to walk your dog on leash if you are staying nearby.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: King Sisters Preserve

properties.description: This road walk in the Teanaway Community Forest has a choice of a lower road along the creek or an upper road on the hillside. The upper road provides a few places with views south across the Middle Creek valley and views of lower peaks in the Teanaway drainage to the west.  The lower road is a walk in the shade along the creek with a few meadows and marshes for wildlife and fall foliage viewing.
properties.title: Middle Creek

properties.description: Getting up Bunker Hill is less of a charge and more of a steady march. The hill, named by early settlers in the valley, used to serve as a fire lookout, and the way to the top is steep and direct. But the fire lookout is gone and the trees have grown up, so with limited views from the summit, it’s better suited to your training regimen than visiting on shore leave. But it’s a great work out, and you can cool down afterwards on the nearby Whistle Punk trail.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Bunker Hill

properties.description: Merrill Lake Conservation Area is a seasonal campground that includes a short and sweet loop trail around a lake. Along the way are 10 interpretative signs that supplement what hikers see around them.
properties.title: Merrill Lake Conservation Area - Old Growth Loop Trail

properties.description: Wild and mercurial, the Olympic Coast has a special appeal in the spring and fall. Grassy bluffs, cliffside caves and tidal pools are all to be found along this four-mile beach hike near the Kalaloch Campground. So shrug on your rain gear and enjoy the bird watching, sense of solitude and stunning seascapes.
properties.title: Kalaloch - Browns Point

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: La Rush/Bear Lakes

properties.description: If you can stand the bugs, this is a very pleasant, well-shaded hike with a very rewarding view at the top. It's a short hike, doable in a day for most hikers.
properties.title: Badger Peak

properties.description: Venture down to a beach in a small Whatcom County park in Point Roberts.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Monument Park

properties.description: Tucked deep into the heart of the infrequently-visited Colville National Forest is the North Fork Sullivan Trail. This trail has no trailhead of its own, but climbs steadily from its junction with the Halliday and Red Bluff Trails to Crowell Ridge, where you'll enjoy expansive views of the surrounding area.
properties.title: North Fork Sullivan Creek

properties.description: A short jaunt off the Clay Pit Road to a deep mineshaft left over from mining activities that used to take place on Cougar Mountain in the late 1800s.
properties.title: Mine Shaft Trail

properties.description: The Timberline Trail is a roughly 40-mile scenic loop trail in northwest Oregon State that circumnavigates the young stratovolcano Wy'East or Mount Hood at or mostly at the treeline. At 11,244 feet, Mount Hood is the highest point in Oregon and the fourth highest peak in the Cascade Range.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Timberline Trail

properties.description: This hike has deep forest, pretty mountain lakes, fall color, and plenty of good trail to walk on without watching your feet all the time.
properties.title: Hope and Mig Lakes

properties.description: The Blowout Creek Trailhead offers a more secluded adventure than the CCC Road: Lower Section, despite its route along an old road. Climb a moderate grade alongside Blowout Creek for almost a mile before arriving at the CCC Road Trail, then hike to a beautiful waterfall.
properties.title: CCC Road: Blowout Creek Trailhead

properties.description: Take the Trail Creek Trail through dry forest on the east side of the Cascade Range. A large fire burned through here more than 100 years ago, opening up the forest and offering views through the remaining trees of the surrounding mountains.
properties.title: Trail Creek

properties.description: This trail offers two options: head downhill to connect with the Middle Fork Teanaway, or hike uphill to summit Johnson Mountain or connect with the Jungle Creek Trail. Both provide an escape from the crowds and relatively early season access in the Teanaway.
properties.title: Way Creek

properties.description: This hike goes primarily through a network of mountain bike trails. Hiking here is not recommended in the summer, when it can be extremely hot. Please know the rules of right-of-way before hiking here.
properties.title: Devils Gulch

properties.description: This trail is a rarely traveled and quite rustic trail used primarily by climbers as an alternate climbing route for Mount Baker. Though not for the faint of heart, this hike has a truly spectacular payoff in views and provides a solitary hiking experience.
properties.title: Boulder Ridge

properties.description: The loop trail combines three of the four trails in the park and takes you along the river a short distance before hiking up the canyon's slopes  with increasing views to the 750 foot highpoint.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Deschutes River

properties.description: A moderate loop trail takes you through ferns and Douglas firs.
properties.title: Port Gamble Forest - Ewok Trail Loop

properties.description: Want to go on a forest stroll, do some tide pooling and have a picnic on the lawn, all in the same place? Look no further than Kitsap Memorial State Park.
properties.title: Kitsap Memorial State Park

properties.description: Vesper Peak is a difficult and demanding hike. Though you get incredible views at the summit, many search and rescue missions get called to Vesper Peak, so assess your skills and be prepared if you choose to hike here.
properties.title: Vesper Peak

properties.description: Cannon Mountain is Washington's 38th highest peak. There is no direct trail to the summit, although the routes to Prussik Pass and Shield's Lake can be used.
properties.title: Cannon Mountain

properties.description: A one mile loop trail takes visitors around a lake that used to be a mill pond.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Carlisle Lake

properties.description: A couple miles beyond Lake Stuart and a few hundred feet up lies Horseshoe Lake--a stunning, silent lake that makes for an excellent day trip for those lucky folks who get to camp at Lake Stuart. It’s also attainable as a day hike, but you’ll want to get an early start.
properties.title: Horseshoe Lake

properties.description: This hike is along the road to Darland Mountain in the Ahtanum area. Along the way, you'll enjoy magnificent views and wildflower areas.
properties.title: Ahtanum State Forest - Eagle's Nest

properties.description: Leaving from the main parking lot in Longmire, hikers can travel a section of the Wonderland Trail to reach Reflections Lakes — passing by several viewpoints an a waterfall along the way.
properties.title: Longmire to Reflection Lakes

properties.description: Walk in a coastal forest south of Bellingham to enjoy scenic Wildcat Cove, with views into the San Juan Islands from the shoreline of Samish Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Larrabee State Park - Wildcat Cove

properties.description: An old trail on Wind Mountain winds through land owned by various agencies. Storm damage and lack of maintenance has made this trail increasingly difficult, and the various land agencies encourage hikers to visit other Columbia Gorge hikes as an alternative to Wind Mountain.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Wind Mountain

properties.description: Thanks to the generosity of the land owners, this privately-owned area is open to hikers, but managed primarily for wildlife habitat and wilderness conservation. Because of this, dogs and mountain biking are not allowed here, and the area may close at various times throughout the year in order to protect wildlife. Please respect any and all closures.
properties.title: Cashmere Canyons Preserve

properties.description: The western section of the Burnt Bridge Creek Trail follows the creek from Leverich Park to Fruit Valley Road. Stewart Glen is the highlight of this section of the trail.
properties.title: Burnt Bridge Creek - Western Section

properties.description: The Port Gamble Forest has a vast network of trails. This loop connects several of those trails together at the very northern tip of the trail network.
properties.title: Port Gamble Forest - Tessa's Trail Loop

properties.description: The mountainous views that once inspired beatnik poets continue to inspire modern-day hikers who take on this strenuous yet rewarding challenge.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Sourdough Mountain

properties.description: This section hike on one of Washington’s longest rail trails includes an impressive vantage point of the nearby Saddle Mountains on a pedestrian-only bridge over the Columbia River.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Beverly Bridge

properties.description: Hoh Lake is a quiet spot in the wilderness of Olympic National Park that is accessible via a steep ascent from the Hoh River Trail or a long approach on the High Divide Trail.
properties.title: Hoh Lake

properties.description: Above the banks of the South Fork Nooksack lies Pioneer Camp and the trailhead for the Elbow Lake Trail. Climb gently the first two miles through mature, mid-elevation forest to the Bell Pass Trail junction, a little used route to Mazama Park, or continue another mile to access the remote beauty of Elbow Lake. Large, ancient yellow cedars can be found on the north side of the lake as the trail continues to wind towards the Middle Fork Nooksack.
properties.title: Elbow Lake

properties.description: This diverse landscape of deep forested valleys and open ridges with beautiful meadows and breathtaking views will leave you hungry for more.
properties.title: Quartz Creek

properties.description: A scramble to a remote peak in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. Climbing experience and technical equipment recommended.
properties.title: Gray Peak

properties.description: This 119-mile section of the 1200-mile Pacific Northwest Trail traverses the entirety of the Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Pacific Northwest Trail - Pasayten Traverse

properties.description: Paradise Point State Park packs a lot into a small, often-overlooked park right along I-5.
properties.title: Paradise Point State Park

properties.description: Spend some time away from the sounds of the city without even needing to leave it on this nature loop.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Dupont Loop

properties.description: One of several short connector trails within the vast trail network of Riverside State Park.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Trail 214

properties.description: Mount Stuart is a popular climb in the Enchantments area of Washington State. Have gear and climbing expertise before you attempt this.
properties.title: Mount Stuart

properties.description: This remote perch in the Kettle Range grants hikers views of the Kettles and beyond.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Barnaby Buttes

properties.description: While Round Lake, tucked securely in a hidden basin on Lost Creek Ridge, is a wonderful locale, this hike is definitely more about the journey than the destination. After a demanding initial grunt, amble along a mile-high, flower-swaying, peak-packed, view-granting ridge. Savor one of the finest vantages for admiring spiraling Sloan Peak's sprawling sparkling glacier. And if you can ever move your eyes away from this mesmerizing mountain, a multitude of others demand your attention as well.
properties.title: Round Lake

properties.description: Lake Isabel is only accessible via bushwhack— hikers can expect to ford a deep and swift-flowing river, and then endure a steep uphill bushwhack to the lake.
properties.title: Lake Isabel

properties.description: Survey wetlands, working farms and Western-movie vistas on this 130-mile rail trail through Eastern Washington’s channeled scablands.
properties.title: Columbia Plateau Trail - Fish Lake

properties.description: This hike up to a former lookout site starts from Noble Knob trail's southern trailhead, and provides spectacular views of Mount Rainier and the surrounding landscape.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Noble Knob via Corral Pass

properties.description: Woods Creek is a 1.5 mile, compact gravel, wheelchair accessible trail that loops through five habitat areas. You can extend this hike, by taking the 1-mile side trail, Old Growth Loop #247A.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Woods Creek

properties.description: This trail can be short or long, depending on how much you want to hike and which trailhead you start from. Along the way, you will pass several quaint waterfalls and some spectacular views of the San Juan Islands and Chuckanut Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Interurban Trail

properties.description: Mount Rainier's Westside Road is closed in winter at the junction with Highway 706, leaving hikers and snowshoers with up to 12 miles of relatively flat and wide road with a gentle grade to enjoy.
properties.title: Westside Road

properties.description: The southeast section of the Timberline Trail can be very exposed and difficult to follow at times due to erosion, but it will reward you with beautiful views of the White River drainage and Mount Hood.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Timberline Trail - Gnarl Ridge Junction to Timberline Lodge

properties.description: A half-mile loop around a wetland in the City of Sammamish.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Illahee Lake Trail

properties.description: This seldom-used trail within Glacier Peak Wilderness leads through an old-growth forest with magnificent, large trees to the site of an old fire lookout build in the 1930s.
properties.title: Red Mountain Lookout

properties.description: This trail has a brutal elevation gain in a short time, but the views from the peak of Sulphur Mountain are worth the climb.
properties.title: Sulphur Mountain

properties.description: Hike a short, steep little-used trail deep within the Tigers. In winter, descend past ghostly leafless trees. In summer, appreciate areas of exuberant moss and greenery. And, with luck, you might have the trail all to yourself.
properties.title: Hidden Forest Trail

properties.description: A local favorite, McDonald Mountain offers great views from the summit and a good workout on the way there. But it borders the Green River Watershed, so please stay on trail to avoid accidentally entering the watershed, which is closed to the public.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: McDonald Mountain

properties.description: This urban park has it all! In a woodsy setting here, you'll find fitness challenge trails and activities for all ages and abilities.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wildwood Park

properties.description: This sweet, short little trail in the Klahowya Campground is a beautiful green-lined pathway, perfect for people camped nearby, or just on their way to adventures out of the Sol Duc trahilead.
properties.title: Pioneer's Path Nature

properties.description: Save yourself the sweat of a summit attempt and simply bask at the cool shores of this delightful little lake.
properties.title: Crescent Lake

properties.description: The trail to Skyscraper Pass makes an ideal dayhike to take you a little further from the popular visitor center at Sunrise, and the crowds that head to Dege Peak and the Burroughs. It's a bit longer, so you'll need to be ready for push. Particularly enthusiastic hikers can push onto Skyscraper Mountain via a bootpath.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Skyscraper Pass

properties.description: The Basin Creek Trail is one of two trails in the Pasayten Wilderness that climb east out of the Chewuch River Valley.  The benefits of this trail’s strenuous climb in the minimal shade are the expansive views from the shoulder of Topaz Mt. Beyond the views is the junction with the Windy Peak trail, with optional extensions to summit Windy Peak or continue past Windy Lake and go on to Horseshoe Basin.
properties.title: Basin Creek

properties.description: You'll enjoy moderate elevation gain and fabulous views on this lakeside trail that stretches more than 30 miles north -- nearly to Canada.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: East Bank Ross Lake

properties.description: Hiking through lowland forest rivers, the North Fork Skokomish Trail leads through the thick Olympic forest to subalpine meadows with unbelievable views of the heart of the craggy, snow-capped Olympic Range.
properties.title: North Fork Skokomish River

properties.description: Explore this Edmonds park, centered on the deep ravine of Shell Creek. Enjoy the surrounding second growth forest, with its tall red alder and fir trees. Observe spring wildflowers or, seasonally, fall colors. And appreciate the sounds of a multitude of bird calls.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Yost Park

properties.description: The McLaughlin Canyon Trail is a part of the Brigade Trail used by the Hudson's Bay Company in the early 1800's and became known as the Caribou Trail during the Gold Rush in the 1850's. Today it is an easy 3 mile round trip. There was a wildfire here in 2007, but wildflowers are just starting to take hold in this area, which makes it worth the trip in spring and summer.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: McLaughlin Canyon Trail

properties.description: Enjoy a quiet mile-long ramble among towering trees just outside of Port Orchard.
properties.title: Wynn-Jones Preserve

properties.description: This park sits at the northern tip of Dyes Inlet and just outside of the urban center of Silverdale. From the parking area a network of trails extends out through the forest.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Old Mill Park

properties.description: A collection of paved trails, dirt trails, and gravel roads provide easy access to a shrub steppe and riparian habitat along the Yakima River.
properties.title: Horn Rapids Park

properties.description: This short loop just off of Interstate 90 offers an easy escape to nature. With plenty to keep little ones occupied, and just enough mileage to give your legs a little workout, this is a delightful detour for anyone venturing west or east over Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Asahel Curtis Nature Trail

properties.description: This hike offers easy walking above the lakes and wetlands of Lower Crab Creek Coulee. You’ll have expansive views and a chance to see spring wildflowers and flocks of migrating waterbirds.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Crab Creek

properties.description: Take some easy to moderate trails along soft terrain in a forested area home to some wildlife, mostly birds. The trails weave in and out of each other, dividing into a maze of smaller trails as they lead to creeks.
properties.title: Salmon-Morgan Creeks Natural Area

properties.description: Known best for the high likelihood of seeing orcas from here, Lighthouse Marine Park also offers beach access, a boardwalk, camping, and picnic areas.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lighthouse Marine Park

properties.description: This seasonal snowshoe route to the shore of Baker Lake is dependent on the snow accumulation at the time of your trip. With the right amount of snow this becomes a 2-mile walk along a snowy road to the lake.
properties.title: Baker Lake - Horseshoe Cove Snowshoe

properties.description: The Big Rock Garden allows visitors to slow down and enjoy a bit of quiet solitude without having to trek far from home. The park features 37 permanent sculptures, over 100 species of maple and dozens of rhododendrons and azaleas which promise enjoyable walking at any time of year.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Big Rock Garden

properties.description: One of the largest petrified forests on the planet sits in the center of Washington State. The ancient trees were mineralized into rock during the great lava flows that swept the inland Northwest. In addition to petrified ginkgos (one of the oldest tree species in the world), the "rock forest" includes mineralized Douglas fir, spruce, walnut, and elm.
properties.title: Ginkgo Petrified Forest Interpretive Trails

properties.description: Visit McKenzie to take in the wild side of Newman Lake, where one can watch for moose in the shallows along the 3,000 feet of lakeshore, or possibly see an eagle nab a fish before returning to its nest in the nearby cottonwoods.  Mount Spokane and Ragged Ridge make the backdrop for this mellow loop trail system.
properties.title: McKenzie Conservation Area

properties.description: The Verlot Nature Trail connects the Verlot Campground with Turlo Campground.
properties.title: Verlot Nature Trail

properties.description: This is a long distance day hike that includes unmaintained trails. You should be an experienced route finder willing to hike trails less traveled, and prepared for a lonely hike. You may need crampons and ice axe.
properties.title: Rock Creek - Red Pass Loop

properties.description: A lush, green refuge with 6 miles of trails is the backyard playground for Western Washington University and Fairhaven College in Bellingham.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Sehome Arboretum

properties.description: The network of hiking trails offer longer rambles for adults as well as a short interactive loop for kids.
properties.title: South Kitsap Regional Park

properties.description: The summit of Freds Mountain is not on a formal trail.
properties.title: Freds Mountain

properties.description: The Cedar River Trail offers an urban river walk, a more rural river walk along a former rail bed, and a roadside bicycle path connecting the two. Bicycle the entire trail, or select one of many access points to explore the trail on foot.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cedar River Trail

properties.description: On the Washington-Idaho border sits Buffalo Eddy, a site where the Nez Perce left their mark a la petroglyphs carved into the rock next to the Snake River. A short trail with informative signage offers information about the petroglyphs and their creators.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Buffalo Eddy

properties.description: Visit a fragrance garden with a Braille trail and a small network of flat, wheelchair-friendly trails for a quiet outing close to town.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Tennant Lake and Hovander Homestead Trails

properties.description: An easy, year-round hike winds through forests and offers views of beaver ponds.
properties.title: Port Gamble Forest - Beaver Pond Trail

properties.description: Formerly known as the John Wayne Trail, this is a rail trail whose route crosses Washington, offering a nice short walk from a myriad of trailheads, or a fun, multi-day bikepacking adventure.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Ellensburg Trailhead

properties.description: An unconventional hike that starts downhill and finishes uphill, the Paul Peak Trail never climbs its namesake. Instead, it skirts the peak while providing a unique glimpse of Mount Rainier's northwest face.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Paul Peak

properties.description: Hike a beautiful, flat 5.8 mile walk (one way) in the woods along the White Chuck River. The trail has been cleared its entire length thanks to WTA trail crews.
properties.title: White Chuck Bench

properties.description: The Basin Lake Trail is located just east of the Crystal Mountain Ski Resort in the Norse Peak Wilderness. This is a little-used trail, which traverses some steep sections with eroding gullies where hikers may get queasy depending on their comfort level with exposure.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Basin Lake

properties.description: A summit outside of Darrington without an official trail system. The approach is on private property. Hikers are requested to respect this and stay on the road if you elect to visit it.
properties.title: Mount Higgins

properties.description: This is a gem of a hike, providing you easy access to the best of the best of the rich L. T. Murray State Wildlife Recreation Area.
properties.title: Robinson Canyon - Ainsley Canyon

properties.description: An easy route with a challenging finish, the main trail through Gazzam Lake Nature Preserve meanders through second-growth forest on Bainbridge Island, plunging down its finish at a small, scenic section of rocky beach.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Gazzam Lake Nature Preserve

properties.description: This moderately difficult trail accesses the William O. Douglas wilderness area. Passing through dense timber near Flat Iron Lake, the way also hosts good campsites for visitors
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Soda Springs

properties.description: This beautiful meadow is visible from a variety of logging roads that surround it. Visitors are asked to not walk in the meadow, as it is a protected research area and a fragile ecosystem.
properties.title: Camas Meadows

properties.description: Explore a beautiful state park near the Skagit River with an extensive trail network and beautiful campsites.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Rasar State Park

properties.description: Take a thru-hike among some of the I-90 corridor's most iconic lakes. Make it a day hike, an overnight, or take as much time as you like and really explore the area.
properties.title: Melakwa - Pratt Lake Traverse

properties.description: A short trail between Multnomah Falls and Wahkeena Falls that makes a loop trail possible between the two.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Return Trail

properties.description: This short and sweet loop hike offers a wonderful little retreat into nature within the city of Snoqualmie. There are plenty of opportunities to spot some waterfowl as you pass the multiple retention ponds along the way.  Listen to croaking frogs as you pass by wetland areas and even some old growth trees.
properties.title: Snoqualmie Ridge Trail Network - Deer Park Trail

properties.description: Take a short, rugged trek to a forested summit. Along the way, you'll enjoy beargrass in spring, get some good views of the Silver Star Scenic Area, but the best thing about this hike is the workout.
properties.title: Larch Mountain (Silver Star)

properties.description: This trail offers vistas of the Okanogan River and Pasayten Wilderness as well as wildlife viewing potential for hikers of all experience levels.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Whistler Canyon Trail

properties.description: This beautiful falls close to the road in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest is just the ticket for folks with young children or waterfall hunters.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Iron Creek Falls

properties.description: Enjoy a steep trail to a summit east of Lake Whatcom with gorgeous views of Puget Sound and the surrounding mountains.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lake Whatcom Park - Chanterelle Trail

properties.description: Walk along a noisy East Cascades creek through big woods, early or late in the season.
properties.title: North Fork Taneum to Fishhook Flat Trail

properties.description: This short connector trail, maintained by WTA, links Max's Shortcut trail to BL-1616 on Blanchard Mountain.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Acorn Trail

properties.description: A little history, a little wildlife, a little botany -- it's all here in this quiet little wetland right off a main road in Federal Way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: West Hylebos Wetlands

properties.description: Hike this unmaintained trail on the dry side of the Cascades. It's a scenic, wildflower wonderland, if you're willing and able to route-find your way to the ridge.
properties.title: Magnet Creek

properties.description: Although best known for its namesake mine and the nearby aircraft wreckage, the Tubal Cain trail also offers a pleasant and scenic route to Marmot Pass, a gateway to further wanderings.
properties.title: Tubal Cain Mine to Buckhorn Lake

properties.description: If you don’t mind descending first, then ascending later, the Sultan River Canyon trail is a nice alternative for the shoulder season when snow is still too deep in the mountains. Drop to the sparkling Sultan River, then climb back up on nicely graded switchbacks in the shade.
properties.title: Sultan River Canyon Trail

properties.description: This small waterfall is just off highway 410, and is visible from the highway, but a paved path is available for those wishing to get a closer look.
properties.title: Horsetail Falls

properties.description: Just west of the town of Leavenworth, the Tumwater Pipeline Trail offers a lovely riverside ramble at any time of year. Enjoy the high waters and flowers blooming in spring, photograph vivid color in fall, and try out your snowshoes in winter. Whatever the season, this is a beautiful, short walk for those looking for something easy and quick.
properties.title: Tumwater Pipeline Trail

properties.description: Follow the Pacific Crest Trail along a lightly used section in the forests south of Snoqualmie Pass, enjoy views, old growth forest, and in season, great huckleberries.
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) - Stampede Pass to Tacoma Pass

properties.description: This hike is a tree hugger's paradise. Huge old growth Douglas firs and hemlocks soar into the sky from a lush green forest floor dotted with woodland flowers. The trail gently ascends only 700 feet in the first four miles, and the slope you hike up is laced by many clear flowing streams bridged by old puncheons.
properties.title: North Fork Skykomish River

properties.description: Follow this steep, to-the-point trail over a river to the top of an old cinder cone volcano.
properties.title: Lava Butte

properties.description: Berthusen Park offers up plenty of great opportunities to get outdoors and explore. This beautiful park, the site of a homestead from the late 1800s, has antique farm machinery, a historical cabin, a big red barn and a great playground with a wonderful swing set for kids.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Berthusen Park

properties.description: Burroughs Mountain can be described as a "mountain against a mountain." At over 7,800 feet, Burroughs Mountain sets right up against the northeastern face of Mount Rainier, hugging the Winthrop Glacier. It offers one of the most dramatic views of Washington's largest volcano.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Burroughs Mountain

properties.description: On the edge of the Columbia River, right before Highway 97 crosses into Oregon is Maryhill State Park. Nestled at the foot of rolling hills and on the shores of the Columbia River, the park is a wonderful place for campers and road trippers.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Maryhill State Park and Stonehenge Memorial

properties.description: Get a good workout on this trail that climbs to a summit with views of the south Cascade range. Continue on to make it a longer hike, continuing down into deep forest to the south trailhead.
properties.title: Monte Carlo

properties.description: Grace Cole Nature Park, located in the community of Lake Forest Park, is a real gem. It occupies only 15 acres, but offers a close-up view of ponds and wetlands at the head of Brookside Creek, plus a half mile of trails that climb up 120 feet to loop over a forested hill. In season enjoy wildflowers, fall colors, and wildlife sightings.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Grace Cole Nature Park

properties.description: The expansive acreage of this park allows for a wide variety of activities, including hiking, biking, boating, fishing, swimming, bird and wildlife viewing, even lawn games such as horseshoes! The hiking trail is a lovely loop around Deep Lake.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Nolte State Park

properties.description: This hike just south of Anacortes offers superb views of the ocean and islands from a pair of high vantage points, and it has some fine trails through mixed forest along the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Sharpe Park - Sares Head

properties.description: The Fishtrap area is part of the Channeled Scablands of Eastern Washington. The deep coulees and canyons were carved by the Great Missoula Floods following the last Ice Age tens of thousands of years ago.
properties.title: Fishtrap Lake - North and South Loop

properties.description: This “shortcut” to the Enchantments Core Zone refers only to mileage. As far as miles per hour goes, Aasgard may be one of the slowest hikes you attempt. Achieving the pass is a thigh-burning, chest-bursting, eye-popping endeavor that offers as many extraordinary views as beads of sweat that will fall  from your brow as you ascend nearly 2,000 feet in just three-quarters of a mile.
properties.title: Aasgard Pass

properties.description: A scramble up the highest peak in the Goat Rocks. Class 3 at times, climbing experience and equipment required.
properties.title: Gilbert Peak

properties.description: The lesser known creek between Bean and Stafford, Standup offers a gentle valley followed by steepness to an open hillside and ridge with views. But this quiet hike is only accessible via a road only appropriate for high-clearance vehicles.
properties.title: Standup Creek

properties.description: This trail loops through the forest around Lake Swano just east of the Grays Harbor College campus. A short spur trail connects to the campus or you can pick up the trail along South Lewis Street.
properties.title: Lake Swano Trail

properties.description: North Kitsap Heritage Park is a small collection of trails supported locally through land trusts. Trails here range from steep to flat and go through sunny meadows and forests.
properties.title: North Kitsap Heritage Park

properties.description: This trail climbs steeply to reach an overlook with views of the San Juan Islands and beyond.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Baker Preserve

properties.description: Mount McCausland delivers mountain views, lake views, and even solitude at the summit. The cost? The first three miles of the trail is easy, but the last half mile to the summit is steep and occasionally brushy. Taking a break on that climb is no hardship, though: the hillside is carpeted in berries and the views start early.
properties.title: Mount McCausland

properties.description: There are many names for this short little hike. Mount Pete, Mount Peak, Pinnacle Peak Park, Cal Magnusson Trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mount Peak (Pinnacle Peak)

properties.description: Hike railroad grades dating from the logging era. Cross many small creeks, some seasonal. Pass tall trees draped with moss. Enjoy ferns and, in season, forest wildflowers and wild berries. Reach a viewpoint that's also a favorite launching spot for paragliders.
properties.title: Poo Poo Point

properties.description: The Milk Creek trail used to offer a gorgeous tour of the Glacier Peak wilderness via a 34.7-mile backpacking loop. Hikers followed the Milk Creek trail to the Pacific Crest Trail, then down to the Suiattle River Trail. Along the way it offered stunning close-up views of Glacier Peak, endless wildflower meadows and ample opportunities for solitude.  Unfortunately, it now requires a potentially dangerous ford of the Suiattle River due to a missing bridge. Because of its inaccessibility and a lack of maintenance, expect a brushy trail with blowdowns beyond this point.
properties.title: Milk Creek - Suiattle River Loop

properties.description: This trail follows the north fork of Asotin Creek before climbing to Pinkham Butte.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: North Fork Asotin Creek to Pinkham Butte

properties.description: This small park in Renton, named after a former park board member, is great for a summer afternoon outside.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Thomas Teasdale Park

properties.description: Skip the crowds of skiers and snowshoers at Hurricane Ridge and try a challenging hike on Obstruction Point Road.
properties.title: Obstruction Point Road Snowshoe

properties.description: A short trail leads to a spectacular view across the Pend Oreille River Canyon, where Peewee Falls plunges 233 feet into the Boundary Lake Reservoir. A nearby viewpoint overlooks Boundary Dam.
properties.title: Peewee Falls Overlook and Boundary Dam Overlook

properties.description: A small park in Snohomish County, Lake Roesiger offers a small network of hiking trails, fishing, picnicking opportunities, even a beach. Originally a homestead, where the settlers farmed and rented boats and cabins to visitors, Lake Roesiger now provides a nice way to spend the afternoon with the whole family.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Roesiger

properties.description: Whether you're looking for a winter training hike, or some Puget Sound views any time of year, this convenient trail will give you a good workout and some good scenery.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Alger Alp (North Route)

properties.description: Joe Watt Canyon is a quiet area of the L.T. Murray Wildlife Area that is a great place to spot fields of colorful lupine and the occasional elk heard.
properties.title: Joe Watt Canyon

properties.description: The Carbon River Rain Forest Nature Trail is a pleasant and easy stroll that offers two short segments which can be combined to create a 0.6 mile roundtrip walk. Both paths penetrate primeval rain forest where giant ferns, maples, and spruce tower above charming cedar puncheon bridges and babbling brooks. This hike is great in any season, and takes on particular wildness in winter. Interpretive signs and photo opportunities abound.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Carbon River Rain Forest Nature Trail

properties.description: This is more of a walk of about 200 yards, but the falls are beautiful when flowing heavily and well worth a visit when in the area.
properties.title: Rocky Brook Falls

properties.description: This is an easy walk on a wide gravel and boardwalk path to views of Big Four Mountain and the caves beneath the snow. Hikers of all ages and abilities can enjoy this trail.
properties.title: Big Four Ice Caves

properties.description: Thanks to a partnership between Washington State Parks and the Swinomish Indian Tribal Community, Kukutali Preserve in Similk Bay near La Conner opened to the public on June 16, 2014.  Believed to be the first park in the United States to be co-owned and managed by a tribe and another government, management of the area focuses on conservation and research, public education and limited recreational use — including hiking!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Kukutali Preserve

properties.description: Visit a wildlife-filled greenspace with a burgeoning trail system in West Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Puget Park - Seattle

properties.description: Featuring a wooded canyon and forested hills, a salmon-bearing stream and new community garden, Swan Creek Park is a 290-acre greenspace which lies on the boundary between East Tacoma and Pierce County. Trails, both paved and soft-surface, as well as those for mountain bikes weave over the property.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Swan Creek Park

properties.description: Nestled in the southeast corner of Mount St Helens, the Pine Creek Trail offers a short, easy graded path into second growth forest at the base of the active stratovolcano. You can visit a historic wood-shingled shelter built in the 1920s and continue on to a viewpoint along the Muddy River Lahar moonscape.
properties.title: Pine Creek

properties.description: Located in the Eaglemont neighborhood of Mount Vernon, this short little out and back gravel trail delivers visitors through wetlands and past beaver ponds.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Beaver Pond Trail

properties.description: Antoine Peak's Canfield Gulch is the east side access to this 1,296 acre conservation area.
properties.title: Antoine Peak Conservation Area - Canfield Gulch

properties.description: A steep and infrequently maintained trail to the summit of Little Grass Mountain.
properties.title: Roosevelt Trail to Little Grass Mountain

properties.description: Banshee Peak is an off-trail summit that requires advanced mountaineering skill to reach. It lies east of Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Banshee Peak

properties.description: Since getting to the trailhead involves a significant drive on gravel road, this hike sees fewer boots than trails leaving from Paradise and Sunrise. Spray Falls is attainable by most day hikers, but the gain up to Spray Park is a good test of your fitness level! Your reward on a clear day will be views, views, views of Echo Rock, Observation Rock and Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Spray Park

properties.description: Cascading 312 feet from Rainbow Creek high above the Stehekin valley floor, Rainbow Falls is perhaps the most popular natural destination for day visitors to the Stehekin Valley. And now, thanks to efforts from the National Park Service trail crew, a short trail exists here, offering a modest amount of elevation gain for a new vantage point of the waterfall.
properties.title: Rainbow Falls Mist Trail

properties.description: The Side Hustle trail is a mountain biker/hiker trail at East Tiger Mountain, with one end at an intersection with Preston RR Grade and East Tiger Summit, and the other end meeting with the Iverson RR Grade.
properties.title: Side Hustle

properties.description: This is a National Audubon Society registered Important Bird Area that encompasses a salt marsh, estuary, lagoon and small islands. It's a wonderful area for walking and enjoying the view from dikes, tide-levels permitting.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Deer Lagoon Nature Preserve

properties.description: Enjoy breathtaking views of the Olympics from a secluded cove with many different types of seabirds and wildlife. Try to keep your feet dry while exploring a series of trails amid the historic 184-acre Guillemot Cove Nature Reserve.
properties.title: Guillemot Cove

properties.description: The Collin Creek Trail is a part of a large network of trails in and around the Redmond Watershed Preserve.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Collin Creek Trail

properties.description: Hikers can reach Noble Knob, a former fire lookout with awesome views near Mount Rainier, via the trail's northern trailhead on Forest Road 7222.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Noble Knob via North Trailhead (FS 7222)

properties.description: Take a couple of ADA-accessible trails to some of the most scenic parts of Cape Disappointment State Park.
properties.title: Cape Disappointment State Park - North Head Lighthouse and Bell's Overlook

properties.description: This hike boasts a great combination of wetland and sea shore. It is doable by hikers of all ages, and most of the trail is wheelchair accessible.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Point Whitehorn Marine Reserve

properties.description: The Coyote Creek Trail runs north-south through the northern half of Cougar Mountain Regional Park.
properties.title: Coyote Creek

properties.description: The Kettle Crest Trail is the granddaddy of long-distance, high-country routes in Eastern Washington. Over the course of its 44 miles, it presents a virtual highlight reel of dry-side beauty, from sage-scented meadows to subalpine parkland.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Kettle Crest Trail

properties.description: Mount Pugh -- also known by its native name "Da Klagwats" -- has one of the most spectacular viewpoints in the North Cascades, offering a vista that includes Glacier and Sloan Peak, Mounts Baker, Shuksan, and Rainier, the Olympics, Monte Cristo, Three Fingers, and White Chuck. The first fire lookout here was established in 1916; a lowly tent perched on the peak until a cabin with a cupola was built in 1922. This was hit by lightning in 1927 and a second lookout was built, but it was subsequently destroyed in 1965 and never rebuilt. Remains of these structures can still be seen on the mountain, when you can tear yourself away from the view.
properties.title: Mount Pugh

properties.description: A smaller, less well known state park on Whidbey Island with gorgeous beach views and a shorter but diverse trail system through woods, grassy meadows, marsh and beach areas.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Joseph Whidbey State Park

properties.description: Explore forest trails along Piper's Creek and adjoining ridges. Visit a Puget Sound beach and enjoy great views across the Sound to the Olympics. In the fall, observe migrating salmon in the creek.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Carkeek Park

properties.description: While the trail near Gold Creek Pond is a great spot for hikers of all ages, the trail back towards Alaska Lake is a more rugged experience. Starting flat, it heads into the heart of the Central Cascades on an old road for four miles, where it then crosses an impressive old avalanche path before heading straight uphill to remote Alaska Lake.
properties.title: Gold Creek Trail to Alaska Lake

properties.description: Granny View Overlook might not be a hike that you’d drive to by itself, but you’d be a fool to pass by it.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Granny View Overlook (Oregon)

properties.description: Take this gentle trail to a beautiful alpine lake surrounded by rocky cliffs before heading up some steeper switchbacks to a pass and junction with the iconic Pacific Crest Trail.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cutthroat Pass via Cutthroat Lake

properties.description: For years, WTA has been coming to Cape Disappointment to work on trails in this area, including this trail, which leads hikers from the iconic North Head lighthouse down to the road that accesses the camping area and beaches at the south end of the park.
properties.title: Cape Disappointment State Park - North Head Trail

properties.description: This is a short hike to a beautiful two-tiered falls along Mosier Creek on the Oregon side of the Columbia River Gorge. Continue on to get up to a plateau where views of the Gorge await you.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Mosier Creek Falls and Mosier Plateau

properties.description: If you are looking for a moderately long amble without much likelihood of seeing others, look no further. The terrain is dry Ponderosa forest cut deeply by winter runoff. The scars of humankind’s usage are quite evident, but the balance of nature’s hand is slowly returning beauty to the area. The elevations are low making access easy early in the season or the potential for a winter outing.
properties.title: Red Hill

properties.description: Wander along this forested slope above Carey Creek in the southern portion of the Taylor Mountain Forest.
properties.title: Mountain Beaver Trail

properties.description: There are ten trails circling Anderson Lake, just eight miles south of Port Townsend. Bring the kids, the dog, your mountain bike, and even your horse, and mix and match the trails to your heart’s content to explore a little over eight miles of multiuse serene and shady forest trails.
properties.title: Anderson Lake State Park

properties.description: This is a quiet alternative to the busy trails in the state parks on Camano Island. The lake is not much more than a pond, but you can hear the bubbling of the small springs feeding into the wetland and listen for birdsong as you stroll along the path.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Four Springs Lake Preserve

properties.description: This moderate hike follows the Pacific Crest Trail south out of Snoqualmie Pass to lovely Olallie Meadow, a place to see native carnivorous sundew plants.
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) - Snoqualmie Pass to Olallie Meadow

properties.description: Spring, summer, and fall all beckon hikers up the slopes of Delancy Ridge toward Driveway Butte, attracted by the views, seasonal flowers, or just a hard workout. The trail tells the tale to two forests, a mature pine forest in the first half and a forest recovering from fire in the second.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Driveway Butte

properties.description: Instead of skipping the crowds, let the crowd skip by you as you enjoy swimming, fishing or just relaxing at these less popular lakes just south of White Pass.
properties.title: Ginnette Lake

properties.description: A nice forested stroll, with views of a small creek, and the valley below.
properties.title: Verne Samuelson Trail

properties.description: At first glance, this small neighborhood park may not seem to have any trails -- the playground and picnic tables are most prominent, as is the off-leash dog park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: North Shorewood Park

properties.description: Take a hike on the edge of Spokane Valley with commanding views of Spokane Valley and the Palouse. On the way, you'll see many plant species typical of western slopes of Cascades, a seasonal stream, and amazing variety of wildflowers through from late March through mid-July.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Conservation Area - Iller Creek

properties.description: A segment of the Columbia Plateau Trail passes through a former railroad tunnel and along an ice age coulee, past the dried basin of what was once Lake Kahlotus.
properties.title: Columbia Plateau Trail - Washtucna Coulee

properties.description: While commonly used to access the Alpine Lakes backcountry, the trail up to Cathedral Pass is a worthy destination on its own. Old growth forest, lakes, subalpine meadows, and an up-close view of the dominating Cathedral Rock make for a satisfying and scenic day hike or short overnight.
properties.title: Cathedral Rock

properties.description: Take an short and simple walk for a couple of miles up the West Fork Methow River valley, enjoying the sounds of the river along with spring flowers from mid-May to mid-June. Or in late season, take a hike in the early snow, before the road is closed.
properties.title: West Fork Methow River

properties.description: A short trail connecting trails 120 and 122 to make larger loops accessed near the main entrance of Mount Spokane State Park.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 121

properties.description: This short trail descends 200 feet to the base of a large 45-foot waterfall.
properties.title: North Fork Sauk Falls

properties.description: Descend into the heart of the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness from the historic Godman Guard Station, crossing through the Rainbow Creek Research Natural Area.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: West Butte Creek

properties.description: Check the weather before heading out for this hike, and if it’s going to be clear, bring a camera. From the summit, it’s possible to see six (yes, six!) volcanoes spanning two states. Baker, Glacier, Adams, Rainier, St. Helens and Hood wait patiently for you to climb the more-than-moderately steep path to the summit of Crystal Peak, where you can take in beautiful snow-capped majesty from the top.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Crystal Peak

properties.description: Enjoy a gentle walk through shaded forest, often within sight and/or sound of the White River. Skookum Falls can be your destination for a 4.6-mile round trip, or use the south trailhead to choose segments of the 8.5-mile trail (one-way) to hike, bike or run. It’s all good.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Skookum Flats

properties.description: Horse Lake Reserve is a 1,500-acre reserve located just west of Wenatchee, open to the public from April 1 through November 31.
properties.title: Horse Lake Reserve

properties.description: This trail at the Evergreen State College leads to the college’s organic farm. Take a short hike through the forest to the small-scale organic farm.
properties.title: Evergreen State College - Organic Farm Trail

properties.description: Experience the Pacific Crest Trail at its finest. This backpacking trip takes you across four passes to two lovely alpine lakes in the shadow of Golden Horn, Tower Mountain and Mount Hardy.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Golden Horn - Snowy Lakes

properties.description: With wildflowers at your feet, wander among old-growth giants on this off-the-beaten-path trail on the southeastern side of the Olympics.
properties.title: Church Creek

properties.description: This is a pleasant hike to a small lake and a notched gap with sweeping views. Sheep Lake is nestled in a subalpine area that explodes with wildflowers in July and August. The lake is a good place to relax and enjoy nature or perhaps take off your boots and go wading. Sourdough Gap is a small saddle in a rocky-edged ridge. The hike from the lake to the gap offers increasingly picturesque views of the south Cascades with every foot of altitude you gain. Once at the gap, you will be rewarded with grand views of Sheep Lake on one side and the Crystal Lakes basin on the other side.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Sheep Lake to Sourdough Gap

properties.description: Whether you're looking for a loop or an out-and-back, Swauk Meadows offers an ideal outing just south of Blewett Pass.
properties.title: Swauk Meadows Snowshoe

properties.description: Follow the trails here to views of Mount Rainier's rocky Nisqually River valley and the much-receded Nisqually Glacier.
properties.title: Nisqually Vista Loop

properties.description: Table Mountain trail offers a variety of nice views, and opportunities to get away from the parking lot crowds at Artist Point. But heed the cautions before you set out.
properties.title: Table Mountain

properties.description: This rugged hike is bound to become a classic, if it isn’t already. The full trail loop provides fantastic views of the Columbia River Gorge, an intimate look at the Cape Horn Falls and a challenging workout as it climbs and descends the rocky slopes of Cape Horn.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Cape Horn

properties.description: Hike along the abandoned Bellingham & Skagit Interurban Railway grade between Fairhaven and Bellingham, which has been reclaimed as pedestrian trail. The gentle grade makes it a good option for new hikers, and excellent views of Bellingham Bay make for great trailside distractions.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: South Bay Trail

properties.description: A semi-urban multi-use trail running between Tukwila and South Park along the Duwamish River.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Green River Trail

properties.description: This small waterfront park in Kenmore has multiple boardwalks and viewing platforms.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: ƛ̕ax̌ʷadis (Tl' awh-ah-dees) Park

properties.description: Cheney Tertiary Wetlands serves as both the third and final enhancement of the Cheney Wastewater Treatment and Reclamation Facility, and also as a looped trail system just outside the city of Cheney.
properties.title: Cheney Tertiary Wetlands

properties.description: Greenbank Farm was saved from becoming a housing community by partnerships with local land officials and the Trust for Public Land.   Thanks to protection from Island County and the Nature Conservancy, hikers can explore the many trails that web the more than 500 acres of fields that surround the expansive property of Greenbank.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Greenbank Farm

properties.description: Visit beautiful Black Lake on your way to Ashnola Pass and the Boundary trail. Enjoy views of peaks and plenty of wildflowers as you make your way through this 2003 burn zone.
properties.title: Lake Creek

properties.description: This informal trail off the historic Columbia River Highway is popular in spring for the flowers. But be prepared for your visit — the route winds between parcels of private land, has very limited parking, and is extremely popular on weekends. Do your research and be prepared with a backup location.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Memaloose Hills

properties.description: Tatoosh Ridge offers numerous choices, all involving a steep approach. Contentedly amble through a steep slope of wildflowers, with occasional mountain views. Drop into a valley with a pair of alpine lakes, or climb to the site of a former lookout. If you like, do all of the above.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Tatoosh Ridge

properties.description: This 1.1-mile trail parallels Hardy Creek as one segment of the Hamilton Mountain loop. It is high up the ridge above the creek, traversing red alder and Douglas-fir forests.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Hardy Creek

properties.description: Three miles of easy hiking on Whitepine Creek trail leads you to Wildhorse Creek Trail. 6.5 on the Wildhorse Creek trail takes you due south to Frosty Pass, Icicle Ridge Trail, and Frosty Creek Trail. It accesses Lake Grace, Big Chiwaukum, Snowgrass Mountain and Doelle Lakes through wide open high country.
properties.title: Frosty - Wildhorse Creek

properties.description: A set of short trails off Highway 119 between Hoodsport and Lake Cushman. With a trailhead kitted out with picnic tables and a restroom, it's a great spot for a picnic, too!
properties.title: Hoodsport Trail

properties.description: This valley trail in the forest gradually climbs 5 miles to a junction with a side trail to nearby Silver Lake.  Beyond the junction, the main trail climbs 3 more miles through alpine meadows and forest to views at Eagle Pass.
properties.title: Eagle Creek

properties.description: Come enjoy a short loop trail through second-growth woods with meadowland views. This is a wonderful, low-key bird watching area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Dragonfly Loop

properties.description: Aptly named, find excellent views of Seattle from this connector trail on Tiger Mountain.
properties.title: Seattle View Trail

properties.description: This multi-use trail travels through a greenbelt in the Kent East Hill area, meandering over gentle hills through forests and wetlands. A year-round escape without the drive.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Soos Creek Trail

properties.description: Be prepared for a real spring workout to reach Elbow Peak and its grand vista of peaks in the central and south Cascades. Along the way, be sure to stop and view the multitude of flowers.
properties.title: Elbow Peak

properties.description: By far the most difficult stretch of PCT in Washington, Section K puts hikers through a grueling 127-mile trek over harsh terrain and treacherous conditions. Yet those intrepid enough to attempt it are rewarded with a true wilderness experience in and among some of the country's most pristine and beautiful surroundings.
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) Section K - Stevens Pass to Rainy Pass

properties.description: An easy, mostly paved hike along the saltwater, with plenty of chances to see wildlife.
properties.title: Port Angeles Waterfront Trail

properties.description: A quiet, infrequently-visited trail in the Eagle Creek Campground. It hasn't seen maintenance in a while, so you may need to do some routefinding, but you'll likely be the only one there.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Buck Point

properties.description: The Phillips Creek trailhead and Flying L Trail provide eastside access to the Glenrose Unit of the Dishman Hills Conservation Area from the Spokane Valley.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Conservation Area - Flying L Trail

properties.description: A good, short destination just outside of the main Paradise visitors area, Myrtle Falls is a beauty.
properties.title: Myrtle Falls

properties.description: This loop connecting Trails 120, 121 and 122 at Mount Spokane State Park is short and sweet, with enough elevation gain to make it a bit spicy, too!
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Entrance Loop

properties.description: Merritt Lake is nestled under Nason Ridge a dozen miles east of Stevens Pass. This is just far enough from the crest to leave west side clouds behind. This hike is an under-appreciated one in the Stevens Pass area, so you may be lucky enough to enjoy a relatively uncrowded hike.
properties.title: Merritt Lake and Lost Lake

properties.description: Explore one of the few true backcountry experiences in Central Washington’s channeled scablands among buttes and mesas carved by ice age floods.
properties.title: Lake Creek

properties.description: The Taylor River Connector is a short connector trail that leads from the Middle Fork River parking area to the vehicle bridge over the Taylor River. Cross this bridge and walk a few feet down the road to access the Garfield Ledges trailhead.
properties.title: Taylor River Connector

properties.description: A scramble up to a peak just off the Alki Crest Trail in Mount Rainier National Park. Climbing experience and equipment strongly recommended.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Florence Peak

properties.description: Hike a shrub steppe slope to a high vantage point along the crest of the Horse Heaven Hills plateau. The trail is typically dry and windy so make sure to bring plenty of water. The best time to hike is in April or early May when the slope is green and wildflowers are blooming.
properties.title: Horse Heaven Hills

properties.description: A snowshoe outside of Longmire at Mount Rainer.
properties.title: Eagle and Chutla Peaks Trail Snowshoe

properties.description: When road conditions allow, take a short hike up Mission Peak for expansive views west into the Cascades and east to Wenatchee and beyond.
properties.title: Mission Peak

properties.description: Just a few miles west of Eatonville, off Highway 7, is Washington's newest state park. Created thanks to a partnership between the Nisqually Tribe, Washington State Parks and other local agencies, the park provides 1,300 acres of forest, prairie and riverside trails to recreate in.
properties.title: Nisqually State Park

properties.description: This gem of a lake is hidden deep in forest in the southeastern side of the Olympic Peninsula.  A full loop around the lake takes you through old growth forests, past waterfalls and through a marsh, and then back up above the lake for a few peek-a-boo views of the mountains.
properties.title: Spider Lake

properties.description: Follow in the footsteps of the intrepid Press Expedition while enjoying the natural beauty, local history and wildlife along the Olympic Peninsula’s Elwha River.
properties.title: Elwha River and Geyser Valley

properties.description: The Marcus trail starts about 18 miles east of the town of Republic in the Colville National Forest. Starting out for the first 1.5 miles on an old road, this trail gradually climbs until meeting up with the Kettle Crest Trail.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Marcus Trail

properties.description: Hiking from Longmire to Indian Henry's Hunting Ground offers a beautiful tour of various environments contained within the park, not to mention stellar views of the surrounding mountains, and a healthy dose of history to boot.
properties.title: Indian Henry's Hunting Ground via Longmire

properties.description: Designed for cross-country skiing, Echo Ridge also offers routes for mountain biking, family hiking, and horse use. Recreation enthusiasts are greeted with a variety of loop trails with spectacular views of Lake Chelan, the Enchantments, Pyramid Peak and Okanogan Highlands.
properties.title: Echo Ridge

properties.description: Due to vandalism to this native peoples' spiritual center in the 1990s, Washington State Parks closed the pictograph and petroglyph area to public entry. Access is now by guided tour only. Reservations are required; contact Columbia Hills State Park.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: She-Who-Watches

properties.description: A paved urban trail along the Highway 16 corridor named for a long time Tacoma planner and bicycle advocate.  The jewel of this walk is access to the Tacoma Narrows and views from the bridge.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Scott Pierson Trail

properties.description: Although the lookout tower has been deconstructed, the hike up Big Butte offers spectacular vistas of the Umatilla National Forest.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Big Butte Lookout

properties.description: A small river access point on the Middle Fork River Road. No official trails have been built here yet, but river access is just a few feet over an embankment. It's a bit of a climb, so not a great access point for folks who might be having mobility challenges.
properties.title: Russian Butte View Day Use Area

properties.description: Discover a pleasant alpine lake alternative to nearby, crowded Lake Ingalls. Tranquil Lake Ann can't boast the same dramatic view of jagged Mount Stuart, but it has its fair share of scenery, especially during fall when the larches around it turn to gold.
properties.title: Lake Ann

properties.description: An oxbow lake near the Snoqualmie River provides bird habitat and a little bit of wandering.
properties.title: Crescent Lake

properties.description: Porter Point Loop offers tremendous views of Willapa Bay from the ridge above and the estuary-lined trail below, with incredible birdwatching opportunities.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Porter Point Loop

properties.description: With the washout of the Olympic Hot Springs road, the Elwha Valley past the Madison Falls trailhead is now only accessible to hikers (and especially adventurous bicyclists). The Glines Canyon Overlook provides a great stopping spot for day hikers, or backpackers can continue the full 10.8 miles to the national park boundary.
properties.title: Elwha - Olympic Hot Springs Road

properties.description: Private property surrounds the parcels of public property in Wallula Gap, rendering them inaccessible to hikers.
properties.title: Wallula Gap Overlook

properties.description: A wildflower-dotted, easy trail near the Lightning Creek campground in the Methow.
properties.title: Pipestone Ridge Lower Coulee

properties.description: A refreshing hike through shady forest along one of the rivers that lends its name to the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Tucannon River Canyon

properties.description: Big Rock South is the newest and final addition to Big Rock Park. A half-mile, WTA-built trail connects Big Rock Central to SE 20th Street, but there are several other trails to explore through this area, and even more in neighboring Big Rock Park Central.
properties.title: Big Rock Park - South

properties.description: The Emerald Necklace trail from Trentwood is one of Spokane's newest trails, built with the help of WTA volunteers and the Evergreen Mountain Bike Alliance's eastern chapter.
properties.title: Antoine Peak Conservation Area - Emerald Necklace

properties.description: While snow still coats the high places of the Methow Valley, the hike to Black Lake offers early-season wildflowers amidst the recovery from a devastating 2003 wildfire.
properties.title: Black Lake

properties.description: Hike all the way around the Phantom Lake area, nestled in between Bellevue's Weowna Park and the main section of Lake Hills Greenbelt Park. Enjoy expansive views across the lake from both the western end and eastern end. Much of the hiking path is bordered by trees that give the illusion of a more rural setting.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Phantom Lake Loop

properties.description: Hike an easy loop trail through a wide forested buffer zone around this lowland lake. Appreciate the many tall trees that give the illusion of being in a much more remote location, and enjoy the view from a dock from which the entire lake can be seen. In season, see a variety of waterfowl.
properties.title: Yellow Lake

properties.description: Zigzag through Roslyn Urban Forest and up to a ridge overlooking the Yakima River Basin, with views extending as far as the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
properties.title: Roslyn Urban Forest - Ewok Trail

properties.description: Take a beautifully constructed boardwalk a little more than three miles out to the wild Olympic Coast. If you can snag a permit, camping here is divine. If not, while away a few hours playing in the water or ambling along the beach.
properties.title: Cape Alava

properties.description: Visit one of the most striking lakes in the Henry M. Jackson wilderness. The vibrant blue of the glacier-fed lake provides the perfect rest stop for hikers who have braved the thirty-odd, steep switchbacks that lead to the lake.
properties.title: Blanca Lake

properties.description: A short connector trail to the Snipes Mountain trail and other adventures on the southern flanks of Mount Adams.
properties.title: Snipes Mountain - Pine Way

properties.description: The Squibbs Creek Trail is part of the City of Bellevue’s Parks and Open Trails System. Take a walk through the old growth trees in the Horizon Heights Open Space.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Squibbs Creek

properties.description: This county park consists of 40 acres of old homestead land in Marblemount. The park is for day use only and includes a picnic shelter, fishing and hiking trails.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Pressentin Park

properties.description: If hikers are interested in this relatively quiet portion of Snohomish County, but not up for the lengthy treks of Boulder or Grieder Lakes, then Reflection Ponds might be the right hike for you! The trail crosses multiple drainages, including Bear Creek, which offers striking views of Spada Lake. Ultimately, the trail highlights a serene loop between the two Reflection Ponds.
properties.title: Reflection Ponds via Greider and Boulder Lakes Trail

properties.description: This short trail descends from the Chewuch Trailhead to connect with the much longer Chewuch Trail.
properties.title: Cathedral Driveway

properties.description: Hike through the relatively uncrowded southeast corner of a park in Seattle. Head up to the South Meadow for the views, then go down to the beaches and get up close to the West Point Lighthouse. Come back up to the park highlands for a close look at old buildings in the Fort Lawton Historic District.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Discovery Park Beach and Highlands Loop
