properties.description: From Bean Creek Basin, a combination of boot trail and scramble lead to the high point 6743, known as Bean Peak.  The 360 degree views provide a great perspective for the peaks of the Teanaway and to the north, the Stuart Range.
properties.title: Bean Peak

properties.description: Take a stroll through 350 acres of undisturbed old-growth forest and thriving wetland ecosystem at the Stimpson Family Nature Reserve, a quiet place where hikers can experience the intricate grandeur of nature. Interpretive signs encourage adults and children to discover the nature of the reserve.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Stimpson Nature Reserve

properties.description: A connector trail that shoots off the Miner's Ridge trail, this 3.5-mile, relatively flat route connects Miner's Ridge to the Pacific Crest Trail.
properties.title: Miners Cabin

properties.description: In spring and early summer, enjoy abundant wildflowers and views of the Stuart Range on these multi-use trails east of the Cascades.
properties.title: Iron Bear - Teanaway Ridge

properties.description: Packer Creek is a non-contiguous part of the BLM’s Rock Creek Recreation Site that's a boon for birdwatchers and lovers of wildflowers.
properties.title: Packer Creek

properties.description: A number of moderate snowshoe trails lie around the Lake Wenatchee area, but with a big, beautiful Ponderosa pine tree and views of the surrounding mountains, Nason Ridge gives you the best bang for your buck.
properties.title: Nason Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: A barrier-free, paved hike of less than one mile from the Johnston Ridge Observatory. The trail includes interpretive kiosks and 360-degree views of Mount St. Helens and the surrounding blast zone.
properties.title: Eruption Trail

properties.description: North Mountain is home to a network of mountain bike trails which can be accessed at many points along the North Mountain road, but the lookout tower is a destination in itself.
properties.title: North Mountain Lookout

properties.description: Hike easy forest trails connecting two adjoining urban parks. Appreciate the tall deciduous trees and some large conifers, plus ferns and small creeks. In season, look for forest wildflowers. Try to identify some of the wild birds, and enjoy the antics of the squirrels that always are present.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Tam O'Shanter - Viewpoint Open Space Trails

properties.description: One of many Dry Creek trails in Washington State, this calf-burner located in the Cowlitz River drainage below White Pass zigzags you through young forest to the abandoned Smith Point fire lookout site and views of the surrounding mountains.  If you are lucky you may even be able to spot Tahoma (Mount Rainier) on the horizon with a clear day!
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Dry Creek

properties.description: Not traveled by the masses, the Meadow Creek trail provides plenty of solitude as you gently climb through old burn and old growth to heather slopes, blueberry patches, and snow-fed lakes near the Cascade Crest.
properties.title: Fortune Ponds

properties.description: Hike through some great second-growth forest to reach the second-highest summit in the Tigers. Then enjoy a superb viewpoint a short distance west of the summit.
properties.title: West Tiger No. 1 via Fred's Corner

properties.description: Snowshoe up 1,800 feet to the expansive views from Diamond Head, the highpoint south of the Blewett Pass Sno-Park. The route includes a road walk, marked ski trail and cross-country climb with a great view pay-off.
properties.title: Diamond Head  Snowshoe

properties.description: Take a short hike up to these lakes in the Stevens Pass Ski Area.
properties.title: Grace Lakes (Stevens Pass)

properties.description: If you want to see the headwaters of the mighty Snoqualmie River, head for the source. Source Lake, that is. It's a modest pond, but the setting is remarkable. Craggy peaks ring this pool, found along the way to one of the state's most popular alpine lake -- Snow Lake.
properties.title: Source Lake

properties.description: This short, family-friendly trail with numerous add-on options visits a pretty lake basin at the easternmost edge of the North Cascades and provides long-distance views of some of Washington's loneliest country.
properties.title: Tiffany Lake

properties.description: This is one of several hikeable sections of the old, original Columbia River Highway that spanned the Oregon side of the Gorge. After years of disuse as a highway, this paved trail is slowly being restored so hikers and cyclists can enjoy it.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Historic Columbia River Highway State Trail - Mitchell Point

properties.description: Right on the Pacific Ocean, Grayland Beach State Park offers visitors easy access to miles of sandy beach via their choice of multiple small trails.
properties.title: Grayland Beach State Park

properties.description: Start out from the Touchet Corral Sno-park in the Umatilla National Forest. The first section is on singletrack trail, but the way quickly transitions to an old roadbed and stays like this until it ends at the intersection with Kendall Skyline Road.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Middle Tie Trail

properties.description: This is a short connector trail between Bear Ridge and Shangri-La trails, allowing hikers to create many loops on Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Surprise Creek

properties.description: A short, family-friendly loop that can be done all year round. You'll meander through douglas fir, western redcedar, bigleaf maple, and other deciduous trees, along a creek, and end at a lovely waterfall, perfect for picnicking.
properties.title: Buck Creek Falls Loop

properties.description: The Stettatle Creek Trail is an infrequently-used path that delivers hikers into a deep canyon in the heart of the North Cascades. Though it clears early in the season, this may not be the best option for those looking for an easy walk -- the trail is rugged and requires scrambling in places.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Stetattle Creek

properties.description: The most prominent peak in the Blue mountains, the views from the trailhead are great, and just get better as hikers approach the Oregon Butte Lookout as the full expanse of the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness unfolds before them in a 360 degree radius.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Oregon Butte

properties.description: With an interesting history, this path wanders through the old Kettle Falls townsite and makes a good choice for a late fall or winter walk.
properties.title: Old Kettle Falls Trail

properties.description: Stagman Ridge is a long spine reaching out southwest from Mount Adams, and the hike through the pleasing forest is never overly steep.
properties.title: Stagman Ridge - The Bumper

properties.description: Hike a 7.5-mile loop from Horseshoe Lake Campground with a side trip to views of South Cascade peaks from the summit of Green Mountain.
properties.title: Spring Creek - Green Mountain

properties.description: The Toutle Trail transects five ecozones over more than 13 miles, but can be done in three sections.
properties.title: Toutle Trail

properties.description: The Westport Light Trail, also known to locals as "The Dunes Trail" is about 1 paved mile dotted with many commemorative stone benches.
properties.title: Westport State Park - Westport Light Trail

properties.description: The trail up Clearwest Peak is inaccessible due to West Fork/Martin Gap Road (FR 74) being closed from a washout in 2007.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Clearwest Peak

properties.description: Enjoy birdwatching opportunities in coastal, marsh and forested environments while exploring the refuge’s three miles of looping trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: George C Reifel Migratory Bird Sanctuary

properties.description: While nearby higher elevations are still covered in snow, the 9.6-mile Huffman Peak Trail connects the lower Siouxon Creek Trail to FR 6403 and provides access to Huffman and Siouxon Peaks. This route once held two fire lookouts and continues to offer standout views of Swift Reservoir to the north, four stratovolcanoes and nearby Mount Mitchell.
properties.title: Huffman Peak

properties.description: Despite the name, Mount Misery trail offers a delightful hike to the Oregon Butte Lookout, situated on a hilltop in the remote Blue Mountains.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Mount Misery

properties.description: A fine little park with beach access, camping, a boat launch and trails. A popular park in the summer, this is a great place for a quiet off-season hike. On this loop trail, there are views, a forest walk, birding and beachcombing.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Camano Island State Park

properties.description: Banner Forest Heritage Park is one square mile of undeveloped forest and wetland on the Kitsap Peninsula with an extensive trail network. An easy grade and well maintained trails invite all ages and abilities to enjoy this prime section of land.
properties.title: Banner Forest

properties.description: What better way to experience the Glacier Peak Wilderness than by hiking round-the-mountain from old-growth glacier valleys to airy alpine ridgelines? This classic volcanic circumnavigation serves up the miles and elevation gain and is best given at least 5-10 days to complete without accounting for side explorations and bad weather.
properties.title: Glacier Peak Circumnavigation

properties.description: This unique, low-elevation hike follows the North Fork Nooksack River to spectacular scenery near the base of Mount Shuksan. This is a great late summer or early fall hike when Ruth Creek is low enough to ford. Keep in mind the limited maintenance this trail sees -- you may be in for a brushbash.
properties.title: Nooksack Cirque

properties.description: The Gatton Creek Trail is a short but delightful segment of the larger Quinault National Recreation Trail System. The well-maintained trail gets hikers close to nature as it travels beneath towering conifers through a lush rainforest ecosystem. As either a short stroll or part of a longer journey, this trail is well worth exploring.
properties.title: Gatton Creek

properties.description: An almost-completely-forgotten nature loop near Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument. You won’t see the mountain here, but two giant trees remain from time gone by, and are impressive enough for a visit if you’re in the area.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Quartz Creek Big Trees

properties.description: Follow the Diablo Lake Trail up and across talus slopes on the flanks of Sourdough Mountain to impressive cascading waterfalls and stunning views of Ross Lake and Colonial, Pyramid, Davis Peaks, as well as Jack Mountain.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Diablo Lake

properties.description: Great views await you at the summit of Bald Mountain or Cutthroat Lakes if you can stand the rough, rocky, and rooty trail that you must brave to get there. Fortunately, lots of lakes and berries keep you busy along the way, and the ever-changing surroundings on this CCC-built, WTA-maintained trail make for a great day hike along the popular Mountain Loop Highway.
properties.title: Cutthroat Lakes via Walt Bailey Trail

properties.description: Enjoy views of peaks and wildflowers along this connector trail between the PCT and the Pasayten Airstrip. This trail features abundant wildlife and a comfortable grade.
properties.title: Rock Creek

properties.description: Climb through the forest, including a short burn area from 2017, up to the American Ridge Trail.  Enroute there is easy access to an unnamed lake and little-used cross-country access to Pleasant Valley Lake.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Pleasant Valley Lake

properties.description: Use this route to access the summit of this Teanaway peak, and you'll be pleased to find it's half as short as the standard 13-mile roundtrip approach. The trailside environment is stark, since this area burned recently, and while life is rebounding here, it’s still more austere than jolly. Note that this summit is also accessible via the West Fork Teanaway Trail, Yellow Hill, and Jolly Creek or Paris Creek, though all those are multi-mile treks, deserving of overnighting, or at least a very early start.
properties.title: Jolly Mountain via Sasse Ridge Trail

properties.description: The Grace Lakes trail itself is only 1.4 miles, but you'll do a longer hike on the White Pine Creek and Wildhorse Creek trails to get there first.
properties.title: Grace Lakes (Wildhorse Creek)

properties.description: Oyster Dome is a rocky promontory on the western slope of Blanchard Mountain, the grandest member of the Chuckanut Mountain range, an extension of the Cascades that rises directly from the ocean. The sheer cliffs of Oyster Dome offer year-round access to commanding views of the San Juans, Skagit River flats, Olympic Mountains, and Samish Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Oyster Dome

properties.description: An old access point to an infrequently-maintained route up Scorpion Mountain. There is no parking available at this trailhead and has not been maintained in years.
properties.title: Kelley Creek

properties.description: See colorful wildflowers in the warmer months and changing leaves in the fall on the Military Road Trail. This 0.7 mile section of trail goes from the Red Town Trailhead to the Cougar Mountain Park boundary at Clay Pit Road
properties.title: Military Road

properties.description: A short trail that travels between forest roads along Naneum Creek through meadows and a burn area, a great option to see some fall color near Blewett Pass and create a loop link up with nearby other trails.
properties.title: Naneum Creek

properties.description: Connect between the PCT and Ross Lake as you take in the incredible sights of the Pasayten Wilderness. Pass over ridges and stop to explore and admire the popular Devil's Dome.
properties.title: Devil's Ridge

properties.description: This trail has it all, from beautiful forests, beautiful waterfalls, good climbing and fun descents to technical sections with views of Mount Rainier from cliffs that will inspire you.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Palisades

properties.description: Find solitude among expansive views of the Olympic interior on this strenuous but rewarding backpack.
properties.title: Gladys Divide

properties.description: Lila Lake is a beautiful lake surrounded by parkland and jagged mountains. While it can be done as a day hike, it is better enjoyed as an overnight destination.  Nearby Alta Mountain and Rampart Lakes make excellent side trips.
properties.title: Lila Lake

properties.description: An out and back hike through the forest with gentle hills for the first two miles or so. It eventually joins Icicle Creek at its confluence with French Creek, and the trail continues beyond.
properties.title: Icicle Creek

properties.description: A short route that provides a way for kayakers and rafters to go around BZ falls. Some locals use the trail to see the rapids and watch people going through them.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: BZ Trail

properties.description: The Columbia River flows past arid land and steep hills, creating an inviting place for fishing and recreation.
properties.title: Jackson Creek Fish Camp

properties.description: Two hikes exist here: One, an old road through the woods; and the other, winding along narrow tread on grassy hillsides and exposed bedrock alongside the Puget Sound. Connecting these two makes a great loop.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Friday Harbor Biological Laboratories Preserve

properties.description: Daroga State Park is a recreational oasis in Central Washington, providing riverside access for a host of outdoor activities. Bring the family for a full day along the Columbia River — everyone is sure to find something that will bring them joy.
properties.title: Daroga State Park

properties.description: Three peaks in a day! It's completely doable thanks to this loop that takes you on a tour of Mount Kit Carson, Day Mountain, and Mount Spokane. Plus there is plenty to see along the way -- don't forget your camera!
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Three Peaks Loop

properties.description: A sub-alpine meadow teeming with wildflowers greets hikers who make their way up the Bean Creek Basin. Beginning along Beverly Creek as it tumbles past the trailhead, the trail then climbs up Bean Creek to the colorful meadow from which it is fed.
properties.title: Bean Creek Basin

properties.description: The rewards for this strenuous hike are vast alpine meadows and a wide panorama of North Cascades peaks.
properties.title: Church Mountain

properties.description: Hiking across bare talus slopes, past rocky outcrops and fields of wildflowers while admiring sweeping vistas, you would think you're at 7,000 feet. But the alpine-like setting at this mid-elevation is the result of period of wildfires that swept the area in the early 1900's.
properties.title: Bluff Mountain

properties.description: A paved urban trail along the Alki beaches and West Seattle industrial area with spectacular mountain, city and Elliott Bay marine views.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Alki Trail

properties.description: This long route from Madison Falls on the Elwha River offers some rewarding diversions along the way, but much of the payoff is in the last 1.5 miles with sweeping views as one ascends the meadows and traverses the switchbacks to Appleton Pass.
properties.title: Appleton Pass

properties.description: The Auspurger Mountain and Dog Mountain trails share the same trailhead, but the Auspurger Mountain trail heads west while the Dog Mountain trail heads east.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Augspurger Trail

properties.description: From Rachel Lake you can access further adventures at Rampart Lakes, Lila Lakes and Alta Peak. This hike is a popular weekend overnight destination; so don’t expect to be by yourself in high season.
properties.title: Rachel Lake

properties.description: The Dosewallips River Road is the gateway to the eastern Olympic Mountains and it penetrates one of the deepest canyons in Olympic National Park. Now closed to vehicles, the old road bed allows hikers to explore true wilderness at a gentle grade. Backpackers, peak baggers and horseback riders take advantage of the easy access to the trails beyond the road's end.
properties.title: Dosewallips River Road

properties.description: This is a great loop which combines everything great about hiking at Crystal, while staying away from crowds and out of the ski area.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Pickhandle Gap Loop

properties.description: A quiet natural area near Brewster that offers wildlife viewing and beautiful views of Okanogan County.
properties.title: Cassimer Bar Natural Area

properties.description: A figure-eight loop around Takhlakh Lake and past Takh Takh Meadow, ascending up a lava flow for fantastic vistas of Mount Rainier, the Goat Rocks, and Mount Adams. You can also do a lake-only loop for a much shorter and more level hike.
properties.title: Takhlakh Lake and Takh Takh Meadow

properties.description: Hike a loop route that features an historic old railroad grade that traverses a very green forest with mossy sections  and several small streams. Enjoy many wildflowers in season.
properties.title: West Tiger Railroad Grade

properties.description: A connector trail on Tiger Mountain. Access from Tiger Mountain Trail, 15 Mile Railroad Grade, East Tiger, and Upper and Middle Bootleg Trail.
properties.title: Paw Print Connector

properties.description: A winter off-trail summit destination.
properties.title: Spinnaker Peak Snowshoe

properties.description: Squak Mountain's Central Peak is accessible from several trailheads around the mountain, but the most direct route is from the Squak Mountain State Park trailhead (also known as the May Valley trailhead).
properties.title: Central Peak

properties.description: This trail starts on private property, and is made accessible thanks to the property owner who built it. There is only room for about 10 cars at the trailhead, so if there are more than that when you arrive, please head elsewhere, since parking beyond the signs is not allowed.
properties.title: Sauer's Mountain

properties.description: Looking for a modest, mostly shaded climb with a view of the San Juan Islands as a mid-hike treat? Check out the Olsen Creek trail system, a part of the Washington Department of Natural Resources' 2019 Baker to Bellingham Non-motorized Recreation Plan. WTA is one of a few partners to have spent many hours helping build the trail system from the ground up.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Olsen Creek

properties.description: There are 6 designated snowshoe trails at Crystal Mountain Resort forming a network in Bullion Basin.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Crystal Mountain Resort Snowshoe Trails

properties.description: Beach 1 is a short but scenic trail that ends on a wild beach on the Pacific Ocean. Photogenic spruce burls can be seen on a unique nature loop that adds minimal time. However, access to the beach is typically over a jam of drift logs that require care to cross.
properties.title: Beach 1

properties.description: Upland birds love this sprawling desert prairie. The ground-hugging birds sprint among the tufts of plants. They take refuge, and find dinner, in such glorious wildflowers as balsamroot, large-headed clover, wild onion, and canyon-bottom communities of beautiful orange globe mallow.
properties.title: Rattlesnake Slope Wildlife Area

properties.description: The East Side Road is an access road on Tiger Mountain that is closed to vehicle traffic and open to hikers.  The road roughly parallels the eastern boundary of Tiger Mountain and connects with several other trails.
properties.title: East Side Road

properties.description: The south end of the William O. Douglas Wilderness is rolling country swathed in mature forest that is interrupted by dozens of named, and many more unnamed, lakes. A visit to scenic Cramer Lake, with its clear water, good fishing, and comfortable campsites will leave you wanting to explore deeper into the Tumac Plateau.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Cramer Lake

properties.description: A lovely-but-rough hike that uses established trail and old logging roads, the Circle Peak Trail has seen a lot of maintenance from the Darrington Ranger District in the past several summers.
properties.title: Circle Peak

properties.description: The trailhead might be busy, but heading to Island and Rainbow Lakes may afford you more solitude than you'd expect on the crowded I-90 corridor. It's a touch longer than many day hikers want to tackle, and even most of the campers will drop off past Ollalie, or Pratt Lake junctions, leaving you (and a few hardy others) to discover these alpine jewels.
properties.title: Island Lake - Rainbow Lake

properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Coast Trail: Mount Maguire Loop

properties.description: Once the largest hospital for people with mental health conditions in Washington State, Northern State Mental Hospital was a town unto itself. Parts of the site are still in use and off-limits, but the farm is now a recreation area. It is located just north of the Skagit River near the town of Sedro-Woolley. Stroll along the wide pastoral trails amongst the buildings and cemetery.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Northern State Ghost Town

properties.description: Once upon a time, the road in Stehekin extended all the way to Cottonwood Camp, more than ten miles further into the lush green valley. But strong river activity due to snowmelt and rain events washed the road out frequently, and for one final time in 2003. Now it's accessible by foot only, and many of the trails found along this route are some of your best chance for solitude in the state.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Upper Stehekin Valley Road Trail

properties.description: Mountains to Sound Greenway did this road to trail conversion in order to create a more sustainable, safer route for hikers to a summit on the I-90 corridor. Hike through second- and third-growth forest, pass a lovely waterfall, and enjoy a slightly less-crowded trail than the nearby Mount Si.
properties.title: Mount Teneriffe

properties.description: Surrounded by a rugged topography cloaked in ancient forest, the setting is as wild as any along the Mountain Loop Highway, except for one noticeable difference. North and Independence lack the crowds that inundate nearby backcountry lakes.
properties.title: Independence and North Lakes

properties.description: Observatory Road on Manastash Ridge is a popular year-round hike. In winter, it's a great snowshoe option, and in summer it offers spectacular views into the central Cascade range.
properties.title: Manastash Ridge - Observatory Road

properties.description: Samish Park’s most difficult trail option features a mostly forested loop above a popular lakeside park that provides year-round hiking opportunities.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lake Samish Park - Hillside Trail

properties.description: Hike a six-mile horseshoe loop up through the bluffs and along the north side of Crab Creek. In spring, you'll be accompanied by a profusion of wildflowers, but look out for ticks.
properties.title: Goose Butte

properties.description: If you’re in need of a quick leg stretch while traveling over the pass, the trail to Alpine Falls may be just the place. The trail is very short and features a powerful waterfall where the Tye River flows over giant granite boulders.
properties.title: Alpine Falls

properties.description: Experience a breathtaking section of the PCT packaged into a great dayhike.
properties.title: Windy Pass

properties.description: This snowshoe route may be relatively flat, but it's a hard one to get to, since the highway to this part of Mount Rainer National Park is closed in the winter. It takes a 3 mile road walk both ways in addition to the loop itself.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Silver Falls - Grove of the Patriarchs Snowshoe

properties.description: A new trail makes this hike a 5-mile roundtrip, gently graded, obstacle-free hike to a broad summit with views of the Methow Valley and Sawtooth Mountains. Most of the trail has no shade and faces south, so it is best done early in the day.
properties.title: Methow Wildlife Area - Lewis Butte

properties.description: Just minutes from downtown Dayton, Middle Point Ridge trail offers a vigorous hike to high meadow and forest views of the Blue Mountains as it climbs the spine of Middle Point Ridge.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Middle Point Ridge

properties.description: A collaboration between Skagit Land Trust and Washington Trails Association created this 1.2-mile trail up Guemes Mountain, offering views of the surrounding San Juan Islands.  A treat year round, you'll also see unique prairie habitat and forest, in addition to those gorgeous views.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Guemes Mountain

properties.description: Discover views similar to Winchester Mountain and hike this seldom-traveled trail with views of Mount Larabee and increased chances of encountering wildlife.
properties.title: High Pass

properties.description: Knapsack Pass follows a no-longer-maintained hiking trail. It now requires GPS or map and compass skills to reach the pass, located near Mother Mountain.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Knapsack Pass

properties.description: The East Fork Quinault River Trail is one of the most popular trails on the south portion of the park and hundreds of hikers visit Enchanted Valley to take in the tremendous views and see the famed chalet each year.
properties.title: Enchanted Valley via East Fork Quinault River

properties.description: The Kelsey Creek Park Nature trails provide a year-round opportunity to enioy a forest experience. In the springtime, blooming flowers offer a heady aroma for people wandering in the area. By summertime, birds flit and trill in the brush as Kelsey Creek babbles beside you. Fall brings vivid oranges and reds as the trees in the area change color. Winter's blanket doesn't deter hikers, as this is a great destination for shaking winter doldrums.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Kelsey Creek Park Nature Trails

properties.description: This meandering trail through old-growth forest follows Jackson Creek, connecting the Shedroof Divide in Washington to Hughes Meadows in Idaho.
properties.title: Jackson Creek

properties.description: This trail connects to Saddle Rock from the Jacobson Preserve, northwest of Saddle Rock.
properties.title: Saddle Rock Traverse Trail

properties.description: Washington Trails Association is working with the San Juan Preservation Trust to create and improve the trail system on this undeveloped and little-known San Juan island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Vendovi Island Trails

properties.description: This is a hike of sounds and smells of the forest, with limited vistas and lots of lakes.  With easy access from White Pass, it can be done in any season as a hike or snow trip.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Cramer Mountain Loop

properties.description: This abandoned trail climbs from the Lennox Creek Valley under thick canopy to a prominent peak in between the North Fork and Middle Fork Snoqualmie Rivers.
properties.title: Lennox Creek (Dog Mountain)

properties.description: Waterfalls, wildflowers, sheltering forests, mountain views and an alpine lake are offered on this well-maintained trail. At the lake, enjoy the sights and relax for a while. If you backpacked in, stay at the campsites for a sunrise and sunset on the lake.
properties.title: Annette Lake

properties.description: This short, easy hike in the Wilson Creek Canyon of Eastern Washington’s channeled scablands offers beautiful vistas, mature sagebrush, wildflowers, and an abundance of birds.
properties.title: Wilson Creek Canyon

properties.description: Take a short but very scenic hike starting from the Altair campground in Olympic National Park. Traverse along the edge of the Elwha River, recently free-flowing thanks to the removal of the Glines Canyon Dam.
properties.title: West Elwha

properties.description: This 2.5 mile loop is in Dosewallips State Park right out of the campground. You'll enjoy a moderate climb, which meanders up, down, and all around the park. Amble past waterfalls, through a valley lined with bigleaf maples and western redcedar before switchbacking up to a ridgeline, then return to the campground via a gentle downhill grade.
properties.title: Dosewallips State Park - Maple Valley Loop

properties.description: A snowshoe route along a ridgeline above the Hurricane Ridge parking area. Maybe difficult or impossible to access in winter.
properties.title: Klahhane Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: The trail at Camano Forest Preserve winds through a typical evergreen forest with plenty of sword ferns, and maple trees that are lovely in autumn. Originally set aside as Camp Lake and managed by the Department of Natural Resources, it is now managed and maintained by the Friends of Camano Island and Island County.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Camano Ridge Trail

properties.description: Valhalla Peak is a modest summit located in the Olympic National Forest and can be reached via the Tunnel Creek Trailhead or via Dosewallips Road.
properties.title: Valhalla Peak

properties.description: Hikers will appreciate the trails that wind through the park and connect to even more miles of walking.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Farrel-McWhirter Trail

properties.description: Just behind the High Bridge Guard Station at the end of the road in Stehekin, a trail leads to a quiet little lake nestled in lush, vibrant forest. This trail is primarily used by hikers heading to the summit of McGregor Mountain, the most prominent peak towering over the Stehekin Valley, but Howard Lake is a nice destination in and of itself, if you don’t have the time or the desire to tackle the 16 mile roundtrip hike up McGregor.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Howard Lake

properties.description: Located on the south side of Whidbey Island, this tiny state park includes the short but fun and challenging Dorothy Cleveland Trail, with plenty of elevation gain in the form of switchbacks.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Possession Point State Park

properties.description: This loop combines the Grandview Trail with the Soundview Trail to make 3.25 miles with some serious incline. Walk around the golf course at Chambers Creek Regional Park, and enjoy views of Chambers Bay and the vivid green grasses of the golf course.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Chambers Bay Loop

properties.description: Like its neighbor, the nearby Monte Carlo trail, the 4.1 mile-long Monte Cristo trail ventures into the small Monte Cristo range in the south Cascades between Willard and Trout Lake. From it, hikers see a myriad of wildflowers in the spring, and the occasional views of the south Cascade range.
properties.title: Monte Cristo

properties.description: The infrequently visited trail to Doe Falls is a good option for hikers preparing for summer hiking. Because of its lower elevation, this hike is snow-free earlier in the year than most in this area, allowing for a pleasant hike to a secluded waterfall early in the season.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Doe Falls

properties.description: Hike to a glacier-fed waterfall pouring out of the heart of a volcano. It doesn’t get much more dramatic than that.
properties.title: Loowit Falls

properties.description: This short and sweet neighborhood trail on the west side of Olympia will take hikers through a quiet forested ravine and out to views of the Puget Sound.
properties.title: Garfield Nature Trail

properties.description: Silver Star mountain provides a rewarding hiking and climbing opportunity right off Highway 20. Its majestic barren rocky spires that raise out of the forested slopes seem beyond reach but in fact the summit block requires a bit of exposed scrambling, after a long hike and a glacier traverse.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Silver Star Mountain (Okanogan)

properties.description: This hike starts at the North Siouxon Creek Trailhead which is also the south end of the Mitchell Peak Trail. Following the Mitchell Peak Trail for about 5.5 miles the route offers a spur down to the falls. Or for the more adventurous a steep climb up to Mitchell Peak makes for a good two day backpacking adventure.
properties.title: Black Hole Falls

properties.description: View one of the best examples of a recessional-cataract canyon. Potholes Coulee caught the attention of J Harlen Bretz in the early 20th century, which led to his “outrageous hypothesis” of Ice Age flooding.
properties.title: Ancient Lakes

properties.description: The O’neil Pass Trail travels through the southeastern corner of Olympic National Park. It is a trail segment that sits well within the backcountry so you must hike a considerable distance to reach the start of this trail.
properties.title: O'Neil Pass

properties.description: This trail provides access to Bachelor Creek Trail, Bachelor Meadows, Cub Lake and the Dome Peak area.
properties.title: Downey Creek

properties.description: This short feeder trail located on the west side of the Kettle River Range provides easy access to the portion of the Kettle Crest National Recreation Trail around Profanity Peak.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Profanity Peak

properties.description: A long approach to access wild creeks that flow through steep terrain from the top to the bottom of the Blue Mountains makes Crooked Creek best hiked as part of a backpacking adventure.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Crooked Creek

properties.description: The trip to Mount Zion is straightforward and short; a steep hike through fir, hemlock cedar, salal, and, the main attraction for many visitors, tall groves of wild rhododendrons. Views from the top are limited, but a little ridgeline wandering to the south afford the intrepid better views of the Olympic Mountains.
properties.title: Mount Zion

properties.description: Visit a former fire lookout location with broad views in a remote location.
properties.title: Goat Peak

properties.description: You’re not likely to find other hikers on this trail around lovely, peaceful Long Lake. You may not find the trail itself either! Sections are lost in thickets of alder, willow, and wild roses.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Long Lake

properties.description: This popular path for horseback riders follows a gentle grade along Carey Creek to connect with the Taylor Mountain trail network.
properties.title: Carey Creek Trail

properties.description: Don’t let the thought of the Brightwater Treatment Plant prevent you from hiking through the Brightwater Center’s 70-acre suburban wetland and woodland preserve that serves as a refuge for local wildlife and plant species. The trails at Brightwater are ideal for families, birdwatchers, pets, and children.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Brightwater Center

properties.description: Often free of snow as early as April, this excellent early season hike offers hikers what they have been missing for months: a good chance of sun (this being the sunny side of the Cascades, a bountiful array of wildflowers, and stunning views of Tumwater and Icicle Canyon, the Wenatchee and Icicle rivers and surrounding mountains.
properties.title: Icicle Ridge

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Louise Lake

properties.description: A hike on an old railroad grade through a Whitman County Park and wildlife preserve.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Colfax Trail

properties.description: South Puyallup to Klapatche is a scenic section along the western portion of the Wonderland Trail.
properties.title: South Puyallup to Klapatche

properties.description: Hiking through a deep canyon with a riparian zone, old-growth, and cliffs, this dramatic trail parallels the river with several crossings. In places, it climbs high above the river to avoid cliffs and other obstructions in the deep, rugged canyon.
properties.title: West Fork Teanaway River

properties.description: Hike trails though sub-alpine forest and across boulder fields and, in season, enjoy a multitude of wildflowers. Pass a beautiful mountain lake. Ascend to a 5584-foot summit and enjoy incredible views of Cascade peaks and nearby lakes.
properties.title: Mount Defiance

properties.description: Reaching the summit of Clark Peak requires going off trail.
properties.title: Clark Peak

properties.description: Hike along an old road being converted to trail in Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Sleepy Hollow Trail

properties.description: This peak allows for unrivaled views of the Olympic Peninsula. Located on the southwest side of the park, views include the Pacific Ocean, Grays Harbor, Lake Quinault and the Quinault River, the Olympic rainforest and Mount Olympus.
properties.title: Pete's Creek - Colonel Bob Peak

properties.description: Get away from the crowds and experience forests, meadows, wetlands, and a secluded lake.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Big Meadow Lake

properties.description: Cultus Mountain is a peak east of Mt. Vernon. The land surrounding the mountain is a patchwork of public and private property.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Cultus Mountain

properties.description: A multi-use trail connecting with the Teanaway Ridge Trail and continuing on to Miller Peak.
properties.title: County Line

properties.description: Bear Lake and sections of Bearscout Peak are in the Cedar River Watershed and are closed to the public. Consult a map before venturing out in order to avoid trespassing.
properties.title: Bearscout Peak

properties.description: A connector trail in the Mount St. Helens area linking Independence Pass with the Boundary Trail. Views from here include Spirit Lake and the north side of the volcano.
properties.title: Independence Ridge

properties.description: This 140.9-acre park has fishing, hiking, swimming and more. You can take a hike by the lake and through the forest at this public park in the city of Kent.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Fenwick Park

properties.description: This horse/hiker trail used to access Bear Creek Mountain, but years of underuse and neglect has rendered it nearly impossible to follow.
properties.title: Tieton Meadows

properties.description: The route to Mount Fernow is a Class 4 and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Mount Fernow

properties.description: Hike Summary: Amos Peak is not on a formal trail and can only be accessed via scrambling up the mountain.
properties.title: Amos Peak

properties.description: With 40+ miles of multi-use trails, Suncadia provides choice through all four seasons. This loop explores the northeast side of the Cle Elum River.
properties.title: Suncadia Trail

properties.description: Heybrook Lookout is a short and moderately steep hike through a fern and moss covered forest to a fun, staircase-ridden lookout with great views of the nearby mountains. If you are introducing someone to hiking, limited on time, or trying to add on another hike or activity in the area, this is the hike for you.
properties.title: Heybrook Lookout

properties.description: The route to Concord Tower is a Class 5+ and involved exposed climbing. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Concord Tower

properties.description: Cougar Rock to Carter Falls is a moderate and readily accessible segment of the Wonderland Trail that packs stunning mountain vistas, river views, waterfalls, wildflowers, old growth, and edible berries into just 1.3 miles of family-friendly hiking in Mount Rainier National Park.
properties.title: Carter Falls

properties.description: This is a beautiful small lake tucked immediately under Grizzly Peak and the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT). Where Heather Lake is often shared with a number of hiking and camping groups, you are pretty much assured to have lunch by yourself at Glasses.  Only a half a dozen trip reports have been filed in the last decade, this is a good predictor of solitude.
properties.title: Glasses Lake

properties.description: When the deeper backcountry is under snow (or just too far away) Burch Mountain can provide a beautiful day hike with views aplenty.
properties.title: Burch Mountain via Falls Creek

properties.description: The McKenny Trail is a long route in Capitol State Forest that connects the Margaret McKenny Campground and Trailhead to the east with the Fall Creel Trailhead to the west.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - McKenny Trail

properties.description: Explore an undeveloped watershed on well-maintained trails just minutes from town.
properties.title: Illahee Forest Preserve

properties.description: Here's a great backdoor access to Mount Townsend. You’ll likely have company at the summit, but this route offers solitude to get there, along with some sweeping views, plus steeps to work those quads! Consider why it's so infrequently used -- a sign at the trailhead warns of grades up to 40% in places! It's short, but there's nothing sweet about it.
properties.title: Dirty Face Ridge

properties.description: In Sahale Arm, the forces of nature have conspired to create an improbably gentle, gorgeous landscape. Simply put, this is one of the most beautiful hikes in all of Washington.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cascade Pass and Sahale Arm

properties.description: Located within the Finn Hill neighborhood in Kirkland, the small Juanita Heights Park has a network of forested trails for urban hikers to explore.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Juanita Heights Park

properties.description: The McDowell Marsh Environmental Education Trail (McMEET) is a 1.2 mile hardened environmental education trail offering hikers an opportunity to explore five distinct ecological habitats, ranging from riparian to semi-arid, which are managed specifically for native plants and wildlife.
properties.title: McDowell Marsh Environmental Education Trail

properties.description: This forested trail connecting two parks in the City of Chehalis (Dobson and McFadden), offers a quick get away into nature on the edge of a residential neighborhood.
properties.title: Dobson and McFadden Park Trail

properties.description: A hike/scramble from Merritt Lake to the summit of Mount Mastiff. Climbing gear and experience and route-finding skills required.
properties.title: Mount Mastiff via Merritt Lake

properties.description: This short but steep hike offers 360-degree views of Lake Chelan and the North Cascades.
properties.title: Fourth of July Mountain

properties.description: Starting in a forested creek valley, climb through alpine forest, meadows, and rocks to expansive vistas at the Stiletto Lookout site. Your destination is visible from the trailhead, on the end of the ridge to the southeast.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Stiletto Peak

properties.description: Walk along a gentle road-to-trail conversion along beautiful old growth groves to a placid lake deep in the Lower Skokomish Valley.
properties.title: Pine Lake

properties.description: This trail is listed in Audubon's Olympic Loop of The Great Washington State Birding Trail. The trail drops fairly steeply from the trailhead to begin a 0.7 mile loop around the lake. There are several benches along the way for resting while bird watching.
properties.title: Hamma Hamma Beaver Pond

properties.description: Get a taste for the south slopes of Mount Adams area when the snow is still in the high country on this eight mile loop combining the Buck Creek Trail, Morrison Creek Trail, and Wicky Creek Trail.
properties.title: Buck Creek-Morrison Creek-Wicky Creek Loop

properties.description: La Conner is well known for its museums, interesting shops, pubs and dining establishments. Less well-known is this small park at the southwest corner of town that offers a forested retreat with a few short hiking trails and some wildflowers in season. As a hike extension, continue on across Swinomish Channel to visit a tribal park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Pioneer Park - La Conner

properties.description: Sky Valley Vista Trail is a scenic, multi-use trail in the Reiter Foothills Forest, offering a mix of forest walking, open fields and panoramic views of the Skykomish Valley. The trail network has several optional loops and side trips, including a waterfall and Olympic Overlook. The viewpoint provides excellent views of Mount Index, Mount Persis and Haystack Mountain.
properties.title: Reiter Foothills Forest Trails

properties.description: Providing access to Bowan Pass, the Rainbow Lake Trail also allows hikers access to deep blue Rainbow Lake. Used mostly by backpackers, the trail lies deep within a network of other access trails.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Rainbow Lake

properties.description: Take a hike through an active working forest to the peaceful Loch Katrine. Be aware that this hike is on private property, and a day permit is required for entry.
properties.title: Loch Katrine

properties.description: Waterworks Gardens is a public park managed by King County Parks. Complete with trails, art, native plants and wildlife this park winds visitors through a series of garden "rooms" of ponds, wetlands and marshes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Waterworks Garden

properties.description: This out-and-back hike takes you through rich wildlife habitat on the south side of the Little Spokane River valley. You’ll find a variety of birds — from tiny songbirds to wild turkeys — and an abundance of wildflowers.
properties.title: St. George's Trail (Trail 503)

properties.description: The Oak Harbor Waterfront Trail is a route that follows the shoreline of Oak Harbor Marina.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Oak Harbor Waterfront Trail

properties.description: The combination of a regional irrigation project, dramatic basalt topography and an arid climate create a unique habitat. You’ll walk with the main irrigation canal on one side and peaceful Trail Lake on the other, surrounded by high basalt outcrops.
properties.title: Trail Lake Coulee

properties.description: This quick out-and-back will satisfy your outdoor craving without the exertion of a full day hike.
properties.title: Donkey Engine Trail

properties.description: Enjoy a peaceful river walk followed by nicely graded switchbacks on the way to Bald Eagle Mountain. Views of Monte Cristo and surrounds will be the reward for your efforts.
properties.title: Bald Eagle Mountain

properties.description: The Lost Beagle Trail is a connector Trail on Cougar Mountain. It does not have its own trailhead so hikers must reach this trail on foot from one of the many connecting trails.
properties.title: Lost Beagle

properties.description: The Gray Wolf Trail extends between Forest Road 2870 and the Main Fork Dosewallips River in the northeast corner of the Olympics. Along the way it goes up and over Gray Wolf Pass.
properties.title: Upper Gray Wolf River to Gray Wolf Pass

properties.description: The Silver Forest Trail is a lesser-known and therefore less-crowded alternative at Mount Rainier’s Sunrise. Enjoy mountain, glacier and river valley views along a gentle trail that is mostly out of sight of the bustle of Sunrise.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Silver Forest - Emmons Vista

properties.description: This 2.2 mile loop boasts a short, steep hike on exposed sandstone slab to some of the most spectacular views of the Teanaway Community Forest, with stunning views of Mount Stuart and surrounding peaks at the top before finishing on a gently graded downhill trail to complete the loop.
properties.title: Teanaway Community Forest - Cheese Rock Loop

properties.description: Start on a trail popular for horses and hikers to Billy Goat Pass, then take a right on a hiker-only trail for a high ridge traverse to a larch grove pass. Finish with a steep climb to a lookout site and 360 degree views.
properties.title: Burch Mountain via Billy Goat Pass

properties.description: Senator Rosa Franklin Park borders Franklin Elementary school in Central Tacoma. The park features a playground, a baseball field, picnic areas, a sprayground, restrooms and several paved paths.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Senator Rosa Franklin Park

properties.description: It's a very short walk from the trailhead to Champion Beach. Along the way, you'll cross a couple of bridges and pass through typical lush Middle Fork forest. The big attraction is the beach, though. It's a big part of the river with beautiful green water and huge rocks. There's lots of room to spread out and tons of trails that lead away from the main beach.
properties.title: Champion Beach

properties.description: Hike a gently climbing trail along a forested hillside near Issaquah High School. It's a good bet for young hikers and, if you are so inclined, it leads to more ambitious ongoing trails. In spring enjoy a few wildflowers, and any time of year be alert for birds and wildlife sightings.
properties.title: High School Trail

properties.description: A pleasant 0.8 mile loop around a beaver pond and wetland is ideal for a morning stroll or post-dinner walk while camping at Brown Creek Campground.
properties.title: Brown Creek

properties.description: Hike up a remote track to one of the highest points in Eastern Washington’s Saddle Mountains, with spectacular views all around.
properties.title: Wahatis Peak

properties.description: This steep but shady trail features a rhododendron forest, and numerous saprophytic plants. At the end, it connects to a Forest Service road, allowing for additional wandering, to find views of Hood Canal and more.
properties.title: Elbo Creek

properties.description: The Willard Springs Trail is a loop along the edge of the Conboy Lake marsh and through the pine forest. Beginning at the refuge headquarters, the trail parallels the west shore of the old Conboy Lake lakebed, with views across the lakebed and north to the 12,000-foot Mt. Adams from the Observation Platform, then returns through the forest.
properties.title: Willard Springs Trail

properties.description: W.E. Johnson Park is a Richland city park with an interesting mix of riparian, wetlands and shrubsteppe habitat adjacent to the Yakima River.
properties.title: W.E. Johnson Park

properties.description: Two small and interesting parks that sit along the Duwamish River highlight the multi-use Duwamish trail that connects West Seattle and South Park. Take in river views, get a glimpse of local wildlife, and even spy downtown Seattle from an urban, traffic-protected trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Duwamish Trail

properties.description: Pritchard Park sits at the mouth of Eagle Harbor on Bainbridge Island, facing the Bainbridge Island ferry terminal. With a network of upland trails and beachfront, this park offers numerous hiking opportunities that take visitors through natural Puget Sound landscapes as well as significant historical sites.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Pritchard Park

properties.description: The Port Susan Bay Preserve, owned by Nature Conservancy, is a 4,122-acre preserve which encompasses much of the Stillaguamish River estuary. A short mile-long dike trail takes you through tidelands and farmlands to the Stillaguamish River, provide the opportunity to view many varieties of  birds and other wildlife.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Port Susan Bay Preserve

properties.description: Explore the shore as you camp on Pierre Lake in Colville National Forest. This trail is great for viewing wildlife, especially bird watching.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Pierre Lake Trail

properties.description: Dirty Harry's Peak was so named by Harvey Manning in recognition of Harry Gault, who operated a logging show on this mountain years ago. The trees have grown back, and Harry is long gone, but his truck remains in what is known as Dirty Harry's Museum. Abandoned 2000 feet above the highway, this relic of a time gone by is a destination for hikers on their way to the peak, though it takes some route finding to get there.
properties.title: Dirty Harry's Museum

properties.description: There are few places where you start your hike at 7,000 feet without any effort. Spectacular views, a dizzying array of wildflowers and larch groves -- this hike is simply gorgeous and a pure Pasayten experience.
properties.title: Silver Lake

properties.description: Magnificent old growth forests, stellar views of Mount Baker, turbulent tributaries, and, of course, a beautiful lake make this trail a great path to travel.
properties.title: Baker Lake - Maple Grove

properties.description: Enjoy this wooded trail leading to a ridge featuring a rock outcropping overlooking the town of Wenatchee.
properties.title: Burch Mountain - Eagle Rock

properties.description: This network of trails that weave through the town of Port Townsend just west of Fort Warden State Park are known as Cappy’s Trails
properties.title: Cappy's Trails

properties.description: Visit an alpine lake via a short walk from the trailhead. Road is rough, 4x4 high clearance vehicles recommended.
properties.title: Coal Lake

properties.description: The Shy Bear runs through the southern portion of Cougar Mountain. The official ends of this trail can only be reached on foot and must be accessed from one of the various trails that connect to Shy Bear.
properties.title: Shy Bear

properties.description: A scramble to a peak off Highway 2 overlooking Money Creek. Routefinding and climbing experience required.
properties.title: Cleveland Mountain

properties.description: The Early Winters Trail #522 is a part of a trail that went between the Methow and Skagit rivers.  Hikers have the opportunity to tread along a short section of this historic trail, where many have gone in the prior centuries.  Depending upon how recently the trail has been maintained, this may include experiencing the difficulties of foot travel through the raw wilds of the North Cascades.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Early Winters

properties.description: The Hemlock Trail is a main east-west arterial of the Chuckanut Mountain trail system that connects the popular (and mostly flat) Interurban Trail with the Pine and Cedar Lakes area. The Raptor Ridge trail is found along this artery, and takes you to a lovely viewpoint over the forested hills of Chuckanut.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Raptor Ridge Trail

properties.description: A trail to the summit of Lookout Mountain from an access point on the southeast corner of Lookout Mountain. This route crosses private property in a couple of sections and is not recommended to access the summit.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lookout Mountain Preserve - Camp 2

properties.description: Olallie Lake is a wonderful first-time destination for hikers or backpackers just beginning to discover trails.
properties.title: Olallie Lake via Pratt Lake Trail

properties.description: A summit scramble in the central Cascades.
properties.title: Natapoc Mountain

properties.description: A great day hike in summer, the route to Lake 22 can be avalanche prone in winter. It's best to wait until the snow is melted on this popular Mountain Loop Highway trail.
properties.title: Lake 22 - Winter

properties.description: “Most Difficult”. If you can accept and safely navigate what that means, the Whittier Ridge Trail offers you an airy and ruggedly scenic connection between the Boundary Trail and the Lakes Trail, for an 8.5-mile loop, part of a 14.3-mile “lollipop” day hike.
properties.title: Whittier Ridge-Lakes Loop

properties.description: On maps, Mount Margaret doesn’t seem impressive enough to warrant its namesake Mount Margaret Backcountry. It is not the tallest nor the most majestic peak in the area. However, it is easily summited and it offers clear unobstructed views of Mount Rainier, Mount Adams, and Mount St. Helens (in three different directions), and expansive views of much more, including legendary Spirit Lake.
properties.title: Mount Margaret

properties.description: Tucked in a lush river valley in the Okanogan region, the Sinlahekin Wildlife Area provides the opportunity to wander at will, through a rich ecosystem harboring hundreds of species of big game, waterfowl, and native plants.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sinlahekin Natural Area

properties.description: The winter route to Boardman Lake involves several miles of road walking from the Mountain Loop Highway followed by a short stretch on the actual Boardman Lake Trail.
properties.title: Boardman Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: A steep trail to the summit of West Tiger 3.
properties.title: Section Line Trail

properties.description: A switchbacking railroad grade that gradually climbs through the forest of east side of Tiger Mountain. Expect mountain bikes for company.
properties.title: Preston Railroad Grade

properties.description: Nestled in the far, far southeast corner of Washington State, Puffer Butte is a year-round favorite, and the jewel of the Fields Spring State Park — a beautiful part of the state park system here.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Field Springs State Park - Puffer Butte

properties.description: This summit off of Highway 20 offers gorgeous views of the craggy North Cascades and a great workout.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Little Jack Mountain

properties.description: Visit any of several beautiful alpine lakes, in rocky basins. The day can be as easy as a 3.6 roundtrip hike to Trout Lake, or as strenuous as the nearly 15-mile hike to Big Heart Lake as you like. Good options exist both for day-hikers and for backpackers.
properties.title: West Fork Foss River and Lakes

properties.description: The route to Scout Lake is not an official Forest Service trail. The route is not maintained and requires route-finding skills to navigate.
properties.title: Scout Lake

properties.description: The Gordy Jolma Family Nature Area is 118-acre open green space — previously a golf course — opened to the public in fall 2022. Combined with the nearby Salmon-Morgan Creeks Nature Area, this area in Clark County is a great place to spend time surrounded by nature without needing to drive far.
properties.title: Gordy Jolma Family Natural Area

properties.description: A short access trail from the Clay Pit Road that connects with the Cave Hole Trail and others to make endless loop options on Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: By Pass Trail

properties.description: A combination of design art and nature, this 104-acre park features a trail that winds through Mill Creek Canyon right in the city of Kent.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Mill Creek Canyon Earthworks Park

properties.description: This regional trail runs along the eastern shore of Lake Sammamish, connecting Redmond and Issaquah.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: East Lake Sammamish Trail

properties.description: This 130-acre park in Kent contains a small lake and several walking trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Clark Lake Park

properties.description: This snowshoe route follows snow-covered forest roads to Camp Lake in the Teanaway Community Forest.
properties.title: Rye Creek to Camp Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: This snowshoe route starts off with a roadwalk, then carries on through the East Fork Foss River Valley on the Necklace Valley Trail.
properties.title: East Fork Foss River Snowshoe

properties.description: Hike through shady forest, accompanied by the sound of Quartz Creek, little waterfalls, wildflowers and interesting things to see (and eat) on this trail.
properties.title: Quartz Creek

properties.description: A relatively short connector trail running through forests and suburbia between Marymoor Park and Bridle Trails State Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bridle Crest Trail

properties.description: Spectacular rolling hills, far off views and a flower explosion make this little-known gem a destination to explore and roam through. It's one of the few places hikers can see sagebrush growing side-by-side with sub-alpine larch.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Wapaloosie Mountain

properties.description: The route to Sherpa Peak is a Class 5 and involved exposed climbing. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Sherpa Peak

properties.description: Franklin Ridge is a rugged route between the Oneonta Trail and the Larch Mountain Trail. It's rarely hiked, but it can create a fun, long loop connecting the Wahkeena Falls trailhead with the Oneonta Trailhead. Alternately, the Franklin Ridge trail can provide create a lollipop loop up to Larch Mountain.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Franklin Ridge

properties.description: This wooded walk enters a lush ravine lined with remnant old-growth and gives way to an isolated beach with views of Protection Island.
properties.title: Miller Peninsula-Thompson Spit

properties.description: A section of the scenic Wonderland Trail, enjoy views of Mount Rainier and the Carbon Glacier, numerous creek crossings, and meadows as you connect between Sunrise and the Carbon River.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Sunrise to Carbon River Traverse

properties.description: This scenic hike can be done in under two hours, and along the way you'll enjoy panoramic views, lush forest, wildflowers, and a historic lookout tower that ups the coolness factor.
properties.title: Lookout Mountain Lookout - Methow

properties.description: Traverse Forest Park via an out-and-back or a point-to-point, soaking in urban forest that has old growth, wildflowers, mushrooms, berries and fauna, enjoying occasional glimpses of the Willamette and the fantastic St. Johns Bridge. If desired, take a side excursion along one of the connector trails near the Springville Road trailhead for an extended Tualatin Mountains experience.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Forest Park - Ridge Trail

properties.description: Lake Easton State Park is not a wilderness park, but it is scenic and peaceful. You can put together a five-mile loop hike on the park trails and on a section of the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail, if you don't mind walking on roads for a bit through the town of Easton. This hike makes for a good leg stretcher when you need a break from I-90.
properties.title: Lake Easton State Park

properties.description: Enjoy a stroll along a flat, paved trail with beautiful views and a good look at a restored estuary.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ebey Waterfront Trail

properties.description: Red Top Lookout — built in 1952, restored in 1997 — and still operational today, provides a fine bang for your hiking buck. A short, steep trail leads to the functioning fire lookout, as well as magnificent 360-degree views of the Stuart Range, Teanaway Ridge, Chelan and Entiat Mountains, Mount Rainier and even Mount Adams on a clear day.
properties.title: Red Top Lookout

properties.description: Officially named Robinson Creek, the Middle Fork Pasayten River trail is loved by locals and visitors alike for its big trees, path alongside the wild river, and access into the central Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Robinson Creek (Middle Fork Pasayten River)

properties.description: A hike near Mount Adams.
properties.title: Hellroaring Meadows

properties.description: A scramble up a peak in the Sawtooth region of the North Cascades. Climbing experience strongly recommended.
properties.title: Star Peak

properties.description: A peaceful walk around the wetlands, this is the perfect stroll for someone who wants to experience a little chunk of nature. The tract of wetlands is well-preserved despite being close to town, making the park an attraction for bird-watchers and plant-lovers in the city of Olympia.
properties.title: Grass Lake Nature Park

properties.description: A small park on Bainbridge Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Nute's Pond Park

properties.description: Panther Creek is a small gem in a setting of big gems. The North Cascades boasts some of the biggest, finest views in the country, and quiet, contemplative hikes like Panther Creek can get lost in the mix. Nevertheless, it’s well worth hikers’ time to venture into these forests and meadows to ascend Fourth of July Pass.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Fourth of July Pass via Panther Creek

properties.description: A steep climber's trail with a gorgeous payoff. Wait until the end of summer before attempting, due to snow staying late in high elevations.
properties.title: Neiderprum Trail

properties.description: A climber's trail past the abandoned lookout on Painted Mountain to higher elevations. Experience and comfort with scrambling necessary for this hike.
properties.title: Painted Mountain (Red Mountain)

properties.description: The Teanaway is a fabulous drainage with year-round opportunities. Koppen sits on an easily accessed ridge line which lacks the crowds of many of the other hikes in this area. Commanding views of the Stuart Range, and further away, the Pacific Crest make for stunning scenery. Although this trail’s rewards are an end unto itself, it may also easily be combined with numerous other peaks, ridgelines, or drainages for longer loop trails.
properties.title: Koppen Mountain

properties.description: Topping out at 5,685 feet, High Rock is dramatically higher than its surroundings. On a clear day, the exposed summit provides outstanding views all around and down.  The trail is moderately steep but short, following Sawtooth Ridge 1.6 miles to the summit, where a fire lookout clings to the top.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: High Rock

properties.description: The Cedar Flats Nature trail is an old growth mixed forest of cedar, Douglas fir, and hemlock. It's a peaceful stroll through deep, quiet forest, perfect for children and grown ups alike.
properties.title: Cedar Flats Nature Trail

properties.description: The Copper Creek Trail leaves from Holden Village in the North Cascades. This trail is relatively short but wastes no time in gaining elevation.
properties.title: Copper Basin via Copper Creek

properties.description: Connect campsites along scenic Mayfield Lake with the Ike Kinswa State Park Campground Loop.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Ike Kinswa State Park - Lake Mayfield Trail

properties.description: There are two ways to get to Larch Lake: either up the Chiwaukum Creek trail to a junction with the trail to Larch Lake, or via Alpine Lakes High Camp (reservations required). The coordinates provided are for the Chiwaukum Creek Trail route.
properties.title: Larch Lake

properties.description: Exploring a verdant canyon on the east side of the Kettle Range, Hoodoo Trail makes a great early-season conditioning hike or introduction to overnighting. The hike up Hoodoo Canyon from Trout Lake to Emerald Lake is a classic, low-elevation Inland Northwest hike through one of the largest remaining low-elevation roadless areas in the Kettle Range.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Emerald Lake via Trout Lake Trailhead

properties.description: Whatever you like most about hiking, this trail has something for you, whether it’s a quick ascent, a period of more level ground, a peek-a-boo view, a quintessential Olympic Peninsula rain forest, or a ridge top.
properties.title: Copper Creek

properties.description: This short but steep little trail just east of the Stevens Pass ski area is an excellent little gem in winter or summer. Get a workout, visit a lake, and all in less than half a day, if you hike at a fast clip.
properties.title: Lanham Lake

properties.description: The route to Cardinal Peak is a Class 3 and involves exposed scrambling. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.title: Cardinal Peak

properties.description: Try this long loop for a challenging day hike. There’s not much in the way of camping options, but it’s a great trainer, and you’ll enjoy views of the Stuart Range, but only after you do a little bushwhacking and a lot of climbing. Bring as much water as you can carry – you’ll parallel creeks on the way in and on the way out, but the majority of the hike is high and dry.
properties.title: Miller Peak Loop

properties.description: If nature excites you, there's plenty here to be excited about. Cool forest, trickling creeks in deep ravines, and a beautiful trail built by WTA volunteers await you here.
properties.title: Margaret's Way and Debbie's View

properties.description: Get a workout on this steep hike from Umtanum Creek along the Vista Trail to the ridge above the canyon. In spring, it is filled with wildflowers and birds, with chances of seeing rattlesnakes and bighorn sheep.
properties.title: Umtanum Ridge Crest

properties.description: This trail follows a gentle grade through open forest, some of which is an old burn scar. Huckleberry bushes can be found along the trail, along with a couple peekaboo views of a grassy meadow and Mount Adams.
properties.title: Salt Creek (Mount Adams)

properties.description: Visit Hawk Creek in the winter to amble along its shoreline, or in the summertime for vistas of incredible geologic landmarks.
properties.title: Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area - Hawk Creek

properties.description: Though the road to Purcell Lookout is long washed-out, and the trail can be rugged and hard to follow, those who head here will be rewarded with incredible panoramic views of the stunning South Cascades.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Purcell Lookout

properties.description: Take a trip through the fragrant Teanaway forest, along a burbling creek, and up to a large lake, where equestrians, ORVers, mountain bikers, and hikers can all enjoy the majestic scenery.
properties.title: De Roux Creek to Gallagher Head Lake

properties.description: Multnomah Falls is one of the most beautiful (and popular) in the Columbia River Gorge. And that's saying something, since the Oregon side of the Gorge flows with more than 70 cascades of varying heights. Of course, all that flowing water has made it famous, and its proximity to Portland and Vancouver mean Multnomah is one of the most crowded of these waterfalls as well.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Multnomah Falls

properties.description: This short hike offers a unique experience traversing across a large sandstone feature for much of the trail and offers some of the most spectacular views of the Teanaway Community Forest, with stunning views of Mount Stuart and surrounding peaks on a clear day.
properties.title: Teanaway Community Forest - Cheese Rock Slab

properties.description: Take in beautiful views of Bonaparte Lake, heady pine forest, and beautiful rock gardens in this Eastern Washington escape.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Pipsissewa Trail

properties.description: The route to Dorado Needle is a Class 3 and involves exposed scrambles and glacier crossings. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Dorado Needle

properties.description: Walk through shady woods, across sunny slopes and into an old-growth forest on this pleasant loop hike.
properties.title: Pack Forest - Trail of the Giants

properties.description: A former Native American route into the high country of the South Cascades, the Klickitat Trail traverses a ridgetop between Kilborn Creek to Elk Peak. Views of Mount Adams and the south Cascades are breathtaking on clear days. From the ridgeline, hikers can spot Castle Butte, Jackpot Lake, St. Michaels Lake, and St. John Lake.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Klickitat Trail

properties.description: Stroll a paved path or walk the lakeshore to find the remains of Moncton, now part of the Rattlesnake Lake Recreation Area near North Bend. Moncton was once a stop along the Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul & Pacific Railroad, also known as the Milwaukee Road. The town became Rattlesnake Lake in 1915 when Masonry Dam was constructed on the hillside above.
properties.title: Moncton Ghost Town

properties.description: With a moderate grade on a wide trail, the hike to Talapus Lake is the perfect introduction to the outdoors for hikers and beginning backpackers. Upon arrival at Talapus, break out lunch or pitch camp. Either way, you can cool off in the large lake. If you feel like pressing on, Ollalie Lake is just about a mile and a half up trail, where open campsites offer lakeside havens with calm waters and views of a beautiful lake basin.
properties.title: Talapus and Olallie Lakes

properties.description: A steep and seldom traveled trail settled in what is now Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Nordrum Lake provides giant old-growth conifers, rivers, streams, waterfalls – and quite a workout! This narrow path cuts off the Taylor River/Snoqualmie Lake trail after about 6.5 miles, and doesn’t stop climbing until you reach the lake at about 3675’. But don’t worry, the giant cedars and firs provide shade throughout the entirety of the hike, keeping you cool on even the hottest of summer days.
properties.title: Nordrum Lake
