properties.description: This beautiful trail makes for an excellent overnight or longer day hike.
properties.title: Trap Lake

properties.description: This is the most direct entry to Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park from Seattle, Issaquah and Bellevue. WTA has done lots of work on Cougar Mountain since 2009, but signage may not be entirely up-to-date.
properties.title: Big Tree Ridge

properties.description: SHADOW (Save Habitat And Diversity Of Wetlands) Lake Nature Preserve is a lovely, small park in Renton that is home to a 5,000 year old peat bog with a short, universally-accessible half-mile boardwalk trail that leads into the heart of the bog.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: SHADOW Lake Nature Preserve

properties.description: Following a meandering path along a valley floor and then steeply up to a broad pass, the Fisher Creek Trail is part of a 14 mile traverse of breathtaking high mountain scenery through the eastern side of the North Cascades National Park.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Fisher Creek

properties.description: This forested trail in the North Cascades National Park Complex leads down to Ross Lake and the network of trails in the Ross Lake National Recreation Area. Look out over both Ross Lake and Ross Dam before making your way down to Ross Dam itself
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Ross Dam Trail

properties.description: Shinglemill Creek Preserve is located in the northwest part of Vashon Island and encompasses 168 acres along the lower mainstem of Shinglemill Creek – Vashon’s second-largest creek.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Shinglemill Creek Preserve

properties.description: Mount Spokane State Park has trails for all types, and something for every season. Hike in the summertime to the relocated fire lookout atop Quartz Mountain, or explore the area in a snowy winter wonderland via cross-country skis.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Quartz Mountain

properties.description: Take a mile-long stroll along a gravelled trail through abandoned farm fields. This trail is barrier free, and trail maintenance WTA is performing will greatly improve it, making it more wheelchair friendly in the future.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Sams Walker Nature Trail

properties.description: The Carbon Glacier is a dramatic expanse of slow-moving ice beneath the shadow of Mount Rainier’s north face. While the glacier sits at a relatively low elevation, the approach is long due to the additional 5 miles of road that must be walked or biked to reach the trailhead. The trail to reach the glacier is equally as exciting as the scenery along the way, including seasonal foot logs and a suspension bridge over the raging Carbon River.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Carbon Glacier

properties.description: A way from the Sky Country Trailhead on Cougar Mountain to access the Cave Hole Trail via a loop with Old Man's Trail.
properties.title: Nike Horse Trail

properties.description: This is an easy scramble from the saddle to the north of the much more popular Mount Townsend.
properties.title: Welch Peaks

properties.description: This loop trail winds through the coastal forest of the Weatherwax Preserve and skirts along the edge of Duck Lake, an important wetland ecosystem.
properties.title: Weatherwax Trail

properties.description: Enjoy a nearly-level forest walk with close-up views of beaver dams and likely sightings of water fowl including (in season) trumpeter swans, plus kingfishers, woodpeckers, and owls.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Big Beaver Pond

properties.description: With plenty of options for visitors — including a playground, picnic tables, walking trails and a campground — Flowing Lake Regional Park is a fun destination for a pit stop, an hour, the afternoon or the whole weekend.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Flowing Lake Regional Park

properties.description: As the huckleberries ripen and the cooler weather chases the bugs away, you can experience peace and serenity in the wild at this beautiful lake.
properties.title: Blue Lake via Cultus Creek

properties.description: A scramble and climb in the North Cascades accessible from the Stehekin Valley. Climbing gear and expertise, as well as routefinding experience required.
properties.title: Dark Peak

properties.description: You can hike to Loch Eileen two ways — via a trailhead off Highway 2, or from trails you can access if you reserve a spot at Alpine Lakes High Camp.
properties.title: Lake Julius and Loch Eileen

properties.description: Wynoochee Falls will entice you to spend more time than you’d expect on a half-mile round-trip hike.  The falls are pretty, and the pool at the bottom is nice for wading.  There is a gravel bar that is perfect for picnics, and there are some good rock scrambling options.
properties.title: Wynoochee Falls

properties.description: This fine loop trail gives you scenery, mileage, and some elevation gain, with the bonus of being hikeable year-round. Start by wandering along the Wallace River as it tumbles down from the famous falls.  Get your pictures of the falls, then continue your hike by including the large forested Wallace Lake. Return through a green shag carpet of moss, sword ferns and hemlock, following the North Fork Wallace River as it rushes to meet the main Wallace River and your return trail.
properties.title: Wallace Falls - Lake Loop

properties.description: A steep, yet surprisingly comfortable climb to views of Mount Adams, Mount Rainier, Mount Hood, Glacier Peak and the Olympics.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Norse Peak

properties.description: Description of a winter routefinding scramble to a summit in the Teanaway region. Routefinding and climbing experience highly recommended.
properties.title: Teanaway Butte via Jungle Creek

properties.description: Enjoy some fine ‘forest bathing’ on a quiet trail just off the busy highway. No grand views, but soft green moss, little creeks and large noisy waterfalls will be your reward. It’s nice anytime, but in spring before the highway opens or fall when the vine maple is turning would be a prime time for this one.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Happy-Panther

properties.description: Views of majestic peaks and the vibrant golden hues of larches come autumn - Goat Peak Lookout offers both, as well as the commanding views you'd expect of a working fire lookout. Though steep at times, the trail's short length makes it a perfect hike to introduce kids and newer hikers to the grandeur of the Methow and North Cascades.
properties.title: Goat Peak Lookout

properties.description: Kodak Peak is a side trip deep in the Glacier Peak Wilderness for those on the Pacific Crest Trail. As it's name implies it has amazing views and perhaps more than a few blueberries in season.
properties.title: Kodak Peak

properties.description: Jumbo Peak's wide, grassy slopes and seemingly endless trailside views make hikers feel like they're trekking through a storybook landscape. With huge extinct and active volcanoes in your sights, and an unbelievable bounty of flowers in the spring and huckleberries in the fall, Jumbo lives up to its name--big and impressive on a grand scale.
properties.title: Jumbo Peak

properties.description: The trail is short and the drive is long from the nearest town. It is however a perfect leg stretcher if you are out exploring the remote forests of Central Washington.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Nine Mile Falls

properties.description: This short, ADA-accessible trail offers a different experience at high tide and low, since it’s in a surge plain that’s affected by tidal action.
properties.title: Johns River State Wildlife Area

properties.description: Largely used as a climbing park, Peshastin Pinnacles also makes an ideal stop on Highway 2 to stretch your legs, or as a destination during a visit to Leavenworth, Wenatchee, Cashmere or Chelan. A short trail system offers a nice zigzag, moderately steep loop tour of the base of the climbing areas, and a picnic area makes for a great way to finish the visit off.
properties.title: Peshastin Pinnacles State Park

properties.description: Put your navigational skills to the test! This unmaintained trail just off Damfino Lakes trail may be brushy, but if you can find your way to Boundary Way, you'll be rewarded with breathtaking views into Canada and the epic North Cascades.
properties.title: Boundary Way

properties.description: Enjoy a mix of solitude and company along a ridgetop with two backcountry lakes and sweeping alpine views.
properties.title: Happy Lake Ridge

properties.description: Hike to the three summits of French Cabin Mountain ending with a class-3 scramble on West Peak.
properties.title: French Cabin Mountain

properties.description: A short one-mile trail that connects to the Iron Horse Trail and provides climbing access to various walls off the south side of I-90.
properties.title: Deception Crags

properties.description: Follow a bootpath along Teanaway Ridge from Iron Bear to the nearby Jester Mountain summit.
properties.title: Jester Mountain

properties.description: Ruby Creek is a short, mellow river ramble that is often traveled as a part of the longer Devils Dome Loop.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Ruby Creek

properties.description: Lewis & Clark State Park contains one of the last intact stands of old-growth forest remaining in the Cowlitz Valley, as well as five miles of trails for hikers to explore.
properties.title: Lewis and Clark State Park

properties.description: A quick hike up to a summit outside of Wenatchee with views of the Columbia River, Horse Lake Mountain, Mission Ridge, and the Enchantments.
properties.title: Chopper Peak

properties.description: Join mountain bikes on this hike with access to many trails all around Tradition Lake, including the Adventure Trail, the Gas Trail, the Wetlands Trail, Section Line Trail, and Bus Trail.
properties.title: Bonneville Trail

properties.description: Still under development, the Gee Creek Trail will ultimately be the backbone of the City of Ridgefield’s trail network. Named after the stream it follows, the route will extend approximately 4 miles from the high school at the south end of the city, and connect to Ridgefield National Wildlife Refuge, just north of the city limits.
properties.title: Gee Creek

properties.description: Starting out along Carey Creek, the Sherwood Trail climbs to a high point on the eastern edge of Taylor Mountain.
properties.title: Sherwood Trail

properties.description: The route to Primus Peak involves exposed climbing and glacier travel. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Primus Peak

properties.description: If you'd like nose-to-nose access to Mount Baker, this first-rate woodsy walk delivers. Over a relatively short, well-maintained trail with mild elevation gain, you can be glacier-side in no time... if the creek crossings allow.
properties.title: Heliotrope Ridge

properties.description: Explore the back door to Hamilton Mountain on the double-track Equestrian Trail. Former logging roads now act as service roads for the park staff and multi-use trails for hikers, bicycles and equestrians to reach the park’s backcountry trails.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Equestrian Trail

properties.description: This remote trail in the Pasayten follows an old mining road up to a pass before dropping down into the adjacent valley and linking up with the unmaintained Mill Creek Trail.
properties.title: Cady Pass

properties.description: This is a climbing route (not a hiking trail) and should only be attempted by experienced climbers. Note that this area is incredibly sensitive; pack out all garbage and human waste.
properties.title: Gunn Peak

properties.description: You'll work up a sweat on this easy to moderate hike to the spectacular Teneriffe Falls. Go in the spring when the tread is snow-free and the waterfall is flowing at full volume. Along the way, you'll be rewarded with views of the surrounding Snoqualmie valley and nearby peaks.
properties.title: Teneriffe Falls

properties.description: Each year, from fall to spring, this area is a bird paradise, with snow geese and trumpeter and tundra swans overwintering in huge numbers. There are several access points in the wildlife refuge. The Headquarters area has a two mile trail and staff may be able to point you to other appropriate areas to visit.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Skagit Wildlife Area

properties.description: A short one-mile loop in the Pioneer Square neighborhood of Seattle outlining the redlined neighborhood in the area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redlining Heritage Trail - Pioneer Square

properties.description: Here is a little largely-forgotten alpine gem nestled in amongst white granite and grizzled pine trees.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Maxwell Lake (Oregon)

properties.description: Use this trail to hike a loop with Snowgrass Trail (96) and the Pacific Crest Trail (2000), or use it to skip (bypass) the crowds at Snowgrass Flats by heading straight over to the PCT.
properties.title: Bypass Trail

properties.description: Located on the north shore of Clear Lake, this interpretive trail forms a lollipop loop that is accessible for all users.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Clear Lake Interpretive Trail

properties.description: A close-in hike near Kirkland. The perfect after-work way to unwind.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Crestwoods Park Trail

properties.description: The Whidbey Institute includes a 106-acre conservation forest with 4.5 miles of trails that are hilly but all below 500 feet. This hike is deep in the forest and very quiet. You will see lots of ferns, cedars and Douglas fir trees.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Whidbey Institute

properties.description: Rampart Lakes is a pretty collection of pothole lakes with a maze of social trails lacing them together. Though doable as a day hike, it is better enjoyed as an overnight destination, with nearby Alta Mountain and Lila Lake making excellent side trips.
properties.title: Rampart Ridge - Rampart Lakes

properties.description: The Chapin Trail is part of the City of Bellevue’s Parks and Open Trails System. The short loop will take you through a charming forested area within a residential neighborhood.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Chapin Trail

properties.description: Devils Peak requires scrambling up the mountain.
properties.title: Devils Peak

properties.description: The entire West Fork Humptulips trail is 17 miles long. As such, it offers access to several other trails in the area, long riverside rambles, and a multi-day beginner backpacking option.
properties.title: West Fork Humptulips River

properties.description: Hike to a viewpoint on the Kettle Crest trail that was the site of a former fire lookout.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Old Stagecoach Trail to Copper Butte

properties.description: This hike is a nice, long road walk leading to a trail, a good alternate to the Klickitat Rail Trail for a change of scenery.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Klickitat Haul Road

properties.description: Visit Rustler's Gulch to enjoy in year-round wetlands, seasonal wildflowers, and an abundance of wildlife.
properties.title: Little Spokane Wildlife Area: Rustler's Gulch - Holly Road Loop

properties.description: Sailing and hiking in the San Juan Islands is always special. It can be even more so when you are alone on an island all your own.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Blind Island

properties.description: Hike a paved 0.1 mile trail ending at the beautiful Madison Falls.
properties.title: Madison Falls

properties.description: The two-story frame cabin of Mount Fremont, built in 1934, provides an opportunity to reminisce about the time when watchmen stood guard over the forest, with an eye out for wildfires.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Fremont Lookout

properties.description: A classic hike in any season, but come in winter and you’ll find that the hordes of tourists, hikers, and climbers who use this trail in the summer have dwindled to just a trickle.
properties.title: Hoh River Trail to Five Mile Island

properties.description: A stroll north on the Pacific Crest Trail to tranquil Lake Janus and neighboring Grizzly Peak offers panoramas of the Central Cascades’ finest peaks and undulating meadows blanketed with wildflowers as far as the eye can see. Traveled by sauntering day hikers, first-time backpackers and dedicated thru-hikers bound for Canada, this well-graded trail has a little something for everyone.
properties.title: Lake Janus and Grizzly Peak

properties.description: The sight and roaring sound of Robinson Creek will accompany you on your forested hike up the valley, following in the footsteps of an early trapper, Billy Robinson.  The low starting elevation makes this a popular late spring/early summer day-hike or overnight.
properties.title: Robinson Creek - South

properties.description: The route to Mount Rahm is a Class 5 and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Mount Rahm

properties.description: Pyramid Mountain is a scenic trail that starts high and stays high. From the trailhead ad 6200 feet, hikers will continue along ridgelines and shallow valleys before making the final ascent to Pyramid Mountain at 8260 feet.
properties.title: Pyramid Mountain

properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Boundary Bay Regional Park

properties.description: A half-mile ramble through quiet forest near Skykomish.
properties.title: Maloney Creek Interpretive Trail

properties.description: If you want to take a quick hike near the Renewable Energy Center of the Wild Horse Wind and Solar Facility, then this is your trail. The trail descends through rigid sage, balsamroot, buckwheat, and bitterroot which thrive in the thin rocky soil on the hillside.
properties.title: Whiskey Dick Wildlife Area - Bitterroot Trail

properties.description: A relatively new feature to northeast Washington’s extensive recreational repertoire, the Ferry County Rail Trail is a 25+-mile long, multi-use, non-motorized rail trail.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Ferry County Rail Trail

properties.description: The eastern section of the Burnt Bridge Creek Trail follows the creek from Meadowbrook Marsh to Devine Road. This section of the trail features meadows and wetlands which host a variety of wildlife, including beavers, deer, and assorted birds. The creek flows through willows, cottonwoods, and red osier dogwood. The understory includes wild roses, spirea, and thimbleberry.
properties.title: Burnt Bridge Creek - Eastern Section

properties.description: Wander across the Long Beach peninsula to see thousands of shorebirds during spring and fall and enjoy the coastal forest along the way.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Bearberry Trail

properties.description: Hike to a small scenic lake on the flanks of Mount Pilchuck. The trail is a bit rough, but its ease of access, short mileage and modest elevation gain make this one of the easier hikes on the Mountain Loop Highway
properties.title: Heather Lake

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Ipsut Falls

properties.description: Ruby Mountain is a 7,408-foot peak in the center of the North Cascades. It has one of the best panoramic views of the lakes, snow-capped peaks and glaciers of the North Cascades National Park.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Ruby Mountain

properties.description: This lightly used connector trail to the Pacific Crest Trail provides an easier “back door” approach to Big Huckleberry Mountain on an in-and-out hike.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Cedar Creek

properties.description: Take a waterside walk along Wiley Slough in the Skagit Wildlife area on Fir Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Wiley Slough - Fir Island

properties.description: The Chiwawa River Trail offers hikers the rugged scenery that's the signature of the Glacier Peak Wilderness but for less effort than other hikes nearby. Try this trail to enjoy solitude while basking in sublime mountain scenery.
properties.title: Chiwawa River

properties.description: Forbidden Peak is one of Washington's 100 steepest peaks. The route to Forbidden Peak is a Class 5 and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Forbidden Peak

properties.description: A winter climb that will require crampons or microspikes, routefinding skills and, in the right conditions, climbing gear.
properties.title: Mount Angeles Snowshoe

properties.description: Whether you’re in the area or just driving through, Diablo Lake is always a good spot to stop and take in the North Cascades. If you want to extend your stop into a hike, check out the Sourdough Creek Trail. This short and moderate trail traverses through lush, mossy forest and leads you up to the Sourdough Creek waterfalls. With wildlife, mountain and lake views and plenty of rest stops, this trail is perfect for all ages.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Sourdough Creek

properties.description: This is one of the longest hike options in Capitol State Forest -- weaving through wooded valleys and along quietly flowing creeks, visitors here may discover not only natural wonders but also relics from the time that this area was the home of many a logging show.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Sherman Creek Loop

properties.description: Explore 11,000 acres of old farm land and grassy meadows in the heart of Central Washington. With three trailhead access points, the area provides hikers with plenty of opportunity to see wildflowers, old farm equipment, and vernal ponds.
properties.title: Telford Recreation Area

properties.description: This short, easy ridge walk climbs to a small summit with huge Cascade views and a chance to see mountain goats.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Burnt Mountain

properties.description: Begin your hike up High Point Trail in wooded, steep terrain, passing a junction with the Lingering Trail and eventually joining up with the Tiger Mountain Trail.
properties.title: High Point Trail

properties.description: Dishman Hills Natural Area's Goldback Spring Loop is located southeast of the main parking area at Camp Caro. The best way to access the Goldback Spring Loop is by combining a trip here with the Deep Ravine Loop.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Natural Area - Goldback Springs

properties.description: Often used as a connector to create larger loops, the Deer Park trail ventures through an old fire area into the wild Pasayten wilderness.
properties.title: Deer Park

properties.description: Oregon white oak woodlands with open ridgetop meadows, wildflowers, and views of the White Salmon Valley make this a delightful hike that is off the beaten track.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Weldon Wagon Road

properties.description: This 6-acre greenspace in residential Bellevue connects to other greenspaces nearby, including Forest Hill Neighborhood Park and Cougar Mountain.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Somerset Greenbelts

properties.description: Do a thru-hike on the main Tiger Mountain Trail, also known as the TMT. Arrange a car shuttle and start at the southern end. Hike north more than fifteen miles over varied terrain and through different types of forest vegetation. Pass a large glacial erratic boulder, and visit some of the most remote places in the Tigers.
properties.title: Tiger Mountain Trail

properties.description: The route to Copper Peak is a Class 4-5 and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Copper Peak

properties.description: A connector trail on Tiger Mountain. Access to or from West Tiger 3, Nook Trail, and Section Line Trail.
properties.title: Talus Rock Trail

properties.description: Dirty Face Lookout is one of the earliest high Central Cascade trails to melt out. At four miles and with 4000 feet of elevation gain, the trail provides hikers with a very good workout. Along the way, you'll have lots to look at, as the elevation change can roll an entire season of wildflowers into a single hike. Rock roses and paintbrush bob near the trailhead, while avalanche lilys sway in the breeze near the summit. When you aren't looking at the wildflowers, the vistas are outstanding.
properties.title: Dirty Face Lookout and Peak

properties.description: A beautiful rocky outcropping provides eye-popping views of Mount Adams.
properties.title: Sleeping Beauty Peak

properties.description: Short loop trails through fields with views of Mount Baker.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Curry Preserve

properties.description: Beautiful views, amazing wildflowers, oak woodlands, open grasslands—this short hike is the perfect way to sample the best of the Catherine Creek area. More than 90 varieties of wildflowers bloom here, making this a favorite springtime destination.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Catherine Creek - Universal Access Trail

properties.description: This is a great weekend backpacking trip for wildflower lovers. Miles of wildflowers along Meander Meadow and Cady Ridge will delight the hiker who passes through during July and August. Fantastic views of the Cascades, Glacier Peak and plunging valleys add to the allure, and it's all packaged up in a 16-mile loop.
properties.title: Meander Meadow - Dishpan Gap - Cady Ridge Loop

properties.description: A strenuous snowshoe trip leads to Buck Mountain Lookout with contrasting views of forest and fire. Whether the views are worth the effort is up to the traveler!
properties.title: Buck Mountain Snowshoe

properties.description: Bogachiel Peak sits above the dramatic Seven Lakes Basin. While you might expect stunning views here, such is not the case. The treed peak has limited views from the top, but it's a short enough side trip, why not make a stop while you're there?
properties.title: Bogachiel Peak

properties.description: The Palisades Conservation Area must have been what the Chamber of Commerce had in mind when it came up with the Spokane logo, “Near Nature, Near Perfect.” Visitors to this city park can both view wildlife and native plants in the foreground and peer out over the cityscape from the edge of the basalt cliffs.
properties.title: Palisades Park

properties.description: This challenging trail is unmaintained by the Forest Service and has been nearly erased by years of damage and blowdowns. Hiking it is not recommended.
properties.title: Hidden Springs

properties.description: Take a short hike through a shady forest to a plunge pool at the base of a sweet waterfall.
properties.title: Langfield Falls

properties.description: This steep connector trail between the Paris Creek and Boulder De Roux trails takes hikers past remnants of old mining activity in the area.
properties.title: Elsnor Mine

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Black Peak

properties.description: This is an 8-mile section of the longer Palouse to Cascades trail.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Army East

properties.description: One of three ways to reach the summit of Mount Zion. It's steep, but short, and you'll be rewarded with view of the Olympics at the top.
properties.title: Snow Creek

properties.description: The paved sidewalk and trail that encircles this large lake in the heart of Olympia serves as a popular location year-round for locals and visitors to run, walk and hike. Additionally, trails to the south along the west edge of Capitol Lake lead to an Interpretive Park, for you to extend your hike.
properties.title: Capitol Lake Trails (Marathon Park and Heritage Park)

properties.description: Found within the Glacier Peak Wilderness, the 45 Mile Sheep Drive trail begins at the Entiat River Trail, and ends at Emerald Park Trail. It's a 4.9-mile, rugged, primitive trail. As such, it is not regularly maintained and not recommended for stock. It was burned in the 2006 Tinpan Fire and there may be blowdown from this incident. Hikers will find it very steep and some routefinding may be required.
properties.title: 45 Mile Sheep Drive

properties.description: The Port Susan Nature Preserve is a small part of the Port Susan Bay Preserve and contains restored tidal wetlands that is home to a variety of fish, birds, and native plants. The preserve is open to the public between February and October, and you must contact the Nature Conservancy for a parking pass and liability waiver to visit.
properties.title: Port Susan Nature Conservancy

properties.description: Hike the southernmost part of the main Tiger Mountain Trail - the TMT - and return via the South Tiger Traverse to complete a loop around South Tiger Mountain, with a side trip to the south summit and, optionally, a visit to the north summit.
properties.title: South Tiger Mountain Loop

properties.description: This trail takes hikers out of the maze of trails at Paradise and up onto one of the many glaciers on Washington's most iconic mountains.
properties.title: Paradise Glacier

properties.description: This trail has spectacular views into the high country and is well worth the effort it takes to get to the top.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Three Forks

properties.description: Stroll in a peaceful slice of nature tucked into south Richland, enjoying old-growth sagebrush, wildflowers, willows, and cattails. Bring your binoculars to watch birds and riparian wildlife.
properties.title: Amon Basin Natural Preserve

properties.description: A roughly 4-mile loop near the city of Puyallup, where locals and visitors can get their exercise and spend some time on trail near an urban center.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Puyallup Loop Trail

properties.description: This 120-acre forest is on private property on Guemes Island managed as forest land, and has 3 miles of trails open to the public to explore.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Dog Woods

properties.description: The Gloyd Seeps Wildlife Area is part of the Columbia Basin Wildlife Area. This long, narrow parcel follows along crab creek through channeled scablands and shrub steppe.
properties.title: Gloyd Seeps - North

properties.description: The Highlands Trail forms a loop around the Highlands neighborhood in the city of Newcastle.
properties.title: Highlands Loop - Newcastle

properties.description: In winter, the Bagley Lakes Loop and Chain Lakes trail creates an intermediate snowshoeing opportunity near the schussing skiers in the Mount Baker Ski Area.
properties.title: Bagley Lakes Snowshoe

properties.description: This accessible trail to Sunset Falls is a great option for hikers of all experience levels. It’s located right next to a campground and day-use area.
properties.title: Sunset Falls

properties.description: Here’s a shortish, moderate trail in the Eagle Creek Recreation Area. You’ll enjoy a nice view of the Bonneville Dam as well as the Columbia River Gorge and even a bit of the upvalley views of the Eagle Creek drainage.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Wauna Viewpoint

properties.description: In one trip you can traverse over five mountain passes, visit four mountain lakes and groves of larches, and experience some of the most remote edges of the Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Billy Goat Loop

properties.description: This short, but steep, hiker-only trail leads to a small, forested lake with a large campsite. The trail is mostly covered in forest duff due to the limited foot traffic, making the climb much more pleasant, as do the berries in late summer.
properties.title: Little Joe Lake

properties.description: Those new to snowshoeing will appreciate the easy access and groomed trails found at Segelsen Creek Sno-Park, along with the mountain views and options for extended exploration.
properties.title: Segelsen Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: Hike up and down (and up again and down again, and then up one more time) around this loop in the northern part of Olympic National Park. You'll get stunning mountain views, pass tranquil lakes, and laze around in gorgeous alpine meadows, and you'll need that break, because the elevation gain on this one is no joke.
properties.title: Grand Valley - Cameron Creek Loop

properties.description: This short dayhike on the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) is a nice alternate route to quiet Mirror Lake, or just a lovely forest hike on a quiet section of a rocky and rooty trail. You could consider it as a first-time backpacking destination, too, since the trail is never particularly steep here.
properties.title: Mirror Lake via the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT)

properties.description: Hike through some of the nicest second-growth forest in the area, and reach the second-highest summit in the Tigers. Then enjoy a superb viewpoint a short distance west of the summit.
properties.title: West Tiger No. 1 via Dwight's Way

properties.description: A short loop trail appropriate for all ages and abilities, this little walk provides an opportunity for anyone to appreciate the history of Longmire while immersing themselves in nature. It can also act as a mellow warm-up for the steep Rampart Ridge Trail.
properties.title: Trail of the Shadows

properties.description: Shaw Lake is a small pond in Wallace Falls State Park, without formal trails accessing it.
properties.title: Shaw Lake

properties.description: Located at the head of Hood Canal, Theler Wetlands consists of more than 3 miles of accessible walking trails within 139 acres of protected salt marsh and estuary wetlands. If they’re open, you and your family can discover the displays and hands-on exhibits that teach more about the wetlands ecosystem.
properties.title: Mary E. Theler Wetlands Nature Preserve

properties.description: This long trail extends all the way from the base of Multnomah Falls to the summit of Larch Mountain, 7.7 miles away. It’s a popular out and back, and links to many other trails to make loops in the Columbia River Gorge. Because of its length and location, it runs the gamut of quality, from wide and paved to rugged, narrow, and infrequently-maintained. But don’t worry, it’s steep for quite a lot of the length, so you’ll get a workout no matter what.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Larch Mountain

properties.description: Play with the family on trails here, or if rain strikes, head indoors to check out the facilities at South Bellevue Community Center.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Eastgate Park

properties.description: Formerly a popular hot springs site, Kennedy Hot Springs were buried in a 2003 flood. They are now inaccessible.
properties.title: Kennedy Hotsprings

properties.description: With options on which way you want to hike, this destination offers great backpacking opportunities and beautiful views.
properties.title: Boulder Creek - Gallagher Head Lake

properties.description: On the edge of Capitol Hill in the city of Seattle, this urban oasis separates the neighborhood from I-5.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: St. Marks Greenbelt

properties.description: A section of the Wonderland Trail. It is a strenuous hike with ample elevation gain and loss through lowland forests, valleys, into high alpine and sub-alpine areas. You move through forests with moss and ferns, wildflower-filled rolling meadows, and along hillsides covered in beargrass and thick with huckleberry bushes.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Wonderland Trail - Mowich to Longmire

properties.description: This short trail connects the River Loop and The Trail of Cedars in the Newhalem Campground. If you are staying in the campground, this is a great alternative to walking the hot gravel campground road.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Linking Trail

properties.description: Climb Alger Alp for a straightforward day hike or after-work ascent, with a steady climb along an access road through second-growth forest. Soak in the wildflowers and fauna along the way, and views of Skagit Valley, Blanchard Mountain and Samish Bay await you at the summit.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Alger Alp (South Route)

properties.description: Share trip reports from your own backyard while we observe Stay Home, Stay Healthy and work together to slow the spread of coronavirus.
properties.title: My Backyard

properties.description: A longer, steeper, pass free, alternate route to the summit of Mount Zion.
properties.title: Deadfall

properties.description: The  Wolf Creek trail departs Hurricane Ridge and plunges eight miles downhill to Whiskey Bend in the Elwha River Valley. It's a lovely route that gets little use along its entire length, though many people wander a couple miles down its length before heading back up.
properties.title: Wolf Creek

properties.description: Follow the footsteps of 19th-century homesteaders for a half mile along a scenic creek that connects historic buildings and surrounding nature to our present story.
properties.title: Olmstead Place Historical State Park

properties.description: This is a scenic, easy to moderate hike or snowshoe up a broad canyon with a good chance of spotting bands of elk.
properties.title: Oak Creek Road - Bethel Ridge

properties.description: A snowy ramble along a river east of Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Cooper River Snowshoe

properties.description: Spencer Spit State Park is located on the northeast corner of Lopez Island in the San Juan Islands. A campground sits at the northern edge of the park. The network of hiking trails loops around the edge of the park, heads along the edge of a lagoon and extends out onto the spit.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Spencer Spit

properties.description: The hike to Stafford Falls drops steeply from the road, requiring a climb to return to your vehicle. But after 0.4 miles, it follows crystal-clear Chinook Creek as it cascades down a gentle slope, with small plunges, narrow chutes, beautiful blue-green pools, and a 25-foot punch-bowl waterfall. Such beauty and serenity are seldom this easy to get to.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Stafford Falls via Deer Creek

properties.description: Mount Bonaparte, the tallest mountain in the Okanogan Highlands, dominates its corner of the world. The summit is 2500 feet higher than nearby Strawberry Mountain, and is 3700 feet higher than Bonaparte Lake. A very fine loop hike is available that will take you all the way around the mountain, with a short dash to the summit lookout included. Once you have completely surrounded Bonaparte, you can claim your own Waterloo success.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Mount Bonaparte Circumnavigation

properties.description: This short loop trail around a quiet lake is a great place to enjoy an after-work outdoor stroll or take the kids on an easy outdoor excursion.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Squires Lake Park

properties.description: This trail is currently under construction, and will eventually become a 42-mile urban route connecting Renton and Snohomish County.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Eastrail

properties.description: This hike is actual a twofer, forking to two paths each leading to a waterfall – go up to Upper McCord Creek’s twin waterfalls, or down to the towering Elowah Falls.  Each waterfall has its own character and it is worth visiting both of them.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Elowah and Upper McCord Creek Falls

properties.description: From Eastern Washington’s second-highest peak, the former home to Eastern Washington’s second-highest lookout, take in hundreds of square miles of rolling forested terrain, from the Canadian Purcells to the Columbia Plateau.
properties.title: Abercrombie Mountain Trail

properties.description: Mount Lillian makes for a great day hike in spring, with its fabulous wildflowers and miles of incredible views paired with mild elevation gains (and mostly good trail).
properties.title: Mount Lillian

properties.description: The iconic Palouse Falls -- Washington State's official falls -- is not to be missed.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Palouse Falls

properties.description: Beaver Lake is a nice short walk through starkly beautiful terrain still recovering from the Okanagon Complex fires in 2015.
properties.title: Beaver Lake

properties.description: Follow the Little Wenatchee River all the way to its headwaters high on the Cascade crest. From mile-high, miles-long alpine meadows, the river meanders. And so will you upon reaching these heavenly flower gardens. The hike in is a long approach and is warm at times across brushy avalanche slopes, but it is worth every ounce of sweat expended and every annoying fly swatted.
properties.title: Meander Meadows

properties.description: Take this lung-busting trail up the north side of Mount Townsend, through coniferous forests offering cameo views to the Strait of Juan de Fuca to the north, opening onto views of the Dungeness and Graywolf watersheds to the west.
properties.title: Little Quilcene River

properties.description: Beautiful multi-day hike that shows off the beauty of the Hoh Rainforest. Hike on relatively level ground until the last two miles, which climb to Elk Lake Campground, a good place to start a day hike to the glacier.
properties.title: Hoh River Trail to Elk Lake

properties.description: Whether you’d like a peaceful break from everyday life or just some exercise, the Salmon Creek Trail is for you. This paved trail takes you through wetlands, around ponds, and across a natural habitat undergoing restoration. Within minutes you can leave city life behind and be immersed in picture-perfect scenery accompanied by the sound of birds. The trail is easily accessible, making it a perfect quick get-away.
properties.title: Salmon Creek Trail

properties.description: Along with the numerous other I-90 hikes there is no shortage of ‘workout’ on this hike. Like its counterparts, this trail is largely for those interested in heading up, steeply. Moderated with switchbacks at times, and with a gradual traverse when you need it, the rewards here are not without effort. The actual summit is a rock-scramble, but the views and the flower-packed west facing slope near the top can be enjoyed without making the true top. More than a few remaining old-growth trees and a soft tread make this a well-rounded hike whether it is a training hike or your weekend reward.
properties.title: McClellan Butte

properties.description: From spring flowers to summer berries to fall colors to winter vistas, this trail through the Columbia Highlands has something new to offer each season of the year. In the warmer months, try the circumnavigation of Sherman Peak plus the bonus excursion out to picturesque Snow Peak cabin. Plan ahead and rent the cabin, which is reservable for $55 per night for up to four people, year-round.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Snow Peak

properties.description: This trail welcomes hikers, equestrians, and ORVs alike an a trail that climbs from Bonaparte Lake to the still actively staffed Bonaparte Lookout. Two lookout, the historic and the more modern one, perch and squat respectively atop the summit of Bonaparte.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Bonaparte Trail

properties.description: Hike along the northern half of the main Tiger Mountain Trail, the TMT. If you like, make it a shorter hike and turn around at any of a number of pleasant stopping spots, or perhaps hike on as far as Custer's Bridge, one of the most remote places in the Tigers.
properties.title: Tiger Mountain Trail North

properties.description: From Navaho Pass, the trail to Navaho Peak is siren-like, pulling you towards the summit long after you realize how tired you are. But for peak-baggers, or those simply interested in getting a gorgeous view from a relatively easy-to-navigate peak, the views are worth the extra effort.
properties.title: Navaho Peak

properties.description: The summit of Thorp Mountain can be accessed from a variety of trails, and the winter route up any of them requires a good amount of preparation and research -- it is not a route for novice winter hikers. Have route-finding experience as well as good traction devices, a navigation reference before you go. The ability to evaluate slopes for avalanche risk can also be useful.
properties.title: Thorp Mountain - Winter

properties.description: Hike a steep trail to a rocky perch with views of Lake Cushman and the southeastern corner of the Olympic Mountains.
properties.title: Mount Rose

properties.description: A beautiful loop trail on the north side of Mount Rainier, this is a shorter, but no less lovely, option to the Wonderland Trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Northern Loop

properties.description: This small network of trails between Anacortes and Burlington offers a nice outing for kids and adults alike.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Port of Skagit Trails

properties.description: Nestled between Spiral Butte and Cramer Mountain on the Tumac Plateau, Cramer Lake draws experienced snowshoers north into the backcountry for peace and solitude just east of White Pass. Although the distance is moderate, a section of steep terrain and creek crossings can make for an adventuresome outing.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Cramer Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: The route to Alaska Lake travels through avalanche terrain. Have avalanche awareness skills, the ability to identify avalanche risk and the proper gear before going.
properties.title: Alaska Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: In the heart of Fidalgo Island lies a natural gem of a forest with wetlands, lakes, and rocky bald meadows with great views. This nice little hike will take you around the lake on a hiker only trail.  Take this hike in spring for the fresh new leaves and the dainty spring flowers, or visit on a rainy day in winter and watch the mist float above the lake among the trees. The lake is very popular on hot summer days.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Whistle Lake

properties.description: This short hike offers something to please the geology buff and the shutterbug alike.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Conservation Area - Rocks of Sharon

properties.description: Hikers can choose from an easy loop partially along Happy Creek, or a longer hike to Happy Creek Falls, site of an old sawmill that supported the mining in the late 1800's.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Happy Creek Nature Trail

properties.description: More than 5,000 acres of marshes, grasslands and wooded areas are home to more than one hundred species of birds, waterfowl and fish. The refuge has a $3 entry fee, which can be waived with an America the Beautiful/Interagency pass.
properties.title: Ridgefield National Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: Hike from a transmission line on the north side of Tiger Mountain to various trails on the mountain.
properties.title: Preston Trail

properties.description: A very remote trail in the Colville National Forest with lake views and narrow, rugged tread.
properties.title: Schalow

properties.description: This quiet, little-used trail wanders through a lowland forest and up the South side of Squak Mountain along Bullitt Creek.
properties.title: May Valley Trail

properties.description: This loop in Yacolt Burn State Forest makes for a lovely day hike with some great views of the forest and the lowland at the base of the forest. The 3-mile Silver Shadow connector makes this loop possible, and exists thanks to efforts from Washington Trails Association, Back Country Horsemen, Washington Conservation Corps, and DNR.
properties.title: Silver Shadow Loop

properties.description: A trail that goes from the Estes Butte Lookout site to Carne Mountain. Some parts may be overgrown and blowdown should be expected.
properties.title: Old Gib

properties.description: You’ll not meet any hunters in Indian Henry’s Hunting Ground these days, but the area is named for one of the most prominent Native American guides in the area, who lived here before it became a national park. Accessible via Longmire or the West Side road, this destination promises abundant wildflowers and berries, as well as excellent up-close views of "The Mountain."
properties.title: Indian Henry's Hunting Ground via Tahoma Creek

properties.description: Timberlake Park consists of 24 acres in the city of Issaquah. While most of the park is forested, the trail leads to the Lake Sammamish shoreline, including a beach area.
properties.title: Timberlake Park

properties.description: Judge Jack Tanner Park features barbeques and areas for families to enjoy views of Puget Sound and the surrounding vistas. Come for a picnic or just to relax, or take Ruston Way -- the hard-surface trail running through the middle of the park -- for a longer stroll along the waterfront.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Judge Jack Tanner Park

properties.description: The Leavenworth Fish Hatchery, on the National Register of Historic Places, is a charming location that provides education about salmon and their life cycles, all on the scenic Icicle River. This is but one hike you can do at the hatchery; create your own hike on its 5 miles of trails.
properties.title: Leavenworth Fish Hatchery

properties.description: This lovely trail through the Glacier View Wilderness can take you across the Wilderness, starting on a ridge with filtered views of Rainier, down past Beljica Meadows Lake(s) up and over a ridge to lovely Goat Lake. Continue up the trail to the National Park boundary and one can continue on to Gobbler's Knob and the old fire lookout there.
properties.title: Puyallup

properties.description: A hike through a gorgeous old growth forest offering excellent views of nearby summits in the Okanogan Highlands.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sweat Creek Basin Trail

properties.description: For a nice location in the Central Cascades, try this rail trail along the western shore of Lake Keechelus. This is a treat for new snowshoers, especially if it has been recently groomed. Because of its easy accessibility, it can often get crowded on nicer days.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Lake Keechelus

properties.description: A short backpacking trip or a long dayhike, the Frying Pan Loop winds hikers through meadows, past lakes, and up to the summit of Frying Pan Mountain.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Frying Pan Loop

properties.description: This hike is in a privately owned forest. The public is allowed to recreate here with a permit that is sold by the land owner.
properties.title: Lake Hancock

properties.description: The 230-acre Washington Park Arboretum offers miles of trails that wind through forests of maples, magnolias, oaks, salmonberry, and the famous Azalea Way. Visit the Pacific Connections Gardens to see a variety of plant life from  various countries that border the Pacific Ocean, or lose yourself in the many groves of trees that line the paths in the park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Washington Park Arboretum

properties.description: A moderate snowshoe along forest roads to a beautiful frozen pond just outside of Yakima.
properties.title: Tieton Pond Snowshoe

properties.description: This short, steep hike leads to an abandoned lookout site, where nature has obscured the views with tree growth.  A careful descent to the southeast from the lookout site leads to the top of a steep rocky area with magnificent views of Mount Rainier and the Greenwater River Valley – just don’t lose your footing if you're snapping pics at the peak!
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Colquhoun Peak

properties.description: Beginning at Forest Road 9712 and ending at the Forest Boundary, the Old Ellensburg Trail comprises one-third of the three trails used to make a popular loop around Mount Lillian.
properties.title: Old Ellensburg

properties.description: This unmaintained trail follows Dexter Ridge south across the Washington-Oregon border and down to the Wenaha River.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Dexter Ridge

properties.description: The Bay View State Park on Padilla Bay has plenty of activities and amenities.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Bay View State Park

properties.description: At 1300 feet, Mount Erie marks the high point of Fidalgo Island. While it's accessible via a road, the hike up to the summit is heart-pounding, and makes an excellent outing for the day, or just a few hours.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Mount Erie

properties.description: Located in Central Oregon, this delightful hike in an extremely popular state park is a great day hike diversion for those hoping to venture deeper into Oregon.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Silver Falls State Park

properties.description: A climb off I-90 near Melakwa Lake. Gear and climbing experience required.
properties.title: Mount Roosevelt

properties.description: Log some easy trail mileage by hopping on this family-friendly trail anywhere between Woodard Bay and Vail for a relaxing stroll any time of year.
properties.title: Chehalis Western Trail

properties.description: Boulder Cave formed millions of years ago from volcanic activity. Today, the cave is home to a dwindling population of Pacific western big-eared bats.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Boulder Cave

properties.description: A connector trail between the Boulder Garden Loop to the main Mount Si trail in the Mount Si Natural Resources Conservation Area.
properties.title: Douglas Fir

properties.description: Beaver Marsh Park is a 32-acre forested city-owned natural area in Vancouver bisected by Burnt Bridge Creek. The level 0.65-mile trail crosses the creek twice as it loops through the park.
properties.title: Beaver Marsh Loop

properties.description: The Little Kachess Trail is a rough rollercoaster of a hike that bounds along the western shore of Little Kachess Lake. Not to be confused with a lakeside stroll, this moderately strenuous trail climbs and drops repeatedly in an attempt to avoid cliffs while providing occasional access to the lakeshore.
properties.title: Little Kachess

properties.description: Snowshoe around a lake in the Salmon La Sac area; you'll share the area with motorized users, as well.
properties.title: Cooper Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: The Bygone Byways Interpretive Trail is an easy loop trail that follows the Great Northern Railway. The trail is entirely ADA-accessible and has several interpretive signs about the natural and cultural history of the area.
properties.title: Bygone Byways Interpretive Trail

properties.description: Maidenhair Falls is proof that you don’t have to hike long distances to see beautiful scenery.  A mere half mile from the trailhead, this waterfall and gorge is sure to delight.
properties.title: Maidenhair Falls

properties.description: Seattle has many pocket parks and natural areas where native species of floral and fauna make their home. The Union Bay Natural Area is one of these wonderful little spots that offers a natural environment within easy reach of many city dwellers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Union Bay Natural Area

properties.description: This community forest is managed as a nature reserve, where hikers will find a wide ranging variety of wildlife, and a retreat from the noise and bustle of city life.
properties.title: Canyon Lake Community Forest

properties.description: The Six Ridge Trail is a rugged route that traverses the South Fork to the North Fork of the Skokomish River. It is known for its solitude, meadows and grand mountain vistas, but it comes at a price -- a steep, long trail to these destinations.
properties.title: Six Ridge

properties.description: A tough route through spectacular scenery.
properties.title: Leroy Creek High Route

properties.description: A small neighborhood park, through a wooded area which leads to an overlook of Puget Sound.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Eagle Landing Park

properties.description: Beginning from the heart of Salmon La Sac and terminating at the Pacific Crest Trail, the Waptus River trail offers miles of hiking through dry, open forest and beautiful lakes in the Alpine Lakes wilderness then a little bit of a climb before arriving at the iconic trail high on a ridgeline in the Central Cascades.
properties.title: Waptus Lake via Waptus River

properties.description: Providing a cool forest walk even on warm summer day, Hansville Greenway is an extensive network of trails encompassing the community of Hansville on the Kitsap peninsula.
properties.title: Hansville Greenway

properties.description: Within a stone’s throw of Seattle, the Snow Lake trail delivers splendorous alpine scenery – crystal clear waters, towering peaks — on a rather exposed and rocky hike. Just don’t expect to have the trail to yourself; it's Washington's most heavily-used trail in a wilderness area!
properties.title: Snow Lake

properties.description: The 64-acre North Creek Forest meets the Washington Department of Fish & Wildlife’s definition of a priority habitat. The trail system in the North Creek Forest is still being established as of 2019.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: North Creek Forest

properties.description: This isolated little island in south Puget Sound attracts boaters to explore it's short shoreline and hiking trail.
properties.title: Hope Island Marine State Park

properties.description: Observe extensive creek restoration efforts while exploring one of the best urban trails in Kitsap County.
properties.title: Clear Creek Trail

properties.description: Stegosaurus Butte (Choir Boy) is a short, but steep well defined climber's path up off the Pratt Lake Trail to a small ridge with views of Garfield, Pulpit, and Preacher Mountains.
properties.title: Stegosaurus Butte

properties.description: A motorized trail in Capitol State Forest.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Waddell Basin West

properties.description: A connector trail between Wildside and De Leo Wall trails on Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Marshall's Hill

properties.description: This 66-acre preserve sits on the shores of the Kitsap Peninsula overlooking the Hood Canal. There are about 2 miles of trails to wander.
properties.title: Anderson Landing Preserve

properties.description: Explore a beautiful riverside forest, perfect for kids and adults alike.
properties.title: Shady Lane

properties.description: Hog Canyon Lake is an excellent hike in spring and fall, showcasing the unique geology and plant diversity of the area.
properties.title: Hog Canyon Lake

properties.description: Enjoy 40 feet of the tallest waterfall in the San Juans during a visit to Moran State Park. Cascade Creek flows through not just Cascade Falls, but a few other fallls as well as it pours into a ravine on its way to the ocean. This trail also features towering trees, many other waterfalls, and connects to other trails in the park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Moran State Park - Cascade Falls

properties.description: Bare Mountain, the site of a former fire lookout, is a superb viewpoint with mountains in every direction and lakes close by. In season, appreciate the great variety of wildflowers, beginning at the trailhead and continuing all the way to the summit. And be alert for birds and wild critters. They are out there.
properties.title: Bare Mountain

properties.description: Hike along a section of the Wenaha River in the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Wenaha River Trail

properties.description: Walk in a coastal forest south of Bellingham to enjoy scenic Wildcat Cove and then to Clayton Beach, with views into the San Juan Islands from the shoreline of Samish Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Wildcat Cove and Clayton Beach

properties.description: A little piece of wilderness tucked away in the middle of civilization, originally established in 1968 as a survey site for Western Washington University. Now open to the public and maintained by the City of Marysville.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Deering Wildflower Acres

properties.description: Pinegrass Ridge Sno-Park offers outings on snowmobile trails that head up to the Section 3 trailhead for Bear Creek Mountain (a fairly steep route) or more casual loops on the closer-in trail network.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Pinegrass Ridge Sno-Park

properties.description: Hike a steep and sometimes difficult to follow trail to where it intersects the Lewis River Trail a half mile downstream of Forest Road 90 near Crab Creek.
properties.title: Bluff Trail

properties.description: This nice valley walk, serenaded by the sound of the Lost River, used to be the easy start of a difficult trail access into the central Pasayten Wilderness. The Eureka Creek bridge makes for a good turn around point, while Lost River access at the wilderness boundary makes a good location for a long break.
properties.title: Lost River

properties.description: One of the lesser-visited lakes in the Enchantments, Lake Caroline is a hard-earned reward for those seeking a bit of solitude in this immensely popular region.
properties.title: Lake Caroline

properties.description: Enjoy a series of easy forest trails in this new Island County park. Descend to the beach at both ends of the bluff. Optionally, tide permitting, hike the entire length of the mile-long beach. Either way, finish your hike on more forest trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Barnum Point

properties.description: Alta Mountain is a rocky summit featuring 360 degree views of Rainier, Hibox, and the Chikamins.  It can be done as a long day hike, but is more easily enjoyed as a side trip from an overnight at Lila Lake, Rampart Lakes, or even Rachel Lake.
properties.title: Alta Mountain

properties.description: A steep, infrequently maintained trail that is part of the White Pass-Pilot Ridge Loop.
properties.title: Pilot Ridge

properties.description: Climb to the summit of a peak near Mount Rainier. Climbing experience and equipment required.
properties.title: Copper Mountain

properties.description: Myrtle Lake is a quaint lake nestled in the Entiat Mountains.
properties.title: Myrtle Lake

properties.description: Washington State has a plethora of amazingly beautiful trails for the avid hiker to tread, but how many take you through an old train tunnel more than two miles long? The Snoqualmie Tunnel is part of the 250-mile Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail (formerly the John Wayne Trail and Iron Horse State Park) and this section is a must do for everyone! Views for most of your trip will be determined by the power of your headlamp, but there will be some sights on the other side. The attraction of this hike is the mysterious, dramatic tunnel itself. However, note that the tunnel is closed November 1st through May 1st, so plan your trip accordingly.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - The Tunnel

properties.description: This trail connects the Foggy Dew Creek Trail with the Summer Blossom Trail. It gradually climbs through forest and meadows, before climbing steeply through larch to the ridge crest, where there are expansive views.
properties.title: Navarre Way

properties.description: Follow this wide path as it winds through tall, ivy-covered Douglas firs.  Although it’s in the middle of the city, this trail around a developing park provides a great way to enjoy the outdoors.
properties.title: Raymond E. Shaffer Park

properties.description: There is no formal trail to the peak of Middle Tiffany Mountain.
properties.title: Middle Tiffany Mountain

properties.description: Woodinville's first public community park, Wilmot Gateway Park, offers visitors several activities to spend a day outside.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wilmot Gateway Park

properties.description: A quiet snowshoe trip to views of Silver Star Mountain awaits the mid-week traveler in late fall and early spring.  This road walk parallels the Early Winters Trail, the old route from Mazama to Washington Pass.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Silver Star View Snowshoe

properties.description: This Mercer Island park offers a dense network of forest trails with tall trees and a lot of moss, ferns and some seasonal wildflowers. All the trails are open to hikers and bicyclists; some also are designated for use by equestrians.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Pioneer Park - Mercer Island

properties.description: This lesser known hike connects two forest service roads via a gentle trail that takes visitors through a shady forest of old growth.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Silver Creek Trail

properties.description: The Black Diamond Open space consists of 1,240 forested acres including wetlands, peat bogs, streams and portions of the protected migratory corridor known as the Wildlife Habitat Network. Explore the 17 miles of non-motorized trails only two miles north of Black Diamond and six miles to the south of Maple Valley.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Black Diamond Open Space

properties.description: The Windy Creek Trail provides the shortest approach route to Windy Peak.  After the 4.8-mile climb up the Windy Creek Trail, mostly through the recovering forest from the 2006 Tripod Fire, it is only an additional 0.3 mile with a 400-foot climb to reach the expansive 360-degree view from the top.
properties.title: Windy Creek

properties.description: Just over the state line in Idaho, McCroskey Memorial State Park is a worthy stop for a leg stretch on a long drive.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: McCroskey Memorial State Park

properties.description: Hike along a Wild and Scenic river, up a rugged ridge, and to a mirror-like iconic lake in Glacier Peak wilderness. This is a long hike, best done as a backpack, but it's absolutely worth the days you invest to explore here.
properties.title: Image Lake via Miners Ridge

properties.description: If you are looking for a walk through deep snow in the winter that will take you into the North Cascades, Oakes Peak is the snowshoe trip for you. Walk along a Forest Service road toward the National Park boundary or up toward Oakes Peak.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Oakes Peak Snowshoe

properties.description: Everything that makes a river hike fun is here, cool bridges, waterfalls, big trees, lots of dripping moss, and mushrooms.
properties.title: Deception Creek

properties.description: Paradise is one of the most gorgeous (and, as a result, popular) parts of Washington. This short but steep trail offers tourists and locals alike one of the most stunning views for the fewest miles in Washington state, but that doesn't mean you won't sweat! Be prepared to climb more than 1,000 feet in less than a mile at the outset of this trail.
properties.title: Glacier Vista - Panorama Point

properties.description: Follow this trail for the first four miles for a pleasant hike with views of peaks and a creek. More experienced hikers can continue down the trail for incredible views of the Pasayten Wilderness and a connection to Hidden Lakes.
properties.title: Monument Creek

properties.description: Visit this 247 acre park on the floodplain of the Yakima River. With two miles of hiking trails, it's a great place to explore if you happen to be camping nearby. With fall foliage, wildflowers, and fishing, it's a delightful destination at any time of the year.
properties.title: Yakima Sportsman State Park

properties.description: This trail only takes about 20 minutes to hike out and back with great views of Mount Baker, Mount Erie, Fidalgo Island, Hope Island and the inner part of Puget Sound.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Ala Spit

properties.description: A short amble along a road in Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park.
properties.title: Clay Pit Road

properties.description: Hike on the Wonderland Trail to three waterfalls on the Paradise River.
properties.title: Longmire to Paradise

properties.description: Goat Creek trail is locally known for being an access point to one of the most special waterfalls in the region, Cathedral Falls. Hike beyond this spectacular feature under wonderfully lush canopy giving yourself options for a full day hike, while adding potential summit peaks or lakeside backcountry camping options to your itinerary.
properties.title: Goat Creek

properties.description: A quick walk along the Bellingham waterfront through industry and out on to the old Georgia Pacific Aeration Stabilization Basin (ASB) for very nice views of downtown and the bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: ASB Trail

properties.description: Saltese Flats Wetland consists of 4.5 miles of relatively flat trails on recently restored wetland habitat on the east end of the Spokane Valley.
properties.title: Saltese Flats Wetland

properties.description: Hike to some remote hot springs on the Olympic Peninsula.
properties.title: Olympic Hot Springs

properties.description: This City of Sultan park is tucked away on the edge of town and provides the perfect short escape into the trees and along the Sultan River.
properties.title: Osprey Park

properties.description: Amble through aspens and plateau shrubs- dogwood, sumac, and currant on this gentle day hike through a portion of the 18,000-acre Turnbull National Wildlife Refuge.
properties.title: Columbia Plateau Trail - Amber Lake

properties.description: Saddle Lake is along the route that accesses the Three Fingers Lookout. It requires an 8-mile road walk before the 2.5 miles to get to the lake. There is no camping allowed at this lake.
properties.title: Saddle Lake via Meadow Mountain

properties.description: Enjoy this mile and a half long walk in the heart of Des Moines.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Barnes Creek Nature Trail

properties.description: A short, rugged trail through meadows and a burn area that leads to great views of the Wenatchee mountains. This is a great option to see some fall color near Blewett Pass and create a loop link up with nearby other trails.
properties.title: Elk Trap Springs Trail

properties.description: A short trail in the sometimes-closed Eagle Creek Group Campground area, this little loop has some of the best views right at the beginning.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Eagle Creek Overlook Trail

properties.description: Only fragments remain of the Buck Creek trail. But it’s easy enough to combine it with other trails to make a short and easy hike to a seldom-visited wooded shore of the White River.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Buck Creek

properties.description: Ever wanted to hike the Wonderland Trail, but have time for only a sneak peek?  Here’s how to enjoy a sampling of the Wonderland’s spectacular scenery — in a single day!
properties.title: Tahoma Creek Suspension Bridge - Emerald Ridge Loop

properties.description: The Craggy Peak Trail is a beautiful, albeit difficult hike located in one of Washington's least recognized areas: the Dark Divide. Nestled between imposing St. Helens to the west, Adams to the east, and Rainier to the north, the Craggy Peak Trail boasts spectacular views of the surrounding snowy peaks. Because of some necessary bushwhacking, this is quite a difficult hike, yet is doable in a day.
properties.title: Craggy Peak

properties.description: The trail to Lena Lake is a pretty, and popular, weekend destination. But hearty hikers and backpackers who venture to Upper Lena Lake will leave the crowds behind and experience a little bit of nirvana.
properties.title: Upper Lena Lake

properties.description: Take a very steep, primitive trail to a creek crossing (only fordable in mid-summer) to the Lewis River Trail.
properties.title: Speed

properties.description: A half mile shortcut from the Chybinski Loop Trail to the junction with the Bullitt Gorge Trail on Squak Mountain.
properties.title: West Peak

properties.description: The Trail for The Blind is a level grade trail adjacent to the Cispus Learning Center in foothills of the Cowlitz Valley. It is a part of the Covel Creek Trail System and is designed to allow easier access and highlight natural features in the forest for those who are visually challenged. This is also a great hike smaller children and those with less mobility.
properties.title: Cispus Braille Trail

properties.description: At low tide, walk along the rocky beach for an up-close view underneath the Tacoma Narrows Bridge and enjoy wildlife viewing from the shore along the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Narrows Park

properties.description: Walk among old-growth giants as you travel to one of Olympic National Park's best-loved waterfalls.
properties.title: Marymere Falls

properties.description: One of many trails on Manastash Ridge, the Boy Scout trail allows hikers to create loops or alternate routes to the summit of Manastash Ridge.
properties.title: Manastash Ridge - Boy Scout Trail

properties.description: Artist Point is the top competitor for best viewpoint in the state. The beautifully shaped Mount Shuksan is the star of the area, with a gorgeous summit pyramid and several impressive glaciers. This relatively easy snowshoe is an excellent winter destination with a virtual guarantee of good snow coverage.
properties.title: Artist Point Snowshoe

properties.description: Explore the Chehalis River between working farmland and recently restored riparian habitat. Your hosts: a bevy of birds, from barn swallows to bald eagles.
properties.title: Chehalis River Discovery Trail

properties.description: Escape the hustle and bustle of nearby Wynoochee Lake by trekking down to the lesser-known Spoon Creek Falls. This short and sweet hike will reward you with both impressive waterfall views, and a calm (yet cold) wading pool to dip your toes.
properties.title: Spoon Creek Falls

properties.description: Witness the polar opposites of land use management in this unique BLM wilderness, accessed through a popular OHV area. Once within the wilderness fence, visitors are rewarded with wide-open hiking through varied terrain, including the largest remaining juniper groves in Washington.
properties.title: Juniper Dunes Wilderness

properties.description: These gardens are owned and operated by a non-profit who is dedicated to the maintenance of both the gardens and a historic house. Visitors can wander the paths and enjoy the tapestry of trees and flowers as well as marvel at the John Stanger home, which was built in 1867.
properties.title: Jane Weber Evergreen Arboretum

properties.description: The Boulder River trail is a nice hike that can be done any time of year. Come in winter while the rain is dripping off the mossy trees, photograph the waterfalls filled with spring snowmelt. Take the kids out for a little picnic in the summer, or leaf collecting in the fall. Come anytime midweek for quiet contemplation.
properties.title: Boulder River

properties.description: A quiet route along a creek on an old rail grade in the city of Newcastle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Honey Dew Creek
