properties.description: A trail that can help hikers create multiple loops in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, the the Cady Creek trail is a steep ascent from the brushy and mucky Cady Creek valley bottom.
properties.title: Cady Creek

properties.description: The year-round, dog-friendly day hike to Fragrance Lake in the Chuckanut Recreation Area is popular with college students and faculty from Western Washington University in nearby Bellingham, and with day visitors and car campers at Larrabee State Park. On a sunny weekend afternoon you could easily lose count of the number of smiles and “hullos” you’ll exchange!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Fragrance Lake

properties.description: The Klickitat Trail is a 31-mile rails-to-trails conversion managed by Columbia Hills State Park. This linear park goes from Lyle to Warwick (on the Lyle-Centerville Highway) with several access points along the way. This Hiking Guide entry describes the route between Lyle and Pitt Road.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Klickitat Rail Trail - Klickitat River

properties.description: With a starting elevation of 4,300, this tour is your best guarantee of good snow, even in a lean year.
properties.title: Huntoon Point Snowshoe

properties.description: Hike and scramble to a summit between Dirty Harry's Peak and Mailbox Peak.
properties.title: Dirtybox Peak

properties.description: You'll get a good workout on this seven mile loop just outside of Spokane. Consider it for an early-season conditioner, or a way to get a lot of miles and elevation close to home all year round. In spring, it's a wildflower haven. Summertime can be hot, so bring plenty of water -- the river here is part of a natural area, so no swimming!
properties.title: Little Spokane River Natural Area - Knothead Loop

properties.description: The South Tiger Traverse Trail breaks off of the Tiger Mountain Trail (TMT) at Hobert Gap and traverses on the west side of South Tiger Mountain while the TMT traverses around the east side of South Tiger Mountain. The South Tiger Traverse Trail rejoins the TMT at the north end.
properties.title: South Tiger Traverse

properties.description: Bring a tide table and a good book on this scenic traverse of the wild Olympic Coast. While much of your hike will be across sandy beaches, there are several places that will require you wait for the tide to go out. Along the way, plan to climb up steep headlands with cable ladders, ropes and your hands and knees. It's a challenge, but a good one.
properties.title: South Coast Wilderness Trail - Toleak Point

properties.description: Glacier Vista snowshoe is a shorter alternative to Panorama Point snowshoe. With 2.5 miles round trip with only 900 feet elevation gain, it is an easy snowshoeing outing with great views of snow-capped mountains.
properties.title: Glacier Vista Snowshoe

properties.description: The Crosshaul Trail is a short segment within the East Tiger Mountain trail network that connects with many other trails.
properties.title: Crosshaul

properties.description: This state park provides plenty of green space for many different outdoor activities just a short drive from Wenatchee.
properties.title: Squilchuck State Park

properties.description: There are no superlatives along the Indian Flat trail, with the possible exception of the unique rock formations. But views are available, and shade is abundant in an area that can get quite hot during the summer.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Indian Flat

properties.description: The Lowell Riverfront Trail in Everett is a 1.6-mile pedestrian trail stretching between Lowell River Road near Rotary Park to its northern end. The ten foot wide, paved path traverses an area revered for its historical significance, natural beauty and central location.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lowell Riverfront Park Trail

properties.description: The short boardwalk at Bowerman Basin provides a quiet, contemplative place to enjoy the wildlife resting at the Grays Harbor National Wildlife Refuge.
properties.title: Grays Harbor National Wildlife Refuge - Bowerman Basin

properties.description: Survey Mount St. Helens’ recovering Blast Zone and get 360-degree, four-peak views from this high perch along the Boundary Trail.
properties.title: Coldwater Peak

properties.description: Set off for a hike in the Anacortes Community Forest Lands (ACFL), a 2,800-acre preserve within the city limits of Anacortes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Little Cranberry Lake

properties.description: Wolframite Mountain is a prominent peak in the Pasayten Wilderness near the Canadian Border. The summit can be reached via the Cathedral Driveway Trailhead.
properties.title: Wolframite Mountain

properties.description: The Press Traverse is a 44-mile hiking trail that traverses through the heart of Olympic National Park. The original route was pioneered by a group led by James Christie between 1889–1890. Today’s version of the route snakes along rivers, through old-growth rainforests and highlights a blend of human and natural history.
properties.title: Press Expedition Traverse

properties.description: If you're looking for the best workout in the park, you'd be hard-pressed to find something better than this, the longest trail. Circumnavigate the park's namesake peak by following trail 130 "round-the-mountain" for nearly 12 miles of forested trail punctuated by the occasional open meadow, or opt to turn around at any time for a shorter stroll.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 130

properties.description: This forest is located in the heart of Bonney Lake, offering a place to walk on trails beneath the trees.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Midtown Park

properties.description: A trail on Tiger Mountain with loop options to Preston Trail, and Dwight's Way. Also use this trail to access the Tiger Mountain Trail.
properties.title: Bootleg Trail

properties.description: A short but steep backdoor connector trail on the lower east side of Chuckanut Mountain, the Alternate Incline offers access to Lily and Lizard Lakes, North Butte, Oyster Dome and even the Pacific Northwest Trail from the spacious Blanchard Hill upper trailhead parking lot.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Blanchard Hill - Alternate Incline Trail

properties.description: Dugualla Bay Preserve (not to be confused with Dugualla Bay State Park just down the road) is a natural area on the northeast area of Whidbey Island. Managed by the Whidbey Camano Land Trust, this is an important section of protected shoreline for salmon recovery.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Dugualla Bay Preserve

properties.description: Hike through some great second-growth forest to reach the second-highest summit in the Tigers. Then enjoy a superb viewpoint a short distance west of the summit.
properties.title: West Tiger 1

properties.description: Dash Point State park is located between Seattle and Tacoma and is a popular spot for water recreation. Birdwatchers can see shorebirds and raptors, while beach explorers can look for crabs and starfish on the shores during low tide. While the park is mostly known for the beach, there are also miles of forested trails for hiking and biking.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Dash Point State Park

properties.description: The Department of Natural Resources has closed this site indefinitely.
properties.title: Butte Creek Sitka Spruce Grove

properties.description: Through the efforts of WTA, King County Parks, Earth Corps and other community partners, this small 5-acre forest has become a green oasis within the North Highline area of Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Glendale Forest

properties.description: This short section of the PCT heads south out of Snoqualmie Pass and to Windy Pass, where it is possible to access Mount Catherine, or do a longer loop before heading back towards the trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) - Hyak to Windy Pass

properties.description: This lesser known trail starts in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest and then enters the northeast corner of the park, is snow-free early in the season and goes through some amazing old growth.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Huckleberry Creek

properties.description: Crooked Thumb Peak is located in the Picket Range of the North Cascades National Park and can be reached via the Big Beaver Trailhead.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Crooked Thumb Peak

properties.description: There are many different trails that lead to the Capitol Peak in the Capitol State Forest.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Capitol Peak

properties.description: Popular with locals and overnight visitors alike, the Rainbow Loop is a short and sweet way to get a feel for the valley and its breathtaking scenery. Combine it with a bike ride and a bakery visit and you'll get the full Stehekin valley experience in one day.
properties.title: Rainbow Loop

properties.description: This very short trail provides astonishing views of nature’s beauty as well as humanity's technological “improvements” upon it. The first section of this loop is paved, allowing an out-and-back for all family members, while the remaining graveled loop section is never steep nor too challenging.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Gorge Lake Overlook

properties.description: Glacier Peak Wilderness, northwest of Lake Wenatchee. You can barely see Glacier Peak from the westside of the Cascades. Not so from the Buck Creek Trail - where it looms over you like a white monolith. Add to that fields of late summer flowers and a pleasant afternoon breeze and you may be close to rapture.
properties.title: Buck Creek Pass

properties.description: Hike downhill, enjoy spring blooms and throw rocks into a punchbowl at the bottom of a 40-foot waterfall.
properties.title: Umtanum Creek Falls

properties.description: The Alta Vista Loop is one of the trails located at Paradise at Mount Rainier National Park. This trail system is known for fantastic displays of wildflowers in the summer and dramatic panoramic views of Mount Rainier and the surrounding foothills all year long.
properties.title: Alta Vista Loop

properties.description: Hike along the Lake Lillian trail to two sparkling lakes, great as both a destination for your hike or as a part of a longer hike to Lake Lillian.
properties.title: Twin Lakes

properties.description: Tucked away in the neighborhood of Hoffman Hill, this trail this is the longest continuous trail in DuPont.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Hoffman Hill Trail

properties.description: This is a commanding area with many options for hiking and other recreation. Hiking options range from double-track roads to cross-country exploring through the shrub-steppe.
properties.title: Big Bend Wildlife Area

properties.description: This steep hike has it all — wildflowers in spring, huckleberries in fall and a 360-degree panoramic view at the top of the South Cascades.
properties.title: Starway

properties.description: This gentle, short hike offers spring flowers and a nice forest ramble, following most of George McClellan's railroad survey of 1852.
properties.title: McClellan Meadows

properties.description: Hiking with kids, new to hiking, or just looking for an easy day hike with a spectacular endpoint? Look no further then Franklin Falls! At just 2 miles with 400 feet in elevation gain it is the perfect destination for any hiker looking for something easy and beautiful!
properties.title: Franklin Falls

properties.description: Mount Ruth is a peak in the northeast corner of Mount Rainier National Park. The route to this peak is an off-trail mountaineering route, not an official trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Mount Ruth

properties.description: Enjoy lakeside views and the surrounding hills plus waterfalls and giant old Douglas-fir trees from an old railroad grade of the Bellingham Bay & Eastern Railway that borders the southeast shore of Lake Whatcom.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lake Whatcom Park - Hertz Trail

properties.description: On the shore of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, you can walk a fine sandy beach between high bluffs and two access points to reach the Point Wilson Lighthouse at Fort Worden State Park.
properties.title: Fort Worden State Park - Point Wilson

properties.description: This trail is a main thoroughfare through Seattle and beyond. It is popular with cyclists, runners and walkers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Burke-Gilman Trail

properties.description: A challenging summit with a big payoff: a 360-degree panorama of more than 10 Cascades peaks.
properties.title: Davis Peak

properties.description: An infrequently-visited trail off the Carbon River Road, the Old Mine Trail follows a short but steep roadbed to a mineshaft. It's a good outing for kids, if they're willing to make the short push up the steep section.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Old Mine Trail

properties.description: A scramble to a wooded summit near Barlow Pass. Climbing experience and route-finding skills required.
properties.title: St'auk Mountain

properties.description: As Clark County's oldest park, Lewisville Regional Park is a delightful place for families to visit and get a shot of history, since the park was developed by The Works Progress Administration (WPA) during the Great Depression.
properties.title: Lewisville Regional Park

properties.description: Although this is a short hike, it's a decent challenge because it's a narrow, steep trail. The terrain is interesting, with waterfalls and its trademark basalt columns.  If you like solitude, this is the trail for you.
properties.title: Blue Lake Creek

properties.description: Hike down the canyon to the White River and a historic hydroelectric power at White River Falls State Park. Located just east of Tygh Valley in Oregon, the park also has dramatic waterfalls, fishing, desert flowers in the spring and fiery colors in the fall.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: White River Falls State Park

properties.description: The Little Lake Forest was acquired by King County Parks in 2018.  A small forested lake sits in the middle of this 155-acre park, and a gravel access road leads to the northern shore of the lake.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Little Lake Forest

properties.description: This is part of the William O. Douglas Trail, which runs from Davis High School in Yakima to Mt. Rainier. This trail is still being established.
properties.title: Box Spring Canyon

properties.description: Trek a dry, strenuous trail to a famous fire lookout. Jack Kerouac stayed here as a lookout and used the experience to inspire Desolation Angels and Dharma Bums. The historic lookout is no longer accessible to the public, but you can still trek to the location and appreciate the view.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Desolation Peak

properties.description: Starting from the west end of Lake Wenatchee, this snowshoe along a snowy forest service road is a great way to get out in the snow on a relatively flat and wide trail. Side roads offer an uphill route to a viewpoint or you can meander down toward the river and turn back at any point you please.
properties.title: Little Wenatchee River Road Snowshoe

properties.description: Beginning at the trailhead off Forest Road 9712 and ending at Naneum Creek Trail 1381, Howard Creek can give visitors either a long ramble through the big Table Mountain burn area, or it can be utilized to make a loop through the Blewett Pass area, including Mount Lillian.
properties.title: Howard Creek

properties.description: Reaching Mount Shuksan's summit involves alpine climbing.
properties.title: Mount Shuksan

properties.description: The Sunrise Rim Trail is a short connector trail that links Sunrise with the Wonderland Trail, providing expansive views of Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Sunrise Rim Trail

properties.description: Hike a short paved trail to the remains of a vehicle that was subject to the 1980 blast when Mount. St. Helens erupted.
properties.title: Miners Car Interpretive Site

properties.description: In winter, and, as with all showshoeing, the right gear, it is possible to snowshoe the Miller River Road to the Dorothy Lake Trailhead.
properties.title: Miller River Road Snowshoe

properties.description: A handful of high lakes nestled in a forested cirque below Granite Mountain deep within the Alpine Lakes Wilderness
properties.title: Klonaqua Lakes

properties.description: An old trail made new! The land on this southwest side of the park was recently donated to the Skagit Land Trust and Mount Vernon Parks to prevent it from becoming a big housing development. Now, the land will be kept for posterity for all to enjoy. Hike this loop for some fine forest walking on the south slope of Little Mountain.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Little Mountain Park - Darvill Loop

properties.description: The Sol Duc River Trail is one of Olympic National Park’s most beloved hikes. Thus it is always crowded and a backcountry camping quota is enforced. Roaring waterfalls, lush old growth, and subalpine meadows where elk bugle and bears browse for berries are just some of the many highlights.
properties.title: Sol Duc River

properties.description: This is a pleasant walk around Briggs Lake on San Juan Island. Don’t let the detailed instructions deter you -- though there are a few intersections to navigate, this is a great way to explore the wooded highlands of San Juan Island, enjoy some lake views, and perhaps catch sight of a bald eagle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Briggs Lake

properties.description: Trail 211 is a short connector trail located within Riverside State Park.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Trail 211

properties.description: Fullbright Park is available for private reservations, but if no one has reserved the park, the trails here are open to the public and a nice place to stretch your hiking muscles.
properties.title: Fullbright Park

properties.description: This infrequently visited trail is the perfect hike early in the season, because the snow melts off the south-facing flanks of the peak early. If you miss the springtime, save it for fall, because the deciduous trees that line the path make it ideal for a shot of fall color. Enjoy a moderately graded that leads you to a summit that boasts views of Rainier and the White River valley from the summit.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Little Ranger Peak via Ranger Creek

properties.description: The Big Creek Falls trail is closed as of spring 2015
properties.title: Big Creek Falls

properties.description: This short, one-mile, downhill jaunt from the hairpin turn on the road to Sunrise makes a great detour when hiking the Palisades Lakes trail, or a nice warm up before tackling longer hikes like Burroughs or Dege Peak from Sunrise.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Sunrise Lake

properties.description: The Third Creek trail immediately plunges into dense forest. This hike drops 2000 feet along its length before intersecting the Diamond Peak Trail and parallelling Crooked Creek before reaching the Wenaha River Trail.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Third Creek

properties.description: A mountain in the North Cascades. Climbing gear and route-finding expertise required to summit.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Big Snagtooth

properties.description: This trail, just over the border in Oregon, begins at a BLM trailhead, and ends at Deduct Pond on Forest Service Road 65-650.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: South Fork Walla Walla River

properties.description: Pass Creek is an easy access point to the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) and provides opportunities for longer loop hikes open to stock when conditions permit.
properties.title: Pass Creek

properties.description: This popular summer trail off I-90 changes quite a bit during the winter months. Note that there is considerable avalanche danger at the falls.
properties.title: Franklin Falls - Winter

properties.description: Take advantage of the diversity of Riverside State Park's Trail 25 by doing this close-to-town loop that includes both forested canyon and scenic overlooks.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Deep Creek Canyon

properties.description: Explore this small park's forested primitive trails near Gig Harbor.
properties.title: Harbor Family Park

properties.description: Hike along the Lower Mad River in a narrow rocky canyon. The first three miles makes an ideal day trip for hikers of all abilities.  Looking for more adventure?  The trail continues for almost 15 miles where it meets the Upper Mad River trail.  Be prepared to share the trail with bikes, horses, and motorcycles.
properties.title: Lower Mad River Valley

properties.description: This 5.4-mile loop hike meanders its way through pine forest and brings trail users to a seasonal pond and large sandstone slab, offering striking views of the Teanaway Community Forest.
properties.title: Teanaway Community Forest - Frog Pond Loop

properties.description: A steep and rough-at-times trail leads hikers into some of the loneliest, yet most stunning, lake basins within the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
properties.title: Chain and Doelle Lakes

properties.description: This is a protected area with no official trails in it. Visitors are encouraged to tread lightly here, since it is a habitat with fragile plants.
properties.title: Tumwater Botanical Area

properties.description: Lose yourself in second-growth forest as you traverse an old logging road that heads into quiet wilderness just an hour from the urban sprawl of Puget Sound. Enjoy the sounds of water rushing and birds singing. Explore mossy boulders and cross multiple burbling creeks, even do a small amount of cross-country travel on the way to the piece de resistance – a 1,200 foot waterfall that streams into tiny Lipsy Lake before draining to the Taylor River.
properties.title: Taylor River - Otter Falls

properties.description: The way to Goldmyer Hot Springs is a delightful forest walk through deep woods, along the rushing Snoqualmie River, and ultimately to a beautiful privately owned hot springs tucked against the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. Because it is privately owned by a non-profit, reservations are strongly recommended and are the only way to assure access to the property and hot springs.
properties.title: Goldmyer Hot Springs

properties.description: Once home to a fire lookout, the granite slabs that make up Kalispell Rock overlook the Priest River drainage.
properties.title: Kalispell Rock

properties.description: This is a half-mile loop hike past giant cedar trees preserved by Harold Engles, a famous Forest Ranger.
properties.title: Harold Engles Memorial Cedars

properties.description: This heavily-used trail passes numerous lakes and meadows and is an excellent foray into the Indian Heaven Wilderness. Hikers will find amble opportunities for a lakeside lunch spot.
properties.title: Thomas, Blue and Tombstone Lakes

properties.description: The Wenatchee Crest near Blewett Pass is an ideal entry-level snowshoe, thanks to its modest elevation gain and panoramic views from the ridgetop. And even with such an easily accessible trailhead, the crowds are often minimal.
properties.title: Wenatchee Crest Snowshoe (Blewett Pass)

properties.description: A challenging offshoot trail from the Heather Maple Pass loop that traverses a large talus field to arrive at two stunning alpine lakes.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Wing Lake

properties.description: Get up close and personal with Mount St. Helens as you explore the northern flanks of the eruption site and meander through the unique ecology of the pumice plains.
properties.title: Truman Trail - Pumice Plains

properties.description: Hike a short, sweet, ADA-accessible trail on a reservoir to a waterfall.
properties.title: Lower Marble Creek Falls

properties.description: This steep, unmaintained trail provides a link between the Easton Ridge and the Domerie Peak Trail
properties.title: Domerie Divide Trail

properties.description: An overlooked trail in a high canopy forest with nice views of the area in Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument.
properties.title: Fossil Trail

properties.description: This trail in Columbia Hills is one of three excellent destinations in this location. Do an out-and-back, or a loop hike! Visit in winter for great views of the Columbia River and Mount Hood, or in spring for a stunning wildflower show.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Columbia Hills State Park - Crawford Oaks

properties.description: Here's a hike that takes you through a stark landscape to a stunningly lush one. Berkeley Park is a flower-filled utopia where creeks chatter, pikas squeak, marmots lounge, and you can soak it all in just a few miles from the Sunrise Visitor Center.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Berkeley Park

properties.description: Three thousand feet in three miles make the Little Wenatchee a substantial albeit relatively short hike for exercise provided. The trail was the primary supply route to the old Poe Mountain lookout, and like many lookout access trails wastes no time in getting to the top. But it is well built, switchbacking up the hill. The first two-thirds of the hike are in light tree cover, so the views come as a surprise when you get to them.
properties.title: Poe Mountain via Little Wenatchee Trailhead

properties.description: From the Moorage at Beacon Rock State Park this short connector trail climbs through tall Douglas-fir trees, through the site of an old homestead and Filbert Orchard, then past Ridell Lake on its way to the namesake Rock. Its a great hike for people who arrive at the park by boat or for anyone wanting to make a longer hike of the 1.0 mile Beacon Rock Trail.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - River To Rock Trail

properties.description: Explore the heart of Seattle, starting at the Museum of History and Industry in South Lake Union and ending downtown at Pike Place Market.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Market to MOHAI

properties.description: The Rocky Creek Conservation Area is a great hiking destination on key peninsula. There is an inner loop (1.2 miles) and outer loop (1.3 miles), but they can be combined to form a longer route.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Rocky Creek Conservation Area

properties.description: Venture into Seattle Park, a wilder, more remote version of more popular Spray Park, and enjoy verdant meadows and rugged scenery.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Seattle Park

properties.description: This lovely trail loops around Oneonta Gorge and takes you behind Ponytail Falls.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Oneonta Gorge

properties.description: Explore a scenic and incredibly varied landscape near Winthrop where you are almost certainly guaranteed to see some of the region’s abundant wildlife.
properties.title: Pipestone Canyon Rim Trail

properties.description: Web Mountain is the peak directly to the west of Putrid Pete's Peak. It can be reached via the P3 trail and then by following the ridge line west.
properties.title: Web Mountain via Putrid Pete's Peak

properties.description: High Divide trail makes up a section of the Seven Lakes Basin trail and leads to the Bailey Range Traverse. While campsites exist along this route, it's important to reserve your spot in advance of your visit here.
properties.title: High Divide

properties.description: Wildflowers, wildlife, and great views of Eastern Washington’s wild Blue Mountains: the Panjab Loop Trail offers it all.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Panjab Trail

properties.description: This popular hike provides a range of alpine experiences in a short loop. Walk along a hillside above a small valley, pause at a viewpoint overlooking a lake and stroll through grassy meadows with stunning views of Mount Rainier. In season, enjoy an abundance of wildflowers or perhaps a handful of huckleberries.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Naches Peak Loop

properties.description: Conboy Lake is now more of a marsh than a lake but it is home to a variety of wildlife. The habitat consists of oak, pine, and aspen forests, wetlands and grassy prairies.
properties.title: Conboy Lake National Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: This trail — closed for years as the private property the trailhead is on underwent a management change — is back open as of early 2025, offering hikers a short but steep hike to the top of Aldrich Butte.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Aldrich Butte

properties.description: This is a snowshoe hike that follows Corral Pass Road, starting at the intersection with highway 410.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Corral Pass Snowshoe

properties.description: This short trail leads through the forest from the Sherman Overlook Campground to the Kettle Crest Trailhead and it makes a pleasant hike on its own.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sherman Pass Tie Trail

properties.description: Rock Creek is a perennial stream flowing through the arid Channeled Scablands of Eastern Washington. The trail follows an old ranch road along the creek with views of basalt outcrops, aspen, spring wildflowers, native bunchgrass and a series of waterfalls.
properties.title: Escure Ranch - Towell Falls

properties.description: Summit above Lake Serene and Bridal Veil Falls. No trail. Gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Philadelphia Mountain

properties.description: This natural area contains 40 acres of beautiful riparian forest just north of Vancouver.
properties.title: Whipple Creek Hollow Natural Area

properties.description: Visit Sunrise Peak at the right time and you'll see why its name is appropriate. The early morning sun gives Mount Adams a brilliant glow that makes for an enthralling way to kick off your day. Luckily, the enchanting views that this hike offers are available from Sunrise to sunset, and if you prefer hiking in full daylight, you won't miss out on any views.
properties.title: Sunrise Peak

properties.description: Enjoy this sheltered beach and lagoon walk year-round. Though there are no defined "trails," beaches are fairly self-limiting. Wonderful wildlife and the forces of nature are your reward.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Jackson Beach and Argyle Lagoon

properties.description: This little-known gem of a hike on the Washington side of the Columbia River Gorge offers spectacular views of the Columbia River, amazing spring wildflowers and an old garry oak forest of gnarled old trees. This stunning preserve is owned by the Friends of the Columbia Gorge and tops out in an old cherry orchard with a few surviving trees.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Lyle Cherry Orchard

properties.description: The Naches Trail takes visitors along the same route that pioneers took in horse drawn wagons in the 1800s. It is now a hiking trail that leads to a scenic meadow and a historic cabin.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Naches Trail

properties.description: This one-mile long paved trail takes you to a beautiful alpine lake.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Rainy Lake

properties.description: Named for the curmudgeon who refused to leave his homestead when St. Helens was on the brink of eruption, Harry’s Ridge offers a fascinating panorama of the restless giant, still smoking and belching occasionally, years after her devastating awakening.
properties.title: Harry's Ridge

properties.description: A family-friendly easy walk into a tranquil forest of giant trees with views over a lake and marsh to Mount St. Helens, but don't forget the insect repellent.
properties.title: Goat Marsh Research Area

properties.description: This long ridge route gives hikers big views in all directions and also serves as a connector to enable big loop opportunities with other nearby trails.
properties.title: Hall - Grassy Divide

properties.description: The Ohanapecosh River is arguably the most beautiful in Mount Rainier National Park, with water so clear you can see all the way to the bottom in many places. Where it's not crashing over rocks, of course. The Silver Falls Loop takes you upstream along this impressive river, to a majestic waterfall and back through humbling forest, all in just three miles.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Silver Falls Loop

properties.description: This winter route is part of the ungroomed Blewett Pass Sno-Park Non-motorized Trail System, and is used for both snowshoeing and cross-country skiing.
properties.title: Tronsen Loop Snowshoe

properties.description: The Highline SeaTac Botanical Gardens were created to preserve two gardens during SeaTac Airport’s third runway project. To avoid demolition, the gardens were physically moved to their current location next to the North SeaTac Community Center.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Highline SeaTac Botanical Garden

properties.description: The Peepsight trail is part of the Okanogan-Wenatchee trail system in the Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Peepsight

properties.description: A short, paved loop trail just outside the town of Lyle that offers excellent bird-watching and a quiet walk in the east side of the Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Balfour Klickitat Day-Use Area

properties.description: Jack's Run is an gentle-grade double track for most of its length. It is mostly in the trees running alongside Driveway Butte with periodic views across meadows and up at Goat wall and peak. The trail's course makes a lollipop loop.
properties.title: Jack's Run

properties.description: On your next trip to Deception Pass State Park, don’t cross over the Deception Pass bridge. Instead, take the road down to Bowman Bay for some fine hiking along the rugged cliffs. Great views of the bridge over Deception and Canoe Pass, calm Lottie Bay, a woodland walk through hemlock, fir and Pacific Madrone, plus the legend of the Maiden of Deception Pass are what await you here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - Headlands / Rosario Head / Lighthouse Point

properties.description: This small park in Shoreline is great for families or an evening stroll.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Kayu Kayu Ac Park

properties.description: Northridge Park is a small greenspace on the edge of Bellingham's Barkley neighborhood with a short forested loop trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Northridge Park Trail

properties.description: This short loop encompasses a host of different craters, all formed during 15,000 year old floods. Native vegetation, interesting scenery and plenty of benches make this trail a great opportunity to embrace Washington's natural history with the whole family.
properties.title: Odessa Craters

properties.description: This park is designed in the style of a Japanese garden, with stone walking paths, ponds, bridges, and contemplative areas.
properties.title: Japanese Peace Garden

properties.description: No matter how you tackle it, this hike is a workout. March through thick Ponderosa forests up to subalpine larch stands and a view from the pass, with options to continue on for a small alpine lake with backcountry campsites and access to other wilderness trails.
properties.title: Chatter Creek

properties.description: The Mima Falls Loop takes hikers through young plantings, lush forest, and quiet wetlands in Olympia's Capitol State Forest. Just 30 minutes from the state capital, this is the perfect year-round waterfall hike for after work or weekends. Hike through a working forest and examine forestry practices up close.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Mima Falls Loop

properties.description: Artesian Lake and Black Lake are dry lake beds on federal land. The lakes went dry in the last century due to overgrazing typical of Eastern Washington and the lowering of the water table by local wells. Willow trees and golden currant shrubs still line the former shoreline and surface water occasionally gathers on the alkaline flats.
properties.title: Artesian & Black Lake

properties.description: A lightly used trail that can be hard to follow, to the summit of a mountain in Eastern Washington that is the site of a former fire lookout.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Fir Mountain

properties.description: Mount Muller offers breathtaking views from a breathtaking trail -- it's a steep climb, but those who make it to the lofty ridgeline are rewarded with a panorama that includes the Strait of Juan de Fuca, massive Mount Olympus, and sapphire, sparkling Lake Crescent.
properties.title: Mount Muller

properties.description: The forest to Mink Lake is beautiful, packed full of Queen's Cup, lilies and bunchberry flowers in bloom. Depending on the season, you may see Western Coralroot orchids and Indian Pipe, or Beargrass, Anenomes and violets around the lake.
properties.title: Mink Lake

properties.description: The Turnbull National Wildlife Refuge protects a portion of the ‘Channeled Scablands’ of ice age flood fame. The refuge has a 5.5-mile auto route through part of it.
properties.title: Turnbull National Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: The Forest Glen Neighborhood Park, sometimes known as the Forest Glen Greenbelt, includes 1.19 acres with a basketball court, picnic tables, playground and walking trails.
properties.title: Forest Glen Neighborhood Park

properties.description: Follow a fisherman's trail to a crystalline blue lake in the North Cascades. This is a bushwhack, so you will need route-finding experience and a map and compass, and you'll need to know how to use them.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Trapper Lake

properties.description: A short, self guided nature trail near Newhalem. See a wide variety of native plants and animals along this hike that is great for kids.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Trail of the Cedars

properties.description: The Salmon Viewing Trail is a short but rewarding stroll that ends at an observation area on the bank of the Cle Elum River where salmon spawn in the fall. The ADA-accessible path beelines beneath cheery conifers and quickly brings the hiker to the riverside.
properties.title: Salmon Viewing Trail

properties.description: As we present this trail here, it is a short before-dinner leg-stretcher to witness some of the most remote country in the lower 48.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Temperance Creek - Warnock Corrals Trailhead (Oregon)

properties.description: This five mile stretch of the Whitehorse Trail is the only passable section, currently. However, the trail is slated to stretch 28 miles, connecting to the Centennial Trail in Arlington and terminating in the trail town of Darrington.
properties.title: Whitehorse Trail - Swede Heaven to Darrington

properties.description: Unlike many of the trails out of Sunrise Visitor Center that lead you closer to the hulking presence of Mount Rainier, Dege Peak walks you just far enough away from the mountain to get a little perspective. With stunning 360-degree views ranging from nearby Cowlitz Chimneys to the far-off peaks of Mount St. Helens, Mount Adams, Glacier Peak and Mount Baker, this perch above Sourdough Ridge is terrific for an easy alpine stroll on a clear day.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Dege Peak

properties.description: Trail 140 represents the only “bottom to top” trail experience for Mount Spokane’s summit, but is frequently enjoyed in smaller sections to create loops of various distances. Middle Trail 140 is located in the heart of the park, connecting between Smith Gap and Saddle Junction.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Middle Trail 140

properties.description: The beautiful lake at Pearrygin Lake State Park is the star of the show here, but a 3-mile trail skirting the eastern edge of the park is a lovely diversion for visitors here.
properties.title: Pearrygin Lake State Park - Rex Derr Trail

properties.description: A steep climb rewards you with huckleberries, stunning mountain views, wildflower meadows and a charming alpine lake along the Pacific Crest Trail.
properties.title: Nannie Ridge-Sheep Lake

properties.description: This loop takes you past two clear and calm lakes, up a steep, brushy trail to the beautifully manicured Pacific Crest Trail, then west under the blocky granite summit of Tinkham Peak and the shining pyramid of Silver Peak before dropping to Windy Pass.
properties.title: Cold Creek Loop via Tinkham and Silver Peaks

properties.description: Enjoy a lowland forest stroll with lots of add-on route options from the Stottlemeyer trailhead on the south end of Port Gamble’s Heritage Forest Park.
properties.title: Port Gamble Heritage Park - Stottlemeyer Loop

properties.description: Peoh Point offers 180-degree views of the Cle Elum Valley and the Stuart range from from atop a 2000-foot cliff with very steep dropoffs. While the views are stunning, use caution at the summit.
properties.title: Peoh Point

properties.description: Wander across the Long Beach peninsula on the Weather Beach Trail to see thousands of shorebirds during spring and fall.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Weather Beach Trail

properties.description: Hike a valley trail through old growth forest to the base of a peak, then an off trail class 2 scramble to the summit.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Hock Mountain

properties.description: The Wetlands Trail is a short (0.65 mile) trail on Tiger Mountain's Tradition Plateau. As the name suggests, it passes through some areas that often are moist and have a prolific growth of ferns. Also, it passes tiny, aptly-named Round Lake whose level fluctuates from year to year, and with the seasons.
properties.title: Wetlands Trail

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Miller Creek Falls

properties.description: A short one-mile loop through a forested park on Vashon Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Fisher Pond Loop

properties.description: Snowshoe or cross-country ski on this road just below the Mount Baker Ski Area.
properties.title: White Salmon Road Snowshoe

properties.description: Per homeowners in Silverton, this trail is on private property and is inaccessible to the public.
properties.title: Silver Gulch Trail

properties.description: Take a short hike up a forested butte near Rattlesnake Lake, just 1.75 miles each way with 900 feet of elevation gain. Reach a summit with views toward the north, from Mount Si to Mailbox Peak, and several other peaks in between. Some hikers judge Cedar Butte to be a better viewpoint than the much-visited West Tiger 3 summit, and it requires less effort and has smaller crowds, so when you are ready for a change of scene check it out.
properties.title: Cedar Butte

properties.description: Bask in a wide variety of wildflowers—including a rare species of cactus, Simpson’s hedgehog, with its hot pink blossoms—chunks of petrified wood, and panoramic views of the Columbia Basin, under usually sunny, blue skies.
properties.title: Whiskey Dick Wildlife Area

properties.description: The gently-rolling Valley Trail offers a 14+ mile one-way hike paralleling Forest Road 28 and links up with a variety of trails along the road so it is possible to do loop or out and back hikes of various lengths and difficulties.
properties.title: Valley Trail

properties.description: Follow a stream between steep sided basalt cliffs up a shady canyon in the transition zone between the Cascade Mountains and the dry shrub-steppe grasslands of eastern Washington.
properties.title: Bear Canyon

properties.description: Combine local art with nature on a stroll through Price Sculpture Forest.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Price Sculpture Forest

properties.description: Take a steep climb through a timber harvest area on the Purcell Mountain Trail. Take a steep climb through a timber harvest area on the Purcell Mountain Trail. This is the longer and more challenging route to Purcell Lookout. If you want a shorter outing, check out the Purcell Lookout entry. Be sure to watch your step, as mountain beavers have been known to dig tunnels in the area and creating hazards for stock animals.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Purcell Mountain Trail

properties.description: With 12 miles of interconnected trails from which to choose, Oxbow Regional Park provides hikers with no end of options for shorter or longer strolls. A variety of walks, from an open meadow upon a ridge, 700-year old trees in an ancient forest, or a National Wild and Scenic River and floodplain to amble along, make for an excellent day trip any time of year.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Oxbow Regional Park

properties.description: Hike a restored trail in the southeast corner of the Tigers, through an area that is very green, with impressive moss cover and with many huge, decaying stumps remaining from logging a century ago.
properties.title: Silent Swamp Loop

properties.description: The trailhead for Griff Creek is behind the Elwha River washout, meaning hikers must do a short road walk to access this steep but quiet trail.
properties.title: Griff Creek

properties.description: A 15-mile one-way bushwhack route along a long ridge west of Lake Wenatchee and north of Highway 2. Route-finding skills required.
properties.title: Poet Ridge (Little Wenatchee Ridge)

properties.description: A long, rambling gateway into the eastern side of Glacier Peak Wilderness, the Entiat River Trail culminates at its namesake glacier with Mount Maude, Seven Fingered Jack and Mount Fernow towering above. Ravaged by wildfires over the years, the majority of the trail is exposed, dry and dusty. Both flora and fauna are slowly returning and the revealed panorama of bordering peaks makes for an extraordinary wilderness corridor.
properties.title: Entiat River

properties.description: Garfield Gulch is a deep ravine located in the north end portion of Tacoma with a short trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Garfield Gulch

properties.description: Access trails, as well as the top of Selah Butte are on private property. Please refrain from visiting this location.
properties.title: Selah Butte

properties.description: This trail is in the William O Douglas wilderness area and offers solitude and unique scenery of Rattlesnake Peaks.
properties.title: Dog Creek

properties.description: This primitive trail can be difficult to follow as it wanders across a broad forested bench in the heart of the Trapper Creek Wilderness.
properties.title: Rim Trail

properties.description: An extensive network of trails is accessible from Camp Sekani Park in the Spokane Valley.
properties.title: Camp Sekani Park

properties.description: The Crystal Springs Sno-Park is a hub for winter recreation. The trails here are open to snowmobilers, cross-country skiers and snowshoers. Some routes are groomed, while others are unmaintained.
properties.title: Crystal Springs Snowshoe

properties.description: Part of King County’s regional trail network, the Lake Youngs Trail is a soft-surface, rolling, sometimes hilly loop around a reservoir and offers a couple connections to other popular trails in the area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Youngs Trail

properties.description: Reaching the summit of Rock Mountain in Okanogan County requires going off trail.
properties.title: Rock Mountain

properties.description: There are more than 12 miles of trails encircling and interweaving the town of North Bonneville. These range from paved and flat to rougher, dirt trails that are somewhat steep in places. All afford nice exercise and views from the valley of the high peaks above the wide Columbia River.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: North Bonneville Heritage Trails

properties.description: Sometimes the crowds at Mount Rainier’s Paradise can be overwhelming. Hike the Moraine Trail to get off of asphalt paths and away from the throngs.  The reward is a view down into the immense Nisqually River Valley from the very edge of its moraine.
properties.title: Moraine Trail

properties.description: The Geophysical Trails are accessible year round, but are primarily used for Nordic skiing in winter (no hiking/snowshoeing on the groomed trails). The trailhead is a SnoPark, so you'll need a Sno-Park permit to park in the winter. For the rest of the year, it's open to non-motorized multi-use.
properties.title: Geophysical Trails

properties.description: Yes, there really is a hut on the Copper Creek Hut trail, and it’s open to the public! The Mount Tahoma Trails Association, a non-profit organization, operates over 50 miles of cross-country ski and snowshoe trails and a system of huts for day and overnight use near Ashford, just west of Mount Rainier National Park.
properties.title: Copper Creek Hut Snowshoe

properties.description: Visit a historic marine camping park that boasts saltwater shoreline that abuts Port Townsend Bay. Rife with military history, the trails here travel through beautiful forest and offer insight into the area's past life, including a former military cemetary.
properties.title: Fort Townsend Historical State Park

properties.description: Carne Mountain is a challenging, yet rewarding hike to the brilliant gold colors of the western larches. Against a backdrop of blue autumn sky and indigo mountains, they are a dazzling sight.
properties.title: Carne Mountain

properties.description: White Chuck Mountain (Northwest Route) is a Class III scramble that requires basic gear, route finding skills, and extreme caution to negotiate successfully and safely. Those who make the hour long trek down a gravel road, deal with a bit of overgrowth and route finding, and brave the scree and chossy rock will be significantly rewarded with phenomenal views of Thornton Lake and nearby peaks Pugh, Sloan and Glacier
properties.title: White Chuck Mountain

properties.description: This short loop is located above Cranberry Lake and introduces visitors to the coastal forest of Deception Pass State Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - Upland Interpretive Trail

properties.description: Climb through second-growth forest to a not-so-dry creek, while enjoying spring wildflowers and views of nearby Lake Cushman and surrounding peaks. WTA has done years of work on this trail, improving it from a rough footpath to a pleasant, easy-to-follow (if steep) trail.
properties.title: Dry Creek

properties.description: Take a shortcut to the summit of Squak Mountain from Phil's Creek Trail.
properties.title: Summit Trail

properties.description: This area is being actively restored to a natural state. A loop hike suitable for all ages winds through wetlands in a critical salmon rearing area.
properties.title: Twisp River Rearing Ponds

properties.description: Take a short, heart-rate-elevating climb to a former fire lookout site with extensive views of the Columbia River Gorge, Oregon, and the Silver Star Scenic Area.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Grassy Knoll

properties.description: At 71-acres, the Tacoma Nature Center preserve boasts more than 20 different species of mammals and about 100 species of birds. It is also home to reptiles, amphibians and native plant populations.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Tacoma Nature Center Interpretive Walks

properties.description: The Independence Pass trail is impassable past the first 1.5 miles due to significant washouts and cannot currently be connected with the Boundary Trail to complete this loop.
properties.title: Independence Pass Loop

properties.description: Explore a restored estuary made possible by fish barrier removal and subsequent habitat restoration.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Greenhead Slough

properties.description: On the edge of Maury Island, this 275-acre natural area has the longest undeveloped shoreline along the Puget Sound in King County.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Maury Island Natural Area

properties.description: You can visit several parks along the way of this urban trail including Celebration Park, Madrona Park and Panther Lake Park. It also passes by the Weyerhaeuser King County Aquatic Centre. The paved path is ADA accessible and allows leashed dogs.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: BPA Trail

properties.description: Take one of three different routes to the top of Swakane Peak for expansive views across the Columbia River and a  peek-a-boo view of Icicle Ridge to the west.  Two of the routes can be combined for a loop day trip.
properties.title: Swakane Peak

properties.description: This very short and flat interpretive trail offers a wonderful way to take in the sights and sounds of a small lake still recovering from the 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens.
properties.title: Meta Lake

properties.description: East Peak is a slightly longer, more challenging hike than the extremely popular route to Rattlesnake Ledge. Allow a little more time, and be sure to bring a map of the area!
properties.title: East Peak

properties.description: You’re bound to run into all manner of people on the Pratt Lake Trail: trail runners, families, beginning hikers, backpackers hungry for a night out in the woods, even folks looking for fish (in the lakes, not on the trail). All that traffic does a number on the trail, but fortunately WTA work parties have worked hard here, ensuring that all trail users can easily follow the picturesque path to Pratt Lake.
properties.title: Pratt Lake Basin

properties.description: The War Creek Trail starts out along the Twisp River, just outside the town of Twisp. It is one of the many great options for accessing the northern shores of Lake Chelan from the Twisp River Road. Although this trail officially ends at the ridge overlooking the lake it connects with the Purple Pass Trail, which descends to the shore.
properties.title: War Creek

properties.description: Miller Peak is an excellent, challenging day hike, which gains 3200 feet to the high point. But all that climbing affords you breathtaking views of the Stuarts, and much of the Teanaway area, as well as Mount Rainier.
properties.title: Miller Peak

properties.description: This unique state park houses one of the largest public observatories in the nation. Visitors can peer through the lens of this telescope to view solar shows and magical glimpses of the night sky.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Goldendale Observatory State Park

properties.description: The south end of Vashon Island is quieter than the business district, making it a lovely place to take a calming walk with your family. Burton Acres park offers a short but fulfilling hike. The 64-acre park features more than 1.2 miles of trails to explore on a loop route.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Burton Acres Park

properties.description: Bearpaw Lake is a small fishing lake near the Damfino Lakes Trail, which is the shortest route to the exquisite High Divide.
properties.title: Bearpaw Mountain Lake

properties.description: This former stock driveway was maintained by sheep herders so they could drive their sheep to the beautiful sloping meadows of grass & flowers above the South Fork Trout Creek. After the 2003 Needle Creek Fire, the maintenance effectively stopped. So, until a significant effort is made to clear the tread, this is a very difficult trail to precisely follow.
properties.title: Trout Creek

properties.description: Following a series of winding, snow-covered forest roads, the route to Coal Pass culminates in sweeping views of Mount Baker’s glaciated northwest flank.
properties.title: Coal Pass Snowshoe

properties.description: A quiet lake surrounded by healthy forest and marshy meadows invites hikers to find a seat on its shoreline and rest the soul.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Jug Lake

properties.description: The Gloyd Seeps Wildlife Area is part of the Columbia Basin Wildlife Area. This southern unit is disconnected from the main Gloyd Seeps area to the north. This is a popular fishing access off of Highway 17 with a short trail running along the edge of Rocky Ford Creek.
properties.title: Gloyd Seeps - South

properties.description: This is a fine hike on a well maintained, albeit busy trail through a cool forest with views of the Cedar River watershed, Mount Si, Mount Washington, Rattlesnake Lake and Chester Morse Lake.
properties.title: Rattlesnake Ledge

properties.description: A summit in the Central Cascades that requires technical experience, gear, and route-finding abilities. There are three ways to access Mount Index.
properties.title: Mount Index

properties.description: It's appropriate that this hike begins in the heart of Issaquah. In the language of the native tribes, Ishquowh means "sound of water birds." The raspy name of this mountain destination, meanwhile, comes from the raucous calls of the herons that migrate through this area in the spring and fall--their mighty squak, squak, squak! echoes off the forested slopes of Squak Mountain.
properties.title: Squak Mountain's East Side Loop

properties.description: Explore the desert of eastern Washington at this National Wildlife Refuge.
properties.title: Columbia National Wildlife Refuge  - Crab Creek

properties.description: A strenuous class 3+ scramble in the Olympic National Forest
properties.title: Mount Washington

properties.description: A short walking path near historic downtown Snohomish offers a moment to connect with nature, mere feet from the hustle and bustle of shops and restaurants.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Snohomish Riverfront Trail

properties.description: The White River Snowshoe follows the Mather Memorial Highway (SR 410) through a snowy river valley in Mount Rainier National Park. What is a bustling highway in summer becomes a quiet snowshoe ramble in the winter.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mather Memorial Highway Snowshoe

properties.description: The Kalama Ski Trail is a ski route near Mount St. Helens that connects the Cougar Sno-Park with the Kalama Horse Camp. Visitors should expect to share the area with snowmobilers on weekends, though it is often very quiet on weekdays.
properties.title: Kalama Ski Trail

properties.description: Pierce Mountain Trail is a gentle trail up Sourdough Mountain from the Big Beaver trail.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Pierce Mountain Trail

properties.description: The Sunrise area of Mount Rainier National Park offers many fantastic views of The Mountain. But don’t neglect the other views. Scramble up Skyscraper Mountain to enjoy a full 360 degree view of numerous lofty peaks, verdant treeless parks, and river valleys far below.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Skyscraper Mountain

properties.description: Fairy-tale roaming! For day hiking, roam and turn around when you feel like it – but you may never feel like heading back due to the wide open views, flower show, ponderosas, and wildlife.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Thirteenmile

properties.description: The family friendly trails of 670-acre Rockport State Park explore an ancient forest where dappled sunlight illuminates mossy trees and lush ferns — perfect for a springtime stroll.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Rockport State Park

properties.description: Hike a challenging loop outside of the Windy Ridge area of Mount St. Helens, including a route-finding scramble to the pass. For your efforts, you’re rewarded with expansive, ever-changing views of one of the world’s most dynamic landscapes.
properties.title: Plains of Abraham - Windy Pass Loop

properties.description: Old ranch roads take you past basalt cliffs and endless expanses of shoulder-high grassland to a small lake under a big sky.
properties.title: Escure Ranch - Turtle Lake

properties.description: Much of the trails in this area follow old roads and Jeep roads around the area. It's an excellent area to bring dogs (on-leash) and apart from some blowdowns, is a very easy trail to follow with a low grade.
properties.title: Indian Dan State Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: This is a hike to a two-tiered waterfall located in a fairyland grotto with many large moss covered boulders.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Wahclella Falls

properties.description: A great first-of-spring hike for the whole family less than an hour from Walla Walla.  A top of ridge hike looks down into the North Fork of the Umatilla River.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Grouse Mountain

properties.description: Seattle's Golden Gardens Park is best known for its wide sandy beach; on summer weekends, the large parking lot may be full and the beach crowded. Less well-known is the extensive trail system on the steep slopes east of the railroad tracks, constructed as a WPA project in the 1930s, with wide trails and stone staircases. Today, some of the stonework shows signs of age but the main trails still are well-maintained and in good condition.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Golden Gardens Park

properties.description: The East Crater Trail is a heavily used connector to the Pacific Crest Trail that also provides relatively easy access to the heart of the Indian Heaven Wilderness.
properties.title: East Crater

properties.description: This strenuous hike out of Monte Cristo features everything from smooth incline to rough rock scrambles. There is tough but absolutely beautiful trail along the way and it gets even better once you reach your destination.
properties.title: Glacier Basin

properties.description: The Williams Lake Trail leads to a sweet lake at the base of La Bohn Peak off the Dutch Miller Gap Trail.  From the junction, the trail climbs about a mile through sub-alpine forests and meadows stuffed with huckleberries, terminating at Williams Lake.
properties.title: Williams Lake

properties.description: With few grand views of sweeping mountains or endless landscapes, the Old Timers' Horse Trail encourages hikers to focus on what's in front of them and enjoy the scenery of the forest. In the Little Pend Oreille Natural Wildlife Refuge, enjoy wildlife viewing and plenty of wildflowers.
properties.title: Old Timers' Horse Trail

properties.description: A short and secluded walk along Fifteenmile creek offers views of waterfalls, cliffs and old coal mines.
properties.title: Grand Canyon of Fifteenmile Creek

properties.description: Whether you're a naturalist looking for flora and fauna, a training trail runner, a dog owner looking for a nice walk, a parent with an energetic child or just a busy urban dweller seeking an break from the city, Seward Park is the place for you.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Seward Park

properties.description: For a more strenuous snowshoe, head out to Deer Creek and the Lake Kelcema trail. From the parking area, the route proceeds up Deer Creek Road (Road 4052).  Watch out for tubers and sledders on the lower portion.
properties.title: Lake Kelcema Snowshoe

properties.description: Dishman Hills Natural Area's Enchanted Ravine is located just south of Camp Caro and within the main entrance loop. Enchanted Ravine is an excellent place to observe the Dishman Hill's exposed 1.5 billion-year-old bedrock, which is among the oldest geologic features in Washington state.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Natural Area - Enchanted Ravine

properties.description: A long, steady climb takes you from the Stehekin Landing to a high pass more than a mile above the surface of Lake Chelan. Those willing to complete the eight miles and 5,700 feet of climbing needed to reach the pass are rewarded with incredible views of the lake gorge, the Stehekin Valley and peaks stretching from the Cascade Pass area to the Glacier Peak Wilderness.
properties.title: Purple Pass

properties.description: Visit a boardwalk and short paved pathway near one of the last remaining waterfront saltwater estuaries in Washington.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Edmonds Marsh

properties.description: Lose yourself amid ancient giants on this 1.5 mile flat loop around the Iron Creek Campground.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Iron Creek Campground Loop

properties.description: Zig Zag is a solitary lake set high in the southern Cascades.  While difficult to get to, it's worth the time and effort to explore this area.
properties.title: Zig Zag Lake

properties.description: Acquired by King County in 2000, McGarvey Park Open Space is a 400-acre multiuse forest connecting King  County’s Petrovitsky Park with Wetland 14 Natural Area and Spring Lake/Lake Desire Park.
properties.title: McGarvey Park

properties.description: Stop over at this park to stretch your legs during a long drive on I-90.
properties.title: Blue Heron Park

properties.description: Kids will love this hike because there’s so much to see: a rushing river, a lush old-growth forest dotted with wildflowers and, if you’re lucky, plenty of wildlife.
properties.title: Cooper River

properties.description: The Pass Lake Loop provides a nice, quiet forested trail near the popular Deception Point State Park. The trailhead is near the boat launch for Pass Lake at the junction of Highway 20 and Rosario Road.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - Pass Lake

properties.description: River Meadows Park is a great place for a nice hike that isn't too far out of town, just about 15 minutes outside of Arlington.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: River Meadows Park

properties.description: A popular trail, thanks to its gentle, family friendly grade with amazing destinations. The natural water slide area at Denny Creek is a must visit for families! Keekwulee Falls offers a stunning viewpoint that is easily accessible. Snowshoe Falls maybe a bit elusive and more difficult to see from the trail, but is also a beautiful natural wonder.
properties.title: Denny Creek

properties.description: The trek to Reflection and Louise Lakes is a quintessential Mount Rainier snowshoeing experience — the bright, flat expanse of snow and ice-covered mountain lakes, subalpine meadows that offer opportunities for romping, stupendous views of The Mountain and the Tatoosh Range, and the south end of the Mazama Ridge beckoning you to follow.
properties.title: Reflection and Louise Lakes Snowshoe

properties.description: Enjoy a short hike through lush greenery on this newly renovated trail.
properties.title: Elk Ridge Trail

properties.description: Pass though both forest and meadow on the way to this heritage site on the aptly named Beauty Mountain within Mount Spokane State Park.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 130 to CCC Cabin

properties.description: Rarely can hikers approach a climbers’ realm so easily, with minimal elevation gain, and enjoy beautiful views all along the way.
properties.title: Ptarmigan Ridge

properties.description: Trade the sounds of the city for birdsong and enjoy some quiet time outside just a short distance from the center of Federal Way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Panther Lake Trail

properties.description: The Sherman Creek Wildlife Area lies just west of Kettle Falls across the Columbia River. A network of trails crisscross through the portion of the wildlife area that sits between Highway 20 and the Columbia River.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sherman Creek Wildlife Area

properties.description: Lake Valhalla is a gem, tucked under Lichtenberg Mountain and Mount McCausland on the PCT North of Stevens Pass. The lake is a great day hike in summer or fall and accessible by snowshoe in the winter. Wildflowers abound in early summer, berries in late summer and fall colors make vivid surroundings in autumn.
properties.title: Lake Valhalla

properties.description: Yellow Island Preserve is an island in the San Juan archipelago. The entire island is a preserve managed by the Nature Conservancy, and luckily for us, visitors are allowed between 10 am and 4 pm.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Yellow Island Preserve

properties.description: An overlook accessible from the Table Mountain trail, Tronsen Head offers nice views of the surrounding valleys, excellent in the fall when the larches are turning.
properties.title: Tronsen Head

properties.description: Pugh Ridge is a steep ridgeline trail branching off of the North Fork Entiat around 2.5 miles in, and connecting back down with South Pyramid Creek, making for a ideal loop trip.
properties.title: Pugh Ridge

properties.description: With the Elwha Dam gone and the landscape re-sculpted to approximate historic contours, the gravel access road to Elwha Dam has opened to non-motorized travel. There's also a very short trail leaving from the parking area to two observation areas.
properties.title: Lake Aldwell Overlook Trail

properties.description: The CrossTown Trail is made up of a patchwork of segments of trail and sidewalk that wind through the town of Newcastle to deliver hikers into Cougar Mountain Regional Park.
properties.title: CrossTown Trail - Newcastle

properties.description: The Mitchell Peak Trail has two trailheads, the northern access has been closed to the public since 2011. A much longer hike (see Black Hole Falls Hike) is now required to get to summit where a Forest Service fire look out used to perch in beautiful sub-alpine terrain with panorama views of the major southwest Washington & Oregon volcanoes.
properties.title: Mitchell Peak

properties.description: Rich in historical artifacts, lush foliage, wooden bridges, and waterfalls, the well-groomed and well-traveled Coal Creek Trail is a satisfying hike for families, trail runners, history buffs, and avid hikers.
properties.title: Coal Creek Trail

properties.description: A good, suburban retreat for getting that outdoor fix on a busy weekend. Here you'll find casual walking with lots of extra attractions, great for families.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lynndale Loop

properties.description: Deception Pass State Park is one of the most popular Washington state parks and it is easy to see why. There are beautiful beaches, mature woodlands, great views, lakes, and a beautifully built bridge high on rocks above two narrow waterways. This nice trail will take you through all of this.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - Goose Rock

properties.description: This infrequently-maintained trail in the Icicle Creek area provides access to Icicle Ridge and Lake Ida, but requires the navigation skills.
properties.title: Painter Creek

properties.description: Burnt Rock is a scenic, fire-scarred outcrop near the Pacific Crest Trail on the west side of Mount Adams. The best way to approach Burnt Rock is via Divide Camp Trail. This route offers the easiest climb to the PCT, after which point the hike becomes a nearly level promenade of vistas, wildflowers, and cascades.
properties.title: Burnt Rock

properties.description: This nature trail is ideal when you’re camping at beautiful Sullivan Lake and want a short, woodsy hike before breakfast or after supper.
properties.title: Sullivan Lake Nature Trail

properties.description: This hike takes you gradually up to a ridge looking west to Mt Rainier’s Tahoma and the White River and on to the Crystal Mountain Summit.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Northway Trail

properties.description: Hike this lovely, flat trail in the forests of the North Cascades to a quiet waterfall about 2.5 miles from Holden Village.
properties.title: Monkey Bear Falls

properties.description: Overgrown, rugged and likely difficult to navigate at times, the Klickitat Loop Trail links together multiple trails (including the eponymous trail itself) to create a large loop just outside of the Goat Rocks Wilderness.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Klickitat Loop Trail

properties.description: This trail follows the drainage to join the Falls Creek Trail. The trailhead is found behind a gated Shaser Road, making it a 4-mile road walk or bike ride to hike this four mile round-trip trail.
properties.title: Etienne Creek

properties.description: Dive deep into the heart of the Pasayten Wilderness on the Andrews Creek trail. Walk along Andrews Creek through a burn zone. Connect to the Boundary trail after passing through a lush meadow of wildflowers.
properties.title: Andrews Creek

properties.description: The Swanson Lakes Wildlife Area consists of approximately 21,000 acres in Lincoln County. Explore riparian and wetland habitats and enjoy beautiful views.
properties.title: Swanson Lakes Wildlife Area

properties.description: Visit a trail where rushing rivers, placid lakes, and wild forests abound.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Greenwater and Echo Lakes

properties.description: A brushy, steep trail to the Cascade high country.
properties.title: Hatchery Creek

properties.description: Escape the crowds and access early season views in the Teanaway. Starting on an old forest road and ending on a climbers’ trail, this mostly exposed hike passes through wildflowers and a burn area to reach the Johnson Mountain summit with views of the Enchantments, Rainier, the Teanaway River Valley, and wind farms of eastern Washington.
properties.title: Johnson Mountain

properties.description: Lions Park is an urban park with a walking loop alongside the Port Washington Narrows.
properties.title: Lions Park

properties.description: This hiker-only route is not an official trail It is a user-built route, and so is a rough and rugged climb. The way is often overgrown and the road to access the trailhead requires a high-clearance car.
properties.title: Church Lake

properties.description: A small nature trail outside of Republic.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Curlew Lake State Park - Curlew Lake Nature Trail

properties.description: Battle Ground Lake State Park is a local favorite, particularly good for families with its short loop around the lake and the playground.
properties.title: Battle Ground Lake State Park - Lower Lake Trail

properties.description: The highest and loveliest of the Scottish Lakes, Lake Donald is reached via a way trail 1/2 mile and 500' above Loch Eileen.
properties.title: Lake Donald

properties.description: The CASEE trail system consists of two looped forest paths and ends in an arboretum.
properties.title: CASEE Forest and Nature Trails

properties.description: Cut across to the south section of the Tiger Mountain Trail from the South Tiger Traverse.
properties.title: South Tiger Powerline

properties.description: Two approaches, one longer and easier and the other shorter and harder, access this spur trail off the PCT to a serene mountain lake.
properties.title: Wood Lake

properties.description: An up and down meandering trail that leads through open forest, wildflower meadows and a side trip to some fantastic views. The road up does most of the work, so the climb is not too long, and can be done by most hikers.
properties.title: Tonga Ridge / Mount Sawyer

properties.description: Just 15 minutes from downtown Olympia, Darlin Creek Preserve is a peaceful getaway where wetlands, creeks and forest come together to create a haven for wildlife.
