This 312-acre nature preserve, protected by Capitol Land Trust in 2016, offers visitors a chance to explore streams and beaver ponds on a network of gentle loop trails.
properties.title: Darlin Creek Preserve

properties.description: This family-friendly educational center features a short nature trail that will take you through forests and meadows. At low-tide, you can also explore down onto the beach via path away from the center and a spiral staircase.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Breazeale Interpretive Center

properties.description: A relaxing walk through land once slated for a housing development, the trail around Upright Head Preserve is an easy hike where one can watch ferries travel from one island to the next while waiting for their own. Remnants of roads and utilities make up part of the trail, with the rest on narrow dirt paths through the dense forest.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Upright Head Preserve

properties.description: Tucked deep in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Ivanhoe Lake is accessible via the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River Trail from the west or the Pacific Crest Trail and Dutch Miller Gap  from the east side.
properties.title: Ivanhoe Lake

properties.description: Often used to create loops in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, the Frosty - Wildhorse trail departs from a junction with the Icicle Creek trail and climbs a moderate grade across densely-wooded terrain.
properties.title: Frosty Pass

properties.description: Follow a trail up an old mining trail before reaching a boulder-filled basin with views of Sloan Peak above. The first half of the hike is fairly easy, while the second is a steep climb through a creek bed. Navigational skills are required for this hike.
properties.title: Bedal Basin

properties.description: An infrequently-used but surprisingly charming trail leading to the site of a former waterfall, and offering the only access to Spirit Lake.
properties.title: Harmony Falls

properties.description: If you’re prepared to do some bushwhacking and trail-finding, this trail offers winding forest trails, sweeping mountain views and solitude.
properties.title: Rock Creek

properties.description: This old railbed now provides recreation for bikes, hikers, and equestrians between Tuwkila and Pacific.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Interurban Trail (South)

properties.description: Hiking to Jumpoff Lookout may not be for everybody, but if you make the trek, it has a lot to offer. From a family-friendly lake to a more challenging climb to a fire lookout.
properties.title: Jumpoff Lookout

properties.description: Hike to a small lava dome with an associated summit crater in southern Washington.
properties.title: West Crater

properties.description: This mostly flat paved trail meanders through two parks and quiet residential neighborhoods, and is a great option for a long walk or jogging workout without traveling very far from home.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Water Flume Line Trail

properties.description: If you've hiked to Rattlesnake Ledges and beyond from Rattlesnake Lake, this is a delightful alternative. Thanks to the handiwork of various groups in the outdoor community, hikers can now reach Rattlesnake Mountain from the west, starting from a trailhead at Snoqualmie Point.
properties.title: Rattlesnake Mountain

properties.description: This agricultural field turned city park is still in development, but it is an open space with wetlands and some informal trails where visitors can wander.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Sammamish Valley Park

properties.description: Slide Lake is a short but remote hike that samples a rugged slice of the Glacier Peak Wilderness. Popular among anglers, the hour-long drive up the single lane logging road deters crowds and ensures relative solitude. Magnificent old growth and a mountain lake with views toward snowy peaks are the reward.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Slide Lake

properties.description: Explore Strawberry Point Preserve on Whidbey Island via a hilly lollipop loop.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Strawberry Point Preserve

properties.description: A short, level hike through second growth conifers to a wide beach and a brackish estuary.
properties.title: Foulweather Bluff Preserve Trail

properties.description: Hike along a ridgeline to the summit of Tiger 1. Access from Tiger Mountain Trail, West Tiger 1, and Main Tiger Trail.
properties.title: Poo Top

properties.description: Find this tiny gem of a state park on the Kitsap Peninsula, tucked between Bainbridge Island and Bremerton. Vistors here will find prime beachside meandering and a relaxing atmosphere, enhanced by the dense forest typical of land in the Puget Sound area.
properties.title: Illahee State Park

properties.description: Northern access to Squak Mountain.
properties.title: Bullitt Access Trail

properties.description: This snowshoe route follows several forest roads to a viewpoint of Lake Wenatchee.
properties.title: Wenatchee Ridge Snowshoe (Lake Wenatchee Area)

properties.description: A short one mile trail around a quiet fishing lake in northeastern Washington.
properties.title: Browns Lake

properties.description: Connecting the Puget and Samish neighborhoods of Bellingham is the Samish Crest Trail, meandering through the Samish Crest Open Space, where hikers will find even more trails to explore.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Samish Crest Open Space

properties.description: Take a one-mile detour off the High Point Trail until it rejoins the Tiger Mountain Trail. Intersect with Dwight's Way Trail about three-quarters of a mile in.
properties.title: Lingering Trail

properties.description: This is a loop made up of several well signed trails on Blanchard Mountain in the Chuckanuts. The trail offers that other-world ancientness with its dark forests, moss and house-sized boulders. It makes a good year-round hike, with a route that passes by waterfalls, swamps, two lakes, wildlife activity, old growth and evidence of logging operations from the nineteenth century.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lily and Lizard Lake Loop

properties.description: The hike suggested here visits the site of the flaming geyser and the bubbling geyser, and includes the River Trail and Ridge Trail, all encompassed in the park. It follows roughly a figure eight path that can be traversed in any order. If you are a weekend visitor, you may need to park where space is available and modify your route accordingly.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Flaming Geyser State Park

properties.description: The Snow Lakes trail is known mostly as the long, gradual way into the Enchantments; but Nada Lake (and nearby Snow Lake) is a worthwhile — if deceptively grueling — destination in its own right. The narrow isthmus between the lakes offers a majestic view across the water to the towering heights of McClellan Peak.
properties.title: Nada Lake

properties.description: Lower Tuscohatchie Lake is accessible from multiple different trailheads, offering hikers multiple hiking options for a great weekend getaway or long day hike.
properties.title: Lower Tuscohatchie Lake via Denny Creek Trail

properties.description: The Steam Hoist Trail is a short loop trail within the Cougar Mountain trail network. One end of this trail connects to the Rainbow Town trail and the other connects to the Wildside Trail.
properties.title: Steam Hoist

properties.description: Running between Wilkeson and Carbonado, this branch off the Foothills Trail is an old railroad grade with a wide path that loops through second growth woodland to gain 400 feet of elevation between the two towns.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Foothills Trail - Wilkeson to Carbonado

properties.description: Take a walk in the forest on this trail as it climbs past a shallow lake and continues nearly to treeline at Twisp Pass. The upper half of the trail is flowered in summer and the power of avalanches is evident in the pick-up-sticks debris field shortly before Dagger Lake. At Twisp Pass in an intersection with many informal trails for further exploration.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Twisp Pass via Dagger Lake

properties.description: A short hike out to an interesting remnant of the mining activity that took place on Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Cave Hole

properties.description: There are three and a half miles of trails in Whatcom Falls Park. Many routes wind through the forests, some overlooking the creek gorge and still pools. Some wind through open meadows, while others stay in deep forest.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Whatcom Falls Park

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mutton Mountain

properties.description: Indian Island County Park offers two glorious miles of shoreline that can be hiked on the beach, on the bluffs, or a combination of the two. Leisurely beach ramblers, trail runners, and everyone in between will enjoy easy access to nature and the breath-taking scenery of Oak Bay.
properties.title: Indian Island County Park

properties.description: Hike a 2-mile forest trail on the north side of Squak Mountain to reach the site of a former cabin owned by the Bullitt family. Only the massive fireplace and foundation remain today.
properties.title: Bullitt Fireplace Trail

properties.description: Birdwatchers will delight in the wide variety of winded beasts to see at Juanita Bay Park. The 110-acre urban wildlife habitat area consists of five major plant communities, including wet meadow, marsh, open water and wetland.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Juanita Bay Park

properties.description: Hunter Falls is a narrow, deep cataract. The crashing waters turn an otherwise dry environment into a burst of white water and greenery.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Hunter Falls (Oregon)

properties.description: Once a popular I-90 guidebook staple, Rooster Mountain trail is actually an unofficial trail up an old road bed. The Forest Service does not maintain it. Route-finding skills to tackle this overgrown, ghostly Cascades excursion. There are far easier and more rewarding peaks in the area, but if you are looking for a challenging trail off the beaten path, quite literally in this case, Rooster Mountain may be just the hike for you.
properties.title: Rooster Mountain

properties.description: While the rest of Eastern Washington is still covered in ice and snow, cross the border into Idaho and descend into North America’s deepest canyon to find early wildflowers and regional history.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Kirkwood Ranch (Oregon)

properties.description: The Whitehorse Trail runs for 27 miles along an old railroad grade, connecting the towns of Arlington and Darrington. The route generally follows Highway 530 and the North Fork Sauk River as it approaches the cascade foothills.
properties.title: Whitehorse Trail

properties.description: This short trail skirts along the northern edge of Steamboat Lake.
properties.title: Steamboat Lake

properties.description: With wide open views at the top, Thorp Mountain is a worthwhile destination, even if the steep ascent to the peak might seem challenging.
properties.title: No Name Ridge - Thorp Mountain

properties.description: A scramble to Cabinet Peak in the North Cascades. Technical expertise recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cabinet Peak

properties.description: Embrace the pastoral as you walk between central Whidbey Island parks alongside working farmland and wide, open fields.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Walking Ebey's Trail System

properties.description: This hike along Baker Lake is a busy, popular trail in summer. It is a nice off season walk though, and is perfect on a crisp, clear winter day. With the leaves off the trees, views that aren't possible in summer emerge; the surrounding peaks and the mossy green silhouettes of the leafless maple trees cover the hillside. A bonus any time of year are the many creeks, quaint bridges, large old-growth trees and of course, Mount Baker as the main attraction.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: East Bank Baker Lake

properties.description: Formerly known as the Nisqually National Wildlife Refuge and renamed to honor the memory of a noted activist,  this an excellent year-round destination for wildlife viewing and photography.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Billy Frank Jr. Nisqually National Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: Hike a short trail that leads to one of the best viewpoints in the San Juans, with views of other San Juan Islands and of Canada's Gulf Islands.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Turtleback Mountain Preserve - Turtlehead Summit

properties.description: The Bayview Trail is a segment of paved trail that runs along a powerline corridor in a residential area in Marysville.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bayview Trail

properties.description: Anderson Glacier is a fantastic multi-night backpacking trip at 34 miles roundtrip to the glacier and back. A big unnamed lake fed by the glacier melt sits under the snowy slopes of Mount Anderson at 7,303 feet, towering above you. It's a beautiful place, but getting here is not an easy trek.
properties.title: Anderson Glacier

properties.description: A suburban utility easement trail with nice views of the Sammamish Valley and Bear Creek watershed with links to many other local walking opportunities.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redmond Powerline Trail

properties.description: The Danville-Georgetown Open Space is a greenspace habitat offering a multi-use trail network through a working forest in King County's Maple Valley. The Danville-Georgetown Open Space is named after the historical railroad line that traveled through the site and the former Georgetown mining town.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Danville-Georgetown Trail System

properties.description: Arnold Peak is located in the Pasayten Wilderness near the Canadian Border.
properties.title: Arnold Peak

properties.description: Wildflowers and views of the Kettle River Valley reward hikers of this lightly-used trail not far from Rebublic. After climbing steeply up to the shoulder of Edds Mountain, you'll ramble ridge-tops until you run into the Kettle Crest Trail.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Edds Mountain

properties.description: A nice riverside walk through former burn areas in the Entiat area of Washington.
properties.title: Upper Mad River Trail

properties.description: Accessible only by bridge or boat, Jarrell Cove State Park is one of a few state parks on Harstine Island. It offers saltwater access and a campground.
properties.title: Jarrell Cove State Park

properties.description: Explore roads and trails on, and around, Cap Sante, an impressive rocky headland at the northeast corner of Anacortes. Enjoy views extending from Mount Baker to Mount Rainier, plus the busy harbor.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Cap Sante Park

properties.description: Hike up a steep, dry ridgeline in the Entiat with 360 degree views of the Columbia River, the wine country of eastern Washington, and wildflowers galore.
properties.title: Keystone Ridge

properties.description: This popular summer trail, with 25 different interpretive stops, offers a wonderful place to learn about woodland ecosystems. Just under 3 miles of trails through woods and meadows near the summit of Blewett Pass, and five log benches throughout, provide hikers with fascinating views. It also gives insight into an area recovering after a burn towards the end of the trail.
properties.title: Swauk Forest Discovery Trail

properties.description: Experience the rugged beauty of the Entiat mountains, rich in wild flower meadows, jagged peaks, and solitude. These trails, though occasionally steep and loose, harbor fantastic corners, wildlife, and old-school outdoorsmanship that many crowded trails now lack.
properties.title: North Fork Entiat River

properties.description: The Wildside Trail runs through the northwest corner of Cougar Mountain Park and offers many connections to other trails.
properties.title: Wildside Connector

properties.description: Stunning views, stargazing, backcountry lakes and plentiful wildlife await you on this classic 19-mile loop on the Olympic Mountains’ stunning Seven Lakes Basin and High Divide Trail.
properties.title: High Divide - Seven Lakes Basin Loop

properties.description: The Willapa National Wildlife Refuge is a haven of quiet in the southwest corner of Washington, just north of Astoria. Long Island is a section of the refuge that is especially quiet, since it's only accessible by boat.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Long Island

properties.description: Mount Townsend offers rhododendrons in May and June, wildflowers June through August, then berries in August and September and fall colors in, well, fall. Add in old growth, some tucked away waterfalls, and a windswept, turtleback summit with views north across the Strait and San Juans, west and south into and along the Olympics and east across the Sound to the Cascades, and you've got the perfect year-round hike.
properties.title: Mount Townsend

properties.description: On a clear day, some of the area’s most notable peaks are visible from the crest of Mallardy Ridge, reached by snowshoeing along an easy-to-follow route.
properties.title: Mallardy Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: Grand Ridge Park includes 7 miles of WTA-built trail through western redcedar trees, sword ferns, nettles, berries and, at times, slugs. This trail is a little piece of the backcountry close to Seattle and is open to hikers, mountain bikers and equestrians.
properties.title: Grand Ridge Park

properties.description: Climb through incredible high-mountain meadows, then scramble up a rocky peak to amazing three-volcano panoramas, and along a stark knife-edge ridge to a divide between the Packwood Lake basin and the Tieton River valley.
properties.title: Old Snowy Mountain - Elk Pass

properties.description: This 6-mile loop offers a nice day hike option in the highlands of Eastern Washington, utilizing part of the scenic Kettle Crest Trail, and exploring the Sherman Pass area.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sherman Peak Loop

properties.description: A scramble to the top of the main ridge that towers above the Snoqualmie Pass section of the Pacific Crest Trail. Climbing gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Kendall Peak

properties.description: The snowshoe route into Commonwealth Basin is not clearly marked or blazed. Visitors here should plan their route in advance, go prepared for winter travel, and be able to identify avalanche risk.
properties.title: Commonwealth Basin Snowshoe

properties.description: This single-track trail starts at the West Fork trailhead and winds its way up the ridge to connect with multiple old roads and trails in the Teanaway Community Forest.
properties.title: Teanaway Community Forest - Big Sandy

properties.description: Swauk Forest Discovery Trail is a scenic loop adventure set among a bountiful mixed forest. Located on the south side of Blewett Pass, the trailhead is both convenient and efficient, giving the hiker a 4120-foot starting point. Periodic views that look onto higher peaks are framed by cheery ponderosa and Douglas fir.
properties.title: Swauk Forest Discovery Trail Snowshoe

properties.description: A very short connector trail between the Elwha River trail and the Geyser Valley trail.
properties.title: Rica Canyon Trail

properties.description: This Whitman County Park is located a short distance west of US 195 and boasts a pretty developed park with a playground, plus a 0.75-mile singletrack loop hiking trail.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Klemgard Park

properties.description: Hike 8 miles on a trail that passes many lakes, through wildflower fields, and connects with the Pacific Crest Trail.
properties.title: Round The Mountain

properties.description: Twin Ponds Park is in the City of Shoreline, and contains several family-friendly trails accessible year-round. The park has two small lakes where diverse waterfowl can be viewed, while areas of forest support other bird life.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Twin Ponds Park

properties.description: Anthracite Peak is the unofficial name for the peak reachable from Coal Lake Road in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.
properties.title: Anthracite Peak

properties.description: An off-trail scramble to a summit above Eightmile Lake.
properties.title: Eightmile Mountain

properties.description: A short trail through undeveloped state park lands to a section of shoreline on the Key Peninsula.
properties.title: Haley State Park

properties.description: This short, family-friendly trail is a great spot for viewing impressive old growth and finding a reprieve from the strong summer sunshine.
properties.title: Twin Firs Loop

properties.description: Wander up this desolate wilderness valley upon a long forgotten trail. A cascading waterfall, and a steep, gravelly trail may be your only friend. Access to this trail is via the well maintained, Robinson Creek Trail.
properties.title: Beauty Creek

properties.description: Hike through and alongside coastal forest, rocky cliffs and the wild Pacific coast on a relatively well-maintained route.
properties.title: North Coast Route

properties.description: A nice afternoon hike near Darrington up an abandoned road to an old mine.
properties.title: Mine Road Trail

properties.description: Preston – Snoqualmie is a 6.5 mile one-way, paved, rail-to-trail path that trail meanders through a densely wooded environ and intermittently offers unique perspectives of the Snoqualmie River Valley, leading to a zoomed-out viewpoint of Snoqualmie Falls.
properties.title: Preston-Snoqualmie Trail

properties.description: Navaho Pass is an excellent introduction to the Teanaway area. Rife with wildflowers, fascinating geology, and just enough elevation gain to keep it interesting, this hike has just about everything that the Teanaway is known for.
properties.title: Navaho Pass

properties.description: The Eightmile Creek Snowshoe is a snowy road walk during the winter. This busy summer road becomes a beautiful backdrop for a winter walk. Turn around at either the Eightmile Lake Trailhead or carry on a little farther to the Stuart Lake trailhead. Be aware of avalanche conditions along the road before heading here for a snowshoe outing.
properties.title: Eightmile Creek Snowshoe

properties.description: This short and sweet trail starts 0.3 miles east on the service road past Newhalem Creek Campground loops C & D, just past the steel-grated Newhalem Creek Bridge.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Newhalem Rock Shelter Trail

properties.description: For those who enjoy the challenge of Mailbox Peak-style climbing, look no further than Issaquah to find her little brother, tightly packaged in a quad-exerting, heart-jerking direct climb to West Tiger 3’s hilltop vista.
properties.title: Nook Trail

properties.description: Follow an old mining route through quiet forest near Darrington. This trail hasn't seen much maintenance in recent years, so it may require some route-finding experience to visit.
properties.title: Marten Creek

properties.description: Hike a gorgeously-graded trail to a marshy lake with views of the backside of the Enchantment mountains.
properties.title: Trout Lake via Jack Trout Trailhead

properties.description: This interpretive center offers three different short trails for visitors to explore the history of firefighting and fire lookouts in the Entiat Valley, as well as learn a bit about plant and fire ecology.
properties.title: Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center

properties.description: This page describes the options for doing a loop hike around the ski slopes, which is the ridge west of Crystal Mountain Boulevard.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Crystal Mountain Loop (Silver King)

properties.description: Hike a steep trail to some high alpine lakes south of Highway 2.
properties.title: Tunnel Creek

properties.description: With one to two miles of nice forest and beach hiking, this park features easy trails for morning jaunts, afternoon excursions, and evening strolls.
properties.title: Maple Hollow Park

properties.description: Lime Kiln State Park is one of the more scenic spots on an already beautiful island. Sometimes called “Whale Watch Park,” it is not uncommon to see orcas or other marine life playing in the water as you wander along the rocky edges of the Salish Sea. The hike described here provides plenty of opportunity for spotting killer whales, while also allowing you to explore the upland environment and see the historic lime kiln.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Lime Kiln State Park

properties.description: Just a few miles west of Chehalis, Rose Park provides 21 acres of green space — including a trail and plenty of places for a picnic — for visitors to enjoy.
properties.title: Rose Park

properties.description: Gorgeous weather and late-season color make this one of the most beautiful autumn hikes in Mount Rainier National Park. This hike is a tough climb, but the payoff is great views and lots of solitude.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Shriner Peak

properties.description: A pale green creek, big old trees, a variety of understory, and peek-a-boo views of snow-capped peaks.  Day-hikers should take it easy, as the joy here is in the journey not the destination.  Backpackers, however, may disagree.  Families and first-time backpackers will enjoy beautiful camps just two miles from the trailhead.  Experienced backpackers will note that Thunder Creek is a gateway to an extensive network of trails.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Thunder Creek

properties.description: On any given day, you'll find hikers, runners and bikers traveling the distance between Colman Beach Park and Seward Park along Lake Washington Boulevard in Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Washington Boulevard

properties.description: This hike through history, both natural and mining, leads to a beautiful emerald lake below the rocky cliffs of Isabella Ridge.  The mix of old mining road and steep trail passes through burnt forest, past an old mine, through flowered meadows, and across a boulder field to reach Copper Glance Lake.
properties.title: Copper Glance Lake

properties.description: The Bogachiel River is a classic example of a lowland rainforest ecosystem, with a rough and tumble trail that extends all the way to the head of the valley. Born on lower mountains than the Hoh, Queets, and Quinault, it lacks the glacial coloration and tremendous flow associated with those valleys. What it makes up for is miles of solitude and adventure.
properties.title: Bogachiel River

properties.description: Dry, subalpine ridges, old growth forest, massive flower packed meadows, and glaciated peaks makes this trip a nonstop North Cascades life-list backpack!
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Devil's Dome Loop

properties.description: A peak scramble in the Olympics to an lower-elevation peak in the Olympics. Route-finding experience is required.
properties.title: Mount Hopper

properties.description: The curiously-named Lake 22 is the center of an oasis of alpine wetland nestled on the northern shoulder of Mount Pilchuck. The hike to the lake combines the best of mountain rainforests, old-growth, wetlands and mountain views, yet it is readily accessible. In winter, the route lends itself to snowshoeing.
properties.title: Lake 22

properties.description: The most prominent peak in the Stehekin Valley, McGregor Mountain offers commanding views of the valley, Lake Chelan and a wide swath of the North Cascades, in addition to a high alpine environment that is equaled by few other trails anywhere. Though long and challenging, the trail is moderate in pitch, gaining a little over 6,000 feet in elevation over a measured eight miles, until the final scramble to the summit.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: McGregor Mountain

properties.description: On the flanks of Mount Baker’s south side, Schriebers Meadow makes for a delightful snowshoe excursion, either for a daytrip or an overnight experience.
properties.title: Schriebers Meadow Snowshoe

properties.description: Take a short walk on Cougar Mountain, shaded by the thick forest, with plenty of options into the trail network to create your own hiking adventure.
properties.title: Harvey Manning Trail

properties.description: Forest lake is a small lake in the Sunrise area of Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Forest Lake

properties.description: Right off the shores of Lake Chelan, Twenty-Five Mile Creek State Park is great for camping (reserved), water activities, hiking or as a home base to explore the surrounding area.
properties.title: Twenty-Five Mile Creek State Park

properties.description: Dry Falls State Park is a stunning stop on any Central Washington road trip. The viewpoint off Highway 17 at the Visitor Center is a good quick stop to see the evidence of the mighty ice age floods that swept through this area. But drive down to the main road through the park, just a couple miles south, and you'll be able to get inside this incredible vista, and see up close what the land looks like now.
properties.title: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park - Deep Lake

properties.description: A multi-use trail system in the city of Roslyn, the trails here offer a variety of outings that can be enjoyed by many different users. Views here extend across the Teanaway Valley to the snow covered peaks of the Stuart Range and even Mount Rainier in the southern distance.
properties.title: Roslyn Urban Forest

properties.description: An easy walk along a paved rail-to-trail down the Sammamish Valley and through the new urban core of Redmond.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redmond Central Connector Trail

properties.description: A scramble up Courtney Peak in the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness. While not as tall as some of the surrounding peaks, it is widely regarded as having the best view in the wilderness.
properties.title: Courtney Peak

properties.description: Ready for a stunning long hike through the otherwordly landscape of Mount St. Helens?  The Loowit Trail reveals the volcano and the blast zone in all its raw glory.
properties.title: Loowit Trail

properties.description: This hike has a little bit of everything (trout-filled lake, views, forest, flowers) and surprisingly a good dose of solitude.
properties.title: Joe Lake

properties.description: Visit this large, quiet lake in the heart of the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. Snoqualmie is accessible both via Highway 2 and the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road. From the trailhead on Highway 2, it's 7.3 miles to Snoqualmie Lake, and from the Middle Fork Road, it's 7.5 miles. You can even make this a thru-hike if you can arrange a pick-up at the other end.
properties.title: Snoqualmie Lake

properties.description: PJ Lake is a short but steep primitive trail to a subalpine tarn teeming with jumping trout. The lake’s beautiful color draws anglers, day hikers, and campers alike. However, the trail is so steep that the short mileage to get there is eclipsed by the vertical exertion and lingering leg pain.
properties.title: PJ Lake

properties.description: The Main Fork Dosewallips Trail is a major artery in the Olympic National Park trail system and offers access to remote areas deep within the park. As such, this route is most often traveled by thru-hikers or multi-night backpackers on a loop tour of flowery meadows and high passes.
properties.title: Main Fork Dosewallips River

properties.description: A long walk (or short mountain bike ride!) leads to a rolling falls that feeds into the rushing Carbon River.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Chenuis Falls

properties.description: Whether you’re visiting for the day or setting up camp for a longer adventure, Potlatch State Park is the perfect place to enjoy the gifts of Hood Canal, featuring a campground for any camping setup, calm waters for kayaking or diving and overnight mooring options.
properties.title: Potlatch State Park

properties.description: A steep and dusty trail to a long, beautiful ridge where the rambling is fine, often among a band of elk.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: American Ridge

properties.description: This multi-use trail, also known as the McLane School Trail, starts at the McLane Elementary School in Olympia. The paved trail goes around the elementary school and includes signs identifying native plant species.
properties.title: McLane School Forest Trail

properties.description: Take a tour of Mount Constitution using one of the longer loops on Orcas Island. There's plenty of elevation gain, plenty of miles, and plenty to see along the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Moran State Park - Cold Springs and North Trail Loop to Mount Constitution

properties.description: Visit a historic arboretum on connected paths that form a 2 mile interpretive trail, with the option to do shorter loops.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Wind River Arboretum

properties.description: Schaefer Lake is a good-sized alpine lake surrounded by the peaks of the Chiwawa Ridge. The trail is easy to access via a good road. This trail is lightly traveled; you will likely not see many other people even at the height of the season.
properties.title: Schaefer Lake

properties.description: This 240-acre park has short walking trails, baseball fields, soccer fields, disc golf, a playground, a picnic shelter and an off-leash dog area.
properties.title: Hockinson Meadows Community Park

properties.description: The Snake River Trail is 4 miles of paved trail along the river and through the popular Boyer Park and Marina. It has stunning views of the river, bluffs, and the Lower Granite Lock & Dam.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Snake River Trail (Boyer Park Bluffs)

properties.description: This trails is a relatively flat path paralleling Gold Creek in the Green Mountain State Forest, a dynamic working forest that is certainly a land of many uses. The trails are open to hikers, mountain bikers and horseback riders.
properties.title: Green Mountain State Forest - Davis Trail

properties.description: Hike up a sheltered canyon along the Q-line turbines. Bluebirds, deer, elk, jack rabbits, and coyotes also seek shelter here, and in the spring the dry creek bed will be teeming with life.
properties.title: Whiskey Dick Wildlife Area - Bluebird Trail

properties.description: Spanish for Duck Island, Patos Island is a hidden gem in the San Juan Islands. This is largely because of the difficulty in accessing it, but if you make the effort, you won't be sorry!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Patos Island

properties.description: At just four miles roundtrip, Tin Mine is a nice year-round hike that features history and is kid-friendly. There’s also lots of beaver ponds along the way and seasonal cascades as well.
properties.title: Green Mountain State Forest - Tin Mine Trail

properties.description: Small local park with large firs and a loop trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Keeney Park

properties.description: This is a super-challenging trek that requires extra pre-planning and likely some route-finding experience, but promises a rugged, gorgeous few days in the landscape south and east of Stevens Pass.
properties.title: Icicle Divide: Stevens Pass to Fourth of July

properties.description: A hike near Mount Adams.
properties.title: Bench Lake Loop

properties.description: This multi-use, steep trail passes through forests and meadows, with views of the surrounding Diamond Head, Miller and Navaho Peaks, and the Enchantments, ultimately connecting with the Tronsen Ridge Trail. From here, access is also possible to Table Mountain.
properties.title: Tronsen Meadow

properties.description: Due to the permanent closure of the Carbon River Road, hikers can now park at the closure and venture to the end of the road to the viewpoint for Ipsut Falls. Along the way, you'll hike through magnificent old-growth forest, and many opportunities to see the power of the Carbon River.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Carbon River to Ipsut Falls

properties.description: This short leg-stretcher winds through old-growth fir and ponderosa forests with amazing geology to entertain even the most curmudgeonly kids in your car.
properties.title: Sculpture Rock

properties.description: This short trail at Pioneer Park in Ferndale features Japanese cherry blossom trees.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Hanadori Trail

properties.description: Lower Wildcat Lake offers an opportunity to get deeper into the backcountry past Snow Lake, while still on a formal trail.
properties.title: Lower Wildcat Lake

properties.description: This loop around a green park is perfect for a quick nature walk right in the city.
properties.title: Yauger Park

properties.description: The Priest Rapids Wildlife Area is a unit of 3,202 acres in the Columbia Basin Wildlife Area.
properties.title: Priest Rapids Wildlife Area

properties.description: The sign outside the Manresa Grotto states simply: "A beautiful grotto exists." And it's true! It does exist, and while it's beautiful in its own way, it can be a little eerie when one visits alone on a rainy day.
properties.title: Manresa Grotto

properties.description: This is a short, mostly level trail around a small tranquil lake that has the potential to be a great family hike. However, in its current condition it is best for adventurous adults and older kids.
properties.title: Lake Elizabeth

properties.description: This 9-mile, rugged trail trail delivers hikers into the remote William O. Douglas Wilderness at mile 3.5 and offers excellent views of Mount Rainier. It's also a great way to access the deep woods off of Highway 12, where you can loop hike to your heart's content.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Carlton Ridge

properties.description: Hike a series of short trails through this hilly forested park at the northern end of Seattle's Capitol Hill.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Interlaken Park

properties.description: Once a booming coal town, Fairfax Ghost Town is an adventure of exploration and discovery. Expect thick vegetation and undefined trails once you arrive at the town site, so pack a good sense of direction, plenty of time and a thirst for exploration is highly recommended.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Fairfax Ghost Town

properties.description: Enjoy sweeping views of Port Angeles and the Strait of Juan de Fuca from the Cirque Rim Overlook on this short trail.
properties.title: Cirque Rim Nature Trail

properties.description: Go north on the Kettle Crest National Scenic Trail across the southwestern flank of Columbia Mountain. The open summit, the high point for this adventure, holds views of the surrounding Kettle Range.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Columbia Mountain Snowshoe

properties.description: Visit one of the best old-growth hikes in the North Cascades, with views of a vivid blue lake and jagged, snowy peaks thrown in for good measure.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Big Beaver Trail

properties.description: A no-longer maintained trail in the Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Ptarmigan Ridge (Pasayten)

properties.description: At Cascade Pass, the wow factor far exceeds the “ow” factor – perhaps no other trail in the state delivers as much reward for the effort. From the high peaks on either side of the pass, verdant meadows curve down to a saddle that offers sweeping views of nearby valleys, glaciers, mountains, and passing wildlife. Sedately climbing a little less than 1,800 feet in 3.6 miles, it is the perfect hike to show new hikers the extraordinary places their feet can take them.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cascade Pass

properties.description: Abandoned side trail to old lookout location on Remmel Mt.
properties.title: Remmel Mountain

properties.description: The Divide Camp Trail features dense forests, glacial creeks and wildflower-strewn meadows. It also sees less traffic than the nearby Killen Creek Trail – the standard approach to High Camp.
properties.title: Divide Camp

properties.description: Climbing steeply up into the mountains to the west of Lake Chelan, the Devore Creek Trail begins in the Lake Chelan National Recreation Area near Weaver Point Campground, offering miles of hiking and adventuring.
properties.title: Devore Creek

properties.description: This 100+ acre park near Edmonds is on the eastern shores of its namesake, Lake Ballinger. Fishing is available year-round, and with beach access, barbeques and picnic tables, it is an excellent place to spend an afternoon with the family.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Ballinger Park

properties.description: Ocean City State Park is a 170-acre camping park with almost 3000 feet of shoreline on the Pacific Ocean. Trails through the  dune grasses and shore pines lead to the Pacific Ocean.
properties.title: Ocean City State Park

properties.description: Enjoy a short, paved walking trail surrounding a public playground and picnic area nestled in the heart of Bellingham’s Lettered Streets neighborhood.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Fouts Park

properties.description: Visit a beautiful, many-tiered waterfall and a small lookout area on the west side of Cougar Mountain. Perfect for photos as well as an escape from the city.
properties.title: Far Country

properties.description: A connector trail to a variety of routes along the northwest section of Tiger Mountain State Forest.
properties.title: Gas Line Trail

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Phantom Peak

properties.description: Take a nice long walk up the old Monte Cristo Road grade and stop by the townsite on your way. Rougher terrain begins on entering the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness area, and past Silver Lake, the trail becomes difficult to find. Trek along a steep mountain-side before finally cresting the ridge to look down on Twin Lakes and make the steep descent to the camp sites.
properties.title: Twin Lakes - Monte Cristo

properties.description: The Golf Course Trail is part of the trail network running through the residential town of Newcastle. This trail parallels Golf Club Road along a forested band.
properties.title: Golf Course Trail - Newcastle

properties.description: Tucked away in the residential city of Fircrest and named after the woman who fought for its protection, this park offers a short loop trail around a small pond.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Thelma Gilmur Park

properties.description: Breeden Road offers expansive views of arid grasslands and basalt outcrops, punctuated with a rushing creek and a small lake.
properties.title: Breeden Road - Wall Lake

properties.description: Mount Ellinor is the southern-most prominence on the eastern front of the Olympics. This makes its peak easy to point out to your friends when you say, ”I was up there.” Mount Ellinor also gives you two trailheads to choose from. The lower trailhead at 2,600 feet welcomes you to the ascent with an easy grade at the outset. The route from the upper trailhead at 3,500 feet starts out with a nearly immediate upward jolt. The trails merge well before the summit and continue upward at a character-building grade.
properties.title: Mount Ellinor

properties.description: A peaceful wetland lake resting just inside the boundary for Goat Rocks Wilderness, Lily Lake is a gentle stroll, perfect for a day out with the family to experience flora and fauna near White Pass and Mount Rainier. However, the forest road to reach the trailhead is not as gentle, and higher clearance vehicles are advised.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Lily Lake

properties.description: The trail to Ericson's Bay is primitive and no longer maintained by Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Ericson's Bay

properties.description: This is a well used trail for trail runners and some bikers. Mostly gravel, it is wide and well-groomed.
properties.title: Lacamas Heritage Trail

properties.description: This short, steep in places, route to Thorp Mountain has flowers, berries, and views along the way.  The big payoff is the grand vista from the lookout, as befits its location as the highest point for many miles in all directions.
properties.title: Thorp Mountain via Knox Creek

properties.description: Scenic Marmot Lake is reachable from both Highway 2 or the Salmon La Sac area, but either way will be a challenge -- it's 14 miles via Deception Pass, or more than 10 miles from the Tucquala Meadows Trailhead.
properties.title: Marmot Lake

properties.description: Visiting Beebe Springs is more of a leg stretcher or bird watching location than a destination hiking location. That much being said, it has bountiful wildlife and broad vistas. Do note that it is closed seasonally from December 1 to March 15.
properties.title: Beebe Springs Wildlife Area - River Trails

properties.description: This short half-mile trail connects Harvey Manning Park to the Big Tree Ridge trail.
properties.title: Precipice Bottom Trail

properties.description: Done as a one-way car shuttle hike, this route takes you past several lakes and streams, through meadows of wild flowers, patches of huckleberries, views of mountains and occasional wildlife such as marmots, black bears, pikas and  mountain goats. And on a warm day you can take a cooling dip in Sheep Lake on your journey.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Chinook Pass to Crystal Mountain via the Pacific Crest Trail

properties.description: Peppered with statues and monuments, this park near the heart of downtown Tacoma is designed in a classical style.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wright Park

properties.description: Tucked into a corner of the Alpine Lakes Wilderness is Sunday Lake, a road less traveled that abounds in wildflowers, berries, fauna, historical artifacts, old growth, and alpine littoral habitat. Much more than the gentle woodland saunter implied by the 300-foot elevation change, the route to Sunday Lake requires the fording of Sunday Creek in spring and fall, making it an adventure any day of the week. Campbell Recreation permit required.
properties.title: Sunday Lake

properties.description: Enjoy a gentle amble through forest — with a dash of ravine, wetland and pasture — and on to sweeping views of Port Townsend Bay as this multi-use trail gently eases hikers, cyclists and equestrians down to the waterfront. (This segment is also known as the Larry Scott Trail.)
properties.title: Olympic Discovery Trail - East

properties.description: Hike the forested Iverson Railroad Trail and the little-used middle section of the main Tiger Mountain Trail (TMT). Look in on the site of a 1925 logging train wreck. Continue on to remote Custer's Bridge, and return via a loop over Middle Tiger Mountain, including views south-side hikers miss.
properties.title: Custer's Bridge - Middle Tiger Loop

properties.description: A popular route in the northwest corner of Mount Rainier National Park -- try this one as a day hike, an overnight (be sure to get permits first) or as a trail run!
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Mother Mountain Loop

properties.description: Potholes State Park  mostly service picknickers and boaters, but there are 3 miles of trail to explore on the Frenchman Hills Trail Loop.
properties.title: Potholes State Park - Frenchman Hills Trail Loop

properties.description: Longs Pass provides unbelievable views, but only after an unbelievable amount of elevation gain. In less than 3 miles, you'll climb more than 2000 feet in elevation -- that's quite like climbing a staircase for three miles. It's shady the first half, but soon comes out into an exposed area; bring as much water as you can carry!
properties.title: Longs Pass

properties.description: Step into the moss-cloaked forest of the Lewis River, where giant cedars, nurse logs, ancient stumps and rushing water abound.
properties.title: Lewis River Falls

properties.description: A short connector trail between Bear Ridge and Shangri La trails that creates a loop out of the two. Also connect to Red Cedars via the No Name Trail.
properties.title: No Name

properties.description: A short trail accessible from the Windy Ridge area of Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument, the Windy Trail makes it possible for hikers to loop up a variety of trails in the blast zone.
properties.title: Windy Trail

properties.description: A peak scramble between Dingford Creek and the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River. Routefinding experience, gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Big Snow Mountain

properties.description: Spider Gap is the pass in the ridge between Spider Meadow and Lyman Lakes. Start out on the Phelps Creek Trail to its end in Spider Meadow. The Spider Gap Trail climbs steeply from here for 1.2 miles, topping out at the ridge and connecting to the Lyman Lakes Trail.
properties.title: Spider Gap

properties.description: Link multiple West Tiger Mountain trails near the Preston Powerline Trail to find a hidden gem of a hike once you leave the rocky powerline trail, delighting in wildflowers every color of the rainbow along the road.
properties.title: Preston Powerline Loop

properties.description: Embark on a long, lovely backpacking trip through some of the wild and open wilderness in the Wenaha-Tucannon area.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Packers Trail - Mount Misery Loop

properties.description: Enjoy a beach walk along a forested coastline, featuring expansive views of the islands, distant mountains, blue sky and sea.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Young's Park - Clark Point

properties.description: Some trails go to lakes, some to high viewpoints. This trail is all about the forest, and what a forest it is! Old-growth trees  reach for the sky on either side of a brush-free trail, since understory is minimal when the big old trees block out the light. Find fantastic mushrooms here in the fall and forest wildflowers in the spring and early summer.
properties.title: North Fork Sauk River

properties.description: There are many big trees in the Olympics, but this enormous cedar is so large it has a trail named after it. Plus, it's just a quarter mile from the road. Unfortunately, storms in 2016 felled the large tree, though it's no less impressive. When you visit, be sure to take only pictures -- the Park Service is leaving the giant there in order to perpetuate the natural cycle.
properties.title: Big Cedar Tree - Quinault

properties.description: A small subalpine lake with backcountry campsites that can be accessed from Icicle Ridge Trail, Chatter Creek Trail or Chiwaukum Creek Trail.
properties.title: Lake Edna

properties.description: Big Finn Hill Park is the lesser-known cousin to the adjoining Saint Edwards State Park in Kirkland. Its expansive 220 acres are worth exploring and getting to know for their miles of meandering trails fit for mountain biking and casual strolling. Chock-full of tall Douglas-firs, ferns and bright green mosses, it offers possibilities to spot eagles, deer and owls.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Big Finn Hill Park

properties.description: The LBA of LBA Park stands for Little Baseball Association, but there is much more to do than just play baseball at this urban park. There are 4 miles of gentle walking trails in the adjoining LBA Woods and more.
properties.title: LBA Park

properties.description: To misquote a famous author, this hike can be "the best of trips or the worst of trips". Done in the right season, it has beautiful flowers, ripe berries, expansive views, great campsites, fishing, and swimming. Done in the wrong season, it has treacherous avalanche chute crossings, wet trail, no flowers, muddy campsites, and horrendous bugs.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Dewey Lake

properties.description: Tucked off of Spur Road 100, the opposite direction from the Cape Disappointment State Park camping area, the Coastal Forest Loop offers a chance to experience the signature environment of this area in either a half mile or mile and a half loop. Be sure to snag the brochure offered at the park office with interpretive information corresponding to posts along the way.
properties.title: Cape Disappointment State Park - Coastal Forest Loop

properties.description: Riser Lake is a short hike just outside of Winthrop that is accessible any time of the year. Enjoy the shrub-steppe and the views of the hills surrounding the Methow Valley.
properties.title: Riser Lake Loop

properties.description: Explore the Norse Peak Wilderness on this trail, which connects the Pacific Crest Trail near the Mike Urich Cabin with the Greenwater Lakes trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Maggie Creek

properties.description: A trail leading from Coal Creek Falls that takes hikers even deeper into Cougar Mountain Wildland Park.
properties.title: Quarry

properties.description: Spend a little time on a short interpretive trail near Lake Roosevelt. Views are nice, and there's lots of history to learn about.
properties.title: Fort Spokane

properties.description: The lonely trail up Leland Creek to Lake Leland has been neglected for many years. It is hard to follow and littered with hundreds of blowdowns, but those who persevere will find solitude and an excellent camp at a beautiful subalpine lake.
properties.title: Leland Lake

properties.description: From the picnic tables scattered throughout, to the brushed back trails and spacious trail head parking lot, these three connecting trail systems reflect the pride, enthusiasm and commitment of the local volunteers who created and now maintain them.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Putney Woods, Saratoga Woods and Metcalf Trail System

properties.description: From Spray Park, in Mount Rainier National Park: a fun, class 2 scramble to Observation Rock.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Observation Rock via Echo Rock

properties.description: This is a relativity little-used trail that offers great views down into the Chiwawa Valley with a backdrop of the Chiwawa Ridge and the Entiat Range from a former lookout site. Follow it through a forest of Douglas-fir, grand fir, Western hemlock and several species of pines and big leaf maple. This is a very dry trail with a southwest exposure so bring plenty of water with you.
properties.title: Estes Butte

properties.description: Hamilton Buttes boasts panoramic views of the South Cascades volcanoes despite a short hike up to its relatively isolated summit.
properties.title: Hamilton Buttes

properties.description: Ascend the west flank of Antoine Peak via an old logging road that switchbacks up the moderate grade, offering occasional views of the Foothills of Mount Spokane to the north before entering a recovering forest. Return via a trail winding through an open hillside offering good views toward the Spokane Valley.
properties.title: Antoine Peak Conservation Area - Robbins Road Snowshoe Loop

properties.description: The “old” trail that ascends Mount Si’s western flank offers a shorter, steeper, slightly more scenic, and if one dare say it — less crowded — route to the summit, where you can rejoin the rest of the people who flock to one of Snoqualmie Pass’s most popular hiking destinations.
properties.title: Mount Si - Old Trail

properties.description: If you’re overnighting in the Stehekin Valley and just want a riverside ramble to while away the hours, try the Stehekin River Trail. It’s an easy forested walk along the mighty Stehekin River on a side of the valley that few visitors get to see.
properties.title: Stehekin River Trail

properties.description: The Indian Trail is one of the main trails running through the western portion of Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Indian Trail

properties.description: Start off with a bit of railroad history, then follow a trail into the Wild Sky Wilderness. Parallel Martin Creek on a bench above the waterway, winding upward through the forest to meet Kelley Creek and the old Kelley Creek trail. WTA  helped construct the connector, designed to increase the connectivity of the trail system of the Iron Goat.
properties.title: Kelley Creek via Martin Creek Trailhead

properties.description: If the best views come to those who earn them, Mount Dickerman offers the fairest vantage along the Mountain Loop. You’ll huff and puff through 4,000 feet of elevation on your way to the summit; in return, you’ll get a superb panorama of nearly every peak in the Mountain Loop. In late summer, it also rewards the intrepid with a bounty of mountain blueberries.
properties.title: Mount Dickerman

properties.description: The Ironstone Mountain Trail provides a challenging rollercoaster of a ridge hike, taking you to the summits of Burnt Mountain, Ironstone Mountain and McNeil Peak, with rewarding views of the surrounding area.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Ironstone Mountain

properties.description: This is a large lake hidden just south of Tonga Ridge in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. Reached by a brushy, boot-beaten fisherman's path, it is less visited than many lakes in the area, but the route is marked on the map, and if you are willing to put up with a bit of inconvenience, this makes a nice day hike or overnight.
properties.title: Fisher Lake

properties.description: Enjoy a nature walk at a popular local park — a great option for a trail run or walk to stretch the legs while traveling or little ones are playing ball.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Petrovitsky Park

properties.description: Table Rock and its fire lookout is a must-visit site accessible by car.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Table Rock

properties.description: This moderate trail makes for a great family hike up Strawberry Mountain with good views of Lost Lake and Bonaparte Mountain.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Strawberry Mountain

properties.description: A bit rugged, but with lots of diversity. This trail loops you through rangeland, shrub-steppe and dry ponderosa forest. Huge views and an intimate creek reward you.
properties.title: Methow Wildlife Area - Bowen Mountain East Loop

properties.description: Bird watching, historical sites and Rainer and Olympic views.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Fort Steilacoom Park

properties.description: Yellowstone Cliffs and Windy Gap offer a chance to experience a side of Mount Rainier National Park like no other. Most trails in the park highlight views of the main mountain, but here, it’s more about the surrounding peaks, which make the area seem more like somewhere in Alaska or Montana, rather than Washington. Add to that the fact that accessing this area now requires an approach hike in the double digits, and you’ve got a remote, high mountain valley where relatively few people come, despite the fact that it’s in Washington’s most popular national park.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Yellowstone Cliffs and Windy Gap

properties.description: If the steep climb up to Lake Minotaur hasn’t taken all the go out of your legs, adding a mile and another 1,000 feet of climbing will get you to the top of Labyrinth Mountain. From the summit you look down on Minotaur and Theseus Lakes directly below.
properties.title: Labyrinth Mountain

properties.description: Currently a nonmotorized recreation trail, historically this trail was the original stagecoach route and first State Highway in Washington, connecting the town of Marcus on the Columbia River to Marblemount in the North Cascades over the Kettle Crest.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Old Stage Trail No. 1

properties.description: Hike a rolling trail to a large open meadow with views and the chance to connect to the Tarbell Trail, a long trail with lots of options to extend your hike.
properties.title: Yacolt Burn State Forest - Bear Grass Trail

properties.description: This short, hiker-only trail in the Dark Divide connects hikers to an arresting, appropriately named blue lake jumping with fish. If you can get past its quiet shores, it's a short jaunt to connect with the Craggy Peak trail and miles of ridgeline hiking that the Dark Divide Roadless Area affords.
properties.title: Blue Lake

properties.description: This is a nice, short hike to a recently repaired fire lookout. Guidebooks do not include recent upgrades to the trail and road to the trailhead. The trail is no longer only accessible via a scramble, but trail that switchbacks through wildflowers and interesting rock walls which was constructed in 2007. The lookout itself has been repaired, making it a nice lunch stop.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Kelly Butte

properties.description: The Badger Valley Trail is located in the NE corner of Olympic National Park. This trail starts at the Obstruction Point Trailhead and trends down into Badger Valley to end at Grand Lake.
properties.title: Badger Valley

properties.description: Skip the long, flat miles along the Entiat River and climb straight up to the Upper Mad River and Garland Peak trails to access hundreds of miles of backcountry travel in the heart of the Entiat.
properties.title: Shetipo

properties.description: The flat terrain of this wide valley east of Snoqualmie Pass is the perfect place to practice snowshoeing with kids or first-timers. This is an area popular with cross-country skiers, and you may spot beaver dams and other winter wildlife. From Mardee Lake to looming Kendall Peak before you, this is premiere terrain for winter enthusiasts.
properties.title: Gold Creek Pond Snowshoe

properties.description: This is a half-mile spur trail in the Three O'Clock Ridge area that ends at its junction with the Lower Dungeness Trail. The trail is a steep ascent for the majority of its length. Minimum parking is available.
properties.title: Three O'Clock Ridge

properties.description: Jutting 800 feet out of Banks Lake in Washington’s majestic coulee country, Steamboat Rock is the crown jewel of this area. The basalt butte has a rich history; first used by native people many years ago, and during the ice age, the Great Missoula Floods carved the canyons here, while the rock stood as an island in the raging river. Now, Steamboat Rock lies high and dry, offering excellent 360-degree panoramas of the landscape surrounding it.
properties.title: Steamboat Rock

properties.description: Take in sweeping views of the Hanford Reach National Monument and the surrounding arid landscape from a scenic overlook in the Saddle Mountains.
properties.title: Saddle Mountain East

properties.description: Explore forested trails in Shoreline's oldest and largest park. These include a main half-mile trail that is wheelchair accessible. Appreciate 100-year-old trees, and hike trails featuring impressive staircases.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Hamlin Park

properties.description: Camp Growden is a former CCC camp, now a restored heritage site with an interpretive trail.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Growden Heritage Site

properties.description: Climb steeply out of the Elwha River Valley to impressive views of the Bailey Range and wide-open meadows on this trail that accesses Hurricane Hill the back way.
properties.title: Elwha To Hurricane Hill

properties.description: Bradley Lake Park in Puyallup has a full suite of amenities including a paved walking trail around the lake. The park is equipped with a large parking area, restrooms, two ballfields, a large picnic shelter, open grassy areas and about 1.5 miles of paved, barrier-free trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bradley Lake

properties.description: Try a multi-day backpack up the tumbling, boisterous, river-like Thunder Creek from the Colonial Creek Campground to just beyond its headwaters at Park Creek Pass. Backpackers can turn around at Park Creek Pass or do a traverse to Cascade Pass.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Park Creek Pass via Thunder Creek

properties.description: This tiny forested pond near the Interurban Trail and Hundred Acre Wood in Bellingham features plenty of waterfowl and other wildlife.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Hoag's Pond

properties.description: Walk through deciduous forests and listen for a raucous bird population at Al Borlin Park. The trails here cross the park's 90 acres; Al Borlin Park is the largest park in Monroe.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Al Borlin Park

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Crater Mountain

properties.description: This trail offers a full tour of the trails at Liberty Lake Regional Park, taking visitors along Split Creek, through a  cedar grove, past Liberty Falls and an old cabin as well as along miles of beautiful trails with views down to the lake.
properties.title: Liberty Lake Regional Park - Liberty Lake Loop Trail

properties.description: The Foothills Trail System sits just south of Port Angeles and west of Hurricane Ridge Road. This patch of DNR land is a working forest interlaced with an 11-mile trail system that is open to hikers, mountain bikers, horseback riders and off road vehicles.
properties.title: Foothills Trails

properties.description: Hike along a gentle grade as it climbs along Porter Creek and crosses it, traveling west on the other side, keeping the road you arrived on in view. As you reach the confluence of Porter Creek and the West Fork of Porter Creek, you also reach the waterfall, your destination.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Porter Falls

properties.description: Discover some of Olympic National Park's most inspired alpine scenery among the meadows, lakes, and vistas of Grand Valley.
properties.title: Grand Valley via Grand Pass Trail

properties.description: Make one of several loops on Bonaparte Mountain using Cabin Trail.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Cabin Trail

properties.description: Climb to a summit between Cle Elum Lake and Lake Kachess. Route finding and climbing experience recommended.
properties.title: Thomas Mountain

properties.description: This preserve is located a few miles from the Mima Mounds near Littlerock. It provides a peek into the Puget Prairie ecosystem that greeted settlers who came here in the 1800’s. Thurston County Parks Department owns this small parcel of land, a tiny remaining fraction of the prairies of old.
properties.title: Glacial Heritage Preserve

properties.description: Visit a quieter trail in the Dungeness network -- one that a lot of folks skip in favor of more well-known trails with more views. But Lower Gray Wolf is beautiful in its own right, and visitors here can discover it for themselves.
properties.title: Lower Gray Wolf River

properties.description: The aptly-named Switchback trail provides a shortcut to Mount Angeles and views of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Port Angeles, and the surrounding area, but it comes at a price. Just 0.6 miles long, it climbs 700 feet from the parking area (more of a pullout) on Hurricane Ridge Road to the junction with the Klahhane Ridge Trail, where four different destinations lie at your feet.
properties.title: Switchback

properties.description: The Rainbow Creek trail provides day-hike diversions to visitors to the Stehekin Valley, but you'll need more than a few hours to truly appreciate the full length of the trail.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Rainbow Creek Trail

properties.description: The Teneriffe Falls Connector trail connects the Mount Teneriffe trail to the Teneriffe Falls trail.
properties.title: Teneriffe Falls Connector

properties.description: The Chybinski Loop is located in the Cougar/Squak Mountain Corridor, and has many connecting trails and loop options.
properties.title: Chybinski Loop

properties.description: The Chelatchie Prairie Rail Trail is the initial one-mile section of the planned 33-mile multiuse paved, ADA-accessible trail in Clark County which allows dogs on leashes.
properties.title: Chelatchie Prairie Rail Trail

properties.description: The route to Little Tahoma requires advanced mountaineering skills including glacier travel.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Little Tahoma

properties.description: This 165-acre conservation futures property preserves a fragment of the Peone Prairie ecosystem at the confluence of Peone Creek and Deadman Creek.
properties.title: Feryn Ranch Conservation Area

properties.description: This simple trail next door provides a brief getaway into nature in the busy Factoria area. The Sunset Ravine trail is a short out-and-back path along the edge of a ravine through a greenbelt. It's easily accessible from the neighborhoods near Tyee Community Gym and Middle School. The other end of the trail is about two tenths of a mile from T-Mobile headquarters.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Sunset Ravine Trail

properties.description: A challenging, largely off-trail, multi-day backpacking scramble across the rough and rugged interior of the Olympic Mountains.
properties.title: Bailey Range Traverse

properties.description: Enjoy this 2.5 mile long beach hike thanks to a donation from the Morgan Family to Whidbey Camano Land Trust.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Morgan Tidelands

properties.description: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park is a mishmash of roads, trails, abandoned Army missile silos, and plenty of wildlife. Not only is Cougar Mountain King County’s largest park, it is one of the largest wildland parks in an urban area in the United States.
properties.title: Precipice Top Trail

properties.description: Emerald Park is a long thru trail connecting Lake Chelan to the east and the Entiat River Trail to the west.
properties.title: Emerald Park (Snowy Brushy)

properties.description: Get a taste of the Alpine Lakes Wilderness on this short climb to a small but scenic lake. The trail winds from a lush meadow into old growth forest. Whether as a short day trek or a first-time overnight, a hike to Nosh Nosh Wahtum is worth the long road in.
properties.title: Nosh Nosh Wahtum

properties.description: This is a steep scramble up Lundin Peak. Gear and prior experience required.
properties.title: Lundin Peak

properties.description: This 5.4 mile long urban trail connects neighborhoods in the Bellevue area, including Clyde Hill, Medina, Yarrow Point, and Hunts Point.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Points Loop Trail

properties.description: Hike the Tunnel Creek Trail to a junction with the PCT that leads to Trap Pass, a small gap on the ridge of Thunder Mountain.
properties.title: Trap Pass

properties.description: One of Washington's most popular destinations in the summer, the trail to Snow Lake is a tempting destination in winter, too. But the steep terrain in the area puts visitors in a high-avalanche risk when snow is present. Have proper gear and an understanding of how to read the snowpack before venturing out on this trail.
properties.title: Snow Lake - Winter

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Bear Creek Falls

properties.description: Walk along an old-railroad-track-turned-trail through the city of Bellingham.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Railroad Trail

properties.description: Make a short and gradual climb through fields of flowers to a quaint two-tier waterfall. This easy early-season hike is most impressive after spring snowmelt when the creek and falls are swollen with turbulent water.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cedar Falls

properties.description: High above the Twisp River Valley, this long-lost trail ambles lonely along a dry ridgeline. For the hardy explorer faints bits of trail may be found periodically through this ponderosa and grassland hilltop. This trail most likely once served the Black Pine Lake area, but it has been largely forgotten and returned to open country.
properties.title: Lookout Ridge

properties.description: Hidden in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest near the town of Entiat is a treasure of a trail with a wide graceful waterfall and panoramic views of the Entiat River Valley. Offering a chance to explore the outdoors for all abilities, it will be easy to see why it has been designated a National Recreational Trail and draws locals and travelers from all over the state.
properties.title: Silver Falls

properties.description: The hike to Camp Pleasant is often included in more lengthy backpacks or dayhikes on the Olympic Peninsula, but hikers will find an easy conditioner when they undertake this early season stroll.
properties.title: Camp Pleasant

properties.description: The snowshoe route up to Lanham Lake is a straightforward climb through trees, but you'll be rewarded with a delightful little lake and a burst of sunshine on a clear, chilly day.
properties.title: Lanham Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: Take a short, fairly flat walk through forest near Highway 104 right outside Port Gamble. It's the perfect little walk to take if you just need an hour or so outside.
properties.title: Port Gamble Forest - Bluff Trail

properties.description: Mowich Lake is a moderate snowshoe tucked into the northwest corner of Mount Rainier National Park.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Mowich Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: A quiet park where locals and visitors can enjoy a placid lake, birdwatching and relaxing.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Sawyer Regional Park

properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Bear Lake

properties.description: The demure Top Lake trail provides easy access and a popular jumping-off point for hikers, backpackers, equestrian riders and trail work volunteers, all headed into the Cascades backcountry during summer and early fall once snow has receded. Take in the beauty of subalpine meadows and regal peaks on the horizon that offer a taste of what draws outdoor enthusiasts here to the Henry M. Jackson and Glacier Peak Wildernesses and beyond.
properties.title: Top Lake

properties.description: The Cowiche Canyon Preserve is a small pocket of wildlands near Yakima. It includes both the canyon itself and the canyon’s southerly uplands. There are approximately 20 miles of interconnected trails open to hikers, runners, mountain bikers, and equestrians. Snowshoeing and cross-country skiing are popular when there is enough snow.
properties.title: Cowiche Canyon Preserve

properties.description: This ADA-accessible trail built on a dike on the edge of this small town is a lovely jaunt, clocking in at just over three miles roundtrip, along a section of the Cowlitz River. A mountain bike course, playground, and several picnic areas dot the trailside, and with various access points to the town of Castle Rock, it’s easy to duck off for a quick bite in town.
properties.title: Castle Rock Riverfront Trail

properties.description: A scramble up a mountain near Lake Ann. Climbing experience and equipment required.
properties.title: Mount Ann

properties.description: The Queets River Trail is legendary for both its wild rainforest scenery and for the challenges it presents to the hiker. To begin, the trail can only be accessed after fording the glacier-born Queets River itself. Across the river, the trail is primitive and remote.
