Most hikers skip this trail either because of the ford or because it dead ends at 11 miles. But anglers and Olympiphiles hold a special place for this valley in their hearts.
properties.title: Queets River

properties.description: Hike up out of the Methow Valley then follow the rim from Fun Rock, with an option to continue to the Mazama Store.
properties.title: Goat Wall Trail

properties.description: This neighborhood park has a short loop trail that takes visitors through a prairie ecosystem brimming with interesting trees, flowers and grasses.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Parkland Prairie

properties.description: With Mount Stuart peeking over the ridge, take a walk, or ride, through agricultural Kittitas County with its irrigated farming & ranching. Two railroad tunnels and an abandoned farm display some history of the region.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Thorp Trailhead

properties.description: Visit an uncommonly lush riparian habitat mixed with old-grown Ponderosa pines along the Touchet River.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Lewis and Clark Trail State Park

properties.description: Aptly named Little Mountain is easily accessible year-round. This 522-acre forested park—just a few miles from Mount Vernon’s downtown area—feels much farther from the city. A narrow road leads to the sub-1,000-foot summit, where Skagit Valley views await. While driving to the top is pleasant, it is far more rewarding to hike.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Little Mountain Park - Bonnie and Clyde Loop

properties.description: Although it is small, this nature preserve on the northwest tip of Fox Island features a sandspit, offering visitors the perfect place for a short scenic beach hike.
properties.title: Tacoma DeMolay Sandspit Nature Preserve

properties.description: Chopaka Lake sits at the entrance to the Chopaka Mountain Wilderness Study Area, a 5,518-acre site owned and managed by the Bureau of Land Management.
properties.title: Chopaka Lake

properties.description: Terrell Creek Marsh is one of the few remaining saltwater/freshwater estuaries in northern Puget Sound. The half mile loop through a mixed forest of maple, alder, paper birch, cedars, and hemlock has 10 informative signs along the way. There are 1.5 miles of saltwater shoreline to explore.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Birch Bay State Park

properties.description: Hike to a peak in a 4,300-acre Douglas-fir forest in the foothills of Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Pack Forest - Hugo Peak Trail

properties.description: Hike easy, very green trails in the northwest corner of Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park. View artifacts from the coal mining era. As optional hike extensions, look in on Far Country Falls, or check out the ongoing downstream Coal Creek Trail.
properties.title: Red Town Meadow & Trails

properties.description: Rough and tumble is the trail, just like the miners that constructed this path. Becoming progressively more rugged, the ascent to Gothic Basin offers tremendous rewards at its end. Early on, one simply meanders alongside the relentless South Fork of the Sauk River, then turns into a forested, increasingly steep bee-line to the basin with waterfalls, flowers, and views of the surrounding mountains to keep one distracted once you leave the forest.
properties.title: Gothic Basin

properties.description: The adventure of this peak starts by simply getting to the trailhead. From there, a moderately overgrown trail winds through classic ponderosa forests with berries or wildflowers in season. The summit area is an otherworldly mix of silvery burnt trees and granite boulders. Your efforts to climb this peak are likely to be rewarded with solitude and dramatic views.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Granite Mountain (Conconully)

properties.description: Accessible from two trailheads, shady Trail 100 provides respite from both the heat of summer and the winds of winter along its approximately 3.5-mile length.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 100

properties.description: The Basalt Ridge trail offers hikers a path to Basalt Peak and Garland Peak.
properties.title: Basalt Ridge

properties.description: In summer and fall this is a bikers trail but come winter it makes an excellent snowshoe or cross country ski trail.
properties.title: Hansen Ridge

properties.description: This short, accessible trail leads to a monument honoring the Hand Shake Agreement of 1932 that reserved a portion of the Sawtooth Berry Fields for use by Native Americans.
properties.title: Hand Shake Trail

properties.description: Dirtyface Lookout is a popular early season and summer leg burner, climbing 4000 feet feet above Lake Wenatchee to an old fire lookout. The first three-quarters of a mile of this trail are a great hike for kids, climbing 700 vertical feet to a small waterfall with excellent views of the Lake Wenatchee Basin. This shorter route makes for a good snowshoe.
properties.title: Dirtyface Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: This is an ideal ‘multi-modal’ kid hike, featuring a two mile bike ride, followed by an easy and quite pretty half mile hike.
properties.title: Upper Twin Lake

properties.description: This trail runs from Puyallup to Buckley, along the way passing along the Carbon River and offering up great views of Mount Rainier. It is popular with cyclists, walkers and horseback riders.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Foothills Trail

properties.description: Meander alongside Liberty Creek, staying close to the water, on a trail that provides a shorter loop option than the full waterfall loop.
properties.title: Liberty Lake Regional Park - Split Creek Loop

properties.description: Most trails are human-made, this one is arguably more so than most. The 1937 Civilian Conservation Corps crew who built this trail hewed hundreds of granite steps from the local bedrock, installing them in twisting fashion up one steep canyon and down another. A trip around this loop is a step back in time to an era when trails built through rock were cut primarily with sweat and muscle.
properties.title: Candy Point Trail

properties.description: Explore the miles of trail that weave through the 240-acre Grand Forest on Bainbridge Island. The relatively flat trails are also used by horses and mountain bikers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Grand Forest

properties.description: Link together six trails for a fall color loop past numerous lakes of the Tumac Plateau and hike Tumac Mountain in the William O. Douglas Wilderness.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Tumac Plateau Loop

properties.description: Enter rarefied air as you climb halfway up the most popular route to the summit of Mount Rainier. This is Camp Muir, a perch higher than the summits of nearly all mountains in the state. In addition to commanding views of the South Cascades, catch a glimpse of both the history of the park and the dramatic landscape of Rainier’s upper reaches.
properties.title: Camp Muir

properties.description: The well-maintained Red Bluff trail is a great place to enjoy the Colville National Forest’s native flora and fauna in May through November.
properties.title: Red Bluff

properties.description: Just outside of the town of Poulsbo, this park features a short loop trail that takes visitors through the forest to a trail that runs along the shore of Liberty Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Keyport Saltwater Park

properties.description: Bellevue's Ardmore Park offers two connected sections of forest habitat, traversed by easy hiking trails. Here, you can enjoy tall conifers and deciduous trees, ferns and other forest vegetation, and small creeks, giving the illusion that you are some distance away from surrounding suburbia. You are likely to find a few wildflowers blooming in season, to hear woodpeckers, crows and other birds, and see a few energetic squirrels
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ardmore Park Trails

properties.description: Known as the South Puyallup Trail, this access point to the Wonderland Trail is a connector 1.7 miles long that wends its way through a mature forest with trees ranging between 100 to 1000 years old.
properties.title: South Puyallup Trail

properties.description: With expansive waterfront views and access to a beach right against the Puget Sound, a walk down the Redondo Beach Boardwalk is a great way to get some fresh air without ever leaving town.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redondo Beach Boardwalk

properties.description: This is a lovely urban trail system outside of Spokane and near the Little Spokane River.
properties.title: Waikiki Springs Nature Preserve

properties.description: This trail in Concrete follows the Lower Baker River through downtown Concrete to the Baker River Clubhouse and Visitors Center. Interpretive signs offer information about the area's history, salmon habitat, hydroelectric development and more.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: S.báliuqw Interpretive Trail (Lower Baker Loop)

properties.description: This moderate trail traverses a ridgeline up and down all the way to Maiden Peak.
properties.title: Elk Mountain to Maiden Peak

properties.description: Fish Creek connects the shore of Lake Chelan with the Chelan Summit Trail to the east.
properties.title: Fish Creek

properties.description: Approachable throughout the year, the Mount Walker trail’s average 20% grade makes it a go-to route for hikers and trail runners looking for a short, brisk tromp. (While it is also a designated stock trail, riders and pack animals rarely make an appearance.) Spring, summer, and fall the 2-mile trail is both ascended and descended by those on foot. In the winter, when the Mount Walker road is gated closed to vehicles, many will pursue the then 2.25-mile jaunt up to the north viewpoint, saunter over to the south viewpoint and then descend on the more gentle grade of the road.
properties.title: Mount Walker

properties.description: The "Harry O" is popular with horseback riders for its many miles of trails to be explored. Visitors here should expect plenty of horseback riding company.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Les Hilde - Harry Osborne State Forest

properties.description: There's no question why Ingalls Lake is one of the most popular destinations in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. It is a stunning blue lake, set high in a basin beneath rocky peaks, showcasing striking Mount Stuart as its backdrop. The trail to this treasure is filled with delights, both for the summer adventurer as well as for those hikers who appreciate fall colors. Views of the craggy Esmeralda Peaks, a walk through beautiful Headlight Basin plus a pretty picture of the imposing Stuart Range are just a few of the wonders along the way.
properties.title: Lake Ingalls

properties.description: This 9-acre park has a baseball field and picnic areas. Take a leisurely stroll on the 0.75-mile trail and look for views of Mount Rainier at this charming city park.
properties.title: Tumwater Hill Park

properties.description: Wander through a true neighborhood park in Bellingham with a creek, playground and art to enjoy.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Storybrook Park (Maplewood-McLeod Open Space)

properties.description: A short trail that loops through a forested gully in North Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Llandover Woods Greenspace

properties.description: Originally a Native American travel route across the Cascade range, the Cowlitz trail now offers visitors multiple loop options and beautiful destinations in the William O. Douglas wilderness.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Cowlitz Trail

properties.description: This short hike to the top of Patterson Mountain provides great views across and along the Methow Valley from Twisp to Mazama, while to the west lies the Sawtooth Range.
properties.title: Patterson Mountain

properties.description: This wheelchair-friendly trail winds through a peaceful forested area in Vancouver’s Bella Vista neighborhood. Built by volunteers, Behrens Woods provides a brief escape from the city.
properties.title: Behrens Woods

properties.description: Start out at a historic lodge, then walk along the edge of a lagoon before heading out to the beach.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Titlow Park

properties.description: This 500-acre community forest and adjacent 75-acre Q'emiln Park offer numerous hiking trails with many loop possibilities up to about 6 miles, and also rock climbing, picnicking, and swimming.
properties.title: Post Falls Community Forest and Q'emiln Park

properties.description: Formerly the Rugged Ridge Trail, the Snider-Jackson Trail is a primitive north to south traverse on the west side of Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Snider-Jackson Traverse

properties.description: Family-friendly Placid Lake is a great hike or first backpack for kids; in less than a mile, you are at a sandy beach with shallow water for wading and fishing, huckleberries for snacking and a big campsite for a picnic or camping. Keep going to visit another lake or a high meadow near the Pacific Crest Trail.
properties.title: Placid and Chenamus Lakes

properties.description: Known as the jewel of Longview, this man-made lake in Southwest Washington is a delightful way to spend a couple of hours. Maple trees blaze red, orange and yellow in autumn, willows provide shade in spring, and the stark skeletons of those trees stand out against grey skies in winter. With various bridges crossing it, it's possible to venture all the way around it, or create smaller loops as needed
properties.title: Lake Sacajawea

properties.description: Trail 25 is the main artery that runs through Riverside State Park. Loop options abound here, as do out-and-backs, or just short wanderings.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Trail 25

properties.description: This trail travels along the valley floor of the Little Wenatchee River for several miles before switchbacking up 1500 feet through intermittent slide alder and mature forest to Meander Meadows. While the trail does receive occasional brushing, the lower section can be challenging.
properties.title: Little Wenatchee River

properties.description: This is a short but popular backpacking destination. This hike will bring you into the heart of the Indian Heaven wilderness where bog blueberries and huckleberries are abundant in August.
properties.title: Junction Lake

properties.description: Explore from ridgelines to river in a remote corner of the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Grizzly Bear Ridge - Wenaha River - Slick Ear Loop

properties.description: The trail has not been maintained since this area was burned in the 2003 Farewell Fire.  It starts at the Chewuch Trail, 5.9 miles up from the Thirtymile Trailhead.  It ends at a junction in the abandoned section of the Coleman Ridge Trail.
properties.title: Fire Creek

properties.description: Take a walk through the grounds of the Washington Park Arboretum, along the edge of Lake Washington, and near the grounds of the old MOHAI building. This is a nice urban romp, perfect for before or after work, or on a day when you just can't get out of the city.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Foster and Marsh Island Loop

properties.description: For a quiet snowshoe on flat terrain, try this ranger recommended hike just outside of Leavenworth.
properties.title: Tumwater Campground Snowshoe

properties.description: Follow an irregularly maintained multi-use trail as it follows the forested ridge crest with periodic views across Foggy Dew Creek to the Sawtooth Range. When not recently maintained, this is a natural hiker-only trail due to downed logs, with many opportunities to see wildlife.
properties.title: Foggy Dew Ridge

properties.description: The Trautman Ranch Conservation Area provides over 275 acres of meadows and open woodland over rolling terrain adjacent to Riverside State Park. This enjoyable loop hike circles the entire property.
properties.title: Trautman Ranch Conservation Area - West Loop

properties.description: Luther Burbank Park is a waterfront park at the North end of Mercer Island, offering three miles of family- and pet-friendly trails with waterfront access, wetlands, and recreational activities.
properties.title: Luther Burbank Park

properties.description: WTA does not recommend attempting this route, as it requires hiking through an active ski resort and in areas that may have high avalanche danger.
properties.title: Lake Susan Jane Snowshoe

properties.description: Located above Clark Fork, Idaho, visitors earn the fantastic views of Lake Pend Oreille by gaining nearly 3,730 feet of elevation in a seven mile roundtrip hike.
properties.title: Scotchman Peak

properties.description: Try this early-season, ADA-accessible hike to enjoy big trees, rushing waters and glimpses of eagles, mergansers and river otters.
properties.title: Old Sauk ADA Loop

properties.description: Edith Creek Basin is a popular Mount Rainier snowshoeing area. The basin lies north of Paradise and connects to Panorama Point.
properties.title: Edith Creek Basin Snowshoe

properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Josephine Lake (Skagit)

properties.description: Hop aboard the free, seasonal ferry to Jetty Island and explore the sandy beaches, active sea life, and bountiful birds. This island, made of sediment dredged from the Snohomish River, is a true gem.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Jetty Island

properties.description: Summit scramble in the Central Cascades off of Highway 2. Gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Palmer Mountain

properties.description: Delve deep into the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness via the shortest access to the upper Wenaha River from the Washington side.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Slick Ear

properties.description: Access some of Washington's loneliest country from this trailhead. But as the name suggests, be on the lookout for wildlife -- it's lonely country but that doesn't mean it's empty.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Thirteenmile via Bear Pot Trailhead

properties.description: A short, hike alongside a creek on the east side of Washington, just outside of Yakima. Lush brush, including balsamroot, yarrow, and lupine can be found along the way, as you enjoy the dramatic canyon walls.
properties.title: East Rim Waterworks Canyon

properties.description: The stunning views and unparalleled springtime flowers make this one of the most popular hikes in the Gorge. On a good day, you can get a bird’s eye view of Mount Hood and the Columbia River. In the spring the top is carpeted with vibrant yellow balsam root. Although the trail is steep and sometimes crowded, this hike is unquestionably worth the effort.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Dog Mountain

properties.description: Grass Camp Trail provides good loop opportunities in the wildflower-rich area southeast of Blewett Pass. Use a variety of nearby trails to create loops or traverses through this area.
properties.title: Grass Camp

properties.description: This is a striking, gorgeous hike -- excellent year round, whether you like snow-dappled trail or high desert. If you visit in summer, bring lots of water and a hat. There's no water available here.
properties.title: White Bluffs - North

properties.description: Bleakly urban, curiously varied; this are is dramatically unique despite its diminutive stature. Select from two short walks -- a short hill climb or a wander through river bottom with interpretive signs.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Duwamish Hill Preserve

properties.description: Take in views of scenic waterfalls, fall foliage, and Bonanza Peak from the trail to Hart Lake. The trail is unique in that it begins at Holden Village, a Lutheran ministry only reachable via a combined ferry and bus trip.
properties.title: Holden to Hart Lake

properties.description: The Chesaw Wildlife Area is also known as the Chesaw Wildlife Unit/Scotch Creek Wildlife Area Chesaw.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Chesaw Wildlife Area

properties.description: This short boardwalk meanders through marshy wetlands just a couple of minutes away from downtown Auburn.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Auburn Environmental Park Wetland Trail Boardwalk

properties.description: Per management at Alderbrook Resort these trails are no longer open to the public.
properties.title: Alderbrook Nature Trails

properties.description: Located deep in the Wenaha-Tucannon wilderness, the Rattlesnake Trail promises wildflowers, expansive views, and even solitude. It's possible to do an out-and-back hike to Indian Corral, but many opt to do the loop with the Panjab Loop.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Rattlesnake Trail

properties.description: The Lakemont Park trail system consists of more than three miles of multi-use trails. Visit a waterfall, learn about stormwater treatment, and get a shot of greenery at this local spot.
properties.title: Lakemont Park

properties.description: Wander through the eastern reaches of Taylor Mountain Forest.
properties.title: Hermit Trail

properties.description: The Airport Levee Trail traces along the western edge of the Chehalis-Centralia airport. The crushed gravel trail surface carries visitors along, offering views of a golf course to the west and the airport tarmac to the east.
properties.title: Airport Levee Trail

properties.description: Connect the Poo Poo Point Trail with the Tiger Mountain Trail on this hike on the west side of Tiger Mountain.
properties.title: One-View Trail

properties.description: Hike to a lovely, glittering, quiet little lake that at Mount St. Helens that few visit. You’ll have to work for it, of course. But it’s a neat little treat to share with friends, or head to it solo for some solitude.
properties.title: Ghost Lake

properties.description: Deming Homestead Eagle Park is an excellent stop along the Nooksack River. Enjoy bald eagle viewing and gorgeous rambly rivers here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Deming Homestead Eagle Park

properties.description: Lester Ghost Town is located in the Green River Watershed, where access is restricted. Please refrain from visiting this location.
properties.title: Lester Ghost Town

properties.description: With an average gradient of 13%, Big Creek Trail (#252) to Cora Lake — and beyond! — is a workout for some hikers despite its modest length, but it’s well worth the effort. You’ll be rewarded with waterfalls, a placid lake, enormous old trees and sweeping views of the surrounding cliffs and Mount Rainier.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Cora Lake via Big Creek Trail

properties.description: Here is a trifecta of lakes — Hobo, Chimney and Laverty — not easily matched. A moderate number of miles gets you into this alpine, lake lottery.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Hobo Lake (Oregon)

properties.description: Unicorn Peak is the tallest in the Tatoosh Mountain Range and offers spectacular views of Mount Rainier. It's top is somewhat jagged which looks like a Unicorn's horn, hence the name. Climbing expertise and gear is required to summit Unicorn.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Unicorn Peak

properties.description: This is a short hike through a lush forest canyon with Goat Creek cascading gently beside you all the way.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Goat Falls

properties.description: The Russell Ridge trail takes you along Russell Ridge, and offers connections to multiple other trails, including the Ironstone Mountain Trail (#1141) — providing access to Ironstone Mountain, Burnt Mountain and McNeil Peak — and the Wildcat Trail (#1113).
properties.title: Russell Ridge

properties.description: This park is just outside the city of Ellensburg along the Yakima River. The park is a long, narrow parcel that stretches between the river and I-90 with a parking area at both ends.
properties.title: Irene Rinehart Riverfront Park

properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Tomlike Mountain

properties.description: "Lightning" Bill Austin from the Goat Peak Lookout had a brief stint here in 2014, but was moved back to Goat Peak before the end of the summer. Hikers to Leecher may or may not find into a ranger staffing the lookout at the summit, but the views from the 40-foot tower are sublime either way.
properties.title: Leecher Mountain Lookout

properties.description: Marvel at old-growth trees amid a lush rain forest landscape while visiting one of Olympic National Park’s most beloved attractions: Sol Duc Falls.
properties.title: Sol Duc Falls

properties.description: A short walk through a forest to a long beach.
properties.title: Beach 2

properties.description: Walk a very pleasant and well-graded trail through old- and new-growth forest. After a moderate elevation gain, the forest opens into meadowlands filled with wildflowers after the snow melts. A pair of shallow but pretty lakes, with a rocky ridge as a backdrop, completes the scene.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Owyhigh Lakes

properties.description: Five miles east of the Stevens Pass Ski Area, the Stevens Pass Nordic Center trails offer a quiet place to snowshoe among quiet giants of the forest. Share the area with cross-country and skate skiers, who schuss past on groomed trails, while dedicated snowshoe routes criss-cross the area and offer a wide variety of outing.
properties.title: Stevens Pass Nordic Center

properties.description: The Lakes Trail offers a nice day hike along a volcano-created lake, or a gateway into the Mount Margaret Backcountry.
properties.title: Lakes Trail

properties.description: A quiet roadwalk near Blewett Pass — a good option for those looking for a wide trail with less elevation gain.
properties.title: Hurley Road Snowshoe

properties.description: Visit a park near Olympia that boasts it all: native flora and fauna, an interpretive nature trail, historical markers and plenty to keep kids entertained all year round.
properties.title: Brewery Park at Tumwater Falls

properties.description: Enjoy the shrub steppe just on the edge of town. Perfect for a short run or exploring with kids.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Iwetemlaykin State Heritage Site (Oregon)

properties.description: Lord Hill Park is a wonderful wild park and an excellent place to hike, covering about 1,463 acres of wetland and forest. Hikers can roam all day on the network of trails leading through the forest, down to the Snohomish River and up to views of the Cascades and Snohomish Valley.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lord Hill Regional Park

properties.description: Hike through alpine meadows and descend into a valley following the West Fork Pasayten River.
properties.title: West Fork Pasayten River

properties.description: A scramble of a peak in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness near I-90. Technical gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Chair Peak

properties.description: Visit a short but interesting trail with interpretive signs explaining studies on tree spacing during replantation.
properties.title: Spacing Study Trail

properties.description: A location outside of Yakima designated for bird-dog training in spring; this area does not have a formal trail system.
properties.title: Pine Canyon

properties.description: This low-key loop in the shadow of Mount Ellinor makes for a great respite on a hot summer day or a low-country winter ramble when it's rainy.
properties.title: Big Creek

properties.description: Take a sojourn in the Hood Canal Ranger District on this way trail within Mount Skokomish Wilderness. If you're looking for solitude, you'll find it on this out-of-the-way gem in the Olympic National Forest.
properties.title: Mildred Lakes

properties.description: Summit scramble off Squire Creek Trail on Mountain Loop Highway. Gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Jumbo Mountain

properties.description: Trillium Park is a small urban park connecting two neighborhoods in Olympia, with a trail running through the park.
properties.title: Trillium Park

properties.description: Dishman Hills Natural Area's East/West Pond Loop is located just west of the main parking area at Camp Caro, making the loop an easy introductory hike to the Dishman Hills, or a jumping off point for further exploration within the Natural Area's trail network.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Natural Area - East/West Pond Loop

properties.description: Orangegate Park Is a large greenspace managed by Pierce County Parks. This parcel has a trail network that is still under development. WTA volunteers have worked here to develop these trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Orangegate Park

properties.description: Walk in the deep shade of towering, ancient Douglas-firs and western redcedars and become humbled in the presence of these survivors of volcanic eruption.
properties.title: Green River

properties.description: This gently graded trail winds through the woods for a short while before turning uphill and summitting a real peak with stupendous views of the surrounding peaks. With good navigation skills an off-trail descent can take you back to your car. The trail can also be connected to several other trails in the Sun Mountain System for a longer outing.
properties.title: Herringbone Hill

properties.description: A trail named for local mountaineer Jim Whittaker, this hike begins at the road and ascends to the summit of Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Whittaker Wilderness Peak

properties.description: There are over three miles of trails in this community park. Visitors can stop by for a quick dose of nature or do the full loop for a longer walk.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Battle Point Park Trail

properties.description: This alternate approach to Iron Peak begins at the Beverly Turnpike trailhead.
properties.title: Iron Peak via Tooth Saddle Trail

properties.description: Located on the White River near Mount Rainier, the Mud Mountain Dam is both a flood control dam operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and a recreation facility. This gentle 2-mile trail will take you along the White River.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mud Mountain Dam - Rim Trail

properties.description: The Yurt is by far the most secluded of the four huts within the Mount Tahoma Trail System. A cozy studio in the wilderness surrounded by trees with access for a day hike to Griffin Mountain.
properties.title: The Yurt

properties.description: Enjoy a trio of lakes and meadows on this excellent summer destination.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Blakenship Lakes

properties.description: Rocky Top is an extensive system of interconnected mountain bike trails open to hikers.  It offers innumerable out-and back and loop options though shrub-steppe on the flanks of Cowiche Mountain as well as a scenic ridge walk on a portion of the William O. Douglas Trail to the summit of the mountain and a connection with the Snow Mountain Ranch trail system.
properties.title: Rocky Top and Cowiche Mountain

properties.description: Not so scenic but plenty peaceful, Jay Lake is one of a small handful of backcountry camping areas in a state park. Just be sure to get a permit before you head out!
properties.title: Wallace Falls State Park - Jay Lake

properties.description: By combining rare prairie wetlands, a large forested area, and an old historic building all in 960 acres, Scatter Creek has attractions for everyone.
properties.title: Scatter Creek

properties.description: The Aurora Ridge Trail is welcome for those who love solitude, and great views of Lake Crescent, Ediz Hook, Mount Baker, Mount Olympus, and Glacier Peak can all be seen from Sourdough Peak and along the ridge.
properties.title: Aurora Ridge

properties.description: Enjoy wildflowers, solitude, and gorgeous views of Puget Sound on this lovely little hike down a pretty trail to Watmaugh Bay Beach. The park is located off Watmough Head Road, and the beach is beautiful; perfect for a picnic.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Point Colville

properties.description: The Working Forest Interpretive Trail is a shaded, half-mile loop through a forest of mixed use and age. Interpretive signs guide hikers along the way through halls of mossy hemlock and offer history on the logging in the area. Conveniently located adjacent to the Coho Campground and Wynoochee Lake, this short hike is perfect for families.
properties.title: Working Forest Nature Trail

properties.description: This trail in the Umatilla National Forest starts at the end of Forest Service Road 6512 at Table Springs Ridge and goes to Bear Creek. It uses to provide access to the Walla Walla River drainage trail loop system which is used for fishing, hunting, camping, horseback riding, hiking and more
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Bear Creek via Table Springs Ridge

properties.description: With an ominous name like Mudhole Lake, it would be easy to set low expectations for this destination. Don’t be fooled though. This infrequently-visited route provides a steep ascent on good trail with expansive views and good berries in season. After just a couple of miles, a hidden pond, nestled in among larches in a high mountain cirque, will be all yours.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Mudhole Lake

properties.description: Bluegrass Butte is the unofficial name for the seldom summited peak five miles northeast of Silverton.
properties.title: Bluegrass Butte

properties.description: Hike from the site of a historic military occupation down to South Beach, the longest public beach on San Juan Island. Wildlife abounds as guests often encounter red foxes and may see orcas in the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: American Camp and South Beach

properties.description: Hike a challenging trail over steep and varied terrain to views of glaciers, mountains, and the remote northeast side of Mount Adams.
properties.title: Mount Adams Highline

properties.description: Nestled on the eastern edge of the Tri-Cities is a lovely little state park dedicated to Sacagawea, the Shoshone woman who was crucial to the success of the Corps of Discovery. An easy loop hike winds through unirrigated sections of the park.
properties.title: Sacajawea Historical State Park

properties.description: Popular because it's the perfect balance between day hike and easy enough for little legs, the Hummocks Trail goes up, down and around the hummocks, strange hills that were left behind by the eruption of Mount St. Helens in 1980, forming a loop from the trailhead.
properties.title: Hummocks Trail

properties.description: A connector to Military Road along 166th Way SE on Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Sky Country

properties.description: Explore lakes, wetlands, and the shrub-steppe landscape on this tour of BLM property west of Spokane.
properties.title: Twin Lakes Recreation Area

properties.description: Enjoy the extensive wildflowers, creeks and views of Mount Adams in a landscape renewing itself following a severe fire.
properties.title: Shorthorn

properties.description: This trail in the William O. Douglas wilderness climbs from the north side of Highway 12 through second-growth forest.  It offers access to Spiral Butte and Shellrock Lake, among other lakes in this area. While it's a lovely spot to enjoy a low-key backpack, the water here can make the area swampy in the spring and early summer.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Sand Ridge

properties.description: Launch a variety of outdoor adventures from this cozy historic guard station located on the edge of the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Godman Guard Station - Winter

properties.description: Though it's hidden behind a more than 12-mile road walk or bike, the West Fork Dosewallips River trail offers tunnels of rhododendrons, a jubilant river, and solitude.
properties.title: West Fork Dosewallips River

properties.description: Flat Creek is a short day hike out of the Flat Creek Campground on the old Stehekin Valley Road. However, to get to the Stehekin road is a day or more trip, so you'll need to plan more than one day for this trip.
properties.title: Flat Creek

properties.description: Climb to the top of a low peak at on the Washington side of the Columbia River, then visit a historic fort, complete with gun battery and old buildings available to rent.
properties.title: Fort Columbia State Park - Scarborough Hill

properties.description: This ski/snowshoe follows the North Fork Teanaway River Road that hikers drive on in the summer to get to the various Teanaway trailheads, passing through open forest and meadows alongside the North Fork Teanaway River.
properties.title: North Fork Teanaway River

properties.description: Just across the Snohomish River from the city of Everett sits a small park with two loop hike options on three miles of paved trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Langus Riverfront Park

properties.description: A parcel of land managed by Mason County Parks near Olympia.
properties.title: Oakland Bay Historical Park

properties.description: Snoqualmie Pass grows ever more developed each year. Condos go up left and right, the ski area plans new ski lifts (or replacements for existing chairs), and hotels pop up east and west. But even with the development, these are still mountains and there is still stunning mountain scenery to enjoy, even on the fringes of the developed areas. Lodge Lake stands as proof.
properties.title: Lodge Lake

properties.description: Hike a scenic ridgeline on a trail connecting Lake Julius and Lake Ethel. Views of the central Cascades abound on this rugged route outside of Leavenworth.
properties.title: Upper Roaring Creek

properties.description: Channel your inner mountain goat on this steep hike to aptly-named High Pass, and bask in glorious views of Glacier Peak and the surrounding mountainscape.
properties.title: High Pass

properties.description: This gem of an alpine lake, situated in a cirque beneath the glaciated summit of Little Devil Peak, is ringed by verdant meadows and frequented by resident wildlife.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Monogram Lake

properties.description: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge has several trails available for exploration, but the Art Walk is the most engaging and kid-friendly.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Art Walk

properties.description: The Iverson Railroad Trail begins at the Tiger Summit Trailhead off SR 18 and heads west along the south side of East Tiger Mountain for roughly 1.7 miles, ending at West Side Road.
properties.title: Iverson Railroad Trail

properties.description: The Wonderland Trail is a 93-mile hiking trail that encircles Washington's most famous volcano. Each year, hikers vie for permits to embark on a backpacking trip on it, with only a handful scoring the permits to undertake this strenuous hike.
properties.title: Wonderland Trail

properties.description: Follow a tumbling, churning, whitewater creek upstream as it thunders through a narrow gorge of glacier-polished rock on your way to a waterfall that drops 301 feet in a single plunge.  Admire numerous small waterfalls and cascades and two significant ones, all in less than 2 miles. This is the Comet Falls trail.
properties.title: Comet Falls

properties.description: Many hikers only see the first couple miles of this trail, since Lily Lake is a popular location for families. But the Clear Fork Trail is many miles long, and offers fantastic adventure past the small lake.
properties.title: Clear Fork Trail

properties.description: Bald eagles, icons of the mossy forests and deep rivers of the Pacific Coast, flock to this desert canyon each winter, and their presence is reason to visit in late fall or winter.
properties.title: Northrup Canyon

properties.description: This is a winter only trail linking Marble Mountain SnoPark to the Worm Flows winter climbing route.
properties.title: Swift Creek

properties.description: The trails on Mount Spokane interlace, offering opportunities to create long or short hikes. Trail 120 allows hikers to loop onto the Kit Carson Trail and beyond.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 120

properties.description: A striking peak off the Mountain Loop Highway that requires climbing experience to summit successfully.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Voodoo Peak

properties.description: Escape the crowds within Mount Rainier National Park without going on a lengthy adventure. Visit one or both of two alpine lakes, the second one just a bit more than a mile from the parking lot.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Bench and Snow Lakes

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Mount Logan

properties.description: Both educational and interesting, the trails around the reclaimed water ponds are a nice place to spend a day.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Hawks Prairie Reclaimed Water Ponds

properties.description: This easy access trail just off I-90 in north Idaho leads to a beautiful alpine lake nestled beneath Stevens Peak in the Bitterroot Mountains.
properties.title: Lone Lake

properties.description: Expansive views of Mount Rainier, up-close views of Emmons Glacier, lakes, and campsites are just a few features of the Glacier Basin Loop's varying landscape.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Glacier Basin Loop

properties.description: This steep hike near Sandpoint has exceptional views and native plant life. Make your way past meadows, around massive rocky outcroppings and beneath towering old growth timber to marvelous views.
properties.title: Mickinnick Trail

properties.description: Enjoy majestic mountain panoramas from this relatively low-effort, high-vista hike on the Olympic Peninsula.
properties.title: Lillian Ridge

properties.description: Ascend the decommissioned portion of the Westside Road to the Lake George Trailhead, and then follow a moderately steep trail through an old-growth Douglas fir and hemlock forest to a secluded and beautiful campground on the shores of a beautiful blue-green mountain lake. Grab a permit at the Longmire Ranger Station and make it an overnight — but bring warm clothes.
properties.title: Lake George

properties.description: This paved trail is about 0.25 miles and loops around the small Spring Creek pond. There is also a short spur to a small bluff that overlooks the Little Pend Oreille River and the valley that the river runs through.
properties.title: Headquarters Trail

properties.description: Found on the outskirts of Port Angeles, the Peabody Creek Trail starts out from the Olympic National Park Visitors Center and follows Peabody Creek through a quiet wooded ravine for 2.8 miles. It’s an excellent short hike for visitors, locals, and trail runners alike.
properties.title: Peabody Creek Trail

properties.description: This trail is the end section of Icicle River Road that is left unplowed in the winter months. It is fun for snowshoers of all ages and skill levels.
properties.title: Icicle River Road Snowshoe

properties.description: The Cameron Pass trail is a brushy bushwhack to a lovely high alpine basin and pass. But it's miles in the backcountry and requires hard work and planning to get there.
properties.title: Cameron Pass

properties.description: Hike through a fire-devastated forest to an alpine lake set below steep cliffs with a waterfall inlet.  Rennie Peak looms to the south and a mature forest shelters many campsites.  Come for the day, or camp and explore.
properties.title: Louis Lake

properties.description: A hike with great scenery in the high country of Olympic with good opportunity to see the endemic Olympic marmot and wildflowers!
properties.title: Moose Lake

properties.description: Mount Grant Preserve is a trail system in development on San Juan Island. Currently, the trails to the top offer the most elevation gain available on San Juan Island, so you'll love this one if you're looking to get high up.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Mount Grant Preserve

properties.description: Ptarmigan Peak is a prominent summit located in the remote Pasayten Wilderness. The peak can be reached via the Slate Peak Trailhead or Eightmile Creek Road.
properties.title: Ptarmigan Peak

properties.description: This flower-lined trail with big views will make you wonder if the Blue Mountains earned their name from the carpets of larkspur along the route.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Sawtooth Ridge

properties.description: This small 20-acre park offers visitors access to the beach along Dumas Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Dumas Bay Sanctuary

properties.description: Hike the Pacific Crest Trail to a relatively unknown but landmark lookout site on a rock pinnacle with a view of 5 snow peaks and segments of the Columbia River. Three Corner Rock sits atop of broad, open ridge surrounded by beargrass meadows in the spring.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Three Corner Rock

properties.description: Dutch Miller Gap is a lovely spot, but takes a drive on rough road and a long hike to access.
properties.title: Dutch Miller Gap

properties.description: Fans of geology, history and, of course, nature can enjoy this 168-acre day-use park. The top of the butte has magnificent views from above the Palouse Hills, and you can learn more about the area’s unique geology from interpretive panels at the summit.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Steptoe Butte State Park Heritage Site

properties.description: A brushy hike up an abandoned logging road to Jumpoff Ridge.
properties.title: Jumpoff Ridge

properties.description: View old growth "big trees" via an easy walk near Willapa Bay.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Teal Slough

properties.description: Where can you find unobstructed views of Mount Rainier and the mountains of Snoqualmie Pass, see rare butterfly species, and go berry-picking, all in return for a modest 1330-foot elevation gain? Mount Catherine, of course! This off-the-beaten-path hike to the summit of a wintertime ski destination is one of the most rewarding climbs along the southern wall of Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Mount Catherine

properties.description: Another favorite area near Sage Hills and Horse Lake Reserve, Castle Rock property provides access for hikers who want adventure near Wenatchee. This hike will take you to the top of Castle Rock, an iconic feature of the Wenatchee skyline.
properties.title: Castle Rock

properties.description: Clallam Bay Spit Community Beach County Park is a unique, 1.2-mile stretch of shoreline 45 miles west of Port Angeles towards Neah Bay, perfect for stretching your legs, bird watching and beachcombing for ocean treasures.  Quietly tucked into a curve on SR-112 as you enter the quaint town of Clallam Bay, it offers year-round restrooms and a dog-friendly place to picnic, walk and learn about local shipping history.
properties.title: Clallam Bay Spit Community Beach County Park

properties.description: Sample the best the North Cascades has to offer—subalpine lakes, forested valleys and rugged mountain passes—on this multiday trek.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Rainbow-McAlester Loop

properties.description: Discover the true beauty of the Bogachiel Rain Forest on the Ira Spring Wetland trail. This short trail will take you on a loop through a fern forest and around a large wetland. While leashed dogs are allowed in on the Ira Wetland trail, they are NOT allowed in the Olympic National Park, the boundary of which is 1.6 miles along the Bogachiel Trail.
properties.title: Ira Spring Wetland

properties.description: Get a different view of the perennially-popular Mount Si on the Talus Loop Trail. A little over 4 miles long, the Talus Trail explores the eastern slopes of the mountain. You'll hike briefly with the crowds headed to the haystack, then peel off and enjoy a much quieter forest walk, along with a good workout.
properties.title: Talus Loop

properties.description: Clackamas Mountain Trail is a focal point for this area. There is a moderate loop here following ridgelines and much of this trail is part of the Pacific Northwest National Scenic Trail. Many options exist, so take a map to make your adventure.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Clackamas Mountain

properties.description: A primitive, difficult to navigate trail switchbacking downhill to the confluence of the forks of Canyon Creek, hence the name. Now situated behind the road closure on the Road 41 system, this trailhead is inaccessible by car.
properties.title: Forks of Canyon Creek

properties.description: Begin in old-growth forest, climb up to one of Mount Rainier's most spectacular wildflower meadows, then continue along the highest section of the Wonderland Trail to reach the alpine world of Panhandle Gap. Along the way be alert for marmots and goats, and it is not unusual to see a black bear.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Summerland - Panhandle Gap

properties.description: Follow an unplowed forest road as it meanders up the Tieton River Valley and keep on the lookout for elk, fox, martens and other wildlife that thrive in this wilderness area. Along the way you can enjoy views of Old Snowy Mountain or explore the wide meadows that line the trail.
properties.title: Tieton River Meadows Snowshoe

properties.description: Less of a trail than a road walk, the route up Quartz Creek offers quiet and solitude in the Middle Fork Valley.
properties.title: Quartz Creek/Lake Blethen

properties.description: An overgrown and hard-to-follow trail in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Cascade Creek offers intrepid hikers backdoor access to Navaho Peak, and the possibility of loops in and all around the Teanaway area.
properties.title: Cascade Creek

properties.description: Hike a rugged trail through second-growth hemlock forest. You'll cross several lively creeks and see waterfalls on your way to a high alpine lake well-stocked with trout.
properties.title: Dingford Creek-Hester Lake

properties.description: Visit the historic Indian Racetrack in the Indian Heaven Wilderness with the option to continue on to the scenic Red Mountain Lookout.
properties.title: Red Mountain Lookout via Indian Racetrack

properties.description: A short but scenic nature trail that begins and ends at the Troublesome Creek Campground. Hikers and campers will enjoy the walk along and over the turquoise creek, which indeed could be troublesome without the bridges spanning the shores.
properties.title: Troublesome Creek Nature

properties.description: A summit scramble near Hannegan Pass in the North Cascades. Route finding experience required.
properties.title: Granite Mountain (Mount Baker)

properties.description: Silver Shadow Trail is a three-mile connector trail in the Yacolt Burn State Forest named for being in the shadow of neighboring Silver Star Mountain. Hike it one-way, or connect it with the Tarbell trail to make a 5 mile loop.
properties.title: Yacolt Burn State Forest - Silver Shadow Trail

properties.description: Enjoy a hike to a beautiful subalpine meadow in the Goat Rocks Wilderness. A good destination all on its own, it can also provide a jumping off point for a longer trip.
properties.title: Snowgrass Flat

properties.description: Short but steep, this trail delivers excellent views of Mount Baker, Mount Shuksan, and Anderson Butte. Similar views can be had from the road to the trailhead, but taking this hike offers solitude--even a hiker’s high--from climbing steeply away from the road and into the mountains.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Anderson Butte

properties.description: The Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) runs from Mexico to the Canadian border through the Columbia Gorge. While it is well-known for traveling along the waterfall-filled Eagle Creek Trail, purists know that it is an alternate route; the actual trail runs a bit south closer to the Bridge of The Gods. Here, the PCT leads you to the secluded gem of Dry Creek Falls just a few miles away from the noise and bustle of I-84.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Dry Creek Falls

properties.description: This long route connects the subalpine environs of Chinook Pass and Tipsoo Lake with the deep, lowland forests of the Ohanapecosh area. It is part of the East Side Loop trail, a long loop that hikers can enjoy in lieu of the Wonderland Trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Eastside Trail

properties.description: A walk through the coastal forest and tidal flats of Leadbetter Point State Park, the Dune Forest Loop is a nice way to see this low-lying peninsula, but the conditions on trail are heavily dependent on the tides and recent rainfall. Come prepared to wade through at least a little bit of water, and don’t be surprised to find yourself navigating deeper stuff. Bring a tide table, and try to visit at low tide for the driest conditions.
properties.title: Leadbetter Point State Park - Dune Forest Loop

properties.description: Visit a scenic bridge, a lovely little waterfall, and a historic area in the Columbia River Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Shepperd's Dell State Natural Area

properties.description: Hike a delightful, somewhat rugged trail past several waterfalls to views of the Columbia River and the stunning Gorge, capped off by a stop by the most popular recreation area in the Northwest: Multnomah Falls.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Wahkeena-Multnomah Falls Loop

properties.description: A short spur trail to a camping area off the Salmo Basin Trail.
properties.title: Salmo Cabin

properties.description: Hike a little more than a mile on a shady lollipop loop trail reserved for hikers near the southern edge of the Capitol State Forest, south of Olympia. Gain 300 feet elevation as you ascend from the confluence of the Mill and Mima Creeks to the high point in the grove of big old hemlock, cedar and fir trees.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Bob Bammert Grove Loop

properties.description: Here's a Mount Baker Highway gem that's low enough to be passable all year and at the same time easy enough for the whole family. It's also a terrific spot to witness the power of water.
properties.title: Horseshoe Bend

properties.description: This short loop trail is in a campground closed for overnight use. Hazard trees make the area dangerous for visitors and hikers are requested to refrain from visiting.
properties.title: Soda Springs Big Trees

properties.description: Tucked high in the mountains of the Olympic Peninsula, in the appropriately named Valley of Heaven, is a breathtaking lake — the Lake of the Angels. The heavenly goal is accessed by a trail built for more mortal interests. Keep in mind, though, if you tackle this trail, it's devilishly difficult. In some places, it requires a vertical climb where falling is not an option. Be prepared, both physically and mentally, for this challenging hike.
properties.title: Lake of the Angels

properties.description: The Lover's Lane trail follows the Sol Duc river upstream, connecting Sol Duc campground, Sol Duc Falls and the resort.
properties.title: Lover's Lane Loop

properties.description: Sather Park is a small park on Morgan Hill in the City of Port Townsend. It is a green space in an otherwise residential neighborhood.
properties.title: Sather Park

properties.description: Stairway to Heaven is a single track hiking and mountain biking trail in the foothills of Wenatchee. It climbs gently through fields of flowers and Ponderosa pine up to the summit of Twin Peaks. Enjoy views of the canyons and Wenatchee Valley down below.
properties.title: Stairway to Heaven

properties.description: This is a short connector trail in the Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park and adjoining lands in the City of Newcastle.
properties.title: China Creek

properties.description: Three waterfalls, multiple viewing areas, and two different trailheads provide great choices for an excursion to Little Mashel Falls. The tallest waterfall plunges over 90 feet.
properties.title: Little Mashel Falls - Pack Forest

properties.description: A peak scramble in the Snoqualmie region. Routefinding experience and climbing gear recommended.
properties.title: Mount Thomson

properties.description: This challenging trail offers panoramic views across Northeast Washington and into Idaho and Canada.
properties.title: Gypsy Peak

properties.description: This city park provides an excellent retreat from the busy area of Vancouver and Portland in the small suburb of Camas.
properties.title: Fallen Leaf Lake

properties.description: This trail system on the outskirts of Deer Park is inviting to a variety of user groups with 3 loops of different lengths through a serene ponderosa forest.
properties.title: Deer Park Missile Site Trails

properties.description: Discover the natural history of South Fidalgo Island on this beautiful forested trail. The trail traverses past meadows and rocky balds, a red rock quarry, a miner’s shack, the “rock” of artist Morris Graves’ lore, and views of Pass Lake, Campbell Lake, and Mount Erie.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: John Tursi Trail

properties.description: A routefinding scramble to the summit of a mountain up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie. Climbing, gear, and routefinding experience required.
properties.title: Mount Price

properties.description: Seven lakes, seas of wildflowers, summer huckleberries, a bevy of wildlife and a good chance of quiet solitude await you on this 9-mile out-and-back. What more could you ask for?
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Palisades Lakes

properties.description: A mostly abandoned trail along (and sometimes in) Rattlesnake Creek that has been washed out in many places due to its numerous crossings of the creek.
properties.title: Rattlesnake Trail

properties.description: Bruni's Snow Bowl Hut is named for Brunhilde (Bruni) Wislicenus, a passionate mountaineer and wilderness skier who donated a substantial portion of the funds to rebuild the hut after a fire in 2007 burnt the original to the ground. Now, it provides skiers and snowshoers a place to warm up after a bracing 4.5 mile jaunt along forest roads in Tahoma State Forest.
properties.title: Snow Bowl Hut Snowshoe

properties.description: The route to Dome Peak is a Class 5 and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.title: Dome Peak

properties.description: A snowshoe up Hwy 410 towards Chinook Pass from the gate at Morse Creek.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Chinook Pass Snowshoe

properties.description: A long, scenic trail with options to meander as long as you like.
properties.title: Ahtanum State Forest - Grey Rock Trail

properties.description: The Skyline Divide is a 6000-foot-high ridgeline extension of Mount Baker that transforms itself into a summertime paradise of unrivaled mountain views and unending wildflower fields, a trail that deposits you just 3.5 miles from the summit itself.
properties.title: Skyline Divide

properties.description: At 470 feet, Chadwick Hill is the second-highest point on Lopez Island. The trail up the hill provides a great workout, with many ups and downs to keep you warm in the cool sea breezes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Chadwick Hill

properties.description: Walk part of an abandoned railroad grade, through two tunnels, in lonely Columbia Plateau country.
properties.title: Devils Canyon - Kahlotus Railroad Grade

properties.description: Circling the summit allows hikers and their pups to take in all of the views while stretching their legs--the Spokane Valley, Liberty Lake, Mount Spokane, and Pleasant Prairie can all be seen along this route.
properties.title: Antoine Peak Conservation Area - Summit Loop

properties.description: Looking for something short, sweet and a little steep? You get all of the above and some nice views to boot on this trail.
properties.title: Roslyn Urban Forest - Crooked Tree Trail

properties.description: Staying at Camp Wooten State Park or the Tucannon Campground and looking for a quick hike to get your blood pumping?  This little trail will fit the bill - if you can follow it
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Hixon Canyon Trail

properties.description: A lookout accessible via a steep Forest Service road. Drive to it in the summer, or get a big workout climbing to it in the winter.
properties.title: Steliko Lookout

properties.description: A beautiful little lake just off the Pacific Crest Trail near Stevens Pass. Several trails lead to it, and it is a great destination for a multi-night backpacking trip.
properties.title: Lake Sally Ann

properties.description: Millersylvania State Park sports camping, boating and more than eight miles of hiking trails. The trails zigzag all around, so visitors can construct a loop of up to five miles, and add some side trips on. The huge old growth cedar and fir, easy accessibility to I-5 and excellent opportunity for a pleasant walk in the woods make this an attractive place to hike, especially in winter.
properties.title: Millersylvania State Park

properties.description: This 55-acre park has grassland, forest and wetland habitats to explore via soft-surface trail and boardwalks. The Lewis Creek Park also has a visitor center, playground, a basketball court, picnic shelter, restrooms and more.
properties.title: Lewis Creek Park

properties.description: Bear Lake Regional Park has a short hiking trail and is a popular spot for families.
properties.title: Bear Lake

properties.description: Hike the routes of two former logging railroads (the Iverson and the Hobart - Middle Tiger) to reach a remote section of Fifteenmile Creek. Follow a short, steep trail to connect with the Tiger Mountain Trail (TMT.) Return via the TMT and, on the way, look in on the site of a 1925 logging train wreck.
properties.title: Hobart - Middle Tiger Railroad Trail

properties.description: Tunnel Creek Trail has two trailheads.The south side trailhead is on the Dosewallips Road, but its notoriously steep grade to 5050 Pass means it is seldom used. Try it and you’ll find out why.
properties.title: Tunnel Creek - Dosewallips Trailhead

properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Allen Mountain

properties.description: Mount St. Helens is a peak that should be on every life list. And because it is an active volcano, it is best not to put it off for too long. Climbing to the crater rim is an opportunity to see not only amazing views in every direction, but to see geology raw, unformed and in its making.
properties.title: Mount St. Helens - Monitor Ridge

properties.description: Take a hike within sight and sound of the wild Sauk River--part of the Skagit Wild and Scenic River System established to maintain the free flowing nature of Washington's rivers. You'll wander through a forest of moss-covered maple, cedar and fir, listening for wildlife and the sound of the river.
properties.title: Old Sauk River Trail

properties.description: Hike a loop around Anti-Aircraft Peak in the Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park. Hike past sites associated with coal and clay mining, and a former 1950s-era anti-aircraft missile installation. Enjoy good forest trails, some seasonal wildflowers, and a million-dollar view.
properties.title: Anti-Aircraft Peak Loop

properties.description: Mount Daniel is the highest peak in both King and Kittitas Counties, and at nearly 8000 feet, it’s a popular scramble. However, caution should be taken. Maintained trails end miles before reaching the summit. The remaining distance is broken into class 2 and 3 sections with significant exposure. Route finding skills, climbing etiquette, and possibly snow travel experience are required for a safe journey.
properties.title: Mount Daniel

properties.description: With two small lakes and numerous branching trails that sport views to Mount Baker and the Puget Sound, this moderate trail through shady forest can be hiked or backpacked year round. Trails circle both of these lakes, and on nice days you’ll find people out fishing or canoeing here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Pine and Cedar Lakes

properties.description: Discover a waterfall utopia with triple the falls and a wonderful place to put down your pack, enjoy some snacks and snap some incredible photos.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Lower Falls Creek Trail

properties.description: Enjoy the path-less-traveled as you ascend to Billy Goat Pass for spectacular views of the surrounding peaks. Connect to Burch Mountain or the Larch Creek trail as you walk through wildflowers as far as the eye can see.
properties.title: Billy Goat

properties.description: Mount Forgotten is an appealing target for the peculiarly determined hiker-turned-climber. Its sheer wall of a summit is very striking and easily instills visions of alpinism in those headed to Mount Forgotten Meadows, but the route takes a roundabout journey that requires not so much vertiginous daring-do as it does oodles of patience. The views from the top are spectacular, particularly the unobstructed view straight up Glacier Peak.
properties.title: Mount Forgotten

properties.description: No trip through Pend Oreille County is complete without a stop at the county park, easily accessible for year-round recreation just off Highway 2 and a popular camping spot during the summer months.
properties.title: Pend Oreille County Park

properties.description: This is a lightly used trail located at the end of the Twin Lakes Road. Finding solitude is not a problem on this seldom used trail. Check out this hike for a break from the crowds at Winchester Lookout and Twin Lakes.
properties.title: Silesia Creek

properties.description: This paved and graveled trail is a great option whether you’re looking for a weekend stroll or somewhere to condition for a race right in your neighborhood.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Vista Ridge Trail

properties.description: Acquired in four phases through Spokane County’s Conservation Futures Program, with additional funding secured through the Washington State Recreation and Conservation Office, the Antoine Peak Conservation Area offers fantastic views overlooking Liberty Lake, the Spokane Valley, and north to Mount Spokane and the Selkirk Range.
properties.title: Antoine Peak Conservation Area

properties.description: Hike to a stunning viewpoint high above two river valleys in the Goat Rocks Wilderness.
properties.title: Cispus Pass

properties.description: If you've been to Cama Beach and Camano Island State Parks, and you're looking for another diversion on Camano Island, consider Iverson Spit Waterfront Preserve. This delightful area offers some short hiking trails and, of course, ever present views of the Cascade Mountains and shoreline wandering.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Iverson Spit

properties.description: Located on the White River near Mount Rainier, the Mud Mountain Dam is both a flood control dam operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and a recreation facility. At about 3.5 miles from the trailhead, Scatter Creek makes the trail impassable.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mud Mountain Dam - River Trail

properties.description: A pleasant walk along the Middle Fork Snoqualmie, as well as a large field and wildflowers. Great for a short hike or picnic.
properties.title: Tanner Landing Park

properties.description: This is a classic Olympics river hike without the crowds, and it's downhill all the way to your destination.
properties.title: Slab Camp Creek and Gray Wolf River

properties.description: Do a short interpretive loop that passes a crashing creek as it heads to the ocean, gaze up at dizzyingly tall trees, and soak it all in – literally. The Quinault rainforest can average 140 inches of rain each year, so bring your gear – there will be plenty of puddles to splash in on this hike!
properties.title: Quinault Rainforest Nature Loop

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Paul Peak Snowshoe

properties.description: Great for kids, this park features a zip line, a boardwalk and several trails wending through a variety of environments. Some of them are even ADA-compliant, so they're wheelchair and stroller accessible.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Big Rock Park - North

properties.description: Ginkgo Petrified Forest State Park presents a unique look at Central Washington's shrub–steppe. The real experience comes from exploring its backcountry.
properties.title: Ginkgo Petrified Forest State Park Backcountry

properties.description: Gibbs Lake sits tucked away in the Northeast corner of the Olympic Peninsula. This county park comes complete with its namesake lake and an intersecting system of trails that are open to hikers, mountain bikers and horseback riders.
properties.title: Gibbs Lake

properties.description: With 6,000 feet of shoreline and an ADA accessible trail, visitors can travel along the coast and keep an eye out for the numerous species that fill the air.
properties.title: Bottle Beach State Park

properties.description: While it’s not quite as tall as nearby Mount Erie, Sugarloaf makes a great summit—this one doesn’t have a parking lot at the top.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Sugarloaf

properties.description: A 122 acre park near Gig Harbor, with trails that offer a wide range of difficulty, from flat, to 200 foot elevation gains.
properties.title: McCormick Forest Park

properties.description: Hikers flock to Mount Storm King for that signature shot, standing on a rocky outcropping above Lake Crescent. But it's a grind to get there, and the climb to the summit can be dangerous in bad weather. Luckily, there are several outcroppings about halfway to the top offering similar views. It's still a steep hike to get to them, but at least it's shorter.
properties.title: Mount Storm King

properties.description: The Nordic Center across from the White Pass Ski Area is a great alternative for those who don't want to zoom downhill. Take it a little slower and soak in the views by snowshoeing around a large lake rife with winter wildlife.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: White Pass Nordic Center

properties.description: It used to be possible to traverse from Ashland Lakes to Bald Mountain, Cutthroat Lakes, and the Walt Bailey trail on trail. Now, the way is an overgrown, hard-to-follow bushwhack.
properties.title: Bald Mountain via Ashland Lakes

properties.description: Hop aboard for an early-season wildflower bloom amid remote terrain and open air. At a healthy clip or a slow meander, this rail trail is fun at any speed!
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Klickitat Rail Trail

properties.description: This trail goes through old-growth timber and meadows, eventually ending at 2.4-acre Pass Lake. This nine-foot-deep lake offers fair fishing.
properties.title: Pass Lake

properties.description: The trail to Blythe and Chukar Lakes is short but also surprisingly entertaining. From beginning to end, the surrounding cliffs and distant vistas are spectacular to behold.
properties.title: Chukar Lake - Blythe Lake

properties.description: Just across the road from the parking area for Fishtrap Lake (just before Fishtrap Resort) is a short access road leading to trails on some shrub grassland, a dilapidated (but photogenic) homestead, and wetlands that provide sanctuary to a wide variety of waterfowl and other wildlife.
properties.title: Folsom Farm - Smick Meadows

properties.description: A rails-to-trails paved path connecting West Spokane to Queen Lucas Lake.
properties.title: Fish Lake Trail

properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Mount Leona

properties.description: An aptly-named alpine gem, Pear Lake nestles below Fortune Mountain and can be reached by combining the Top Lake Trail with a short jaunt north on the Pacific Crest Trail. It provides access and a jumping-off point for hikers, backpackers, equestrian riders and trail work parties alike headed into the backcountry of the Henry M. Jackson and Glacier Peak Wildernesses and beyond.
properties.title: Pear Lake

properties.description: The Northwest Timber Trail can be an easy first hike for young hikers, or it can be a pleasant stroll for experienced hikers when they have limited time. For many, this trail is a gateway to other routes that lead to more distant goals, such as the Silent Swamp Loop or the Preston Railroad Grade, or to forest roads that lead to the summit of East Tiger.
properties.title: Northwest Timber Trail

properties.description: Located just east of the Pasayten Wilderness and connecting to that trail system, Border Camp Trail is a short trail segment within the Loomis State Forest, which is managed by the Department of Natural Resources as a Natural Resources Conservation Area. Border Camp is among several trails on the looped trail system located on DNR land, so-named for a historic campsite that appears on the old USGS topo maps near Snowshoe Peak and the Canadian border.
properties.title: Border Camp Trail

properties.description: Visit one of the nation's largest public campgrounds and marvel at the geographic phenomenon that is the Clatsop Spit at Fort Stevens State Park. Learn about local history and embrace the rugged Oregon coast where the Columbia meets the Pacific.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Fort Stevens Clatsop Spit

properties.description: Located within the day use area of the popular Middle Fork Campground, a pleasant nature trail winds through a patch of forest adjacent to the Taylor River.
properties.title: Middle Fork Campground Nature Trail

properties.description: A short, but rough hike to two small lakes on the eastern slope of Mount Pilchuck. The first, Bear Lake is under a half mile from the trailhead on a good trail. Once on the way to Pinnacle, however, the trail changes to a rocky, rooty, muddy mess, slow going up, and slow coming down. The reward for putting up with this mess of a trail, is a nice quiet little lake ringed by rocks and trees, usually not crowded, even on a sunny Saturday.
properties.title: Pinnacle Lake

properties.description: A peak near Melakwa Lake on the north side of I-90. Climbing experience and route finding necessary to gain the summit.
properties.title: Kaleetan Peak

properties.description: A short rainforest loop from the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center in Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Hall of Mosses

properties.description: Take an amble through moss-laden forest and along churning waters in colors only the Olympic Peninsula can provide. For the most part, it’s ramble with moderate grade, but the last two and a half miles change character dramatically—giving you a steep, thigh-burning workout before rewarding you with views of Mount Mystery and Little Mystery just inside the park boundary.
properties.title: Heather Creek Trail via Upper Dungeness River

properties.description: Short stroll to a pretty cobble beach, plus a longer hike through mature forest.
properties.title: Murdock Beach and Majestic Trail

properties.description: A great trail for solitude and a cloudy winter day, this is a forest walk, complete with old growth giants, mature alder and a green understory of sword ferns. A tree huggers hike! This loop will give you a nice variety of forest ecosystems.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - Hoypus Point

properties.description: High, exposed ridgelines on this trail make this steep climb a difficult one, but it offers hikers commanding views of the wind facility as well as the Columbia Basin.
properties.title: Whiskey Dick Wildlife Area - Ridgeline Solar Trail
