properties.description: In logging's heyday, whistle punks were men tasked with operating the signal that let other loggers know a log had been hooked up and was ready to be moved. Using interpretive signage, this trail illustrates what was like to be on a logging show, from the crew, to the cook, to camp.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Whistle Punk Trail

properties.description: The route to Austera Peak involves exposed climbing and glacier travel. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Austera Peak

properties.description: If you are looking for heart-pumping elevation gain and solitude outside of the city of Chelan, Pot Peak is your trail.  Best hiked in the early hours due to exposure, this multi-use connector near Twenty-Five Mile Creek State Park rises above Lake Chelan on a climbing ridge walk with views of Stormy Mountain, the Chelan Valley and southern peaks of the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.
properties.title: Pot Peak

properties.description: In a state with so many places offering a day's walk to big, peaky views, Green Mountain still makes the short-list of Washington's all-time finest hikes. From woods to meadows to panoramic views and even a historic lookout, it just doesn't get much better than this.
properties.title: Green Mountain (Suiattle River)

properties.description: This short hike to a lake in the Boulder River Wilderness is a great trail for families.
properties.title: Kelcema Lake

properties.description: This small 9-acre beach park on Mercer Island has a swimming area and a small loop trail through the forest.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Clarke Beach Park

properties.description: Hike on the scenic Pacific Crest Trail through the Central Cascades as you pass through meadows, clear cut regrowth, and enjoy views of Mount Rainier.
properties.title: Tacoma Pass to Government Meadows

properties.description: Visit this gentle trail climbing through old lava flows, lodgepole pine trees, meadows of wildflowers and huckleberries with breathtaking views of Mount St. Helens. A creek at Lower Butte Camp offers a good opportunity for camping and plenty of day hike potential on to the Loowit Trail.
properties.title: Butte Camp

properties.description: You will see plenty in the first 7.2 miles of this trip that take you to the shores of Royal Lake, but you should plan your hike to have the time — and energy — to enjoy the wildflower-dotted alpine basin and its milky blue tarns in Upper Royal Basin about three-quarters of a mile past the lake.
properties.title: Royal Basin via Royal Lake

properties.description: Formerly the Frog Lake Trail, this area is breathtakingly scenic, compensating for the fact that there is no actual lake en route. Frog Lake dried up years ago, leaving a seasonal marsh that occupies a small basin below the trail's ultimate destination; a broad mesa with a 360 degree view of the surrounding scablands of the Columbia National Wildlife Refuge.
properties.title: Columbia National Wildlife Refuge - Rimrock Lake

properties.description: The route to the Picket Range is a Class 3 and involves exposed scrambling. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Picket Range

properties.description: Cypress Island Natural Resources Conservation Area (NRCA) is the largest relatively undeveloped island in the San Juan Islands and is home to over 5,200 acres of protected forests, wetlands, grasslands and tidelands.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Strawberry Bay and Reef Point

properties.description: Located just outside of the Wenatchee city limits, Jacobson Preserve is part of the just 3 percent of historic, undisturbed shrub-steppe in Washington. Here you'll find rabbitbrush, Sagebrush, Arrowhead balsamroot and  antelope bitterbrush, all main sources of food for muledeer. The area is so important, in fact, that it has been established as important habitat for the deer, and there are three monitoring points in the preserve to observe the shrub steppe as it is being reclaimed to native habitat.
properties.title: Jacobson Preserve

properties.description: Come visit this WTA-built trail, a nearly 2-mile hike through palustrine forest and wetlands, mostly flat with some rolling hills. Great for walkers, kids, and dogs.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Greenbrier Trail

properties.description: The Bellevue Botanical Garden (BBG) is a tranquil gem nestled in Wilburton Hill Park. The BBG’s winding pathways, elegant gardens and 150 foot suspension bridge provide hikers and families with a visual cornucopia and gentle refuge from the hustle and bustle of everyday life.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bellevue Botanical Garden

properties.description: This trail is an essential link for access to the west and central Pasayten wilderness. It allows hikers to avoid the steepest parts of the Buckskin Ridge Trail and the minimally maintained West Fork Pasayten Trail. Or, it can be part of a multi-day loop trip on any of the four major north-south trails: Pacific Crest Trail, West Fork Pasayten Trail, Buckskin Ridge Trail, and Robinson Creek (Middle Fork Pasayten) Trail.
properties.title: Whistler Cutoff

properties.description: Who doesn’t love a secret passageway? While the hordes gain Townsend from Quilcene side, sneak up on them from behind, then continue to Silver Lake for lovely camping and wandering opportunities.
properties.title: Mount Townsend - Silver Lakes Traverse

properties.description: Nestled against I-5, this neighborhood park boasts the title of oldest park in the Metro Parks Tacoma network.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: McKinley Park

properties.description: This 28-mile round trip offers the best of the Columbia Highlands as it passes through old-growth ponderosa pine stands, skirts five significant peaks in the Kettle Range, and showcases the effects of the White Mountain Fire of 1988.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: White Mountain via Kettle Crest Trail South

properties.description: Explore waterfalls, enjoy expansive views, and have a look at how forest rebounds from fires all along this lovely loop in the Columbia River Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Angel's Rest-Devil's Rest Loop

properties.description: North Star Mountain can be reached via scrambling from the Cloudy Pass trail.
properties.title: North Star Mountain

properties.description: This 0.75 miles accessible trail winds through the dunes, offering a pleasant path with many benches along the way to pause and enjoy the flora and fauna views.
properties.title: High Dune Trail

properties.description: Logging paid for most of the trails in the Cascades, so sometimes hikers must expect to hike the terrain that provided that rich stock of timber. This trail starts on an old logging road, leads through old clearcuts—now nicely regrown as lush berry meadows and forest stands—and enters lush old second-growth forest. It’s a great way to experience both the natural and human history of the area, while enjoying some remarkable wild country around a pristine alpine lake.
properties.title: Margaret Lake

properties.description: The route to Northwest Mox Peak is a Class 5 or above and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Northwest Mox Peak

properties.description: For those searching for alpine vistas with fewer visitors than on the most popular trails of the I-90 corridor, Greider Lakes is just right. This trailhead is located in the Sultan Basin Watershed.
properties.title: Greider Lakes

properties.description: Hike along one of the old railroad grades on Tiger Mountain, exploring the forests near Issaquah. Begin from the Hidden Forest Trail on the south side of Tiger Mountain.
properties.title: Fifteenmile Creek Railroad Grade

properties.description: Devil's Backbone is a multi-use trail for bikers and hikers.
properties.title: Devil's Backbone

properties.description: This little stopover off the road that encircles Mount Rainier is a wonderful, short leg-stretcher with gorgeous views of the dramatic canyon of the Muddy Fork of the Cowlitz River, and a short hike to a box canyon — an unusual feature in this park.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Box Canyon and Nickel Creek

properties.description: This trail starts out in Neppel Park in the City of Moses Lake and runs along the shore of the lake; it is paved and flat.
properties.title: Neppel Landing Trail

properties.description: "Loop Trail" may be a misnomer but this "Creekside" trail delivers. Even on the hottest Eastern Washington days, this trail delivers cool comfort.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Creekside Loop Trail

properties.description: Visit a majestic old-growth grove in eastern Washington! Just 14 miles north of Nordman, Idaho, is the Roosevelt Grove of Ancient Cedars, boasting some trees that are almost 3000 years old.
properties.title: Roosevelt Grove of Ancient Cedars

properties.description: Snowking Mountain is a strenuous mountaineering trip or class 3 alpine scramble with stunning panoramic mountain views, deep blue alpine lakes and rewarding isolation.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Snowking Mountain

properties.description: The Nathan Chapman Memorial Trail connects the Heritage Recreation Center to the South Hill Community Park via a wide paved trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Nathan Chapman Memorial Trail

properties.description: Most folks enjoy the view of Spiral Butte from afar, whether they're skiing downhill or cross-country at White Pass, or hiking along other trails in the area. But if you want to tackle this trail, it makes a good diversion for those camping at Dog Lake, or simply looking for a day hike in the area.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Spiral Butte

properties.description: Grand Ridge is the highest continuous trail in the Olympic Mountains. On a clear day it is among the most beautiful places in Washington; the 360 degree view includes the interior of the Olympics, the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Canada, and the Cascades.
properties.title: Grand Ridge

properties.description: The 1,000-acre Green River Natural Area is a wonderful gateway to the middle stretch of the Green River. Composed of steep valley walls and a broad valley floor, the natural area provides trails for hiking and horseback riding as well as access to the most dynamic reach of the Green River in King County.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Green River Natural Area

properties.description: Stairs are the attraction at Mercerdale. The main stairway here includes 302 wooden steps climbing from Bicentennial Park to 74th Place SE, and several other locations offer plenty of ways to get your heart rate up.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Mercerdale Hillside Park

properties.description: This short trail connects the Boulder De Roux and Paris Creek trails, and provides hikers a method to link together a much longer hike.
properties.title: South Fork Boulder Creek

properties.description: Start with a pleasant walk along Bridge & Slate Creeks and then earn your way to the high country with a climb up to the miles of sloping meadows, flowered in July.  Finish with a steep climb through the heather to larch fringed Copper Pass with its views to the east/west with scrambles to the north/south.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Copper Pass via Copper Creek

properties.description: Hike trails that form a loop in the Anacortes Community Forest Lands (ACFL.) If you already have been to Mount Erie and to Sugarloaf, this hike will take you to one - or optionally to both - of the other two named high points in the ACFL. These are Little Round Top and Sugar Cube. As a bonus, you also will visit a great viewpoint.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Little Round Top

properties.description: Well-maintained but secluded 2.3 mile loop through savannah and pine forest inside Lake Chelan State Park.
properties.title: Lake Chelan State Park - Little Bear Trail

properties.description: Access to Home Lake is possible via several trailheads, but any way you slice it, you're in for a long trip.
properties.title: Home Lake

properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: King Mountain

properties.description: Bear Lake snowshoe is a road walk along the Mountain Loop Highway ending with a short trail to the lake.
properties.title: Bear Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: When most of Washington’s alpine lakes are still snow-covered, Packwood Lake rewards hikers with a relaxing early-season hike ideal for dusting off your boots.
properties.title: Packwood Lake

properties.description: A trail that accesses Squak Mountain from the Trails Center in downtown Issaquah. Take the Squak Mountain Access Trail to access trails on the east side of the mountain: East Ridge, East Side, Phil's Creek, Old Griz, and more.
properties.title: Squak Mountain Access Trail

properties.description: Located just outside the city of Yakima, this arboretum showcases hundreds of different plant species through display gardens and themed areas.
properties.title: Yakima Area Arboretum and Botanical Garden

properties.description: This popular trail parallels a thunderous creek on a gentle grade, making for an excellent springtime river romp.
properties.title: Ingalls Creek

properties.description: The Maui Loop is more of an adventure than a hike. You get to go up, over and around mogul-like mounds peppered with volcanic rock, explore the upper rim of Coyote Wall, and descend a grassy slope with uninterrupted views of the Columbia River Gorge. In the spring there is a steady progression of wildflowers, making this an especially good early-season hike.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Coyote Wall - Moab/Maui Loop

properties.description: This level, paved trail on a former railroad grade offers a pleasant, accessible route alongside the tiny town of Wilson Creek in central Washington.
properties.title: Wilson Creek Cottontail Trail

properties.description: Hike a short stint on the Palouse to Cascades Trail, crossing high trestle bridges and roaming through the forest with expansive views of nearby peaks, just a short drive away from the city.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Homestead Valley to Mine Creek Trestle

properties.description: Some days are perfect for quiet contemplation, and an easygoing trail. Chirping birds, fragrant Ponderosa pines, and soft duff underfoot make this a perfect short, casual hike. In snow, it's steady climb will make it a moderate challenge in winter when showshoeing is in season.
properties.title: Clara and Marion Lakes

properties.description: A snowshoe along a road to the summit of a mountain in the Snoqualmie Pass area.
properties.title: Roaring Ridge Snowshoe via Road 9070

properties.description: This 2.5 mile long horseshoe trail is part of a nice 8-mile lollipop loop in the Yacolt Burn State Forest. Expect a shaded section of trail and to share the way with mountain bikers.
properties.title: Yacolt Burn State Forest - Sword Fern Trail

properties.description: The Whites Ridge trailhead is a forested hike with mountain views located in Ahtanum Forest. It is only open to hikers and equestrians from April 1 to November 30.
properties.title: Ahtanum State Forest - Whites Ridge

properties.description: This trail is a short one, just a few hundred feet from the parking area, but it takes you to one of the most easily-accessible, impressive giants of the west coast.
properties.title: Big Cedar Tree - Kalaloch

properties.description: Take a short but steep hike on a wide trail to visit two lakes in a beautiful craggy setting. It's only three miles to the upper lake, with 2,300 feet of elevation gain. In season find many wildflowers in the basin near the upper lake, and be alert for wildlife sightings.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Crystal Lakes

properties.description: This is an abandoned trail that heads south along Rainy Creek off of the downstream section of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trail up to Rainy Lake. The lake is popular among fishermen, since it is home to lots of trout, but be warned -- route-finding skills are a must on this trip.
properties.title: Rainy Lake

properties.description: A Rail-to-Trail conversion through the heart of the Spokane Valley, the Appleway Trail provides a non-motorized option for traveling through town.
properties.title: Appleway Trail

properties.description: This loop trail connects Spiritridge Park, Robbinswood Park and the Phantom Lake Loop and will take you through the Bellevue Airfield Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Spiritridge Trail

properties.description: This forested park in Bellingham was made possible by the Jensen Family’s generous donation of a public easement. The short, stroller-friendly loop trail includes a picnic table and parking area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Jensen Family Forest Park

properties.description: This trail takes you to Blowout Mountain through a forested area.  The views from the mountain are spectacular.
properties.title: Blowout Mountain

properties.description: A scramble up a peak above Gem Lake. Climbing gear and experience required.
properties.title: Wright Mountain

properties.description: Marymoor Park features a handful of trails to explore that offer chances to spot wildlife along the Sammamish River.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Marymoor Park

properties.description: The name of this trail may suggest this is horseback rider heaven, but it’s also great for hikers.
properties.title: Equestrian Loop

properties.description: This mile-long gentle climb in the Dark Divide brings you to the Boundary Trail, where you can turn left towards Badger Lake or right towards Mount St. Helens.
properties.title: Mosquito Meadows

properties.description: Visitors to the Hamma Hamma Campground will attest to the delightful Living Legacy Interpretive Trail. The 1.5 mile trail tells the story of the Civilian Conservation Corps through interpretive signs and photographs along the way.
properties.title: Living Legacy Interpretive Trail

properties.description: Cypress Island Natural Resources Conservation Area (NRCA) is the largest relatively undeveloped island in the San Juan Islands and is home to over 5,200 acres of protected forests, wetlands, grasslands and tidelands.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Eagle Cliff (Cypress Island)

properties.description: Phelps Creek Trail offers relatively easy access to the remote Glacier Peak Wilderness, particularly Spider Meadows and the larch-ridden Carne Mountain.
properties.title: Phelps Creek

properties.description: The Two Dollar Trail is one of three approaches to Fragrance Lake. It is popular with runners, bikers and hikers alike because of its good surface throughout. It traverses a west facing ridge through a forest of cedar, Douglas fir, hemlock, bigleaf maple and red maple with views out to the Salish Sea. The trail wanders through a groundcover of salal, Oregon grape and a variety of ferns and a small waterfall whose configuration changes with the seasons.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Two Dollar Trail

properties.description: A rewarding hike on an unmaintained trail takes you past peaks and across meadows to a stunning lake.
properties.title: Canyon Lake

properties.description: Follow a gentle path along the eastern portion of the Iron Goat Trail near Stevens Pass, once the original path of the Great Northern Railway. Visit the townsite of Wellington (later named Tye) known for the first Cascade Tunnel and as the site of one of the worst natural disasters in US history.
properties.title: Wellington Ghost Town

properties.description: A still-under-construction route along the north part of the Olympic Peninsula, the Olympic Discovery Trail (ODT) will eventually span nearly 130 miles and be usable by bikes, walkers, runners, strollers, and in some places, equestrians.
properties.title: Olympic Discovery Trail

properties.description: The short hike follows the river around the Newhalem Creek Campground on a mostly-level trail. The signs along the way denote the common trees and plants of the lush understory and tall trees surrounding the trail.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: To Know a Tree

properties.description: Don’t want to drive the very rough last 6 miles to the Iron Gate Trailhead? This mostly forested alternate approach adds 3 miles and 1000 feet elevation gain to the trip into Horseshoe Basin.
properties.title: Middle Fork (Toats Coulee)

properties.description: A short walk on a cobble beach with mudflats and shorebirds.
properties.title: Shine Tidelands State Park

properties.description: Great views of the entire Stuart Range on this scramble via the Beverly Turnpike trail.
properties.title: Teanaway Peak/Gene's Peak

properties.description: The Roaring Creek Trail connects the popular Mount Si and Mount Teneriffe Trails. This short trail through serene forests can be used to make a small loop with nearby trails such as Talus Loop Trail, or as a connector for a challenging day that includes both Mount Si Trail and Mount Teneriffe Trail.
properties.title: Roaring Creek

properties.description: The Lower Dungeness Trail travels through mostly conifer forests high above the river with a fair bit of elevation gain for a river hike.
properties.title: Lower Dungeness River

properties.description: Potato Hill is a summit just off from the Pacific Crest Trail in the Mount Adams Area. There is no trail to the summit, and the top marks the boundary to the Yakama Reservation.
properties.title: Potato Hill

properties.description: The short route to Crater Lake was originally constructed by miners and fishermen, and is NOT a well-maintained trail. However, the tread is well defined and generally easy to follow.
properties.title: Crater Lake

properties.description: Enjoy an easy walk (or a jog) around a small lake in a very green, open setting. If you have occasion to be in the Monroe area anyway, come by for a pre-lunch stroll. Or, Lake Tye can be a pleasant add-on if you stop in Monroe for a meal after a longer hike in the Stevens Pass area. Either way, relax and take in the vista of open fields and forested hills.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Tye

properties.description: Mystic Lake is a charming emerald tarn nestled in a subalpine basin along the Wonderland Trail. A scenic saddle separates it from Moraine Park, an expansive mountain meadow threaded with gurgling brooks under the dome of Mount Rainier. Getting there requires first hiking or biking the 5 miles of closed Carbon River Road and then hiking to the Carbon Glacier. This route is longer than starting at Sunrise, but backpackers will appreciate the numerous streams and forest shade.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Moraine Park - Mystic Lake

properties.description: This stunning Olympic coastal hike is one of the more photographed places in Washington for good reason.
properties.title: Shi Shi Beach and Point of the Arches

properties.description: Originally home to the Suquamish Indian tribe and legendary for being the supposed birthplace of Chief Sealth, over the years Blake Island has also served as a timber source, a private estate, Army base, and even a smuggler’s refuge. It now may be best known for Tillicum Village, a Native American cultural center that is currently closed.  Access to Blake Island State Park is only possible by personal watercraft.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Blake Island State Park

properties.description: There is a small network of trails at the south end of Lummi Island with lovely views to explore!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Aiston Preserve

properties.description: If you’ve been to Mount Rainier’s Paradise, you may be familiar with Narada Falls, and the short hike down to its popular viewpoint. But are you aware of the other trails this short hike connects to? Do you wonder what "Narada" means? Read on to find out.
properties.title: Narada Falls

properties.description: A mellow, flat forest hike between downtown Index and the North Fork Skykomish River park.
properties.title: Crescent Trail

properties.description: Named for a Puyallup-Klickitat tribal member who lived nearby, this park is a strip of green forest that sits between a residential neighborhood and an industrial area below.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Julia's Gulch Park

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Kangaroo Temple

properties.description: English Camp is the historical site of the Royal British Marines’ outpost established in the 1860’s. Part of a joint English-American occupation of San Juan Island while international water boundaries were decided, many of the buildings remain for visitors to explore. The gentle, family-friendly loop trail from English Camp to Bell Point offers hikers peaceful water views and pleasant bird watching.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Bell Point and English Camp

properties.description: A short walk through historic farmland turned wetland and forest just east of downtown Redmond.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Evans Creek Trail (Redmond)

properties.description: Peaceful is the best way to describe the Stewart Glen portion of the Burnt Bridge Creek Greenway. This hike begins at backwaters on the west end of Stewart Glen and follows the Burnt Bridge Creek upstream though thick woods, grassy bottom lands, and a meadow. You will be immediately immersed in the serenity of nature, making this the perfect break from city life.
properties.title: Burnt Bridge Creek - Stewart Glen Section

properties.description: This lightly used trail connects Robinson Pass and Slate Pass.
properties.title: Robinson Pass Loop

properties.description: Explore beautiful Turtleback Mountain Preserve and take in of the most breathtaking views on Orcas Island. Ship Peak, is a moderate loop full of views and a summit starting at the south end of the preserve.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Turtleback Mountain Preserve - Ship Peak Loop

properties.description: Short, easy hike with beautiful trees, goes up to a lake full of tadpoles/frogs. Foliage and spiderwebs can get in the way, so bring a stick.
properties.title: Frog Lake

properties.description: Start at one of the higher trailheads in the state (6560 feet) and follow the trail even higher. In early summer, if the thinner air doesn't take your breath away, the flowers and views will.
properties.title: Tiffany Mountain via Freezeout Ridge

properties.description: This is a nice two season hike on an old road with views of the Columbia River valley from Badger Mountain to Wenatchee. Enroute you may see spring flowers, unique rock formations, and animals like deer, coyotes, snakes and hawks.
properties.title: Swakane Canyon

properties.description: Crow Butte Park is located near Patterson, along the Columbia River. The park is operated by the Port of Benton, and it is possible to camp here as well as explore six miles of trail.
properties.title: Crow Butte Park

properties.description: Gravel roads, dirt tracks and game trails provide many options for hikers to enjoy the Revere Wildlife Area. This loop hike begins on an upland road, descends to Rock Creek and then returns via the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail.
properties.title: Revere Wildlife Area

properties.description: One of the most popular routes on Mount Rainier for its varied terrain, wide-open meadows, and incredible views, this 17-mile one-way hike along the mountain’s eastern side showcases the kind of scenery that will have you doing happy little dances of joy from one stunning panorama to the next.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Indian Bar - Summerland Traverse

properties.description: This wide well-maintained paved path is perfect for a quiet leisurely stroll or brisk run surrounded by greenery, without ever having to leave the city.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Milton Interurban Trail

properties.description: These mysterious mounds inspire imagination and speculation among visitors. With a half-mile ADA accessible path and another two miles of more rugged wandering, the Mima Mounds are a great destination for many hikers.
properties.title: Mima Mounds

properties.description: A popular summertime destination for many hikers and backpackers, Lake Valhalla also makes a rewarding advanced snowshoe route.
properties.title: Lake Valhalla Snowshoe

properties.description: A short interpretive trail on private land near the Hoh entrance of Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Land of Legends (Hoh Valley)

properties.description: This is a class A paved cycling and walking trail. It parallels the new North Spokane Corridor from the Little Spokane River to Hillyard. Eventually it will connect with the Centennial Trail. The trail will be extended as road construction continues.
properties.title: Children of the Sun

properties.description: Enjoy the easy, forested trail to Cranberry Lake - an extensive wetland created by energetic beavers - plus trails along the high bluffs with views out to Saratoga Passage and Whidbey Island. Optionally, explore a trail to the eastern edge of the park. To finish up, visit the Historic District and vintage beach cabins.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Cama Beach Historical State Park

properties.description: This last leg of the Pacific Crest Trail (or first depending on whether you're north- or southbound) offers breathtaking views as it passes along the eastern edge of the North Cascades and into the Pasayten Wilderness. Note that as of 2025, hikers are no longer allowed to cross the border into Canada.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) Section L - Rainy Pass to Manning Park

properties.description: The hike from the Cedar Falls trailhead to the junction with the Change Creek route is one through history. You will walk along a decommissioned railroad passing by the remnants of the line. Starting at the Cedar Falls trailhead, begin your hike just past the outhouse, crossing a paved road, and picking up the gravel path.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Cedar Falls to Change Creek

properties.description: A good short day hike with the best views on Taylor Mountain.
properties.title: Holder Knob

properties.description: A destination, or a location on a through-hike in the Teanaway area.
properties.title: Fortune Creek Pass

properties.description: The dominant feature in the North Cascades is Mount Baker, a glaciated volcano that can be seen on clear days from as far as Seattle and makes a great backdrop for photos of Vancouver, BC. Many hiking trails follow the ridges around Mount Baker and offer stunning views of the summit. Climbing to the summit is done mainly via the Coleman and Easton glaciers and requires technical expertise with high-altitude snow and ice.
properties.title: Mount Baker

properties.description: The trailhead for this section of the Palouse to Cascades Trail is found just south of Spokane and west of Tekoa.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Tekoa Trailhead

properties.description: A peak scramble on the southern end of Kangaroo Ridge. Climbing experience and equipment required.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Wallaby Peak

properties.description: A long, meandering snowshoe route just off the Mount Baker Highway.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Huckleberry Snowshoe Route

properties.description: Try this ridgeline hike on the Round Butte trail, featuring open meadows, excellent views of the surrounding canyons, and plenty of solitude.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Round Butte

properties.description: Take a gentle walk next to the White River in an old-growth forest.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: John Muir Discovery

properties.description: Explore one of the many trails in Capitol State Forest as an out-and-back, or combined with another trail in the area.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Mount Molly

properties.description: Cowen and Ravenna Parks form a contiguous urban nature area and green space, containing Ravenna Ravine and Ravenna Creek, in the middle of North Seattle. They contain 4.5 miles of trails that traverse a 0.75-mile stretch of Ravenna Ravine.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cowen and Ravenna Parks

properties.description: This rugged route is long, but there are many options along the way for side trips, stopping spots, and places to relax.
properties.title: Oval Lakes

properties.description: Ascend Squak Mountain via the most direct route available, the South Access Road, which still permits you to experience preserved mountain rainforest, wildflowers, mushrooms, and fauna, enjoying occasional glimpses of the surrounding mountains and lowlands. If desired, take a side excursion along one of the connector trails on Squak’s southern flank for a more intense nature experience.
properties.title: South Access Road

properties.description: This trail is no longer maintained by USFS.
properties.title: Marten Lake

properties.description: Hike steeply up a scenic and little-used trail to Red Top Lookout.
properties.title: Blue Creek

properties.description: Looking for a challenge in route finding, with the payoff of partially obscured views? Then this trail is for you.  What was once a popular non-motorized, multi-use trail was overrun by the 2006 Tripod Fire and the 2014 Carleton Complex Fire. Since the fires, a lack of maintenance and road washouts make access, route finding, and travel difficult.
properties.title: Pearrygin Creek

properties.description: This multi-use trail climbs from the Beaver Creek Valley along Lightning Creek to a road on a secondary ridge of Starvation Mountain. It passes through the areas affected by multiple fires, allowing the hiker to see the various types of recovering forest. In the upper third of the trail, there is a peek-a-boo view of peaks. In spring, there are flowers along the lower part of the trail, and in fall, there are young larches along the higher part.
properties.title: Lightning Creek

properties.description: A great exploratory hike to an old coal mining ghost town, with views of the underside of the Fairfax bridge.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Melmont Ghost Town

properties.description: Follow a loop trail around Oxbow Lake in the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River valley, where solitude intersects with calm lake waters, ever-present river murmurs of the Middle Fork, mountain views, and Snoqualmie rainforest. Depending on the season, fall colors, wildflowers, or fresh berries may be present for your enjoyment.
properties.title: Oxbow Loop Trail

properties.description: An easy, pleasant four-season ramble along the Dungeness River, good for bird watching.
properties.title: Dungeness River Dike Trail

properties.description: The Taneum Ridge Trail extends for 12.1 miles, starting at Forest Road 3300 and ending at the Manastash Ridge Trail. This trail is open to off road vehicles so you are likely to encounter dirt bikes and other motorized vehicles, depending when you go hiking here.
properties.title: Taneum Ridge

properties.description: This is a trail where the journey is as interesting as the destination. Enjoy a beautiful waterfall and views of icy Winthrop Glacier. Gaze directly at Mount Rainier and witness the fascinating destruction caused by the floods of 2006. All of this is chased by the peaceful basin of Mystic Lake and surrounding meadows.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Sunrise to Mystic Lake

properties.description: This hike in the Yakima River Canyon is an excellent conditioning hike for anyone looking to train in the winter months. It reaches one of the highest points on the east side of the river in the Canyon.
properties.title: Baldy Mountain

properties.description: This trail follows salmon-spawning Holder Creek before a short climb in the northern section of Taylor Mountain.
properties.title: Holder Creek

properties.description: Deadhorse Canyon forms most of Lakeridge Park. This deep, north-facing gorge provides sanctuary for wildlife and a quite place to walk-off your day or just to stretch your legs.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lakeridge Park

properties.description: High ridge traverse from Gold Hill Mine to North American Mine, connects East Creek to Canyon Creek.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Boulder Creek

properties.description: Popular with hikers, mountain bikers and off-road vehicle users, this multi use trail climbs out of the Lewis River Valley into the forested hills above.
properties.title: Wright Meadow

properties.description: This trail on Tiger Mountain offers an alternative to taking the service road on the last 0.6 mile to the East Tiger summit.
properties.title: Powerlink

properties.description: A short hike through history, the Ranger Hole trailhead features a ranger’s cabin built over 100 years ago, a short trail through a re-growing forest, and a walk down to the turquoise waters of the Duckabush River.
properties.title: Ranger Hole - Interrorem Nature Trail

properties.description: Take a side trip from Lake Caroline up to a saddle with gorgeous, sweeping views of the Alpine Lakes wilderness.
properties.title: Windy Pass

properties.description: If the long, rocky loop around the summit of Hamilton Mountain is too much, don't despair. There are alternative hikes in the area, and the trail to the twin cascades of Hardy and Rodney Falls is, hands down, the best option.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Hardy and Rodney Falls

properties.description: Take an urban hike with plenty of up-and-down as you follow the Tolt pipeline easement, a 12-mile corridor with wildflowers, berries, and occasional wildlife on a multi-use trail for equestrians, dog walkers, mountain bikers, joggers, and hikers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Tolt Pipeline Trail

properties.description: The Three Lakes Trail is a tour of some of Olympic's finest old growth forests, and is the traditional start of the much longer Queets-Quinault Skyline route. Starting in lowland rainforest, the trail works its way through exemplary stands of montane and then subalpine forests before finally breaking out into meadows dotted with tiny lakes. This is a truly wild and remote corner of the Olympics that leaves a lasting impression on the lucky hiker who experiences its beauty.
properties.title: Three Lakes

properties.description: This long day hike heads to an overlook visible from Walupt Lake, but you have to invest a few hours of uphill hiking to access it. But the climb is worth it; from the top, you get peek-a-book views of Mounts Adams, Rainier, and St. Helens, as well as the Goat Rocks, Walupt Lake, and the expansive green valley that is the Coleman Weedpatch.
properties.title: Coleman Weedpatch

properties.description: This trail leaves from a forest service road in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest south of Cle Elum and reaches the lake in under a mile. The trail is simple and straightforward and stays nearly level the entire way.
properties.title: Taneum Lake

properties.description: Drive a rough road to a short trail leading to extremely popular hot springs near Mount Baker.
properties.title: Baker Hot Springs

properties.description: Walk along a high ridge which connects to several other trails in the Manastash Ridge area, with views out to the Enchantment Range as well as Mount Daniel and Mount Hinman.
properties.title: Blazed Ridge

properties.description: A peak accessible off the Yellow Aster Butte trail, featuring a rock scramble at the end and 360-degree views north to Canada and south to Baker and Shuksan.
properties.title: Tomyhoi Peak

properties.description: What a workout! The Cable Line Trail on Tiger Mountain is not for the weak of heart, nor the weak of knees. A steep, slippery incline awaits you here, up to the summit of West Tiger 3.
properties.title: Cable Line Trail

properties.description: A rough, former roadbed connects the Tarbell Trail to the Silver Star trail, passing a notable fin of exposed rock in the Silver Star Recreation Area known as Sturgeon Rock. The trail is remote, so while it's just a bit more than a mile long, it's at least 3 miles to access the trail junction.
properties.title: Yacolt Burn State Forest - Sturgeon Rock Trail

properties.description: This small West Seattle park across the street from the shore has a small trail network, as well as a lawn with picnic tables.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Me-Kwa-Mooks Park

properties.description: On this hike you’ll drop down through the bluffs and walk along the last free-flowing stretch of the Columbia River, climb to a ridge walk with panoramic views, and perhaps visit a sandstone pillar.
properties.title: White Bluffs - South Slope

properties.description: Hike an urban park near Bellevue through extensive old-growth forest (yes, really)! Marvel at the many large conifers and deciduous trees. View a small creek in a steep canyon. Listen for, and perhaps see, abundant bird life. And, in season, note a few wildflowers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Weowna Park

properties.description: Bring the family for this easy hike at Heather Meadows. Two sparkling alpine lakes, an abundance of wildflowers, an impressive mountainous backdrop and a year-round snowfield make this a hike that will please everybody. What's more, this trail gets a fraction of the foot traffic that the trails at Artist Point get in late summer.
properties.title: Bagley Lakes

properties.description: The Monte Cristo Range just north of Willard offers quiet forest, and miles of solitary rambling. There are a myriad of ways to access this trail network, including this one, which starts in the middle of the mountains.
properties.title: Monte Carlo via Middle Fork Camp

properties.description: This West Seattle urban trail features a peat bog, public art, a salmon stream that runs through front yards, and a shopping center parking lot.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Longfellow Creek Legacy Trail

properties.description: Widely regarded as the crown jewel of hiking in Washington, the Enchantment Lakes are an alpine wonderland of pristine lakes set among polished granite, soaring peaks, blazing larches and ambling mountain goats.
properties.title: The Enchantments

properties.description: The astounding views from the summit of the Granite Mountain trail come at a price. A nearly-1000-feet-of-elevation-gain-per-mile price. But views of pointed Kaleetan Peak, deep blue Crystal Lake, the climber-dotted Tooth, and Mount Rainier dominating the skyline to the south make it all worth it.
properties.title: Granite Mountain

properties.description: This short trail serves as a connector to form loops of varying distances.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 132

properties.description: The hike up Young Hill is a San Juan Island classic. A moderate trail leading to surprisingly expansive views, and the short side trip to the English Camp cemetery offers a chance to observe unique natural and historical features.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Young Hill

properties.description: The Lake Christine trail begins on Forest Road 5920 and climbs briefly through a former logging show to the Glacier View wilderness. Offering access to the lovely little Lake Christine, it rambles through a conifer forest after passing through the cut.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Lake Christine

properties.description: Hike a series of short, nearly level trails that offer views of two lakes and of some swampy areas, and pass one of the largest trees in the Tigers. Appreciate the forest vegetation and wildflowers. Along the way, hear and perhaps see a variety of song birds and waterfowl.
properties.title: Tradition Lake Loop

properties.description: The Hemlock Trail is one of the many trails on Chuckanut Mountain, just south of Fairhaven. This is a main trail, with many alternate routes branching off to provide visitors with a variety of hiking options.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Hemlock Trail

properties.description: The Lower Wolf trails, adjacent to Newport, include some wide-open views of the Pend Oreille River valley. The trails are popular with hikers, mountain bikers, cross-country skiers, and snowshoers.
properties.title: Lower Wolf Trail

properties.description: A short trail on Tiger Mountain that makes up some of the Tiger Mountain Trail thru-hike.
properties.title: Middle Tiger

properties.description: Hike a varied, nearly-four-mile forest loop in the eastern part of the Anacortes Community Forest Lands (ACFL). Appreciate the variety of coniferous and deciduous trees of different sizes and ages. View a few wildflowers in season, and some fall colors later in the year.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Eastern Fringe Forest Loop

properties.description: Lower Tuscohatchie Lake is accessible from multiple different trailheads, offering hikers multiple hiking options for a great weekend getaway or long day hike.
properties.title: Lower Tuscohatchie Lake

properties.description: A boardwalk winds through a literal swamp tucked into the shoreline of Lake Washington. Several viewing spots make for excellent birdwatching.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Yesler Swamp

properties.description: This gentle 2.2 mile trail winds its way through the native shrubs and old growth conifers that surround the Jackson Park Golf Course. Only a short section of the mostly flat gravel trail is wheelchair accessible, and there are two short, steep climbs along the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Jackson Park

properties.description: This infrequently-maintained trail within Alpine Lakes Wilderness branches off the Chiwaukum Creek trail 10 miles in. It's possible to connect to the Icicle Ridge trail from here, provided you're willing to undertake some brushbashing.
properties.title: Index Creek

properties.description: If you don’t have the time or the inclination for the longer hike to Owyhigh Lakes, you can take a bite off the bigger trail and zip down about half a mile to see the charming 62-foot tiered falls of Deer Creek and a pair of footbridges traversing creeks flanked by a dense old forest.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Deer Creek Falls

properties.description: If you’ve been to Magnuson it is likely that you have walked a section of the trail on the way to a sporting event. However, it is well worth taking the time to explore all the meandering paths – less frequently known as Frog Pond Trail. If you have time to kill while your kid warms up before a game, or if you just want to sneak away for a moment of silence at halftime, these paths are perfect for a calming wander, no matter how much time you have.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Magnuson Park

properties.description: The route to Caroline Peak is a Class 3 and requires exposed scrambles. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Caroline Peak

properties.description: In a word, Tronsen Ridge is dynamic. It’s a place that evolves with each new season, showcasing the variance of Washington state as few trails can.
properties.title: Tronsen Ridge

properties.description: This park has something for everyone! There is a large, fully accessible shelter with picnic tables, BBQ, sink and electricity. In addition, pump track, playground, splash pad and exercise equipment are sure to provide some fun for all who visit Cordata Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Cordata Park

properties.description: This winter-only summit route is a straight shot from Bald Knob Campground to the summit of Mount Spokane.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Snowshoe Summit Route

properties.description: The Terrace Trail is part of the network of trails in the city of Newcastle. It connects the Highlands Loop Trail with the Crosstown Trail by starting low in a residential neighborhood and climbing via a series of switchbacks.
properties.title: Terrace Trail - Newcastle

properties.description: Hike along old logging roads to a 25-foot tall waterfall on Cherry Creek just outside of Duvall. Note that access to this area is part of an agreement with nearby homeowners, and part of the trail is on private land, so please remain on the main path, observe leash laws and keep noise to a minimum as a courtesy to homeowners along trail. There are no toilets at the trailhead. Plan ahead.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cherry Creek Falls

properties.description: This is a pleasant hike through sparse east-of-Snoqualmie pine forests. Once off trail, you will be ascending alpine meadows of kinnikinnick, heather, low blueberries until you reach the talus and rocky top of the peak.
properties.title: Hawkins Mountain

properties.description: Within walking distance of the Bainbridge Island ferry dock, this short loop hike follows Winslow Ravine.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: John Nelson Trail

properties.description: A multi-use county park with a short system of rambling trails through native rhododendron forest in central Whidbey Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Rhododendron Park

properties.description: Hug the shoreline for a lovely out-and-back trek along the undeveloped side of Bead Lake.
properties.title: Bead Lake

properties.description: Wander along shoreline and through a coastal forest to savor the Long Beach peninsula.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Bay Loop Trail

properties.description: A snowshoe route accessed from the Crow Creek Sno-Park.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Crow Creek Snowshoe

properties.description: This one-mile long rail trail in the City of Millwood, just east of Spokane.
properties.title: Millwood Interurban Trail

properties.description: The conservation area on the west slopes of Mica Peak afford visitors of all types a healthy workout close to the city of Spokane.
properties.title: Mica Peak

properties.description: A class 2 scramble to Mary's Peak in the Teanaway, featuring stunning views of the Stuart Range. Climbing experience recommended.
properties.title: Mary's Peak

properties.description: Waiting quietly on Maury Island (a peninsula just off Vashon Island), Dockton Forest welcomes walkers, bikers, and equestrians, as well as boaters to their 9 miles of trails and shorefront property.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Dockton Forest

properties.description: A forest walk near the boat launch for Lake Roosevelt.
properties.title: Lake Roosevelt National Recreation Area - Bradbury Beach Forest Walk

properties.description: It’s possible to reach the lookout on top of Thorp Mountain four different ways. But this route offers a nice detour to a little lake, where you can have a snack and size up your objective before continuing on your way.
properties.title: Thorp Mountain Lookout via Thorp Creek

properties.description: On this short trail, admire the Columbia River view and in season, catch soaring turkey vultures around the cliffside, enjoy blooming wildflowers or, on clear days, spot Mount Hood in the distance.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Raptor Trail

properties.description: The valley that Snowall Creek runs through is laden with amazing meadows of wildflowers, great views of the peaks surrounding it and tons of wildlife. It's part of a loop that you
properties.title: Snowall Cradle Lake

properties.description: The lookout is gone, but the stunning views remain. To the north is Mount Rainier with a turquoise tarn and rugged rock ridges in the foreground. A clear day reveals three other volcanos to the south and west.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Tatoosh Lookout

properties.description: Linking the cities of Yelm and Tenino, this paved trail offers a delightful jaunt through a greenspace just east of Olympia.
properties.title: Yelm-Tenino Trail

properties.description: A lake located above the extremely popular Snow Lake; Upper Wildcat offers backpacking opportunities for the route-finding enthusiasts in the summer months.
properties.title: Upper Wildcat Lake

properties.description: This is a multi-use trail in a multi-use area.  Activities include hiking and riding horses, mountain bikes, motorcycles, along with cattle grazing. The trail follows the West Fork Salmon Creek through a recovering forest burn and climbs the steep meadows of the headwaters to a pass with views to the east and options for ridge hiking to the north or south. In mid-summer the meadows are full of wildflowers.
properties.title: Golden Stairway

properties.description: This is a short hike into a tree-filled gorge.  Views include a waterfall, Elbo Creek, and the Quilcene River.
properties.title: Rainbow Canyon

properties.description: Take the Wynoochee Pass trail over Wynoochee Pass onto the Sundown Lake trail, where you can continue past Sundown Pass to beautiful Sundown Lake.
properties.title: Wynoochee Pass to Sundown Lake

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Hidden Lake Spur - Palisades

properties.description: Hike through beautiful woods, subalpine meadows and glacial moraines to the Hellroaring Viewpoint. The trail then becomes poorly defined up to Sunrise Camp.
properties.title: Mountain Climbers Trail

properties.description: The West Fork Agnes Creek trail used to head west from Fivemile Camp on the Pacific Crest Trail (also known here as the South Fork Agnes Creek Trail).  The West Fork Agnes Creek trail is now all but vanished. Navigating it is a rough bushwhack along the West Fork of Agnes Creek, with no destination except the base of 8115-foot Agnes Mountain.
properties.title: West Fork Agnes Creek

properties.description: Moran State Park might have mountains and lakes, but Obstruction Pass has quiet, open forest, secluded campgrounds, and the largest public beach on Orcas Island. Take a quiet walk here and soak in the peaceful shoreline.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Obstruction Pass State Park

properties.description: Explore the upland forest areas and hiking trails with interpretive signs at the 73.37-acre Kirkland Watershed Park.  There are a few hiking options to choose from Check out the Cochran Springs Creek trail or take a hike to the old reservoir. From the reservoir near the top of the park, there are two more loop options to explore.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Kirkland Watershed Park

properties.description: It is possible to drive all the way to the top of Tyee Ridge for majestic views of the land below. But the last 4 miles of the road to the top is extremely rough, so visitors can make that section a short hike with fabulous views.
properties.title: Tyee Lookout

properties.description: Families will enjoy this small community park in the city of Woodinville. Take a walk in the woods along a half-mile boardwalk loop trail or blow off some steam on the playground pr climbing boulder.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Rotary Community Park (Woodinville)

properties.description: Preston Creek Road is a relaxing snowshoe along Forest Service Road 5501, accessible directly off Entiat River Road. The path is easy to follow and features several amazing viewpoints. Less than a mile from the trailhead (0.75 miles to be precise), views of the Entait Valley open up, and as you continue up 1.5 miles, Baldy Mountain comes into view. The modest elevation gain is quite gradual, and while you can usually hear the traffic from the Entiat River Road, the noise is minimal.
properties.title: Preston Creek Road Snowshoe

properties.description: The Snow Lakes trail is known mostly as the long, gradual way into the Enchantments; but it is a worthwhile - if deceptively grueling - destination in its own right. The narrow isthmus between the lakes offers a majestic view across the water to the towering heights of McClellan Peak.
properties.title: Snow Lakes

properties.description: Hiking to Twin Sisters Rock is the definition of a leg-stretcher. At one mile round trip, it is the perfect way to get a little more than a couple minutes out of the car, but less commitment than a day hike requires.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Twin Sisters Rock

properties.description: Hike a short but steep trail with many stone steps. Pause at a viewpoint offering a fine view of Mount Rainier, then continue on to Poo Poo Point itself, only 1.9 miles from the trailhead. Enjoy views to the northwest, and perhaps watch paragliders sailing off into the sky.
properties.title: Poo Poo Point - Chirico Trail

properties.description: Three Peaks is a ridgeline trail that takes hikers into the edges of the Goat Rock Wilderness. Hike it in a day, or use it as a starting point for a number of backpacking options.
properties.title: Three Peaks and Mosquito Lake

properties.description: Located on the White River near Mount Rainier, the Mud Mountain Dam is both a flood control dam operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and a recreation facility. The Vista Trail is short but steep.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mud Mountain Dam – Vista Trail

properties.description: This is a 1.2-mile loop trail that takes hikers on a tour of the structure the Army Corps of Engineers built to keep sediment from Mount St. Helens from washing down the Toutle River and inundating the communities downstream.
properties.title: Toutle River Sediment Retention Structure Trail

properties.description: Hike to a pair of beautiful lakes. Haloed by larch on the steep, rocky slopes above, once here, you'll see the reason this area is called the Golden Lakes.
properties.title: Crater Lakes

properties.description: The route to Change Peak is not an official Forest Service trail. The route is not maintained and requires route-finding skills to navigate.
properties.title: Change Peak

properties.description: This area of the Willapa National Wildlife Refuge is no longer open to hikers.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Bear River

properties.description: The Shellrock Pass trail has not been maintained for 25 years. However, the way is relatively easy to follow if you have a map and are familiar with cross-country travel.
properties.title: Shellrock Pass

properties.description: The Cougar Trails network contains six miles of moderately trafficked trails on the WSU Vancouver campus. Encompassing a river, a disc golf field, and quiet forested areas, this network is good for all skill levels.
properties.title: Cougar Trails

properties.description: A short detour off Highway 2 east of Stevens Pass will lead you a montane masterpiece tucked in the foothills of the Central Cascades. Gentle meandering hiking trails along the 489-acre state park offer scenic views of Nason Ridge, Dirty Face Mountain and the iconic Emerald Island.
properties.title: Lake Wenatchee State Park

properties.description: Come hike the headwaters of the Bear Creek watershed in this close in Snohomish County Park near Woodinville. Here you will find a mature second growth forest, a wetland that plays a vital role in the health of this salmon stream plus a network of trails for any fitness level.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Paradise Valley Conservation Area

properties.description: Accessible only at low-tide, this trail (called the North Tidal Area Trail on the Dosewallips State Park map) is a short, gravelled trail that meanders along the north end of the beach at the state park.  While this trail is quite short, and only accessible during a limited time, there are 10 total miles of trail in the state park, found across Highway 101 and departing from the camping area. If you want a longer hike, try the Steam Donkey or the Maple Valley trail.
properties.title: Dosewallips State Park - Beach Trail

properties.description: This trail has easy access, is relatively flat and is only 3.6 miles round trip. The payoff is a broad and picturesque curtain of water, dropping 109 feet over a basalt ledge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Tamanawas Falls

properties.description: The Cougar Pass Trail is a short connector in the northern part of Cougar Mountain Regional Park. It links the Klondike Swamp trail at its western end to Tibbett’s Marsh Trail at its eastern end.
properties.title: Cougar Pass

properties.description: Nestled in the City of Yelm, Cochrane Memorial Park offers quiet paths, a catch and release fishing pond, a covered picnic area and an educational interpretive center.
properties.title: Cochrane Memorial Park

properties.description: Hike along a raucous waterway to a gorgeous alpine meadow with hiker and stock camps available. It's the perfect basecamp for multi-night adventures.
properties.title: Chiwaukum Creek

properties.description: If you just need some quiet time in nature and are not looking for a big workout, this little walk will be perfect. There is good access to the Snohomish River where you can find a place to throw a line in the water plus some good birding opportunities near the small lakes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bob Heirman Wildlife Preserve

properties.description: Hike along a steep-sided ravine with some highly eroded banks. Enjoy the deciduous forest with a few large trees, and appreciate the moss and ferns along the creek. There's also an option to extend your hike to include the historic district of Des Moines Beach Park, and stroll out onto the Des Moines Public Fishing Pier for the view.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Des Moines Creek Trail

properties.description: A little-known, yet spectacular waterfall, Denman Falls offers a relatively easy hike to it, if you can bear the 7.25 mile approach.
properties.title: Denman Falls

properties.description: Smooth Ridge offers incredible views into the rugged heart of the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Smooth Ridge

properties.description: This route is in the Teanaway / 29 Pines Staging Area Groomed Trail System. The long and mostly flat road can be used for snowshoeing, snowmobiling and cross-country skiing when weather permits.
properties.title: Jack Creek Snowshoe

properties.description: A climb near Granite Mountain on the I-90 corridor. In winter, high avalanche danger exists on this route. Have gear and expertise navigating in snowy conditions before you go.
properties.title: West Granite Mountain

properties.description: Witness up close one of the most frequently viewed public artworks in the state of Washington, while admiring a broad view of the Columbia River and the tiny hamlet of Vantage.
properties.title: Wild Horses Monument

properties.description: Spectacular views into Alpine Lakes Wilderness, from the Teanaway backcountry and The Enchantments to the east, Mount Daniel and surrounding peaks to the north, to Snoqualmie mountain ranges to the west. As always, Mount Rainier solemnly guarding the south as always.
properties.title: Red Mountain Snowshoe

properties.description: This is a nice woods trail, but views don't reward the hiker until she or he arrives at Stevens Canyon Road in Mount Rainier National Park. Trail starts alongside a grassy rock slab and works its way to the top of the ridge.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Backbone Ridge

properties.description: A short access trail to a stretch of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie.
properties.title: Granite Creek Flats Natural Area

properties.description: Also known as the portal to the popular Dungeness Spit, there are many equestrian and hiker friendly trails here. Situated on the bluff above the Strait of Juan De Fuca, this area boasts 67 campsites in addition to the scenic, mile-long bluff trail and excellent birdwatching.
properties.title: Dungeness Recreation Area

properties.description: The Lower Pete's Creek trail starts on the same side of the road as the parking area and privy. The Pete’s Creek trail to Colonel Bob is on the opposite side of the road, just behind the “Pete’s Creek Trail” sign. They’re easy to tell apart because Lower Pete's Creek starts flat, and the Pete's Creek trail to Colonel Bob begins climbing right away.
properties.title: Lower Pete's Creek

properties.description: A boat ride up Lake Chelan to a summer camp, then a long hike to beautiful remote lakes east of Glacier Peak.
properties.title: Lyman Lakes

properties.description: Former lookout sites are ideal for views, and Strawberry Mountain is right up there with the best of them. See peaks in two states, the blast zone of an active volcano, and a few sapphire lakes set into the dramatic landscape. That is, of course, if you can bear the drive to get there.
properties.title: Strawberry Mountain

properties.description: Formerly a trail that bordered Lake Mills, the West Lake Mills trail winds through the second-growth forest along the now free-flowing Elwha River.
properties.title: West Lake Mills

properties.description: Hike a well-built trail to a beautiful, quiet, forested lake at the edge of the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
properties.title: Thompson Lake via Granite Creek Trail

properties.description: This is a King County regional trail that winds through the Redmond Ridge neighborhood, offering travellers a non-motorized alternative for getting around.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redmond Ridge Trail

properties.description: View the South Cascades peaks in all directions from this loop hike across a craggy summit of Indian Heaven's spine.
properties.title: Sawtooth

properties.description: Miles of riverside rambling, alpine wandering, a beautiful lonely lake, and high desert hiking, as well as all the planning and logistics that goes into a long-distance hike – this will satisfy your thruhiking cravings (at least for a month or so).
properties.title: Middle Fork to Salmon La Sac Traverse

properties.description: The relatively flat hike to this long, shallow lake makes an excellent destination for families with children or an easy overnight camping trip.
properties.title: Hyas Lake

properties.description: Tolt-MacDonald Park is an outdoor recreation treasure for all King County residents! With 12 miles of forested and riverside trails, this is a favorite mountain biking and hiking destination. The backcountry area of the park is located on the west side of the Snoqualmie River across the suspension bridge.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Tolt-MacDonald Park

properties.description: The trail up Little Bald Mountain follows the edge of a a northwest-facing rim rock cliff that melts out a month or so earlier than areas farther west. It's the perfect answer for those looking for an early season high country fix and often has wildflowers blooming when, or even before, Chinook pass opens.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Little Bald Mountain

properties.description: A trail that leads into the William O. Douglas wilderness, Richmond Mine offers miles of rugged rambling through a remote part of the state.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Richmond Mine

properties.description: Lacamas Park is a surprising swatch of forest between Camas and Washougal where you can easily take time out to relax and enjoy nature. The park has over six miles of trails, with both wide-hard surfaced paths and more primitive dirt tracks. This loop hike combines both types to give you the optimum experience while exploring a lake, creek, and two waterfalls. There is also an optional side trip to visit the Lily Fields, which are infused with purple camas blossoms from mid-April to mid-May. Although there are some heart-thumping uphill sections, the hike is generally easy and appropriate for reasonably fit people of all ages.
properties.title: Lacamas Park - Round Lake to Lower Falls

properties.description: This popular summer trail offers wildflower-filled meadows, a glistening alpine lake, big mountain views and wildlife sighting aplenty.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Summit Lake

properties.description: With four miles of beach walking and water on three sides, Damon Point is one of the best places to hike and view wildlife in the North Beach area of Washington's Pacific Coast.
properties.title: Damon Point

properties.description: A very challenging hike to a lookout in the Mountain Loop Area. Hike a road, then along a trail to gorgeous Goat Flats. From there, the route kicks up in difficulty as it accesses Tin Can Gap. The final push, up ladders rebarred into rock is exposed, and surefootedness is an absolute must at the lookout.
properties.title: Three Fingers

properties.description: While the hunting grounds here hold their fair share of human history, the Kautz Creek drainage that holds the trail leading to the hunting grounds has an even more extensive background — one that's eons old, rather than generations. Witness the way volcanic activity has affected this area and appreciate the awesome power of Rainier up close.
properties.title: Kautz Creek to Indian Henry's Hunting Ground

properties.description: On this hike you’ll walk a long string of sand dunes or explore the nooks and crannies of a recent landslide, all beside the last free-flowing stretch of the Columbia River with panoramic views up and down the river, north to the Saddle Mountains, and across the Hanford Nuclear Site to the distant Cascade Mountains.
properties.title: White Bluffs - Central Slope

properties.description: The South Fork Hoh Trail penetrates a wild and remote wilderness and offers hikers solitude just a short distance from the crowded main Hoh Rain Forest. The easy trail stays in the bottomland among groves of towering spruce and grassy maple glades.
properties.title: South Fork Hoh River - Big Flat

properties.description: A clear, sparkling lake, up-close views of Mount Rainier, and a historic fire lookout await you on the short but steep Gobblers Knob Trail. This route is an eastern approach to the lookout via Westside Road.
properties.title: Gobblers Knob

properties.description: The Snider Ridge Trail is part of a trail network that runs along the ridge just north of Highway 101 and east of Lake Crescent. Two trailheads access the trail: the Kloshe Nantich trailhead on the west, and the Mount Muller trailhead on the east.
properties.title: Snider Ridge

properties.description: Located in the Dungeness River recreational area, this hidden gem provides miles of pleasant hiking, and the scenery is delightful the whole way. And with nearly 15 miles of steep hiking, this also makes a great training hike as well.
properties.title: Gold Creek

properties.description: Enjoy a stroll on the main loop trail that goes around Lake Padden or lengthen your trip by exploring some of the short trails at the east end of the park. To find a little solitude take a turn off the beaten path to rise above the south side of the lake on a less-trodden upper trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lake Padden Park

properties.description: The drive to Mount St. Helens’ Windy Ridge is spectacular! From this east side of the mountain, the summit is close — more so than from the Johnston Observatory side. And it is quiet; on a busy weekend, you can often find the parking lot less than half full.
properties.title: Windy Ridge Trail

properties.description: This gorgeous loop hike has it all: big views of Mounts Baker and Shuksan, as well as the North Cascades, alpine lakes for swimming, and well-maintained trail winding through meadows and heather. And with wildflowers in spring, blueberry bushes for trail-side snacking in late summer and blazing color in the fall, you can't pick a bad season to visit.
properties.title: Chain Lakes Loop

properties.description: This 20-mile section of the longer 93-mile Wonderland Trail covers the northern section of the loop from Mowich to Sunrise, utilizing the Spray Park alternate.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Wonderland Trail - Mowich Lake to Sunrise via Spray Park

properties.description: This 10-mile motorcycle trail has an interesting section for hikers, a steep 1.2 mile climb that provides access to the east end of the Foggy Dew Ridge Trail, with its remote feel.
properties.title: Pasayten Drive

properties.description: Walk through an old burn with views of the Wallowas and the Blue Mountains.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Melton Creek Trail

properties.description: Old logging roads wend through forest and an abandoned golf course, passing several ponds.
properties.title: Timberton Loop

properties.description: This hike is in a minimally-developed park in the City of Shoreline, north of Seattle. It offers steep hillsides and some fine mixed forest. Trails descend into the park from both a northern and a southern trailhead, with the northern trail being longer.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Innis Arden Reserve Park

properties.description: This long but easy valley romp follows boisterous Phelps Creek to a mile-long broad flower-bursting meadow and a giant cirque beneath a formidable wall of towering peaks. But don't expect solitude, for Spider Meadow crawls with backpackers-brigades of them! The valley is large enough to disperse in, though, and Phelps Basin offers a quiet retreat from the meadow's loungers and shutterbugs and their tent cities.
properties.title: Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin

properties.description: Take one of three trails available from Antoine Peak's newest trailhead.
properties.title: Antoine Peak Conservation Area - Arrowleaf Trail

properties.description: Easton Ridge is a hiker’s friend. Located on the east side of Cascades, hikers will often find drier weather here than on the west side, and with a relatively low peak elevation (4462 feet), snow melts out earlier than other nearby summits at higher elevation.
properties.title: Easton Ridge

properties.description: Washington Park sits at the northwestern tip of Anacortes. When viewed from the sea the area is referred to as Fidalgo Head. The terrain varies from rain forest on the north to open, stony hillsides with few trees on the south.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Washington Park

properties.description: Open to both hikers and mountain bikers, this trail connects Gateway Park to the east end of the nearby 360 Trails park. Walk beneath the shade of the towering green trees that line the trail.
properties.title: East Wing Trail

properties.description: Named for a Duwamish chief who led a village on Lake Union, this six-mile, mostly-paved urban loop connects pocket parks and multi-use paths around Lake Union in Seattle.  If you don't stop for a bite to eat in one of the neighborhoods along the way, Gasworks Park (on the north side of the loop) and Lake Union Park (on the south side) both make great picnic spots with lake views.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cheshiahud Lake Union Loop

properties.description: For confident hikers willing to put in the work for a shortcut to stunning views, Dean Creek trail leading to Bunker Hill is a good option.
properties.title: Dean Creek

properties.description: This beach walk demonstrates the successful rehabilitation of a former dumpsite into a popular hiking destination, with views of the Strait of San Juan de Fuca and ample opportunities for wildlife viewing.
properties.title: North Beach County Park to McCurdy Point
