properties.description: This trail climbs from the Trapper Creek trailhead through an old-growth forest to views of the many mountains of the South Cascades from Observation Peak.
properties.title: Trapper Creek

properties.description: Prince Creek is the starting point for hikers tackling the full Lakeshore Trail, a popular spring backpacking trip. This trail is free from winter snow earlier than many thanks to its low elevation, and because of that, it can get quite full in the early season. Consider starting your hike midweek if you prefer to hike in solitude.
properties.title: Prince Creek

properties.description: Enjoy excellent river access and picnic opportunities on this short, flat and easy loop trail.
properties.title: Mine Creek

properties.description: Here's an unusual hike through a very mossy forest and along a narrow river canyon, past sites that were important in local history. A railroad once ran along the canyon, passing through small communities. Logging was done in the area, and lime once was produced from limestone here, in a kiln that still stands. The railroad and communities are gone now, and much has disappeared over the past eighty years. But a few artifacts still remain and can be seen near the trail.
properties.title: Lime Kiln Trail

properties.description: This short trail is located near Coldwater Lake and connects visitors to the Science and Learning Center at Coldwater to the Lakes Trail and the Mount Margaret backcountry.
properties.title: Elk Bench

properties.description: Follow well-signed but sometimes rough trails to a great viewpoint near the water's edge at Porpoise Point. Enjoy views of distant islands, and on a clear day of the distant Olympic Mountains. Sightings of seals, eagles, waterfowl, and sometimes otters are likely.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Sharpe Park - Montgomery - Duban Headlands

properties.description: This is a lovely trail year-round. If you don’t live in the area, it makes an excellent quick stop if you’re in the vicinity of the Hood Canal Bridge.
properties.title: Ludlow Falls Interpretive Trail

properties.description: This pleasant trail offers an almost level walk to a grassy forested lake set in the rocky basin beneath Cutthroat Peak. This is an easy hike in an area of rugged, steep country and one of the few that are suitable for small children. It is an especially pretty hike in the fall when the larch are turning golden.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cutthroat Lake

properties.description: Just outside of Sequim sits Sequim Bay State Park, where visitors can take in beautiful views of Sequim Bay and easily access the 126-mile Olympic Discovery Trail.
properties.title: Sequim Bay State Park

properties.description: The Coal Mines trail is a mellow hike from Cle Elum, through Roslyn and onto Ronald with views of many different coal mining remains. This trail is great for hiking, biking, horseback riding and running.
properties.title: Coal Mines Trail

properties.description: A paved urban trail running from Montlake, across the new 520 bridge and through several eastside communities with excellent views of Union Bay, Foster Island wetlands and Lake Washington.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: 520 Trail

properties.description: Granite Creek courses through the gorge between Mailbox Peak and Russian Butte. Ascend through the creek’s ravine, immersed in mountain rainforest, alongside whitewater rapids, waterfalls, wildflowers and mushrooms, while you take in majestic views of the mountains of the Middle Fork Valley. Seasonal treats include berries and fall colors.
properties.title: Granite Creek Trail to Granite Lakes

properties.description: This 8.2-mile trail from the center of Ilwaco along Long Beach provides a nice outing for those wanting to experience the area on foot. The route takes you through forested hills and features nice views of the ocean from the Beard's Hollow Overlook, and then beach and dune walking to the town of Long Beach.
properties.title: Lewis and Clark Discovery Trail

properties.description: This creek trail takes hikers high above the creek itself and to a nice overlook near the terminus, where adventurers can extend their hike further along the Middle Fork Teanaway or Elsnor Mine trails.
properties.title: Paris Creek

properties.description: Local, national and world histories intersect on this peaceful farm north of Arlington.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: North Centennial Trail (Snohomish)

properties.description: Baldy is a windswept mountain outpost that commands a view over the northeast Olympic Mountains, Vancouver Island, and the Strait of Juan de Fuca. To reach its lofty summit, the hiker must trade traditional grade for a seemingly never-ending staircase. However, your efforts are greatly rewarded, as views can be had along the ridge. And even if the summit itself is lost in the clouds, dwarf flowers and lichens decorate a foreground to the icy blue Olympic high country.
properties.title: Baldy

properties.description: Hike through a pastoral area first settled and farmed in the 1880s. Along the way, enjoy a dense grove of cedars, followed by close-up views of blueberry fields that still produce an annual crop. Circle Larsen Lake, and view a restored pioneer home. Optionally, extend your hike to view nearby Phantom Lake.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Hills Greenbelt

properties.description: Day hikers and backpackers alike visit Lake Dorothy; some continue on to Bear and Deer Lakes. The hike used to be shorter but a washout on the road has resulted in an extra few miles each way.
properties.title: Lake Dorothy - Lake Bear - Lake Deer

properties.description: The Pika Trail is a scenic winter non-motorized connector trail between Swift Trail 244 and June Lake Trail 216B.
properties.title: Pika Trail Snowshoe Loop

properties.description: This middle section of the Toutle Trail starts at Forest Road 81 on the north side of Red Rock Pass.
properties.title: Toutle Trail - Red Rock Pass to Blue Lake Trailhead

properties.description: Access the Owyhigh Lakes Trail via Deer Creek Falls on this slightly longer hike than the one from the Sunrise Road. This trailhead is marked on the right of southbound Highway 123, across the street from the parking area. Quickly cross the road (watch for traffic, it’s a busy road on a blind corner) to the marker and you will finally see the trailhead, which is mostly invisible from the road due to brush and low hanging tree branches.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Deer Creek Falls to Owyhigh Lakes

properties.description: Located approximately eleven miles down the Middle Fork Road, this gently meandering half-mile loop trail, built following Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards, provides scenic views of the congressionally-designated Wild and Scenic Middle Fork Snoqualmie River.
properties.title: Camp Brown

properties.description: A segment of the cross-state Palouse to Cascades Trail
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - Easton

properties.description: Walk through a rocky, desert landscape with expansive views of the Columbia River. These trails are short and well built with rock steps for stable footing. This loop trail system may be started at either the Chelan Hatchery or at the loop’s top just off Highway 150 on the way into Chelan.
properties.title: Beebe Springs Wildlife Area - Cultus Jim and Chelan Bob Loop

properties.description: A small network of trails connects the neighborhoods of South Cliff and DuBois across Blandford Road in Vancouver. Visit both parks, but do know you’ll have to cross a road to get the full experience.
properties.title: Blandford Canyon

properties.description: A Sno-Park opened in 2021 consisting of an open space for families to play in the snow.
properties.title: Easton Reload Sno-Park

properties.description: Mount Si via the back way. Begin from the large Mount Teneriffe parking are and add on some miles to sneak up this popular peak from behind.
properties.title: Mount Si via Mount Teneriffe Trail

properties.description: Hike through a riparian area on a gently rolling double-track before arriving at an expansive prairie with big skies, swooping birds and native vegetation.
properties.title: West Rocky Prairie Wildlife Area

properties.description: Wonder past streams, a deep canyon and old-growth trees on the Big Creek Trail. Located in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, this narrow, rocky trail provides a challenge for adventurous hikers.
properties.title: Big Creek Trail

properties.description: With several miles of wooded trails, a self-guided nature tour plus hill climb and orienteering courses, Forest Park gives you plenty of reasons to get outdoors without leaving the city.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Forest Park - Everett

properties.description: Hike to an old mining town by heading up a long-closed road along the South Fork Sauk River. This route largely sticks to the old route taken by miners over a century ago.
properties.title: Monte Cristo Ghost Town

properties.description: Picnic Point Park doesn't have any established trails per se, but the scenery here is delightful, and at low tide, it is possible to hike 1.5 miles to Meadowdale Beach, or 5 miles north to Point Elliot at Mukilteo. Just don't get stuck out there!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Picnic Point

properties.description: This trail completely encircles South Skookum Lake, a quiet fee-campground in Pend Oreille County. Since the campground is managed by a concessionaire, there is a $5 day-use fee for those not staying in the campground.
properties.title: South Skookum Lake Trail

properties.description: Drive almost to the top of a mountain with exquisite views all around you. Your destination is only about a quarter mile from where you park - what a great view for such little effort.
properties.title: Sugarloaf

properties.description: The South Swofford Pond Trail is a joint venture by Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife and the Cowlitz River Project of Tacoma Power and runs almost two miles around the south side of Swofford Pond to its southwest corner. It is an easy graded, mostly wooded trail that offers plenty of opportunities to view wildlife, marvel at old-growth cedars and enjoy glimpses of the surrounding Swofford Valley.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Swofford Pond

properties.description: A road walk and short boot path to a big falls
properties.title: Lazy Bear Falls

properties.description: Built with the help of Washington Trails Association and Mountains to Sound Greenway crews, the trail to Garfield Ledges will offer visitors expansive views of the Middle Fork valley and a short but steep workout.
properties.title: Garfield Ledges

properties.description: This forest is tucked away in a residential neighborhood in Bothell. A series of short trails wander through forested ravines, and provide opportunities to see birds and other wildlife.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Shelton View Forest

properties.description: Narnia provides a nice option to hike a short trail through the woods while at the beach. It is open for all trail purposes, so watch for bikes and horses. The trail is well maintained and easy to navigate.
properties.title: Narnia Trail

properties.description: The route to Bonanza Peak is a Class 4 and involves exposed scrambling. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.title: Bonanza Peak

properties.description: La Center Bottoms is a county-owned stewardship site and a stop along The Audubon Society’s The Great Washington State Birding Trail Southwest Loop. It is a pleasant short stroll, perfect to stretch your legs or share nature observation tips with the family.
properties.title: La Center Bottoms

properties.description: Visitors to Sasse Ridge in the winter should have winter travel experience, a route planned, and the ability identify and understand avalanche risk in the backcountry.
properties.title: Sasse Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: The full experience at Ape Cave includes the easy exploration of a spacious lava tube, followed by more difficult travel through a smaller, longer, and more rugged lava tube to an exit. Then, enjoy an easy return hike winding through shady forest and crusty lava formations.
properties.title: Ape Caves

properties.description: Stretch your definition of a day hike with a trip to Shoe Lake. This gorgeous lake is the perfect introduction to the Goat Rocks wilderness, but because it's closed to camping, you have to hike even further into the backcountry to overnight. The way is gently- to moderately-graded, making for relatively fast hiking, and the views along the way are a perfect unveiling of this gorgeous area: first deep green woods give way to an airier, fragrant forest, then after an alpine traverse you burst onto the Shoe Lake basin and stunning views of the Goat Rocks beyond.
properties.title: Shoe Lake

properties.description: This hike on Bainbridge Island is a great option for a short stroll through the woods.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ted Olson Nature Preserve Trail

properties.description: Meander along this path to a loud and misty falls near Newhalem which offer a great respite from heat on hot summer afternoons.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Ladder Creek Falls

properties.description: Marmot Pass offers great views and a gentle hike through old-growth forest as well as high meadows. It is a great day hike, but also offers a great starting place for a variety of overnight options.
properties.title: Marmot Pass

properties.description: Staircase Rapids is a beautiful 2.1 mile loop trail following the North Fork of the Skokomish River.  Enjoy the Olympic old growth forests with a lush understory of mosses and ferns.
properties.title: Staircase Rapids

properties.description: A short, easy trail leads to a dramatic view of the Pend Oreille River Canyon near the Canadian border.
properties.title: Riverside Canyon Overlook

properties.description: This short loop trail visits a riparian island rich with birdlife and beavers in this forgotten corner of the Okanogan River.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Roundup Park

properties.description: Looking to walk between Bellingham parks without cars passing by? The Old Village trail passes by several historic Bellingham locations as it connects Maritime Heritage Park with Elizabeth Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Old Village

properties.description: The 1930s saw Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) teams building trail in the woods all over America. The Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road benefited from these efforts, which constructed the CCC Road, a 13.5 mile long route that parallels (roughly) the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road. The Lower Section can be tricky to navigate, as it borders private property, and signage here can send mixed messages. The trail itself is on DNR land, but be sure to bring an up-to-date map to verify your location as you hike.
properties.title: CCC Road: Lower Section

properties.description: This strenuous uphill climb leads to big-payout views of the San Juans from Oyster Dome before visiting tranquil Lily Lake.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lily Lake Loop

properties.description: Hike a short, moderately steep trail to Angel's Rest, an exposed bluff with stunning views into the Columbia River Gorge. You'll be able to see the river glittering below your feet at the overlook, which seems close enough for a quick dip, but be careful, it's a long fall from the balcony.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Angel's Rest

properties.description: This loop trail takes visitors on a tour through the forest with the option to hang out on the shore of Lake Washington.
properties.title: Newcastle Beach Nature Trail

properties.description: This unofficial trail is short, steep and extremely eroded. Because it's not officially built or managed hikers are encouraged to find other locations to explore in the area.
properties.title: Index Town Wall

properties.description: Hike an old logging road that is slated to have a full conversion to trail in 2017.
properties.title: IP Road (former Yale Reservoir Logging Road)

properties.description: When you need a dose of nature therapy but are limited for time, look for a suburban nature trail. The Walker Preserve in Normandy Park offers a level easy trail, plus optional steep and narrow side trails that lead down to two small creeks. There is even a picnic table available at the small parking lot.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Walker Preserve

properties.description: Seek solitude and stupendous views at this high alpine lake in the Entiat Mountains. A steep slog of a trail ensures you'll have plenty of room at this lake.
properties.title: Fern Lake

properties.description: Bridle Trails State Park offers more than 28 miles of pleasant, forested trails conveniently located between Bellevue and Kirkland. This park is popular with horseback riders, so while dogs are allowed, they must be kept on leash to avoid startling horses.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bridle Trails State Park

properties.description: Tucked in a cirque a few miles east of Stevens Pass are Minotaur Lake, its immediate neighbor Theseus and overlooking Labyrinth Mountain. This group of alpine destinations, named for symbols in the Greek mythos, make for a great day hike and an excellent workout.
properties.title: Minotaur Lake

properties.description: A lovely feeder trail to the Kettle Crest, Midnight Ridge boasts expansive views and impressive old growth western larch.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Midnight Mountain

properties.description: A moderately strenuous hike that traverses a forested ridge, climbs to alpine meadows and ends at a 6,000 foot viewpoint with a spectacular view of the west side of Mount Rainier. Waterfalls and wildflowers abound.
properties.title: Mildred Point

properties.description: This little urban trail is tucked away on the far west side of the Providence Regional Medical Center. The trail is closed from sunset to sunrise.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Forgotten Creek Natural Area Trail

properties.description: The hidden forest trails here are actually two nature preserves gifted to the county, the northern Loretta Naurene Forest Preserve in 1992 and the southern Groth Nature Preserve in 1997.
properties.title: Lauretta Norene and Groth Nature Preserve

properties.description: The Arthur G. Rempel Nature Trail is a small series of trails inside the Fort Walla Walla Natural Area. The trail is easily accessible from Walla Walla and College Place, providing a great respite from the city and a close-in opportunity for birdwatching.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Arthur G. Rempel Nature Trail

properties.description: The Whiskey Still trail is part of the Taylor Mountain trail system and can be used to make a variety of loops.
properties.title: Whiskey Still Trail

properties.description: Venture up the Lower South Fork of the Skokomish River for an abundance of flora and fauna amid lush old growth.
properties.title: Lower South Fork Skokomish River

properties.description: A variety of different loop routes in this area pass through Anderson Pass, making it a well-travelled revolving door in the mountainous terrain of the Olympics.
properties.title: Anderson Pass

properties.description: The loop trail in this park is a nice place for families to go walking or for anyone to get some steps in.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: South Hill Loop Trail

properties.description: A wooded hike from the West Beach area of Deception Pass State Park to the North Beach Parking area. Enjoy the numerous side trails to the wonderful beach and rock outcroppings along the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - North Beach

properties.description: Chinook Bend Natural Area is a green space along the Snoqualmie River just outside the town of Carnation.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Chinook Bend Natural Area

properties.description: Tunnel Creek Trail has two trailheads. Nearly all hikers access the trail from the north side where for the first three miles the moderately easy grade is often within earshot of Tunnel Creek.  After crossing the South Fork of Tunnel Creek, the route rises at a steeper but manageable grade past Harrison Lakes to 5050 Pass and some nearby viewpoints. The south side trailhead is on the Dosewallips Road. This segment’s notoriously steep grade to 5050 Pass means it is seldom used. Try it and you’ll find out why.
properties.title: Tunnel Creek

properties.description: A quiet but sometimes rough trail that provides access to the Pacific Crest Trail from Salmon La Sac.
properties.title: Mineral Creek

properties.description: A gentle hike through stands of mature larches and other conifers along the shores of Bumping Lake. The trail is also a good alternate route to Swamp Lake Trail #970 or to Pacific Crest Trail #2000 when a ford of the Bumping River is too hazardous.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Bumping Lake

properties.description: Spring Lake – Lake Desire Park is a 390-acre forested site with a bald rocky outcrop, a bog and 3 miles of trails situated between…Spring Lake and Lake Desire! Echo Mountain is the 900-foot-tall rocky outcrop that provides great views of the two lakes and the Cascade foothills.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Spring Lake/Lake Desire Park - Echo Mountain

properties.description: The Sagebrush Trail was built in the spring of 2010 by the Friends of Badger Mountain with help from WTA. While most of the gravel trail is wide and smooth, there are a few dips and holes to look out for. The Sagebrush Trail starts in the City of Richland’s Trailhead Park. It then passes through some private land and Richland Utilities land and ends in the Badger Mountain Centennial Preserve.
properties.title: Badger Mountain - Sagebrush Trail

properties.description: Believed to be a former Native American trading route through the Olympics, this historic trail was rebuilt by the Civilian Conservation Corps (the CCC) in the 1930s. It was relocated in the early 2000s and is a popular WTA volunteer work party site to this day. The route now goes through a notch easily spied from Highway 101 in the Quilcene Range, climbing steeply to the notch and then traversing the hillside.
properties.title: Notch Pass

properties.description: This delightful little park in the heart of Coeur D'Alene boasts swimming holes, plenty of trails to give you a workout, and great views of the majestic Lake Coeur D'Alene.
properties.title: Tubbs Hill

properties.description: This is a 10-mile, paved loop on both sides of the Columbia River near Wenatchee. The trail was completed in 1990 by the Chelan County PUD, connecting residents in the area with nature right in their backyards.
properties.title: Apple Capital Recreation Loop Trail

properties.description: One of the best ways to access the heart of Chuckanut Mountain is via the North Lost Lake Trail, entering from the Interurban Trail at Arroyo Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Larrabee State Park - North Lost Lake Trail

properties.description: Hike along the edge of the massive jumble of Big Lava Bed, formed about 8,200 years ago when a cinder cone erupted, and climb to the summit of Big Huckleberry Mountain.
properties.title: Big Lava Bed

properties.description: With a couple highway crossings, and several turns and junctions, this is not the most glamourous loop through the woods, but it offers an all-purpose trail that can be chunked up into mostly flat options for hikers who want to plan their own route as well as connections and extensions to other trails in the area.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Pleasant Valley Loop

properties.description: Hike good trails in this very green, forested park on Mercer Island. Enjoy moss, ferns and bird life. And see whether the missing suspension bridge has returned.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Island Crest Park

properties.description: Descend 90 feet beneath the surface on a guided tour of the third-longest limestone cave in Washington.
properties.title: Crawford State Park - Gardner Cave

properties.description: This loop route begins and ends near the campground at Bowl and Pitcher and includes a trip across the footbridge over the Spokane River both going and returning.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Bowl and Pitcher Snowshoe

properties.description: Follow this rugged trail through a former burn to views of Mount Baker and the expansive Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Windy Peak

properties.description: This is an excellent location to get some conditioning in during the winter months, or to stretch legs after a long day behind a desk. Please respect trail closures for rehabilitation.
properties.title: Saddle Rock

properties.description: Aptly named High Camp sits at timberline on the northwest side of Mount Adams and offers stupendous views.
properties.title: High Camp

properties.description: The route to West McMillan Spire is a strenuous Class 3 and involved exposed scrambling. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: West McMillan Spire via Goodell Creek

properties.description: Get up close and personal with an enchanting glacier-sculpted landscape at Olympic National Park’s Lake Angeles.
properties.title: Lake Angeles

properties.description: This 10-mile loop hike through various parks in the suburbs northeast of Lake Washington is close in, always open and a trail for most of the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Tolt Pipeline - Sammamish River Loop

properties.description: This short trail heads down a forested ravine to a tidal inlet.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Fairy Dell Trail

properties.description: The first 1.7 miles of the Lake Ethel trail provide hikers with views of nearby mountains like Nason Ridge — the trail is closed past this point due to being on private property.
properties.title: Lake Ethel

properties.description: The Eagle Trail is a grassy urban course on the Stillaguamish River dike from Haller Park to the Dike Road in the City of Arlington. Opened in 2011, it provides an opportunity for nature and wildlife viewing while wandering green space within the city limits and a designated area for dogs to romp and play.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Eagle Trail

properties.description: A small park tucked into the Crown Hill neighborhood of Ballard.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Sunset Hill Park

properties.description: This conservation area is a 38.5-acre parcel of land along Siebert Creek between Port Angeles and Sequim. For the last two years, volunteer trail work crews have removed invasive plants like Scotch Broom, built new trails, trailheads, and a picnic area and planted more than 600 native trees and shrubs.
properties.title: Siebert Creek Conservation Area

properties.description: Discover this quiet ramble along the Wild and Scenic Sauk River as you follow the site of an old railroad grade. The trail is more about the journey than the destination, but this mellow walk can be enjoyed any time of year. The lake itself is small and more of a pond.
properties.title: Beaver Lake

properties.description: The loop around Mountain Lake is the perfect way to spend a relaxing day on Orcas Island. If part of your crew is interested in the more challenging Mount Constitution, this is a good way to while away the time that they're trekking to the top.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Moran State Park - Mountain Lake

properties.description: A winter scramble to the summit of a mountain in Snoqualmie Pass. Technical experience and equipment required.
properties.title: Avalanche Mountain

properties.description: This 140-acre public garden has trails, a reflection pool, a Japanese garden and more. Visitors must obtain a timed ticket in advance online.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bloedel Reserve

properties.description: A lovely ridge walk to a somewhat underwhelming mountaintop, with connections to other destinations in the area.
properties.title: Sasse Ridge

properties.description: The trail to Lake Ann is a wonderful, short way to see the impressive glaciated valley encircled by the popular Heather - Maple Pass Loop. Lake Ann features views of ridgelines blanketed in wildflowers in summer, a lake ringed with golden larches in fall, and before the highway closes for the season, a dramatic place to experience early winter’s snows.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Lake Ann (Rainy Pass)

properties.description: Tamanos is a moderately strenuous 10 mile round trip hike that goes through forest, meadows, rock and ridge scrambles ending in glorious up close views of Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Tamanos Mountain

properties.description: A lovely short trail in a gorgeous setting, this hike is worth planning as a weekend trip to include camping at nearby Lost Lake.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Big Tree Botanical Area Interpretive Site

properties.description: The Yurt is by far the most secluded of the four huts within the Mount Tahoma Trail System. A cozy studio in the wilderness surrounded by trees with easy access for a day hike to Griffin Mountain, you'll have to really hoof it through the snow to get there.
properties.title: Yurt Snowshoe

properties.description: Soaring Eagle Regional Park features 12 miles of trails that are regularly used by hikers, mountain bikers and equestrians. The Pipeline Trail crosses through the park and is wide and flat—in fact, it is quite common to see families with baby strollers out enjoying the trail. Soaring Eagle is also popular for trail running competitions.
properties.title: Soaring Eagle Regional Park

properties.description: Are you looking for an early summer, dry-side, flowered workout? The eastern third of this trail is for you, with its many flowers and increasing views over the American River valley. Just be ready for the stark nature of the fire ravaged forest.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Crow Lake Way

properties.description: Hike trails named in honor of mountaineers Jim Whittaker and Nawang Gombu, of 1963 Mount Everest ascent fame. Wilderness Peak may not be Everest, but it is the highest point in King County's Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park and it does have some wonderful old-growth conifers. This loop offers a diversity of steep forested hillsides, huge mossy boulders, and a low swampy area traversed via a narrow boardwalk.
properties.title: Wilderness Peak Loop

properties.description: The St. Cloud Day use area features a ½ mile ADA accessible pathway that meanders through an old orchard that was the site of a homestead ranch from the turn of the century.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: St. Cloud

properties.description: Bird, salmon, history, and river lovers will enjoy this trail in a Leavenworth park
properties.title: Blackbird Island - Waterfront Park

properties.description: With steep, broad slopes and no maintained trail to the summit, Jove Peak is a popular winter destination, but is attainable year round.  Climbing experience recommended.
properties.title: Jove Peak

properties.description: Located in the heart of Bellingham, this transit-accessible pocket of nature in the city has a little something for everyone.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Cornwall Park

properties.description: The popular Latourell Falls in Guy W. Talbot State Park offers hikers several loop options, a family friendly one-mile roundtrip accessible walk to the Lower Falls and historic bridge, or a 2 mile loop to also take in the 134-foot Upper Falls, the third tallest in the Columbia Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Latourell Falls

properties.description: Owl Mountain is a challenging hike to a remote viewpoint in the far northeast corner of the Kettle River Range.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Owl Mountain

properties.description: This climber's access trail to Glacier Peak also offers backpackers a delightful morning meander out of White Pass after a very long approach hike.
properties.title: Foam Creek Basin

properties.description: The aspen groves and golden larch are a sight to behold on this remote hike through a seldom-seen corner of the Colville National Forest.
properties.title: South Fork Silver Creek Trail to Gunsight Pass

properties.description: While Washingtonians work together to slow the spread of COVID-19, hikers are looking for nature close to home to help abide by Stay Home, Stay Healthy. Use this entry to share photos and stories from your recent neighborhood nature walk.
properties.title: My Neighborhood

properties.description: This southwest section of the Timberline Trail is characterized by loose, sandy soil and pockets of forest filled with day hikers exploring close to the lodge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Timberline Trail - Timberline Lodge To Ramona Falls

properties.description: This trail begins at the easily accessible Teepee trailhead and connects to multiple trails within the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness, making it possible to hike as an out-and-back or create longer routes.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: East Butte Creek

properties.description: The Sunrise Lake trail is a steep one-mile section of trail that is part of the Sawtooth Backcountry Trail system.
properties.title: Sunrise Lake

properties.description: Like most lookouts, South Point offers excellent views at a price. A trail that sees little maintenance on a remote ranger district, you'll expend a little sweat getting to this gorgeous vista.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: South Point Lookout

properties.description: The Granite Mountain trail is one of Washington's most popular in summer. But in winter, the route crosses an avalanche chute and is extremely dangerous when snow is present.
properties.title: Granite Mountain - Winter

properties.description: A mix of light bushwhacking and free-and-easy rambling, Gee Point is a quick hike into some of the prettiest—and least-known—country anywhere in the Cascade Range.
properties.title: Gee Point

properties.description: Gold Creek Pond is an ADA-accessible paved loop hike around a picturesque mountain pond atop Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Gold Creek Pond

properties.description: Hikers on the Noisy Creek trail can view exceptional old growth trees and also serves as the start of a cross country route into Noisy Diobsud Wilderness.
properties.title: Noisy Creek

properties.description: The Douglas Falls Grange Park makes for a nice roadside stopoff, if you want to get a little exercise and do the Nature Loop.
properties.title: Douglas Falls Grange Park - Nature Loop Trail

properties.description: Connect between the Stehekin River and Rainy Pass on this section of the Pacific Crest Trail. Views of peaks in every direction capture the hiker's attention as you walk through the beautiful North Cascades.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail - Stehekin to Rainy Pass

properties.description: Paradise Pond Park consists of 9.5 acres of undeveloped natural area next to Morrison Pond. There is no developed trail system, but there are a few undefined/unmarked trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Paradise Pond Park

properties.description: This easy day hike is a great destination for families staying in the Stehekin Valley. Huckleberries line the slopes in the fall, and the 200-foot deep gorge you hike along provides thrills at any time of year. Plus, it's a relatively short hike in a valley of miles-long trails.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Agnes Gorge

properties.description: Spectacle Lake is truly worthy of the name - it's quite a sight to see. Nestled at the base of Chikamin Ridge and just a short jaunt from the Pacific Crest Trail, this lake is one of the true gems of Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Spectacle Lake

properties.description: Esmeralda Basin promises hikers the opportunity to walk through old forest, meadows brimming with wildflowers, and along rocky hillsides, all while enjoying the striking scenery of the jagged and craggy Esmeralda Peaks.
properties.title: Esmeralda Basin (Esmerelda)

properties.description: The Necklace Valley makes a wonderful 2-3 night backpack trip for hearty hikers, and rewards with cool alpine lakes to swim and fish in, or just camp beside. Or take a day trip along the East Fork Foss River admire the amazing second-growth tree canopy.
properties.title: East Fork Foss - Necklace Valley

properties.description: Kendall Peak Lakes are popular snowshoe destinations, since the trailhead is about one hour from Seattle, the grade is gentle and the views superb. The route is relatively easy to follow because it follows an closed forest road.
properties.title: Kendall Peak Lakes Snowshoe

properties.description: Nestled far from civilization, at the end of Deep Creek, you will likely have this glorious loop to yourself. A brief, three-mile section of the famous Pacific Crest Trail makes up the western link of this loop.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Tumac Mountain Loop

properties.description: This pleasant woodland trail follows the historic route of the Seattle-Walla Walla Railroad, which transported coal from the mines once operating in present-day Cougar Mountain Park.
properties.title: May Creek Trail

properties.description: The route to Martin Peak is a Class 3 and involves exposed scrambling. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Martin Peak

properties.description: A roadwalk turned trail on Taylor Mountain.
properties.title: Taylor Mountain - Road G

properties.description: This trail is a really nice accompaniment to your morning coffee, but bring a thermos -- it's long enough that the coffee might get cold by the time you reach the end!
properties.title: Heart O' the Forest

properties.description: This half-mile loop trail goes through old-growth forest with views of the Sol Duc River.
properties.title: Ancient Groves

properties.description: An accessible hike for seasoned veterans and neophytes alike, Wallace Falls provides visitors with breathtaking views of the Wallace River and the surrounding falls on a relatively low difficulty, scenic 5.6 mile round-trip. Although well attended and often busy, the trail stands as a true showcase of the diversity and majestic beauty that the Central Cascades can offer to hikers who journey into the heart of this sublime mountain range.
properties.title: Wallace Falls State Park

properties.description: Hike up an abandoned road, through a logged area, and into mature forest on the edge of the Alpine Lakes wilderness. What the trail lacks in ruggedness is more than made up for by the quantity of berries that line the trail.
properties.title: Mount Margaret

properties.description: This moderate in-and-out trail makes a lovely picnic destination, or ideal short backpack, to a brilliant blue lake with peeks of Mount Adams.
properties.title: Deep Lake

properties.description: This is a rugged trail that climbs steeply yet briefly to fabulous views of the Columbia River Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Mitchell Point

properties.description: Dramatic mounds of snow, a frozen lake and sweeping views into the Alpine Lakes and Glacier Peak Wildernesses await snowshoers at Skyline Lake. Easily accessed from the Stevens Pass ski area, this steep and rewarding ridge walk is a classic on a sunny day.
properties.title: Skyline Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: Here are two quick and easy trails to view an unnamed waterfall splashing 100 feet down into the Big Quilcene River. Though the campground is seasonal, the trails are open year round. Bring the dog and the kids, stretch your legs, and take in some fantastic scenery located 4 miles south of Quilcene, immediately off of Olympic Highway 101.
properties.title: Fallsview Canyon (Falls View)

properties.description: This series of trails extends through the forest behind the Hidden Cove Ballfields.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Hidden Cove Trail

properties.description: The Granite Creek Connector Trail provides hikers with an alternative start to a hike along the Granite Creek Trail.
properties.title: Granite Creek Connector Trail

properties.description: There are two routes to Kalama Falls; the longer route starts from the Kalama Horse Camp and takes hikers through the forest.
properties.title: Kalama Horse Camp to Kalama Falls

properties.description: The Pomas Creek trail is a 5-mile connector trail that can be used to create a 21.5-mile lollipop loop in conjunction with the Entiat River Trail.
properties.title: Pomas Creek

properties.description: This urban trail loops around the peninsula of North Everett offering a healthy dose of history and some decent natural scenery, too.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Mill Town Trail

properties.description: Three waterfalls, multiple viewing areas, and two different trailheads provide great choices for an excursion to Little Mashel Falls. The tallest waterfall plunges over 90 feet.
properties.title: Little Mashel Falls -  Bud Blancher Trail

properties.description: If you’re willing to take on the short but steep Basalt Pass trail and commit to some more climbing even after that, you’ll be rewarded with 360-degree views of the Entiat Mountains and the nearby Henry M. Jackson and Glacier Peak Wildernesses.
properties.title: Basalt Peak via Basalt Pass

properties.description: A motorized sno-park where cross country skiers and snowshoers can also get a good workout.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Rock Creek Sno-Park

properties.description: Jones Island is a beautiful State Park located in the San Juan Islands that contains two remarkable trails that circumnavigate the entire island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Jones Island Trail

properties.description: This snowshoe route follows a forest road, with a brief stint on the forested summer trail near the top, to a lookout building near Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Sun Top Snowshoe

properties.description: The Upper South Fork Skokomish River to Sundown Pass can be considered a tale of two trails. The first half stays low in lush valley bottom on brushy but obvious tread, while the second half makes up for lost time, ascending steeply through subalpine forest between wet meadows on faint and broken tread. The scenery improves with every step near the top, and reaching Lake Sundown is a welcome reward after all the toil.
properties.title: Upper South Fork Skokomish River

properties.description: There is no official trail to the peak of Humility Hill. Reaching the peak requires going off trail.
properties.title: Humility Hill

properties.description: On the south side of Taylor Mountain, this trail gains a couple hundred feet as it curves through the forest above Carey Creek.
properties.title: Boot Trail

properties.description: The Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial is an outdoor exhibit commemorating the internment of Japanese Americans from Bainbridge Island in the state of Washington. It is a unit of the Minidoka National Historic Site in Idaho.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial

properties.description: In spring the hills are alive with blooming balsamroot, lupine, phlox  and many other wildflowers. The balsamroot and lupine are the stars of the show at Columbia Hills State Park.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Columbia Hills State Park - Crawford Ranch Trail

properties.description: Cross over two small creeks as you make your way up and over Holder Ridge.
properties.title: Holder Ridge Trail

properties.description: This un-maintained trail can be accessed from the Pacific Crest Trail. The trail can be difficult to follow, so be sure to take appropriate precautions.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Deadwood Lakes

properties.description: Formerly a short, two-mile trail, the washout of the Elwha River Road has made this a 7.15 mile roundtrip hike.  Luckily, it's mostly flat road, and you're even allowed to take a bike the whole way, if you don't mind a rough ride.
properties.title: Glines Canyon Overlook Trail

properties.description: Take a long weekend and enjoy some of the best backcountry in the state on this long loop hike. Along the way, you'll see massive wildflower meadows, glaciers, alpine lakes, high mountain passes and supreme views of Glacier Peak.
properties.title: Spider Gap - Buck Creek Pass Loop

properties.description: Just a short drive from civilization, this is a good moderate choice if you're seeking a relaxing, riverside ramble.
properties.title: Pratt Connector to Pratt River Trail

properties.description: Dock Butte boasts sweeping views of Mount Baker, Baker Lake, and several prominent peaks in the North Cascades and Olympic Peninsula. It is a great option for beginner hikers looking to up their hiking game as well as those looking for exceptional mountain views without the mileage and time commitment of a longer hike.
properties.title: Dock Butte

properties.description: Hop aboard the paved Spruce Railroad Trail for a scenic and historic hike along the sparkling shores of massive Lake Crescent.
properties.title: Spruce Railroad Trail

properties.description: Excellent groomed Nordic Trails in winter convert to a nice double track trail for summer use. The trails are Nordic-only in winter (no snowshoeing allowed), but multi-use in summer (hike, bike, & equestrian).
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Nordic Trails

properties.description: The Rock Trail is one of WTA's signature projects, built from scratch thanks to WTA’s partnerships with various organizations, including Larrabee State Park and Chuckanut Conservancy. A dedicated group of enthusiastic WTA volunteers worked countless hours here, carving a connector trail out of the steep, rugged hillside from the top of Cleator Road to the South Lost Lake Trail. The Rock Trail provides hikers and trail runners a steep climb, gorgeous views, and a peek at the area's fascinating geology.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Larrabee State Park - Rock Trail

properties.description: A class 2 scramble up Esmerelda Peak.
properties.title: Esmeralda Peak (Esmerelda)

properties.description: Hiking the North Cascades is a treat for all ages. This short nature trail gives a taste of moss-draped old growth with moderate elevation gain.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Thunder Woods Nature Trail

properties.description: In Washington, trails can be found just about anywhere. This one takes off from Parking Lot F on the campus of Evergreen State College! A short hike down to a lovely little beach, this is just the ticket for students and families alike.
properties.title: Evergreen Beach Trail

properties.description: Tucked between Silverdale and Poulsbo, Island Lake County Park features a paved trail around the namesake lake and through the adjacent forest. With a section of shorefront access as well, it's great for families!
properties.title: Island Lake

properties.description: The Leovy Trail, a testament to community land conservation, is a moderate ascent through second-growth Cascade rainforest to the summit of Heybrook Ridge. At the top, take in stunning views of Mount Index, Bridal Veil Falls, and the Skykomish Valley.
properties.title: Heybrook Ridge

properties.description: The Chewuch River Trail provides access to the very popular Cathedral Lakes area on the Boundary trail. Walk through a burn zone, lodgepole pine, and meadows as you travel deep into the Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Chewuch River Trail

properties.description: WTA began construction of this half mile new trail in 2013. Since then they've built several boardwalks and brushed out a rough corridor leading to a connection with the existing trail system through the forested dunes.
properties.title: Leadbetter Point State Park - Martha Jordan Birding Trail

properties.description: Open year-round, this trail system is best known for its winter groomed loop trails.
properties.title: Frater Lake

properties.description: With more than 600 acres of rolling fields, pine-forested buttes and wetlands, the Slavin Conservation Area provides plenty of room to stretch legs all year-round.
properties.title: Slavin Pond Loop

properties.description: Susie’s Trail offers a relaxing nature stroll on a wide gravel path along the Sultan River as it connects the city’s River Park with the nearby trails at multi-use Osprey Park.
properties.title: Susie's Trail

properties.description: Branch off from the Paw Print Connector to the east side of Tiger Mountain and explore this trail with many access points.
properties.title: East Tiger

properties.description: A paved interpretive trail on the Mountain Loop Highway near Verlot. Perfect for exploring children and curious adults, an extra add-on after a longer hike or a leg stretch during a driving tour of the area.
properties.title: Youth-on-Age Interpretive Trail

properties.description: After it was deemed impractical for cars, the old Columbia River Highway was closed to traffic, and opened to hikers and bikers! The winding route of this historic highway hearkens back to a time when roads were designed for Sunday drives, and the twists and turns of the highway make for a diverting hike or bike along the scenic Columbia River Gorge.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Historic Columbia River Highway State Trail - Mosier Twin Tunnels

properties.description: The Coyote Trail is within the Goat Rock Wilderness, part of the Gifford Pinchot Forest. It begins at a junction with the Packwood Lake Trail, offering access to Lost Lake and after a grueling climb, the Pacific Crest Trail. This trail will provide the hiker and the backpacker with great views and challenging terrain along with some solitude since it is not a popular or a frequented trail.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Coyote Trail

properties.description: This Shoreline city park seems to be little-known outside its immediate neighborhood, but it's worth a visit. The park is minimally developed, and it offers a variety of trails through open grassy areas and forested areas.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Paramount Open Space

properties.description: This is a nice little leg stretcher just off the North Cascades Highway. Especially good in winter, when the highway is closed, and the eagles are feeding along the Skagit River.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Marblemount Boat Launch Trail

properties.description: The trail up to Winchester Mountain is less than two miles long and only 1300 feet of elevation gain, with access to a lookout at 6500 feet with outstanding 360 degree views. What’s the catch? The road.
properties.title: Winchester Mountain

properties.description: This trail begins with an amazing, ADA accessible, interpretive trail before proceeding down a steep rugged canyon to a one-of-a-kind swinging bridge.
properties.title: Lava Canyon

properties.description: Meandering along Goldsborough Creek through 9.4 acre Hilburn Preserve, the trail follows the water from clay cliffs to muddy banks. The river’s edge is lined with rows of bare white alder trunks in the winter or bright green foliage in the summer, and the surrounding forest is made up of a mixture of coniferous and deciduous trees, a range of fern species, and epiphytes blending from one type to the next.
properties.title: Hilburn Preserve

properties.description: Walk along the Pacific Crest Trail through some of the most stunning landscape Washington has to offer. Traverse the treeline as you enjoy sweeping views and mountain passes.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Hart's Pass to Rainy Pass

properties.description: This is not an official Forest Service trail. The route is not maintained and requires route-finding skills to navigate. There is no designated parking area and may lead into a private watershed area where hiking is prohibited.
properties.title: Zig Zag Trail

properties.description: There are plenty of interesting things to see at Fort Ebey, and lots of trails to take you there.  A beach walk, bluff views, a lake, forest, and history can all be found here. The park has 26 miles of trails, allowing you to put together a very interesting hike, either long or short, that includes most or all of the sights. This loop of approximately four miles will take you on a nice tour.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Fort Ebey State Park

properties.description: A trail providing a connection between the crest of the Cascades near Snoqualmie and the Middle Fork River valley. You'll need route-finding gear and equipment, as well as plenty of stamina to hike this one.
properties.title: Rock Creek

properties.description: A section of the Wonderland Trail between Ipsut Creek and Mystic Lake, starting from the Carbon River trailhead.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Wonderland Trail -  Ipsut Creek to Mystic Lake

properties.description: Deep Creek Trail begins at Azalea Park and connects to a variety of local trails in the city of Snoqualmie.
properties.title: Snoqualmie Ridge Trail – Deep Creek Trail

properties.description: Lunch Lake is a popular stop or overnight camping area along the Seven Lakes Basin Loop in Olympic National Park. Visitors here will need an overnight permit to stay here, attainable from Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Lunch Lake

properties.description: Vanson Ridge is a 3.3-mile connector trail between the Goat Mountain and Green River trails in Mount St. Helens National Monument. A welcome respite for many thru-hikers traveling the Goat Mountain loop route, it is also popular with mountain bikers as an exciting offshoot of the Green River trail.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Vanson Ridge

properties.description: The route to Buttermilk Ridge is a Class 3 and involved exposed scrambling. Gear and expertise are recommended.
properties.title: Buttermilk Ridge

properties.description: A loop trail that starts at Sun Mountain Lodge.
properties.title: Kraule - Sunnyside

properties.description: On this little used trail, hikers can see history, both natural and man-made. Large sections of the forest are recovering from the 2006 Tripod Complex Fire, and the two lookouts on the summit provide a glimpse of the 1920's and 1940's construction.
properties.title: North Twentymile Peak

properties.description: Find supreme wildflower gardens and a high-country plateau speckled with shimmering tarns-but that's not all. Spectacular alpine vistas abound too-of Baker, Shuksan, and all those rugged and craggy peaks straddling the 49th parallel. Yellow Aster Butte may be a misnomer (those yellow-petaled delights are actually daisies), but you definitely don't want to miss hiking here.
properties.title: Yellow Aster Butte

properties.description: A brushy hike through dense forest, giant trees, and quiet spots to sit.
properties.title: French Creek

properties.description: The Mount Aix trail leads to a lofty world above the tree line, with views in all directions, and access to other trails for wandering in the open. On a clear day, you can see Mount Adams, Mount St. Helens, the Goat Rocks, Mount Rainier and the Stuart Range, just to mention the more identifiable peaks.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mount Aix

properties.description: Just a mile outside the tiny town of Montesano is a quiet, calm lake, fishing, swimming, camping and five miles of hiking trails. Stop by Lake Sylvia State Park for a day or a whole weekend of fun.
properties.title: Lake Sylvia State Park

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mount Christoff

properties.description: With multi-season beauty of summer flowers and golden fall larch, the Eagle Lakes naturally demonstrate why this multi-user trail is designated as a National Recreation Trail and is part of the popular Sawtooth Lakes Loop (aka Golden Lakes Loop). The more scenic Upper Eagle Lake has many campsites and provides a base for fishing, swimming, roaming, and climbing.
properties.title: Eagle Lakes

properties.description: Include a visit to this multi-use, frontcountry trail network on your next road trip to the Northern Olympic Peninsula!
properties.title: Robin Hill Farm

properties.description: Seeley Lake Park offers a 1.3 mile roundtrip urban hike in the city of Lakewood. Though the lake itself is more of a marsh, the wildlife here is plentiful, Hikers see ducks, squirrels, and other creatures flitting about, and in spring the flowers blooming provide a cheerful background.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Seeley Lake Park

properties.description: A series of very short trails at Point Robinson lead to and around a lighthouse on Maury Island whose mate is across the Sound at Alki Point.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Point Robinson Park

properties.description: A steep as all heck hike (think: 1200 feet-per-mile) from the Twisp River Valley up to Abernathy Ridge with 360-degree views. The trail continues on to Slate Lake, but this side-trip adds 4 miles roundtrip for this add-on.
properties.title: Slate Creek

properties.description: A welcome change of pace from some of the busier nearby hikes, this North Cascades ridge hike offers the same stunning views minus the crowds.
properties.title: Shannon Ridge

properties.description: A loop hike, beginning and ending in the old-growth forests of the North Fork Sauk River that traverses high ridges and passes of the Pacific crest, visits beautiful alpine lakes, and finally follows the high and lonesome Pilot Ridge Trail before descending back down to the trail junction on the North Fork Sauk River.
properties.title: White Pass - Pilot Ridge Loop

properties.description: Hike along the edge of a ridgeline just above an invisible I-90 at the north end of Tiger Mountain.
properties.title: Brink Trail

properties.description: This small park has a playground, picnic area, off-leash dog park and more, as well a short walking trails in a wooded area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Rainier Woods Park

properties.description: A beautiful destination along the Chief Sealth Trail, Kubota Garden is gorgeous oasis where Northwest native plants thrive in the style of Japanese garden, thanks to horticultural pioneer Fujitaro Kubota.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Kubota Gardens

properties.description: One of several feeder trails to the Kettle Crest, the Ryan Cabin Trail provides easy access to numerous route options in the Kettle Range.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Ryan Cabin

properties.description: This route is a section of the Chinook Trail System, a yet-to-be-completed 300-mile bi-state loop encircling the Columbia River Gorge. The #180B section connects the Tarbell Trail to the Silver Star Trail. Many still refer to this section as the Kloochman Butte Trail.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Kloochman Butte Trail

properties.description: This is a great hike for kids with lots to see including wild flowers, big views of Mount Rainier and maybe even some wildlife including marmots and goats. Take a picnic and enjoy the wonderful sights along this trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Rainier View

properties.description: This 16-acre park sits at the top of a hill in the Snoqualmie Ridge neighborhood in Snoqualmie.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Jeanne Hansen Community Park

properties.description: The Sa Teekh Wa Trail is a two-mile interpretive trail along the Chewuch River from downtown Winthrop. The trail is easily accessed from a bridge at the northwest end of Winthrop's boardwalk. It's a pleasant stroll through the pines along the river, which is also a major salmon spawning area.
properties.title: Sa Teekh Wa Trail

properties.description: A lovely protected space on a half-mile of beach along the Strait of Juan de Fuca. This area is just 20 miles west of Port Angeles -- perfect for a picnic or a short day trip.
properties.title: Lyre Conservation Area

properties.description: Holden Lake is set in a fantastic glacial basin, with stunning views of Bonanza, the highest non-volcanic peak in Washington State. It can be a hot, brushy bushwhack to the lake, but the views from lakeshore are worth it.
properties.title: Holden Lake

properties.description: This 2.1 mile loop trail follows a restored section of the historic Columbia River Highway, which was constructed to route around the Tooth Rock (aptly named, for its shape). It then jogs right on a much older road, from the 1850s, before looping back to the beginning.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Tooth Rock

properties.description: A beautiful hike through an interesting forest, often over boardwalks, ends at the beach with the potential for birdwatching and wildlife viewing. If you plan ahead and get a permit, it's a nice overnight destination.
properties.title: Sand Point

properties.description: This park in Edmonds features 120-acres of open space with plenty of branching, interconnecting trails for exploring.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Southwest County Park

properties.description: This wildlife refuge hugging the north side of the Snohomish River is just a short drive from downtown Snohomish and provides visitors with a space to take a quiet stroll or go birdwatching.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Riverview Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: This hike may seem virtually an informality after the arduous drive to its trailhead. However, if fire lookouts intrigue you, and the aesthetic of the rough Okanogan Highlands appeal to you, then this hike is for you.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Cornell Butte

properties.description: Dalles Ridge is one way hikers can reach Noble Knob, a former fire lookout with awesome views, near Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Noble Knob via Dalles Ridge

properties.description: Enjoy an easy hike along a salmon-spawning stream in a lush emerald ravine. Twanoh is derived from the Skokomish people, meaning "gathering place."Twanoh State Park protects 182 acres of prime Hood Canal real estate-a perfect place for hikers and wildlife to gather.
properties.title: Twanoh State Park

properties.description: The Lake Lois Habitat Reserve consists of 28.6 acres within the city of Lacey. You can take a hike on the 0.25-mile interpretive loop trail, and try to spot some local wildlife. Relax on the beach or even go fishing in Lake Lois which is fed by Woodland Creek.
properties.title: Lake Lois Habitat Reserve

properties.description: A reclaimed industrial site converted to a showcase park offers trails linking local communities to nature.
properties.title: Washougal Waterfront Park Trail - Columbia River Connector Trail

properties.description: On the east side of Stevens Pass, near Lake Wenatchee, two large, calm lakes wait in a lush basin lined with pine trees, bigleaf maples, and an understory of salmonberry and blackberry. On the way in, the trail shows off gigantic western redcedars, as well as rushing mountain streams, and an impressive rocky canyon.
properties.title: Twin Lakes (Wenatchee)

properties.description: This trail is popular for training and improved thanks to the Department of Natural Resources and Washington Trails Association volunteers. But note that the true peak lies on a small parcel of private land. Bring a map and know where that boundary is.
properties.title: Dirty Harry's Peak

properties.description: This is a beautiful hike that "has it all," from wonderful wildflowers and a deep forest, to wild creeks and an alpine lake. You will even see an abandoned gold mine along the way!
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Henskin Lake

properties.description: Falls Creek Trail is a good one for introductory backpacking trips, or simply a long, woodsy day hike through the forest. You'll enjoy a gradual grade of this 9 mile trail. Hike the full-length (making for an 18-mile trip) or turn around at any point.
properties.title: Upper Falls Creek Trail

properties.description: A multi-night backpacking trip around the eastern edge of Mount Rainier National Park.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Eastside Loop

properties.description: Stunning alpine meadows and peak views, Dishpan Gaps charming trail leads you to a gateway of more trails.
properties.title: Dishpan Gap

properties.description: Vantage is primarily a destination for rock climbers, with the fascinating rock formations of the Gorge making for a great challenge to those wishing to hone their belaying skills. But nearby Frenchman Coulee allows hikers to enjoy the same surroundings with both feet planted firmly on the ground.
properties.title: Frenchman Coulee

properties.description: This state park is a waterfront gem with hiking trails, history and many camping options
properties.title: Manchester State Park

properties.description: If the name Kendall Katwalk conjures up an image of a narrow pathway blasted out of a steeply sloped rock face, that’s part of it. But the whole package includes old growth forest, gorgeous wildflowers, and stunning views into the Alpine Lakes Wilderness from both sides of the pass below Kendall Peak, where the Katwalk begins.
properties.title: Kendall Katwalk

properties.description: Wander a loop around the Long Beach peninsula, crossing between Willapa National Wildlife Refuge and Leadbetter Point State Park, to see thousands of shorebirds during spring and fall.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Leadbetter Point Loop

properties.description: The hike to Round Mountain is a good one for those looking for a shorter hike than heading all the way to Alpine Lookout. The views aren't quite as good, but you'll still enjoy a good workout and a classic central Washington ridge walk.
properties.title: Round Mountain

properties.description: WTA is helping Little Pend Oreille to develop a trail for refuge visitors in the 40,200 acre Little Pend Oreille National Wildlife Refuge 13 miles southeast of Colville. The loop trail starts at the Refuge headquarters and heads upward gaining 600 ft to the regional views from Mill Butte.
properties.title: Little Pend Oreille National Wildlife Refuge - Mill Butte

properties.description: This small park near the SeaTac airport is great for outdoor sports lovers — baseball, soccer, basketball, disc golf, even BMX! — and those seeking some urban trails.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: North SeaTac Park

properties.description: A short but stiff climb through an old burn, old growth forest, and alpine meadows to a restored fire lookout standing sentinel over the western flanks of the Wild Sky Wilderness.
properties.title: Evergreen Mountain Lookout

properties.description: A gentle meandering barrier-free path leads through a mature cottonwood forest just west of Vancouver Lake. Although you can't see the lake through all the trees, there are other sights and sounds to enjoy along this route. Most notably the vibrant greens of the understory in spring, beautiful fall yellows and quite a few species of birds nearly all year.
properties.title: Vancouver Lake - North Trail

properties.description: Dip into a forested lollipop loop in a shoreline park on Lake Godwin in Snohomish County.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wenberg County Park

properties.description: Walk, run or bike along the scenic Skagit River and enjoy the breathtaking views.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Skagit Riverwalk Trail

properties.description: Fort Flagler State Park is one of five impressive military installations that were established in close proximity to protect Puget Sound from invaders during times of war.
properties.title: Fort Flagler State Park

properties.description: This is a nice, quiet little forest hike, where the journey is half the destination. The lake is pond sized, and surrounded by large boulders. It is pretty in its own way, a still lake with nice reflections, yellow waterlilies and silvered logs floating on the surface. The clumps of grasses and moss growing on the floating logs create a mini ecosystem to observe up close.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Pyramid Lake

properties.description: A long dirt road provides access to the central trailhead for the William O. Douglas Wilderness Area. The popular, easy forest hike to the Twin Sisters Lakes is a prelude to miles of exploration possible on trails and cross-country through open forest, past meadows, ponds, and lakes.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Twin Sisters Lakes

properties.description: This short, easy trail that loops through both forested and grassy areas with access to Issaquah Creek.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Confluence Park

properties.description: A trek through the Little Beaver valley in the heart of the North Cascades offers remarkable old-growth forest, phenomenal mountain views and plenty of options for backpackers.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Little Beaver Creek

properties.description: English Boom County Park is an all-season area that offers bird watching, beach combing, wildflowers and views of the Cascades. It is also a historical area with remnants of early logging operations for transporting logs by rail and water. There are picnic facilities and wheelchair-friendly boardwalks and a viewing platform.  A short walk takes you through an estuary cut through with small channels. A small parking lot accommodates about ten vehicles which includes some spaces along the end of the road.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: English Boom

properties.description: You may have heard Mailbox Peak mentioned in slightly hushed tones, the kind reserved for stories about some legendary storm or a bad accident. What inspires such reverence? The original route, which entails 4,000 feet of climbing in less than three miles. The newer, gentler trail takes twice as much distance to achieve the summit, but nothing will permanently erase the original trail's fearsome reputation.
properties.title: Mailbox Peak - Old Trail

properties.description: This hike sits just over the Idaho border near the town of Coeur d’Alene. Although it’s in Idaho, the trailhead can be reached in under an hour from downtown Spokane.
properties.title: Caribou Ridge

properties.description: Because of the presence of deep snow on Mount Rainier in the winter, accessing Camp Muir in winter requires route-finding skills and proper equipment, including traction devices, GPS devices, a map and other supplies (including mountaineering gear) to stay safe.
properties.title: Camp Muir - Winter

properties.description: This short, level walk with interpretive signs is a beautiful introduction to the grandeur and intoxicating fragrance of an old growth forest.
properties.title: Peeled Cedar

properties.description: The Duckabush River trail spans two land management agencies -- the US Forest Service and the National Park service. The first 6.2 miles of the trail weaves through Olympic National Forest. It's a popular early season backpack and a frequent site for WTA work crews. The upper section, in Olympic National Park, melts out much later, but provides a gateway to gorgeous backpacking destinations.
properties.title: Upper Duckabush

properties.description: There are two sides to Bandera Mountain — gentle and well-groomed on the one hand, rough and untamed on the other. Together, they make for a very satisfying hike along a rocky ridge to a false summit (Little Bandera) with views impressive enough to dissuade most from completing the final half mile of informal trail to the "real" summit.
properties.title: Bandera Mountain

properties.description: Beautiful mixed forests surround you as saunter up Indian Creek towards the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT). Surrounded by peaks on all sides, this crucial connector to the PCT in the ultra-rugged Glacier Peak Wilderness requires keen navigation skills (and a strong sense of adventure) as years of overgrown brush make this trail difficult to follow.
properties.title: Indian Creek

properties.description: Hike a multi-use trail past a beaver pond to connect with the Tongue Mountain Trail and eventually the summit of craggy Tongue Mountain.
properties.title: High Bridge

properties.description: This park with a handful of trails is nestled into a residential area in South Tacoma.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wapato Hills Park

properties.description: The 0.7-mile interpretive trail from the upper falls viewpoints to the lower falls viewpoint is family- and pet-friendly, good for beginners, teaches the basics of the flora and fauna near Snoqualmie Pass, informs about local Native American culture and ends with impressive views of a Washington icon.
properties.title: Snoqualmie Falls

properties.description: This is more of a stroll than a hike, with beach walking. It is of historical interest with interpretive signs along the way. Fort Casey was one of three forts chosen in 1896 to form a triangle for protection of Puget Sound. Fort Worden and Fort Flagler were the other two. All have become state parks. Their use for coastal protection proved to be impractical so their use became a place for instruction and training of troops during both of the world wars.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Fort Casey State Park

properties.description: Hike an almost level forest loop trail along a creek in this Snohomish County park. It's a welcome break from the surrounding suburbia, and offers large trees and ferns, plus a few wildflowers and birds. Optionally, check out a more urbanized trail that continues on far to the south.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: McCollum Park

properties.description: The Moss Lake Nature Trail is wheelchair-accessible, by design. Bring along a copy of the interpretive guide for a more informational hike.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Moss Lake Loop

properties.description: Here, find spectacular views of Mount Baker, Twin Sisters and other peaks. Activities include beachcombing, birdwatching, and picnicking.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Semiahmoo Spit

properties.description: A nice spot on Marrowstone Island for a picnic, birding or a very short walk on a beach.
properties.title: Mystery Bay State Park

properties.description: This short dayhike also offers campsites near the site of an old B-17 crash site. Please leave what you see so others may discover this historic site as you do.
properties.title: Tubal Cain Mine

properties.description: The Kettle Crest South begins at the White Mountain Trailhead and extends to Sherman Pass, passing by White Mountain, Barnaby Butte, Bald Mountain, Snow Peak, and Sherman Peak along the way.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Kettle Crest South

properties.description: This easy-access day hike delivers comparable — if not superior — panoramic views and lung-busting switchbacks to Mount Si, with significantly less foot traffic.
