properties.title: Mount Washington

properties.description: Wander woods reminiscent of eastern hardwood forest, filled with aspen, hemlock and birch along the largest natural lake in the Colville National Forest—plus enjoy one of the best western larch displays in Eastern Washington.
properties.title: Sullivan Lakeshore

properties.description: A climb to a peak on the North Cascades Highway. Climbing gear and experience as well as route finding knowledge required.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Colonial Peak

properties.description: This well-maintained trail follows along the North Fork Walla Walla River. Large trees provide shade for most of the hike, and all the flora and fauna that come with being near water.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: North Fork Walla Walla River

properties.description: Seattle's Discovery Park Loop Trail is a designated National Recreation Trail, 2.8 miles long with an elevation change of just 140 feet. It passes through both forest and open meadows, offers extensive views, good prospects for bird watchers, and it can be hiked or jogged year-round.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Discovery Park Loop Trail

properties.description: Take this wide, graveled path to get a quick dose of nature near home.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Pacific Way Trail

properties.description: A trail off Clay Pit Road with access to Coal Creek Falls, as well as Shy Bear area, Wilderness Peak, and other areas.
properties.title: Fred's Railroad

properties.description: The Golden Gate trail provides a quick route to amazing panoramas of Mount Rainier and the craggy peaks of the Tatoosh Range. Pass through wildflower-studded alpine meadows, a clear sparkling stream, and up a steep, well-maintained trail. You can even make it a loop, if you want to explore the lush parkland at the foot of Washington's tallest mountain.
properties.title: Golden Gate

properties.description: Take a short dayhike in a ghost forest to a beautiful babbling brook on the southwest side of Mount St. Helens.
properties.title: Toutle Trail - Blue Lake to Loowit Trail

properties.description: The Graves Creek primitive trail provides access to old growth forests high above the Quinault River Valley and solitude compared to the high use trails along the Quinault River. Expect glimpses of waterfalls across the gorge in spring and signs of wild-life including bear, deer, and elk.
properties.title: Graves Creek

properties.description: A hidden gem revealed! The South Fork Cascade Trail was in the Mineral Park Fire of 2003, but recent efforts by WTA crews and other volunteer organizations have helped reopen a section of it, and continue to repair it.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: South Fork Cascade River

properties.description: Hike along a lofty ridge at the demarcation of the blast zone. Look south at blown-down and toppled forests and a series of sparkling alpine lakes surrounded by silver snags. Look north at alpine meadows flush with wildflowers and hillsides cloaked in verdant old-growth canopies. One of the best trails for comparing before and after the eruption landscapes, Goat Mountain is also one of the best for views.
properties.title: Goat Mountain and Deadman's Lake

properties.description: This strenuous trek from creek to peak offers up-close views of impressive waterfalls and far-off views of Cascade volcanoes.
properties.title: Siouxon Peak Loop

properties.description: A short dead end trail coming off the High Ridge trail at Hurricane Ridge in Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Sunrise Point Trail

properties.description: Gotchen Creek Trail is a 2.9-mile, high-elevation, single-track in the middle of Gotchen Meadow, south of Mount Adams and the Mount Adams Wilderness. This trail intersects with Cold Springs Trail (#72) and Morrison Creek Trail (#39) and crosses Hole-in-the-Ground Creek.
properties.title: Gotchen Creek

properties.description: This loop hike in a popular recreation area offers a good mix of forest and meadow, with just enough elevation gain to work your legs and lungs.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Springboard Trail

properties.description: Offering spectacular views of the three southern volcanoes in Washington, lakes, meadows and wildlife over relatively moderate terrain, Section H is the perfect starting point for the Washington portion of the Pacific Crest Trail.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) Section H - Bridge of the Gods to White Pass

properties.description: Accessible from Highway 2, I-90, or the iconic Pacific Crest Trail, Deception Pass is a gateway to alpine lakes, stunning mountain views or, if you're a thru-hiker, Mexico or Canada.
properties.title: Deception Pass

properties.description: Enchantment Park is part of a large network of different trails and parks located along the Wenatchee River in downtown Leavenworth. The trails are well maintained, and dotted with informative plaques all along their length.
properties.title: Enchantment Park

properties.description: With expansive views of the Strait of Juan de Fuca contrasting with deep forest lagoons, the Mount Finlayson loop features the variety of ecosystems that San Juan Island offers in an easy and scenic trail. Options for shorter or longer routes make this a suitable destination for hikers of all ages.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Mount Finlayson

properties.description: The way to Lake James offers a myriad of experiences, from deep rainforest to the high country of Mount Rainier National Park. Undertake an ambitious dayhike, or be more leisurely about it and make it a backpacking trip.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Lake James

properties.description: Hike on the Pacific Crest Trail in a section where its name describes its location. From the trail high on the ridge, the views abound.  In the three passes are flowers in the summer and golden larch in the fall. A side trip up Tatie Peak provides 360 degree views of the North Cascades.
properties.title: Tatie Peak and Grasshopper Pass

properties.description: A lake in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest a few miles off the Pacific Crest Trail. This lake is extremely difficult to access without route-finding experience.
properties.title: Glacier Lake

properties.description: The Trautman Ranch Conservation Area provides over 275 acres of meadows and open woodland over rolling terrain adjacent to Riverside State Park. This double-lollipop loop includes a portion of the paved Centennial Trail, as well as more rugged trails through the forest.
properties.title: Trautman Ranch Conservation Area - East Loop

properties.description: The Wonderland Trail has been described as magical, hiking through a wispy-clouded August sky to the many glaciers, river valleys and high alpine meadows all while traveling through the through Rainier's backcountry. Klapatche Park will give you a chance to experience the Wonderland Trail with only 21 miles of hiking.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Klapatche Park

properties.description: Explore the vivid green ravine that makes up Frink Park. The network of trails connect Frink Park with the adjoining Leschi Park. Enjoy wandering beneath towering cedar trees, along the babbling creek and even through a rhododendron glen that blossoms in the spring.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Frink Park

properties.description: A short hike to an historic mining camp and recently restored buildings on the Colville National Forest.
properties.title: Gypsy Copper Camp

properties.description: A suburban walk around the Arlington Airport with forest, mountain and airport views and interpretative signage.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Arlington Airport Trail

properties.description: Nearly level double track runs alongside the Methow River alternating between open meadows and Ponderosa forests. Do this quiet trail as an out and back or connect to Jack's Trail for a nice loop.
properties.title: River Run

properties.description: A local spot to cool down when the temperatures soar in Walla Walla, Bennington Lake is a favored spot for hikers, birders, anglers, runners, and lots of local wildlife.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Bennington Lake

properties.description: Dishman Hills Natural Area's Eagle Peak Loop takes hikers to the highest point in the Natural Area for outstanding views of the surrounding area.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Natural Area - Eagle Peak Loop

properties.description: One of many trails in the network at Riverside State Park.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Trail 10

properties.description: Access to such a grand location, with such ease, should be illegal. For the low admission price of a half dozen miles one can gain entrance to a primordial world of receding glaciers, wildflower carpeted meadows, and purple mountains majesties. The last mile to the lake will test many hikers’ nerves but the rewards are worth it. This pond is an excellent destination unto itself. It is also a stepping stone to more ambitious cross country ramblings in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
properties.title: Peggy's Pond

properties.description: The High Ridge Trail gets lots of visitors in summer, since it starts near the beginning of the parking lot at the Visitors Center on top of Hurricane Ridge. Beginning as a paved trail and gradually turning into a dirt trail, it connects with the Sunrise Trail. It'll give you a good workout, and you'll have plenty of company in summer.
properties.title: High Ridge Trail

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Mount Challenger

properties.description: While still relatively steep, this new route up Mailbox Peak, built in part with help from WTA volunteers, offers a safer and more easily navigable way for folks to summit this formidable peak than the old trail.
properties.title: Mailbox Peak

properties.description: This hidden gem offers picnic tables and benches with views over Puget Sound, and access to a section of public beach. The trail network can be confusing. Familiarize yourself with the map ahead of time.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Marine View Park

properties.description: This 23-mile paved trail runs through the cities of Pasco, Richland, and Kennewick. Showcasing interpretive areas, the trail was conceived of and built to be an amenity for locals and an attraction for visitors. Dedicated to the woman who helped Lewis and Clark complete their expedition, the trail displays the stark shrub steppe environment, and the mighty Columbia River in a lovely outing accessible to all.
properties.title: Sacagawea Heritage Trail

properties.description: A long road walk through a logging operation is required to access this trailhead.
properties.title: Mount Jupiter

properties.description: Just a half mile off the Lemei Lake Trail is a gorgeous blue lake nestled in an old volcanic crater. Surrounded by trees, this is a sheltered refuge perfect for an overnight in Indian Heaven.
properties.title: Lake Wapiki

properties.description: Per the Snoqualmie Tribe, this trail has been closed to the public. Please refrain from visiting.
properties.title: Traditional Knowledge Trail

properties.description: Fine, in your face views, of Mount Rainier await hikers willing to hoof it 4,000 vertical feet up to the top of Mount Ararat from the Kautz Creek parking area.
properties.title: Mount Ararat

properties.description: This mostly-undeveloped park site near Yelm offers visitors waterfall views from a viewing deck and trails through the forest.
properties.title: Deschutes Falls Park

properties.description: Hike a short trail out of Holden Village to see gorgeous falls up close. The 2015 Wolverine Fire hit this area hard and you can see the devastation; if it's windy, be aware these trees could topple. A new viewing platform at the falls opened in 2018.
properties.title: Tenmile Falls

properties.description: Kayak Point Park is a lovely saltwater beach park with a short trail system located along the shores of picturesque Port Susan. It's great for family outings by the shore or an easy night of camping.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Kayak Point Park

properties.description: Shave off 2.5 miles of distance with this 0.5 mile shortcut on the Tiger Mountain Trail. Also access the West Tiger Railroad Grade Trail just 0.1 miles off the TMT.
properties.title: K-3 Trail

properties.description: This strenuous hike passes through varied climate zones of the Sawtooth Range, ending at stark Libby Lake, tucked into a talus bowl with a larch-fringed outlet. Enjoy the view, soak your feet, catch some fish, or — for those so inclined — backtrack to the cabin and scramble up Hoodoo Peak.
properties.title: Libby Lake

properties.description: Nearly 5 miles of easy hiking on trails and forest roads, with mountain and valley views.
properties.title: Chimacum Ridge Community Forest

properties.description: This forested trail leads to a fine campsite primed for exploring the base of Mount Adams.
properties.title: Muddy Meadows/Foggy Flat

properties.description: This entry describes the most direct approach to the Pratt River Trail, which starts by fording the Middle Fork Snoqualmie River.
properties.title: Pratt River Trail

properties.description: This section of the Redlining Heritage Trail traverses Seattle's Chinatown and International District. It is just adjacent to the 1-mile section through Pioneer Square and the nearly two-mile First Hill section.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redlining Heritage Trail - Chinatown / International District

properties.description: This quiet trail will lead you alongside Crofton Ridge and through the Mount Adams Wilderness. In the spring, lupine flowers welcome you into an area still recovering from a 2015 wildfire. Later in the summer, you can fill up on ripe blueberries and tiny wild strawberries.
properties.title: Crofton Butte

properties.description: Take a short jaunt in Tolmie State Park. Great for families or just a quick stretch of the legs.
properties.title: Tolmie State Park - Four Cedars Trail

properties.description: A half-mile loop off Highway 20 in Deception Pass State Park, the Lottie Point loop is a nice forest walk in this popular location.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - Lottie Point Loop

properties.description: A hidden gem of Snohomish County — whether you do a couple of miles or the whole trek to Boulder Lake, there's plenty for all to enjoy. Hikers will be surrounded by a bounty of wild berries in the summer and misty Pacific Northwest clouds in the spring and fall. The trail has been quietly closed for several seasons; now, hikers can find tranquil solitude with an amazing lake!
properties.title: Boulder Lake

properties.description: Walk along a ridge to a couple of high points in Central Washington, with gigantic views in all directions.
properties.title: Moses Stool - Badger Mountain

properties.description: Spend some time in the quiet countryside on a wide gravel trail just a few miles away from the city of Everett.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Fobes-Ebey Slough Dike Road Trail

properties.description: A tough climb on loose, small rock at a very steep grade offering views from the Strait of Juan de Fuca to Glacier Peak, Mount Rainier and The Brothers. Route finding experience required.
properties.title: Buckhorn Mountain

properties.description: This spectacular, short trail gets lots of love during its short hiking season. Accessible for less than three months each year, hordes of hikers and tourists take to it as the snow finally begins to melt.
properties.title: Artist Ridge - Huntoon Point

properties.description: Bauerman Ridge is located in the north eastern region of the Pasayten Wilderness and can be reached by several routes.
properties.title: Bauerman Ridge

properties.description: The route to Jack Mountain is a Class 5 and above and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Jack Mountain

properties.description: A beautiful granite basin housing two sparkling lakes and big views. Explorations abound with nearly a dozen lakes to look down upon or explore around.
properties.title: Tuck and Robin Lakes

properties.description: You'll enjoy relative silence on this hushed snowshoe along a Forest Service road near Mount Rainier. As you hike, look closely for elk signs, then look up to see gorgeous views of Sun Top and The Mountain standing in all her glory (that is, if she isn't hiding behind clouds).
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Dalles Ridge Snowshoe

properties.description: Looking for adventure and solitude? Angry Mountain is the destination for you, though trail conditions may make put you in the mood the mountain is named for. It's a steep, challenging climb from Forest Road 21, but the payoff comes miles later, when you finally gain the ridge crest separating two glaciated valleys.
properties.title: Angry Mountain

properties.description: Trekking quietly is easy on this gentle woodland trail, allowing you to take advantage of prime wildlife spotting.
properties.title: Cussed Hollow

properties.description: Ueland Tree Farm is a parcel of private property that is made available to the public for responsible, non-motorized recreation.
properties.title: Ueland Tree Farm

properties.description: Take a stroll on the sunny, warm slopes of Studhorse Mountain just outside of Winthrop. This hike is usually among the first to melt out and bloom in the spring, providing much needed forage for the mule deer population. An easy 2.5 mile loop gives great views of the Sawtooth/Chelan Wilderness and Winthrop’s downtown is at your feet.
properties.title: Meadowlark Natural Area

properties.description: A short hike not far from Joseph, OR, gets you to a fun little waterfall perhaps perfect for a hot day.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Falls Creek Falls (Joseph, OR)

properties.description: Mount Baldy is a summit with excellent views along the I-90 corridor near Easton. The trailhead is little more than an hour from Seattle.
properties.title: Mount Baldy

properties.description: A short, graveled trail wanders through Sternwheeler Park in La Center.
properties.title: Breeze Creek Trail

properties.description: Breathe in the sea spray on this anything-but-disappointing hike out to the scenic Cape Disappointment Lighthouse, which offers a trail through a coastal forest and glimpses of the powerful Pacific Ocean.
properties.title: Cape Disappointment State Park - Cape Disappointment Lighthouse

properties.description: The hike to Lena Lake is a mild to moderate hike through old- and second-growth forest to a large beautiful lake, where the traffic on the trail is evidence of its beauty.
properties.title: Lena Lake

properties.description: In the fast growing area of north Spokane, this natural area on the banks of the Little Spokane River is a welcome escape. A couple different loop trails circle through the ponderosa forest in the uplands, and a spur trail splits off to head down to the river. There is about a half mile of shoreline to explore.
properties.title: Haynes Estate Conservation Area

properties.description: Hike along a knife's edge to Eldorado Peak. Climbing experience and equipment required.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Eldorado Peak

properties.description: Hike through a diverse century-old second-growth forest with a dense canopy to the undeveloped shoreline of Lake Washington. This historic 316-acre state park, nestled in the midst of the Seattle metropolitan area, has playground facilities for children, picnic areas, trails for mountain bikers and fields for sports teams as well.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Saint Edward State Park

properties.description: Rainbow Falls State Park is an island remnant of exquisite old growth forest in the upper Chehalis Valley, with a small cascade as the centerpiece of the park. Surrounding a half-mile stretch of the Chehalis River, this fragile patch of stunning Douglas fir, western hemlock, and western redcedar is among the last, albeit diminished, stores of Washington heritage to pass onto the future forest of the region.
properties.title: Rainbow Falls State Park

properties.description: If you want both a walk in the sunshine and a walk through the trees, Mesatchee Creek is the place to go! Keep your feet dry on the turnpikes and bridge made by WTA.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Mesatchee Creek

properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Herman Creek

properties.description: The Freezeout Ridge trail is located in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest.
properties.title: Freezeout Ridge

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Klawatti Peak

properties.description: There are two routes to Kalama Falls; the shorter route starts at a two-track gravel road and goes through the Merrill Lake Wildlife Area.
properties.title: Merrill Lake Conservation Area - Kalama River Falls

properties.description: The Tumac plateau is a wonderland of rolling sub-alpine forest broken by wildflower meadows, ponds, and lake after lake. The 14-mile loolipop loop to Dumbbell Lake will take you past seven lakes large enough to have been named along with many smaller ponds and marshes that provide some of the finest elk, trout, and mosquito habitat in the Cascades.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Dumbbell Lake

properties.description: Marckworth Forest offers some wonderful walking among forest, marshes, and rumpled rocky hills, as long as you're ok doing your own routefinding on logging roads. It's a quiet, little known and infrequently visited spot, less than an hour's drive from Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Marckworth Forest

properties.description: The Ice Cave and Natural Bridges are two short nature trails near the Peterson Prairie Campground in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest that are fascinating to children and not as well known as they deserve to be. This is also a popular area to cross country ski and snowshoe in winter.
properties.title: Ice Cave - Natural Bridges Nature Trails

properties.description: This trail offers passage through magnificent old growth forest, and past sparkling clear streams. It may not be as scenic as other trails in the area, but it requires no parking pass or entrance fee to enjoy the beauty of Mount Rainier.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Deer Creek to Tipsoo Lake

properties.description: This 82-acre park sits right on the water, providing visitors with nearly half a mile of shoreline and 2 miles of trails.
properties.title: Sunrise Beach Park

properties.description: What looks good on paper doesn’t always reflect reality.  The Eureka Creek Trail would be part of a fine loop except for the fact the trail is only maintained on the ends and has been abandoned in the middle.  It provides access to the Ferguson Lake Trail on the southern end.  The northern end accesses Fred’s Lake and Lake Doris.
properties.title: Eureka Creek

properties.description: The Military Ridge Trail is part of the vast Cougar Mountain trail network. The trail is a connector trail, so it can only be reached via other trails in the area and does not have its own trailhead.
properties.title: Military Ridge

properties.description: The short Layser Cave interpretive trail is a quick detour off the main route south of Randle that transports visitors into the Gifford Pinchot National Forest. The trail takes just a half-hour to hike and provides a nice immersion into the human history of the area.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Layser Cave

properties.description: The Green Lake Trail is a moderately strenuous but relatively short hike to a pocket lake set among a rare high-elevation rain forest. The trail's wide, ambitious grade rewards accordingly for your efforts, ascending through stands of humbling firs, passing a picturesque waterfall, and ending on the shore of a lovely mountain lake.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Green Lake

properties.description: One of the most popular hikes on the Colville National Forest is the short but challenging hike to the summit of Columbia Mountain, where vistas of surrounding mountains, wildflowers and one of the oldest fire lookouts in the state await you.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Columbia Mountain

properties.description: Boulder River leads to magnificent views of Napeequa Valley and the Glacier Peak Wilderness.
properties.title: Boulder Creek

properties.description: If the rugged trek to Pinnacle Lake is too much, but you still want a nice hike to an alpine lake, try Bear Lake. The Pinnacle Lake trail passes Bear Lake, which makes a great destination for new hikers, or those who just want a short stroll.
properties.title: Bear Lake

properties.description: Barclay Lake offers something for almost everyone: a well-maintained trail that is accessible to beginners and children, stunning mountain views, mycology, camping, a serene alpine lake, and a staging area for challenging adventures in the 106,000-acre Wild Sky Wilderness. Keep your camera charged, as this popular pathway in the shadow of Baring Mountain offers many photo opportunities.
properties.title: Barclay Lake

properties.description: Climb a peak near Mount Rainier for infrequently seen views of Washington's most famous peak. Climbing experience and equipment required.
properties.title: Iron Mountain

properties.description: Let the car take care of most of the climbing, then enjoy this gently contouring trail that begins in forest and passes through thickets of huckleberries before arriving in the upper grassy meadows that provide spectacular views of the surrounding peaks in the Selkirk range.
properties.title: Grassy Top

properties.description: This hike is full of the best things the Columbia Gorge has to offer: easy access and parking, well-maintained trail, wildflowers galore, two waterfalls, and views to knock off your sweaty socks.  It’s a long journey at about 7.5 miles, and steep in places, but nothing a healthy dog, child or senior citizen can’t do. You’ll meet all of these smiling folks on this hike during the peak seasons.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Hamilton Mountain

properties.description: This short stretch of a much longer trail is open to all users, horse, hiker, 4WD… Don’t let this put you off, though — everyone here has the same goal to see some amazing country.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Western Rim National Recreation Trail - Warnock Corrals to Grassy Knoll

properties.description: This local location for after-work hiking in Spokane boasts nearly 25 miles of trails. From a flat traverse high above the railroad tracks to longer loops; there are many possible outings to be done at South Hill.
properties.title: South Hill Bluff

properties.description: Take a short hike to the best views of the Skagit flats and the bay, as well as the Cascades to the east, the Olympics to the west, and Rainier to the south.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Craft Island

properties.description: Starting in well-protected sub-alpine wilderness and descending into heavily-logged, privately-owned land, this stretch of the PCT offers a dramatic illustration of the effects of public land protection and private industry on Washington's landscape.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) Section I - White Pass to Snoqualmie Pass

properties.description: This long, meandering hike heads upstream along the Middle Fork of the Snoqualmie River, offering a long day hike, or a great beginning backpacking experience.
properties.title: Middle Fork Snoqualmie River

properties.description: Considered one of the best loop hikes in Mount Rainier National Park, the trail through the alpine meadows of Spray and Seattle Parks blazes with a bounty of seasonal wildflowers. Throw in an ample serving of glassy tarns, a couple of wispy waterfalls, an optional side trip to Carbon Glacier and a forested stroll up Ipsut Creek, and you have a photographer’s dreamland.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Spray Park Loop

properties.description: This sweet little loop leaves from the Sunrise Visitor Center at Mount Rainier and encompasses a lovely little lake, an unexpected campsite, and views of the mountain's eastern flanks and glaciers.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Shadow Lake - Sunrise Camp Loop

properties.description: Explorer Falls is in the watershed for the City of Everett.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Explorer Falls

properties.description: You’ve done Sauk Mountain and marveled at the fabulous views, now hike down to the delightful little lake you see from the top! The trail is a bit rough and overgrown, but the lake is a quiet alternative to the busy trail above.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Sauk Lake

properties.description: This short loop hike showcases the dry Hells Canyon environment and a pretty cool fire lookout tower.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Hat Point Lookout (Oregon)

properties.description: Horseshoe Mountain is a peak in the Pasayten Wilderness near the Canadian Border, overlooking Horseshoe Basin. With expansive views into Canada and of the eastern Pasayten.
properties.title: Horseshoe Mountain

properties.description: Some of the biggest, oldest trees in the Washington Cascades stand tall in the Grove of the Patriarchs. These silent old men of moss tower overhead, with a few lying down to show us just how massive the trunks really are. The Grove resides in a low, boggy area across the Ohanapecosh River, so you'll need to cross a sweet little suspension bridge to get there, offering you a chance to enjoy a bit of adventure on this simple little trail. Youngsters typically love the bridge, and kids of all ages marvel at the massive trees.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Grove of the Patriarchs Loop

properties.description: This trail in Tacoma follows Puget Creek through a gulch just above Commencement Bay.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Puget Creek Natural Area

properties.description: Hike this 7.4 mile forested trail in the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness. You'll wander among gorgeous stands of ponderosa pines and larches, reaching 7,480 feet at Fish Creek Pass.
properties.title: West Fork Buttermilk

properties.description: Cascading waterfalls from the numerous streams and the frequent tarns located along the way make this an enjoyable hike. Mountain goats are known to frequent the area. During the late summer, ripe huckleberries can be found at the pass. But it comes at a cost -- a steep scramble on an unmaintained trail.
properties.title: Squire Creek Pass via Eight-mile Trail

properties.description: The route to Tower Mountain is a Class 3 and involved exposed scrambling. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Tower Mountain

properties.description: Spade Lake is a lovely, lonesome lake nestled in a rocky cirque high on Mount Daniel. It is one of the most remote lakes in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
properties.title: Spade Lake

properties.description: Highlands SnoPark features over 30k of groomed Nordic ski trails as well as nearby snowshoe trails for excellent winter recreation opportunities in the Columbia Highlands.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Highlands SnoPark

properties.description: The nice thing about old aircraft navigation beacon sites is that they always afford a decent view. The trail to Kachess Beacon is steep much of the way, but it is easy to get to, well-shaded, and less than three miles long.
properties.title: Kachess Ridge / Kachess Beacon

properties.description: A short but steep climb on the Wonderland Trail from a campground in Mount Rainier National Park to the Sunrise Visitor Center area.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: White River to Sunrise

properties.description: Find spring wildflowers and one of the best ridge hikes in the Gorge; just be prepared for a difficult drive to get there. While Dog Mountain to the south is crowded, you’ll have these sweeping vistas to yourself. WTA volunteers have put in many hours to improve this trail.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Augspurger Mountain - North

properties.description: The Swauk Campground turns into a winter recreation wonderland in snow, with plenty of space to explore on your snowshoes or cross-country skis.
properties.title: Swauk Campground Snowshoe

properties.description: This short, sweet loop with spring flowers, old-growth trees and views of the Okanogan Highlands is just waiting to be explored.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Virginia Lilly

properties.description: Bresemann Forest is a 70-acre park located between Spanaway and Parkland. There is an extensive network of trails here where hikers can pick and choose to make a route that works for them.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bresemann Forest

properties.description: Connect to Horseshoe Mountain on this scenic ridge trail that takes you through a lodgepole pine forest and some of the most spectacular views in the Pasayten Wilderness.
properties.title: Albert Camp

properties.description: The Pacific Northwest Trail is a 1,200-mile linear trail that stretches from Glacier National Park in Montana to Cape Alava on the Pacific Ocean in the Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Pacific Northwest Trail

properties.description: This trail loops through two forests that stand side by side, but are separated in age by 2,000 years. One forest is old-growth Douglas-fir and western redcedar, and the other is a young forest that was originally engulfed by lava flows from an eruption of Mount St. Helens over two millennia ago.
properties.title: Trail of Two Forests

properties.description: Lined with waterfalls, stunning basalt cliffs and plenty of spots to turn around, the Oneonta Trail is a wonderful destination for a day hike, and even includes campsites for backpacking. However, the trail was part of the Eagle Creek Fire, so the upper section of the trail is in a former burn; unideal to hike in windy conditions.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Oneonta Trail to Triple Falls

properties.description: Even though the 2012 Table Mountain Fire changed the formerly picturesque Haney Meadows area, the views above the meadows are still spectacular.  This lollipop loop consists of marked ski trail, snowmobile trail (short) and cross-country in the forest, along with a 0.5-mile walk along the ridge crest with expansive views to the west.
properties.title: Haney Meadow Loop Snowshoe

properties.description: This is one of the best day hikes for larch-spotting in the fall. In the summer, enjoy the reward of swimming or fishing after a steep climb. Scatter Lake is also an excellent destination for an overnight backpack.
properties.title: Scatter Lake

properties.description: Take this short one-mile stroll around an interpretive trail near the base of Mount Finlayson on San Juan Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Jakle's Lagoon

properties.description: Mount Beljica is just outside the boundary of Mount Rainier National Park, so you can bring your dog and still experience a well-kept trail leading to astounding views of Washington's tallest mountain.
properties.title: Mount Beljica

properties.description: Even without a tour guide, this interpretative trail has plenty to offer hikers who enjoy learning about local history. The trail starts next to Saint Paul's Mission, built around 1847 at the Fort Colville fur-trading site. From there it goes to an overlook of the Kettle Falls site, though the falls are now submerged beneath Lake Roosevelt.
properties.title: Mission Point Trail

properties.description: Explore many miles of trails in the West Duwamish Greenbelt - a local park in West Seattle that is best accessed by the various bus lines that service it.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: West Duwamish Greenbelt Trails

properties.description: Mount Adams, at 12,276 feet, dominates the South Cascades and provides the most dramatic scenery of the region. The mountain is a standout destination also for the massive basalt lava beds that cover large portions of the surrounding landscape. This relatively young volcano initially formed nearly a million years ago, about 3 miles southeast of its current location. That first cone was ground down by glaciers during the long succession of ice ages that swept the region, while the "hot spot" that gave birth to the mountain shifted northwest as plate tectonics and continental drift rearranged the landscape.
properties.title: Muddy Fork Lava Bed

properties.description: There are many reasons – besides its proximity to Seattle – why Mount Si is the most popular hike in the state: beautiful views, wildlife (some of it not so wild), old-growth forest and a dramatic summit worthy of a more remote peak. Rising dramatically above the Snoqualmie Valley, it serves as a literal and figurative gateway to the Cascades for thousands of hikers.
properties.title: Mount Si

properties.description: Visit the remains of an old mining town in a basin surrounded by high peaks. Climb to Silver Lake nestled under the steep side of Silvertip Peak with good camping and good views of surrounding peaks.
properties.title: Silver Lake - Monte Cristo

properties.description: A scramble and climbing route to the summit of a mountain in the Olympic range. Climbing gear and expertise required.
properties.title: The Brothers

properties.description: A short, steep and rough ridgeline ascent to a summit with great views up and down the Yakima River Canyon.
properties.title: Rattlesnake Dance Ridge Trail

properties.description: This section of the Wonderland Trail, which begins at Box Canyon, continues along the Cowlitz Divide, and eventually concludes in the valley that houses Indian Bar, will certainly test your trail stamina. But the rewards for all of your efforts are plentiful: swaths of old-growth forests, bountiful berries (when in season), rolling alpine meadows, an epic in-your-face view of Mount Rainier, and finally, the rushing waters of the Ohanapecosh River and Wauhaukaupauken Falls, which offer a cooling respite after your long, and sometimes arduous, climb and descent into this famed valley.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Indian Bar - Cowlitz Divide

properties.description: A long, meandering hike in Mount Rainier National Park that tours Tolmie Creek, August and Virginia Peaks, and Martin Peak.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Alki Crest

properties.description: This is a fairly flat route with views of Mount Rainier and a diverse mixture of flowers in the spring. Look for hillsides tinted pink in May as Big Headed Clover and Hedgehog Cacti bloom on the slopes.
properties.title: Whiskey Dick Wildlife Area - Backcountry Trail

properties.description: Bird's-eye views of the stunning Yakima Canyon, wildflower fields for days, and a line of ragged fenceposts marching all the way along the trail -- the Yakima Skyline Trail is a great conditioner, or extend it to a full day hike.
properties.title: Yakima Skyline Trail

properties.description: Historically, this trail provided good access for the landscape west of the popular Enchantments area. However, a lack of trail maintenance and winter storm damage has rendered the route almost unhikeable.
properties.title: North Fork Chiwaukum River

properties.description: Z Lake is a short hike to a small narrow lake surrounded by shrub-steppe habitat teeming with wildlife and wildflowers.
properties.title: Z Lake

properties.description: Follow a gentle, stroller-friendly slope for about a mile along the eastern and northern shores of scenic Lake Ballinger. You can extend your walk by continuing west along Lakeview Drive to the nearby Interurban Trail, or head east to explore the gravel forested path through Terrace Creek Park
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lakeview Trail

properties.description: This comfortable, easy to follow trail winds through intermittent old growth, occasional remnants of the past, and alongside a sometimes babbling and other times a crashing creek. You will follow the original Snoqualmie Pass Wagon Road, and it is possible to connect with the trail to Franklin Falls for a scenic and delightful 2-mile loop.
properties.title: Wagon Road Trail

properties.description: A former archaeological site, Marmes Pond is now a destination for fishermen and hikers looking for a short exploration of the Channeled Scablands.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Lyons Ferry State Park - Marmes Pond

properties.description: Key Central Forest is 480 acres. It’s large but gets relatively little use. There are two main entrances that are connected by an old access road which now functions as the main trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Key Central Forest

properties.description: This route at Catherine Creek takes hikers past a natural arch and into the higher country around the meadows at Catherine Creek.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Catherine Creek Loop

properties.description: The Upper Dungeness Trail is a gateway trail. It is not only a great hike all by itself --on the way to its end at Marmot Pass it links to other high reward hikes in the northeast Olympics – Royal Basin, Goat Lake, Heather Creek, and Home Lake. From Marmot Pass one can continue to either the Upper Big Quilcene or Tubal Cain Trail.
properties.title: Marmot Pass via Upper Dungeness River Trail

properties.description: Deer Park is rarely accessible by vehicle in the winter. Hikers will likely have to undertake a long road walk to access Deer Park and Blue Mountain.
properties.title: Blue Mountain - Deer Park Snowshoe

properties.description: A beautiful city beach park at an important historic location that is wheelchair-accessible (except the beach). Great place for a picnic, sunset or exploring the beach.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Mukilteo Lighthouse Park

properties.description: This loop takes you into the high country of the Pasayten wilderness to Sunny Pass, the to another pass through Horsehoe Mountain and Pick Peak, and over Windy Peak.
properties.title: Windy Peak Loop

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Ptarmigan Ridge (Mount Rainier)

properties.description: Once the center of mining activity in Yakima County, Copper City served 42 active mining claims from 1907 to 1942. The founders of the town hoped to boom when the railroad came through, but the tracks were never put down.  Walk the old mine-to-market road into town, where only the collapsed remains of a few buildings remain.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Copper City Ghost Town

properties.description: The Shedroof Divide offers some of the best views in northeast Washington as it traverses the wild high country of the Salmo-Priest Wilderness.
properties.title: Shedroof Divide

properties.description: Experience the beautiful shores of Whidbey Island along this waterfront park's seawall walkway and pebble beach.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Seawall Park

properties.description: The Willow Lake Trail is part of the East Bank Trail in the North Cascades National Park. Willow Lake is a small lake along the route and sits on the north end of Ross Lake.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Willow Lake Trail
Antoine Peak Conservation Area - Lost Apple

properties.description: Reachable only by boat, Turn Island is a small island off the east side of San Juan Island, near Friday Harbor. This loop trail offers visitors the opportunity to hike the perimeter of the island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Turn Island Marine State Park Loop

properties.description: Wedge Mountain is a non-system trail (or a social trail) that allows hikers to scramble to the summit of a mountain outside Leavenworth. The road to the trailhead is rough, and the route is quite steep in places.
properties.title: Wedge Mountain

properties.description: Walk along a quiet flat grassy trail with plenty of space to take picnic breaks in some quiet, not far from the city.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: South Fork County Park

properties.description: The scenic Ellen Davis Trail goes on and off the street to connect the Burnt Bridge Creek Greenway Trail at Leverich Park to St. James Road. This muti-purpose trail, open from 7:00 a.m. to dusk, is mostly flat, but it does have a few steep switchbacks.
properties.title: Ellen Davis Trail

properties.description: A little-known summit south of I-90. Route finding skills and climbing equipment are necessary to achieve the summit.
properties.title: Olallie Mountain Snowshoe

properties.description: Boasting views of massive Cascade volcanoes, constellations of wildflowers, and an embarrassment of huckleberries, the Juniper Ridge Trail offers an excellent opportunity for a backpacking trip, complete with views or shorter day hikes from the ridge.
properties.title: Juniper Ridge

properties.description: This forested trail to a small, secluded lake — uniquely set on a ridge with a few campsites— provides an easy day hike or backpack trip.
properties.title: Bluff Lake

properties.description: Stephenson Canyon Loop is a great trail for a quick dip into nature in an urban landscape — complete with a forested canyon, a small creek and a seasonal waterfall.
properties.title: Stephenson Canyon

properties.description: Cavanaugh Pond Natural Area is on the banks of the Cedar River near the city of Renton. A short, 0.4-mile, trail extends from the parking area to a beach along the river.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cavanaugh Pond Natural Area

properties.description: A trail on the west side of Squak Mountain. Part of the Phil's Trail - Thrush Gap Loop, and connects to Old Griz, Summit Trail, May Valley Loop, and East Side Trail.
properties.title: Phil's Creek

properties.description: Not every hike is pristine or an easy trek, and Bessemer fits this definition. This trail is almost completely a logging road, much of which is still active. If you are still reading, let me say it is not without its charms. The forest is recovering, views of the Snoqualmie region are fantastic, and due to its low elevation it is accessible virtually year-round.
properties.title: Bessemer Mountain

properties.description: The Capitol State Forest – Porter Trail is 13 miles long, so you can take a long hike through the forest or turn around whenever you please. Along the way, you will find wetlands, railroad grades, native plants and even a lovely view of the Chehalis River Valley.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Porter Trail

properties.description: The Walupt Lake Loop offers a long hike along a lake, across a creek, and through green bottomlands to peek-a-boo views of the Goat Rocks. Then follow it back down through forest and to the shores of Walupt Lake for a refreshing post-hike dip!
properties.title: Walupt Lake Loop

properties.description: Approach a calm, quiet lake on a rugged canyon trail, where wildflowers bloom in spring, and you can rest lakeside in the heat of the summer.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Emerald Lake via Deadman Trailhead

properties.description: This steep trail goes from Forest Road 4517-117 to the Cle Elum Ridge Trail. Hike up switchbacks beneath a forest of ponderosa pine and fir trees to reach some spectacular views of the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. Be sure to bring waterproof shoes, as the creek comes over the trail in places.
properties.title: Granite Creek

properties.description: Following an abandoned trail, Howson Creek provides an enjoyable hike in light forest. The trail is steep and the tread is narrow, but it offers progressively better views above 4000 feet, north toward Thorp Mountain and the Snoqualmie Peaks, especially from West Sasse Peak.
properties.title: Howson Creek

properties.description: Bring out some waterproof shoes and explore both forest and wetlands–right in your neighborhood.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Bingaman Pond Nature Area

properties.description: This is not an official Forest Service trail. The route is not maintained and requires route-finding skills to navigate.
properties.title: Hall Point

properties.description: Hike a steep trail up to a high pass in the Wenatchee mountains above the upper Cle Elum River.
properties.title: North Scatter Creek

properties.description: Enjoy up-close, breathtaking views of Mount Shuksan’s west face, along with views of Fisher Chimney, the upper and lower Curtis Glacier, as well as Mount Baker from the trail to Lake Ann. The lake in a rocky basin, in the midst of this spectacular scenery. On some days you can hear ice echoing through the valley as it crashes down the face of Mount Shuksan. This is a late season hike, as snow can linger here into August.
properties.title: Lake Ann (Mount Baker Highway)

properties.description: This pleasant Vancouver trail follows Burnt Bridge Creek through a variety of landscapes, including open grasslands, wetlands, and forests. Nature lovers use the trail to watch waterfowl, listen to song birds, and perhaps spot a coyote or deer. The eight-mile greenbelt has multiple access points, allowing this hard-surfaced trail to be conveniently divided into sections.
properties.title: Burnt Bridge Creek Greenway Trail

properties.description: Whether you’re camping nearby or just out for a day, the trail around peaceful Swan Lake makes a beautiful outing. Loons and beavers make this place home.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Swan Lake

properties.description: Beacon Rock's native name is "Che-Che-op-tin," which translates to "the navel of the world." Native Americans weren't far off in their comparison, since the 848-foot basalt column once formed the core, or belly, of an ancient volcano.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Beacon Rock

properties.description: This trail features ridgetop views and numerous steep switchbacks through forest and open meadows. Beginning at the Blackpine Trailhead, it climbs through second-growth forest to wide open views of the Icicle Ridge area and ends at the Snowall-Cradle Lake trail.
properties.title: Blackjack Ridge

properties.description: Enjoy a swim in a nice quiet lake surrounded by forest. Due to the narrow road, lack of spectacular scenery and few campsites, this lake does not get as many visitors as other hikes in the area do. The trail receives little maintenance so it is a bit rough, but it is easily followed.
properties.title: Peek-a-Boo Lake

properties.description: In spite of old-growth trees and stunning views of waterfalls and mountains, this trail is rarely visited. The road is rough, but if you're willing to brave it, you'll be rewarded with a beautiful, quiet hike on this trail.
properties.title: Rock Creek Falls

properties.description: Monument 78 can be found along the Pacific Crest Trail at the US-Canadian Border.
properties.title: Monument 78

properties.description: A forest walk near the Bainbridge Island Ferry Terminal featuring forest, a pond and one of the new trolls. This entry includes the walk from the ferry terminal.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Sakai Park

properties.description: Troublesome Mountain is a modest peak scramble that can be reached via the Index-Galena Road.
properties.title: Troublesome Mountain

properties.description: This connector trail follows the historic abandoned Seattle Lake Shore & Eastern Railway grade from Issaquah to the town of Preston through the Mountains to Sound Greenway.
properties.title: Issaquah - Preston Trail

properties.description: Hike a trail built mostly of boardwalk planking through peaty bogs beside three quiet little lakes. As you hike, enjoy the many plants and animals that make the lowland bog environment home.
properties.title: Ashland Lakes

properties.description: WTA has worked on trails in this 552-acre conservation area to help prevent erosion. Over 7 miles of trail wind throughout the property, exploring canyons that embrace year-round springs and climbing ridge tops with views of Liberty Lake, Mount Spokane, and Saltese Flats.
properties.title: Saltese Uplands

properties.description: The route to Damnation Peak is a Class 3 and involved exposed scrambling. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Damnation Peak

properties.description: On this remote hike in the Colville National Forest, you'll find wooded trails and panoramic views of the Columbia River, the Pend Oreille Valley, and Deep Creek.
properties.title: Sherlock Peak

properties.description: Primarily used by motorized users, this trail climbs gradually to a scenic sub-alpine ridge, with views of Mount St. Helens, Mount Rainier, and the Goat Rocks. Shaded from top to bottom, but still quite strenuous, Bishop Ridge makes for a unique trip in a seldom-hiked part of Washington.
properties.title: Bishop Ridge

properties.description: The West Boundary Trail is one of the remaining fragments of the historic Boundary Trail that allowed rangers to patrol the perimeter of Mount Rainier National Park. Now an out-and-back, the trail is moderately popular despite its brutally steep grade. The lush rainforest, delightful cascades and potential to add a summit to the day give this hike reason to investigate.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: West Boundary Trail

properties.description: Easy access and a gentle grade make this a great wildlife-viewing hike for all ability levels.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sherman Point Loop

properties.description: Hike along a lush green valley wall above Goat Creek to Cathedral Falls. Because this part is so infrequently visited, it's possible you won't see another soul on the trail, meaning you'll get to have the incredible falls all to yourself.
properties.title: Cathedral Falls

properties.description: Mount Custer is a mountain within the norther reaches North Cascades National Park and can be reached via the Chilliwack Lake Forest Service Road in Canada.
properties.title: Mount Custer

properties.description: A small neighborhood park on a hillside in the Columbia City region of Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake People Park (Xacua'bs)

properties.description: A gorgeous trail accessible from the Harvey Manning trailhead on Cougar Mountain. Enjoy wildflowers, as well as the notable "Fantastic Erratic" glacier boulder.
properties.title: Shangri La

properties.description: A blacktop trail with some gravel and dirt sections that meanders along the Columbia River in Richland. Start or end at Columbia Point Marina Park at the south end or USS Triton Submarine Memorial Park in the north. The 7-mile trail has many benches along the way to take a breather and soak up the beauty of the fast-moving Columbia.
properties.title: Riverfront Trail

properties.description: The center parcel of three Big Rock Parks in Sammamish, Central Big Rock Park has trails, a treehouse, a heritage garden, even an audio tour. It's a fantastic little spot for kids and adults alike to explore.
properties.title: Big Rock Park - Central

properties.description: A short and steep hike in the woods leads to the top of Pyramid Peak, where the hiker is rewarded with an expansive southerly view of the Greenwater River Valley.  From this former lookout’s rocky perch, Mount Rainier dominates the skyline to the southwest.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Pyramid Peak

properties.description: The trail from Oil City starts out as a short forest jaunt along the Hoh River, and ends at the sandy shores of the Pacific Ocean.
properties.title: Oil City

properties.description: The Fire and Ice trail is the Mount Baker area's premiere interpretive trail, telling the story of how glaciers and volcanoes shaped this impressive place.
properties.title: Fire and Ice Trail

properties.description: While this is a popular location to snowshoe in wintertime, there is high risk in winter from avalanches off the mountain that feeds these caves. Keep to the main trail, and do not venture onto the snowfields at the end of the route.
properties.title: Big Four Ice Caves Snowshoe

properties.description: If you're looking for a place to stretch your legs while traveling over Highway 20 near Sherman Pass, the Log Flume interpretative trail is the perfect choice. Interpretative signs along the route illustrate the dangers of early logging operations, as well as provide information on how the surrounding terrain has been shaped by wildfire.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Log Flume

properties.description: The route to Panorama Point in the snow can vary depending on how much snow is on the mountain, and how many other visitors have tromped a path up the hillside. One thing is certain — you'll want to consult the Paradise Green Trails map No. 270S, which includes both summer and snowshoe routes for the area.
properties.title: Panorama Point Snowshoe

properties.description: The Klondike Swamp Trail traverses much of what is special about Cougar Mountain Park, utilizing old logging roads and railroad grades that take you through charming second growth forest. The loop is easily accessed from the Sky Country Trailhead in Bellevue, and offers a nearly level grade for most of the journey.
properties.title: Klondike Swamp

properties.description: At the end of the Wolf Creek Trail lies a magnificently remote place: Gardner Meadows, a subalpine valley of old growth firs and myriad other plant and animal life. Once the snow melts, it is a bonanza of wildflowers and a haven for Columbian ground squirrels, birds, deer, and other animals.
properties.title: Wolf Creek

properties.description: A mix of history and natural wonder pervades in this park where you can hike along a forested lagoon out to a clearing on Puget Sound.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Blakely Harbor Park Trail

properties.description: This route provides both spectacular views and solitude at the summit, but keep in mind trail etiquette. You'll likely share the trail with skiers enjoying the groomed route.
properties.title: Amabilis Mountain Snowshoe

properties.description: As the largest urban park in Pierce County, the network of roads and trails weaving through the forest preserve provides a quiet retreat for joggers, cyclists, and hikers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Point Defiance Park

properties.description: This short and sweet little hike to Round Mountain offers nice views, and a good half-day hike for those looking to explore the Goat Rocks Wilderness while staying at a nearby resort. Alternatively, you can tack it onto a longer day, make it a thru-hike, or even a side trip while hiking the PCT. For such a low-key destination, it’s remarkably accessible.
properties.title: Round Mountain

properties.description: At 5605 feet of elevation, Silver Peak is the tallest mountain guarding the southern wall of Snoqualmie Pass. Silver Peak has more than 2000 feet of prominence and provides commanding, panoramic views of the eastern end of Snoqualmie Pass and the surrounding mountains and lakes.
properties.title: Silver Peak

properties.description: This SnoPark at the northern end of the Kettle Crest offers 9 kilometers of groomed Nordic ski trails as well as non-groomed ski routes.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Deer Creek/Boulder SnoPark

properties.description: A trail ascending from the Methow valley floor towards Goat Wall, Spokane Gulch is a local favorite. Trails and roads continue on up to Flagg Mountain to the south or Goat Peak's lookout 4000 feet above the valley floor.
properties.title: Spokane Gulch

properties.description: A short trail that offers an hour or so of pleasant hiking near the Sleeping Lady resort in Leavenworth.
properties.title: Chihuly Trail

properties.description: Vanson Peak is a summit located within the northeastern reaches of the Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument. Reachable as a day hike, it features a small rock outcropping and provides commanding views of Mount Rainier, Mount Adams and nearby Riffe Lake. While it’s an exciting destination itself, the journey to and from this special viewpoint also presents many options for camping and sightseeing.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Vanson Peak via Goat Mountain

properties.description: This trek to a former lookout site ambles past lakes, up through quiet forest, and into the popular Goat Rocks Wilderness.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Clear Lost Trail to Lost Lake Lookout

properties.description: Castle Peak is a very prominent peak in the northwestern portion of the Pasayten Wilderness. It can be reached several ways, from Provincial Park on the north, the PCT on the west or Freezeout Creek on the east.
properties.title: Castle Peak

properties.description: This beautiful hike takes you through a canopy of old growth trees until you find yourself in a high alpine meadow with small quiet lakes. Yes it's gorgeous but this hike isn't easy.
properties.title: Black & White Lakes

properties.description: Humble Sand Lake and its neighboring Deer Lake, provide snowshoers and backcountry skiers a wintry getaway along the Pacific Crest Trail a short distance away from the bustle of the White Pass ski resort and groomed ski trails.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Sand Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: Located just off the pavement, this short and easy hike offers good views of the namesake falls, along with glimpses of Hall Mountain in the distance. Come in spring for the highest water volume, seek shade and mist in summer, and return in fall for the best foliage color.
properties.title: Elk Creek Falls

properties.description: Explore an abandoned tungsten mine as you connect between the Chewuch Trail and Boundary Trail. Enjoy views of mountain peaks, meadows, and refreshing streams along the way.
properties.title: Tungsten

properties.description: The Yakima Greenway is a 10-mile paved trail along the Yakima and Naches Rivers with a mix of developed parks, fishing lakes, boat landings, picnic areas, playgrounds and nature trails—perfect for anything from a short walk or a picnic with the kids to a run or an all-day hike.
properties.title: Yakima Greenway

properties.description: A glittering lake awaits you at the end of this hike, a nice alternative to the popular Cathedral Pass and Marmot Lake from the same trailhead.
properties.title: Moonshine Lake

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Davis Peak

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Mount Ballard

properties.description: With lovely Douglas-fir forest, wetlands, and a great network of trails, Island Center Forest is one of King County's best-kept secrets. Birds are abundant on the wetlands, and the forest is lush, with large, second-growth trees, a testament to the effort that several groups have put into managing this forest in order to restore the health of this area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Island Center Forest

properties.description: The short half-mile interpretive trail along Deception Falls is a great stop for a quick stretch of the legs as you drive over Stevens Pass. The highlight is the tumbling, multi-tiered waterfall and its distinctive 90 degree turn the creek makes at a stop along the way.
properties.title: Deception Falls National Recreation Area

properties.description: With its lush old growth forest, Thunder Creek is arguably the best of the feeder trails leading to the Shedroof Divide and the heart of the Salmo Priest Wilderness.
properties.title: Thunder Creek

properties.description: Hike the Hay Ridge Loop on Mount Spokane to a warming hut that's a great option for a picnic in the summertime.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Hay Ridge Loop

properties.description: Jungle Hill and Wapaloosie traverse a staggering diversity of classic Kettle Range habitats, from interior mixed-conifer forest to aspen groves and sagebrush meadows.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Jungle Hill Loop

properties.description: This short trail crosses the Inter Fork of the White River to views of The Mountain's largest glacier and the valley carved by this river of ice.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Emmons Moraine

properties.description: Get a forest experience right on the edge of the town of Newport, with a network of trails for hikers, mountain bikers, cross-country skiers, and snowshoers.
properties.title: Upper Wolf Trails

properties.description: This trail is one of the few trails designated as hiker-only, although it is only 0.6 mile one-way. Consider that this is a long drive to a short trail when deciding if it’s worth it to make a trip here.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest Fuzzy Top

properties.description: This excellent early-season romp heads up a lush river canyon boasting three gorgeous waterfalls with riverside campsites for an overnight, or a longer, more challenging loop.
properties.title: Horseshoe and Chinook Creek Falls via Upper Siouxon Creek

properties.description: The Quick Link Trail is a short segment in the middle of the East Tiger trail system. Combine this trail with others to form any number of loop hikes, including a trip to the east tiger summit.
properties.title: Quick Link

properties.description: This lakeside trail begins in Beaver Lake Campground and travels 1.9 flat miles to Beth Lake, offering opportunities to view fish and waterfowl including the Common Loon.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Beth Lake

properties.description: Built with the help of many WTA work parties, the Frog Mountain trail is the newest trail on the Skykomish Ranger District. It offers views of the Skykomish Valley from the summit and a great shoulder-season hike.
properties.title: Frog Mountain

properties.description: The Sun Mountain Trails are a vast and dynamic network of trails that radiate out from Sun Mountain Lodge located in the hills west of the town of Winthrop.
properties.title: Sun Mountain Trails

properties.description: This short trail leads to an observation area overlooking the waterfall on the North Fork Nooksack River.
properties.title: Nooksack Falls

properties.description: The Mill Gulch Trail is open to off-road vehicles and hikers and travels through the forest to a ridge overlooking the Teanaway.
properties.title: Mill Gulch Trail

properties.description: This small park is located on the shoreline next to the Hood Canal Bridge. A popular spot for boaters, this park also has something to offer hikers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Salsbury Point Park

properties.description: Experience the variety offered by the North Cascades: high mountain ridges with spectacular views, a remote river valley, and even a self-propelled cable car river crossing. Popular side trips include Hannegan Peak and Whatcom Pass.
properties.title: Copper Ridge Loop

properties.description: Take a quick stroll and breathe in the mixed forest smells of lodgepole pine and western larches around this campground loop off Highway 410 near Mount Rainier National Park. Claim a campground reservation and stay for a couple days!
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Lodgepole Campground

properties.description: This trail in Idaho’s Heyburn State Park starts off on a remnant of a historic wagon road, then winds through ponderosa pine forests to top out on Shoeffler Butte.
properties.title: Shoeffler Butte-Heyburn State Park

properties.description: Lake Serene and Bridal Veil Falls compete for attention on this hike. Either would be a worthy destination by themselves and combined they are a great day on the trail.
properties.title: Lake Serene

properties.description: Thanks to planning and partnerships from WTA and local land managers, this fantastic new trail is located on a parcel of public land very close to Spokane. Get a full-day hike just 30 minutes from downtown!
properties.title: Mica Peak to Liberty Lake Traverse

properties.description: Vesper Lake is squeezed, like a thumbprint in clay, deep in the saddle between the twin summits of Sperry Peak and Vesper Peak. Rarely is a lake situated so close and steeply below two summits like this; its unique setting gives you remarkably up-close (and straight-up) views of mountainous terrain.
properties.title: Headlee Pass and Vesper Lake

properties.description: A series of trails near the town of Chelan wind along the contours of the hills and dip into the rocky plain of Washington’s shortest river.
properties.title: Chelan Gorge Trail

properties.description: The Cape Alava Loop (Ozette Triangle) is two hikes in one: a forest stroll and a walk on the beach. Take the Cape Alava Trail out to the beach and back for a 6.2 mile hike, or continue south along the beach to connect up with the Sand Point Trail for a 9.4 mile loop.
properties.title: Cape Alava Loop (Ozette Triangle)

properties.description: Hike a network of forest trails in this large park in the southwestern corner of Seattle. Douglas-fir, redcedar, maples, madrone — they are all here in abundance, some of them quite large.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Westcrest Park

properties.description: Trail 140 represents the only “bottom to top” trail experience for Mount Spokane’s summit, but is frequently enjoyed in smaller sections to create loops of various distances. Lower Trail 140 is the portion of the trail located adjacent to the park entrance, featuring some fantastic old-growth forest sections.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Lower Trail 140

properties.description: This 2.5-mile loop hike meanders its way through pine forest and offers a shorter alternative to the full Frog Pond Loop.
properties.title: Teanaway Community Forest - Frog Pond Half-Loop

properties.description: A scramble up Mount Angeles just off the Klahhane Ridge hike in Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Mount Angeles

properties.description: This well-marked snowshoe route near Sun Mountain Lodge offers outstanding views, a variety of terrain, and more solitude than you might expect.
properties.title: Sun Mountain Snowshoe Loop

properties.description: At the easterly edge of the Pasayten Wilderness, almost touching the Canadian border, lies a truly unique and beautifully remote place. Horseshoe Basin is one of the few places in the Lower 48 to contain alpine tundra and is home to bears, deer and pronghorn sheep, if you know where to look.
properties.title: Horseshoe Basin

properties.description: Hike out along a skyline ridge looking over with the Snake and Salmon River Canyons thousands of feet below. In season, the flower show is stunning. Bring lots of water as there is none along the ridge.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Craig Mountain Wildlife Area - Wapshilla Ridge

properties.description: A little-known trail on the Oregon side of the Columbia River Gorge. This route escaped damage from the Eagle Creek Fire, but it is still recovering from a flash flood event in 2016 that blew out a bridge crossing Perham Creek.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Wygant Peak Trail

properties.description: A quiet forest trail with small creeks and ponds, the Clay Pit vista, mining artifacts, and a deep mineshaft. Don't worry, it's covered by a grate.
properties.title: East Fork

properties.description: This is a great trail to observe seasonal changes within the Dishman Hills Natural Area. While the ponds may be lost by mid-summer, they are full of aquatic life in the spring.
properties.title: Dishman Hills Natural Area - Lost Ponds Trail

properties.description: This trail, on the Oregon side of the Columbia Gorge, weaves through old-growth Doug-firs and offers hikers a nice day hike, or access to longer backpacking loops.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Wyeth

properties.description: This delightful little park is part of the Olympic Discovery Trail, which means you can hike as far as time allows, or as little as you like. You'll see salmon spawning in the fall, interpretive signs year round, and can watch the seasons turn by visiting as often as you like.
properties.title: Railroad Bridge Park

properties.description: This hike on Rattlesnake Mountain near North Bend follows good trails through second-growth forest, with possible wildlife sightings. It leads to some outstanding high viewpoints. In spite of the name, there are no rattlesnakes here.
properties.title: Rattlesnake Mountain - Grand Prospect

properties.description: Venture through dusty lahars, cool forest and the high country on the shoulder of Mount St. Helens on this 12-mile loop. Do it in a day, or plan to camp along the way—this hike is both beautiful and a bit of a challenge; you’ll need a little scrambling experience to be comfortable hiking the whole thing.
properties.title: Southwest Loowit Loop

properties.description: This hike requires a potentially dangerous ford of the Suiattle River due to a missing bridge. Because of its inaccessibility and a lack of maintenance, expect a brushy trail with blowdowns beyond this point.
properties.title: Milk Creek

properties.description: This trail was damaged in the the Mineral Park Fire and more recently in the Pincer Fire. In the interim, flooding has damaged it and the trail has not seen maintenance since 2007.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Middle Fork Cascade River

properties.description: A little-traveled, short hike offering some impressive trees and lovely territorial views.
properties.title: Primrose Overlook

properties.description: A nice hike to some ridgelines in Larrabee State Park. Connect to Fragrance Lake Trail, South Lost Lake Trail, Clayton Beach Trail, and Interurban Trail. This is also a very popular downhill mountain biking trail, so if you venture onto it, please keep an eye out for bikers.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Larrabee State Park - Double Diamond Trail

properties.description: Culmback Dam and Spada Lake provide lovely retreat off Highway 2, just east of Sultan and up the Sultan Basin Road. Spada Lake is a source of drinking water, so in-water activities are prohibited, but there are hiking trails that circle the lake and nearby just waiting for your exploration.
properties.title: Spada Lake - Culmback Dam

properties.description: Bird Creek Meadows is a crowd pleaser of a hike. Known for its abundant wildflower meadows, views of Mount Adams and the Hellroaring Canyon, and little creeks, lakes and waterfalls, this trail provides a nice 5.2-mile loop for hikers.
properties.title: Bird Creek Meadows

properties.description: High Hut is the highlight of the Mount Tahoma Trail System. From the warmth of a cozy alpine hut, enjoy some of the best views in the southern Cascades.
properties.title: High Hut Snowshoe

properties.description: A nice hike with plenty of variety.  Beautiful forest, a rushing creek, waterfalls of all shapes and sizes, history, and of course a large blue-green lake surrounded by snowy peaks.  At 10.4 miles, it can be either a day-hike or a quick early season overnight.  You won’t be alone, though – this is a popular trail with both hikers and backpackers.
properties.title: Goat Lake
