properties.description: A strenuous loop hike in the Teanaway area of Washington. Cross two mountain passes, hike alongside of a creek, and climb, climb, climb to some excellent views.
properties.title: Iron Peak Loop

properties.description: Flume Creek provides access to Abercrombie Mountain from the east side of the peak via a nicely graded and well-maintained trail.
properties.title: Flume Creek Trail

properties.description: Hike a 1.2 mile loop trail through this forest preserve. Appreciate the exceptionally tall trees, both deciduous and coniferous. Pass some swampy areas with standing water, and note the exuberant growth of ferns and hanging moss.
properties.title: Beaver Lake Preserve

properties.description: A lovely alternative to walking the West Side Road, the Round Pass trail heads east to the South Puyallup Trail.
properties.title: Round Pass Trail

properties.description: Cooney Peak, also known as Switchback Peak, sits within the Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness and can be reached from the Eagle Lakes Trailhead. The route to Cooney Peak is a Class 3 and involves exposed scrambling. Gear and experience are recommended.
properties.title: Cooney Peak

properties.description: The Mission Ridge trail is primarily used by mountain bikes and dirt bikes, which can make for a nice, compacted trail. But by the same token, parts of the single-track can be a bit narrow and cupped, having been carved out by bikes. This can be a bit hard on the knees and ankles after awhile (especially with the additional weight of a backpack).
properties.title: Mission Ridge

properties.description: Enjoy this low-key, child-friendly hike through aspen forest close to Seattle, just off the parking lot for Mailbox Peak.
properties.title: Grouse Basin Loop

properties.description: This popular route for summitting Mount Baker is also a brilliant summer wildflower hiking destination.
properties.title: Railroad Grade

properties.description: A few inches of new snow prior to a mid-week snowshoe outing transform this trip into a tranquil walk into the Eightmile Creek valley.  Extending the trip with a climb out of the valley leads to viewpoints along the road.
properties.title: Paul Mountain Snowshoe

properties.description: Take this trail to escape the heat on summer days, or to observe how the snow brings profound quiet to the forest in the middle of winter. Regardless of season, this trail is a good introduction to the trails at Mount Spokane State Park.
properties.title: Mount Spokane - Burping Brook-Smith Gap Loop

properties.description: A scramble to the summit of a peak near Alpental. Proper gear and expertise recommended.
properties.title: Snoqualmie Mountain

properties.description: The Peterson Lake Natural Area is a haven for wildlife and an important part of keeping clean water running through the Cedar River Watershed in the ever-growing urban areas of King County. It is essential wetland habitat for many species of fish, birds, mammals, amphibians, and reptiles.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Peterson Lake Natural Area

properties.description: This close-to-the-city wild land trail provides stunning views, great forestlands and ample opportunities to see birds and critters. Of the three peaks on West Tiger, this peak offers the best views, despite being the lowest of the triplets.
properties.title: West Tiger 3

properties.description: Mink Lake and the Little Divide offer miles of delightful hiking and showcase some of what makes the Sol Duc Valley so popular. Because it lacks the stunning scenery of the High Divide, Little Divide gets a fraction of the traffic. The option to loop back to the trailhead and see Deer Lake and Sol Duc Falls makes this an especially attractive and slightly shorter alternative.
properties.title: Mink Lake to Little Divide

properties.description: Gold Mountain is a beautiful hike from the Gold Creek Trailhead up a logging road and across country. With spectacular views of the Hood Canal and the Olympics to the west, as well as Mount Rainier, the Cascades, and Bremerton to the east, this is a definitely a half day hike you must experience.
properties.title: Gold Mountain

properties.description: The trails on Hope Island have been permanently closed and decommissioned by Washington State Parks to protect the Natural Area Preserve. Primitive camping is still open to the public at the north part of the island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Hope Island Marine State Park - Skagit County

properties.description: Start at 200 feet above sea level and climb to a lofty, scenic peak of 4492 feet on a long, switchbacking trail through stunning old growth forest. WTA has done a lot of work on this trail to improve it after a huge storm in 2007.
properties.title: Colonel Bob Trail - Colonel Bob Peak

properties.description: Used largely as part of the Nannie Peak Loop, Walupt Lake and Creek are a nice little hike in their own right. While not big on views, the flat grade of this trail makes it a good outing for families, since the river partway through the route offers a good turnaround point if little legs get tired. If you want to keep exploring, head up to where this trail terminates at the Pacific Crest Trail, and see if you can meet some thru-hikers.
properties.title: Walupt Lake and Walupt Creek

properties.description: Follow a gentle old railroad grade into the coal-mining ghost town of Franklin, along the Green River near Black Diamond. It’s an easy walk up to the coal cart and sealed mine shaft. Follow the narrow footpath beyond to discover the powerhouse foundation and cemetery.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Franklin Ghost Town

properties.description: Running like a spine through the Icicle Creek area, the Jack Creek Trail is 12 miles long, running from just outside Leavenworth to the Ingalls Creek valley and the northern border of the Teanway. Along the way, it offers a myriad of hiking options for visitors. Sections of this trail have burned in the past, so the odds of running into downed trees across the trail are high, especially in spring and early summer.
properties.title: Jack Creek

properties.description: Walk as far as you like up-valley on this moderate snowshoe. Enterprising hikers may consider making this a thru-hike.
properties.title: Pleasant Valley Snowshoe

properties.description: This lollipop hike follows the shoreline of Patterson Lake then turns up the steep-walled Rader Creek. Keep your eyes open since wildlife frequents this riparian zone.
properties.title: Patterson Lake and Rader Creek Snowshoe Loop

properties.description: This is the western approach to Squak Mountain. Here, you'll have access to the Coal Mine Trail, Bullitt Fireplace Trail, and Chybinski Loop Trail.
properties.title: West Access Trail

properties.description: Rock spires across the Naches River from Highway 410 catch the eye of travelers from the roadway. For a closer look, consider a hike to the top of Edgar Rock by way of the Lost Creek Trail. This route proves popular early in the season as well as late in the year. The hike is not very long and features good views at the top.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Edgar Rock

properties.description: Trail 110 is one of the core trails within Mount Spokane State Park, beginning just inside the park entrance and providing access to numerous connector trails. Hike it as an out-and-back to learn the intersections, then explore the connecting trails to form loop routes.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 110

properties.description: A short access trail to the cave holes on Cougar Mountain.
properties.title: Old Man's Trail

properties.description: Moses Coulee is a splendid expanse of intact shrub steppe near the better-known Grand Coulee. A short trail to a seasonal waterfall makes a nice introduction to the preserve, and you can wander along faint tracks and old wheel ruts for more adventure.
properties.title: Moses Coulee Preserve and Dutch Henry Falls

properties.description: From Barlow Point’s rocky promontory, hikers can take in views of Mount Dickerman, Big Four, and Stillaguamish Peak.
properties.title: Barlow Point

properties.description: Used primarily by mountain bikers, this trail is very popular due to its proximity to the town of Leavenworth. It is also frequently used as a logging road, and is subject to occasional closures because of this.
properties.title: Freund Canyon

properties.description: WTA does not recommend winter use on the Iron Goat Trail due to avalanche danger and lack of parking. The Iron Goat Scenic Interpretive Site is also closed in winter.
properties.title: Iron Goat Trail - Winter Route

properties.description: Less than a mile, this is a delightful connector trail between LeBar Horse Camp and the South Skokomish River Trail.  The junction between the trails is in an old growth area and more old growth is visible along this trail.  Only about 50-100ft elevation gain.
properties.title: LeBar Horse Camp Trail

properties.description: In an area known for rhododendrons and stunning mountain views, find a relatively easy hike to a high ridgeline that used to house a fire lookout tower.
properties.title: Jefferson Ridge

properties.description: This strip of green space in the middle of the Mount Baker and Columbia City neighborhoods of Seattle offers mountain bikers and hikers reprieve from the hustle and bustle of the city.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cheasty Natural Area

properties.description: Hike through wildflower-filled burned forest to subalpine meadows, a small reflecting lake and views of Mount Adams.
properties.title: Stagman Ridge, Horseshoe Meadow, Lookingglass Lake

properties.description: This is a 12-mile traverse of the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) that makes a great warm-up thru-hike for the full PCT, or a nice overnight backpacking trip.
properties.title: Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) - Stampede Pass to Windy Pass

properties.description: You don’t have to be circumnavigating Mount Rainier to see Sylvia Falls and Martha Falls. Do this section of the Wonderland Trail in the shoulder season, or when the weather obscures higher views, or just when you would just rather hike in shaded forest.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Stevens Canyon Waterfalls

properties.description: The White River Trail in Auburn is a paved, multi-use trail that starts at the East Valley Highway and runs through Roegner Park and Game Farm Wilderness Park before ending at Stuck River Road.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: White River Trail - Auburn

properties.description: Enjoy Garfield Mountain from the Taylor River, spot Stegosaurus Butte through the trees, enjoy the lush moss, and get a quick dose of nature on this short ramble.
properties.title: Middle Fork Connector Trail

properties.description: A short half-mile hike, the Rain Shadow Loop takes you to the top of Blue Mountain. Views of the Cascades, Vancouver Island and the Strait of Juan De Fuca, Gray Wolf Ridge, and so much more await you here.
properties.title: Rain Shadow Loop

properties.description: Climb a ridge to a rocky promontory nine miles due west of Tahoma’s summit and experience multi-volcano, jaw-dropping views under clear conditions. Glacier View’s short but moderately intense route is ideal for lovers of huckleberries, wildflowers, old-growth forest, mushrooms, fauna and lakes.
properties.title: Glacier View

properties.description: Beginning at a large intersection of Forest Road 3500, the Wilson Creek Trail meanders along a plateau of lodgepole pines. At the end of this trail, you'll be at the junction with the High Creek trail and further adventures.
properties.title: Wilson Creek

properties.description: The Lily Basin trail climbs gently through corridors of huckleberry, mountain azalea and patches of bear grass to sweet little Heart Lake.
properties.title: Heart Lake via Lily Basin Trail

properties.description: The Hegg-Benson Trail, designed and constructed by Skagit Land Trust members and volunteers in 2009-2010, provides a short walk through mossy forest to a picturesque waterfall on Barr Creek in this lovely conservation area.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Hegg-Benson Trail

properties.description: A great quick neighborhood escape, or stay longer and there is something for everyone. A cultivated arboretum with additional trails in a small forest, with playground, disc golf course, a lake with swimming, fishing, boat rentals, and more.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Wilderness Park

properties.description: Part of the trail system at Manastash Ridge, the Prater trail allows hikers to make loops or alternate routes for the more well-known Westberg Trail.
properties.title: Manastash Ridge - Prater Trail

properties.description: Covel Creek trail is a very short, one mile trail with only 50 feet of elevation gain. Hikers can travel through dense forest to a small waterfall, but there is an option to continue on the Angel Falls Loop, which creates a figure-eight, making this longer hike about 4 miles roundtrip.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Angel Falls Loop

properties.description: Take a walk around the historic (and still operational) apple orchard in the Stehekin valley.
properties.title: Buckner Orchard Walk

properties.description: This grand tour of Mount Spokane State Park includes all eight summits within Washington's largest state park.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Eight Peaks Tour

properties.description: Enjoy this delightful trail in Olympic National Park. You'll climb 8 miles up from a valley and end at the Hurricane Hill Trail.
properties.title: Little River

properties.description: Enjoy two miles of hiking trails at Toppenish National Wildlife Refuge. There is a variety of habitat, from native grasses to shrub steppe, to riparian areas and ponds that support many types of wildlife.
properties.title: Toppenish National Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: An interpretive trail outside of Forks. Great for a midday walk or a leg stretch during a long drive.
properties.title: Elk Creek Conservation Area

properties.description: This area is managed primarily as important riparian habitat, but there are a couple short trails, one heading into the upland portion of the property and the other following along the river.
properties.title: Raging River Natural Area

properties.description: This City of Port Townsend park offers an accessible network of trails in the uplands above a lagoon.
properties.title: Kah Tai Lagoon Nature Park

properties.description: A popular camping and birding spot, this area is best known for its free (with Discover Pass) camping, but has some nice hiking options as well.
properties.title: Cascade Park Wenas Wildlife Area

properties.description: Hex Mountain is now located partially on private property and is inaccessible to vehicles.
properties.title: Hex Mountain

properties.description: This short hike boasts a lot of bang for your buck. At just 2.1 miles, the loop won't take too long, but you'll enjoy views of an impressive river, rocky outcroppings, and some expansive views.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Bowl & Pitcher

properties.description: Perry Creek proves you can have it all in a single hike — old-growth forest, wildflowers, waterfalls, meadows, expansive mountain views, even lakes! Tread lightly, though — due to its unparalleled diversity of native plants, the area between the summits of Stillaguamish Peak, Mount Forgotten and Mount Dickerman is a research natural area that could (in theory) be closed to all uses but scientific study.
properties.title: Perry Creek

properties.description: This feeder trail for The Kettle Crest is popular with mountain bikers but also makes a great hiking route.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Taylor Ridge

properties.description: Visit this wheelchair-friendly trail on the north side of Tacoma with views of Commencement Bay, Vashon Island and close up of a lighthouse!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Brown's Point Lighthouse Park

properties.description: Visit this trail in the springtime and you can expect to see an explosion of wildflower color! At more than 4500 feet in 5.5 miles of trail, the route to the old Icicle Ridge Lookout site is quite an undertaking, but the views and the flowers are truly worth the energy it takes to get up there.
properties.title: Icicle Ridge via Fourth of July Creek

properties.description: This little gem of a park is located in Kitsap County, at the west end of Newberry Hill Road right before the T to Seabeck Highway.
properties.title: Newberry Hill Heritage Park

properties.description: The Klickitat Rail Trail is a 31-mile rails-to-trails conversion managed by Columbia Hills State Park. This linear park goes from Lyle to Warwick (on the Lyle-Centerville Highway) with several access points along the way. Swale Canyon lies on the eastern end of the trail and offers a quiet canyon, a burbly creek, wildflowers and solitude.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Klickitat Rail Trail - Swale Canyon

properties.description: Take three or four days to explore this rugged trail near Glacier Peak. If you're feeling ambitious, make it a traverse either to or from White Chuck Bench.
properties.title: Meadow Mountain

properties.description: A connector trail between East Ridge and Bullitt Fireplace trail on Squak Mountain.
properties.title: East Side Trail

properties.description: Pebble Creek is roughly the halfway point between Paradise and Camp Muir. This alpine creek marks the boundary between the front country trails that crisscross Paradise meadows and the trail-less zone of tundra above. Although not usually a destination in itself, the area is scenic, with Panorama Point close by.
properties.title: Pebble Creek

properties.description: Hike down a lushly forested ravine with a babbling creek to its estuary as it empties into Puget Sound. Heading to the beach, breathe in the serene panorama of Brown’s Bay, Puget Sound, the islands, and the Olympic Mountains. Watch seabirds and go beachcombing to look for crabshells, anemones, and other treasures.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Meadowdale Beach Park - Lunds Gulch

properties.description: Ruby Beach offers several miles of beach exploration, with unique rock formations and swirling sun-bleached driftwood.
properties.title: Ruby Beach

properties.description: Packwood Lake makes for an arduous snowshoe adventure through old-growth forest in the Goat Rocks Wilderness area. Higher-elevation routes may still be waiting to melt out but views of snowy mountain peaks and precious solitude are your well-earned reward for the miles you will cover into the backcountry.
properties.title: Packwood Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: Here is an easy snowshoe on a wide U.S. Forest Service road with spectacular views of Chimney Rock, Coyote Ridge and, at the end, Mount Rainier.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Maintenance Shed Road

properties.description: The Pigeon Creek Trail takes you for a stroll along Everett's industrial waterfront. Watch the Port of Everett operate, relax on the beach, watch for trains, and enjoy bird watching from the end of the trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Pigeon Creek Trail

properties.description: From the same trailhead as Northrup Canyon, the Old Wagon Road Trail heads high, rather than into the canyon. Begin on the same trail as that to Northrup, but after just a few hundred yards, look for a trail branching off to the south. There's a sign where the trail enters the trees, reading 'Old Wagon Road Trail'. Do note that this trail is closed from November to March to protect bald eagle nesting habitat.
properties.title: Old Wagon Road Trail

properties.description: Walk along an old railroad grade that climbs gently though forested hillsides. In summer, look for wildflowers: blackberry, elderberry, pea, daisy, buttercup and wild rose.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Snoqualmie Valley Trail

properties.description: This is a great close to Seattle option of creating lots of loops and getting your exercise.
properties.title: West Tiger 2

properties.description: A partially completed paved trail that stretches between the cities of Everett and Seattle.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Interurban Trail - Snohomish County

properties.description: Enjoy beautiful views, quiet forest and wildlife activity on this peaceful trail, perfect in spring or on a crisp and clear day in winter.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Howard Miller Steelhead Park - Wetland Wildlife Trail

properties.description: Cross one of the three major peaks in the Issaquah Alps. You'll see forest, an historic fireplace, and, if you use Trailhead Direct to do this hike, you won't have to look for parking!
properties.title: Squak Mountain Traverse

properties.description: This short interpretive trail guides you through the woods above the Pend Oreille River to learn about the traditional culture of the Kalispel People.
properties.title: Pioneer Park Kalispel Heritage Trail

properties.description: This short hike is an excellent option during a visit to the Naches area in the spring and summertime. You'll enjoy a ramble along a river, impressive geologic formations, and relative solitude, though the area is open to mountain bikers and popular with rock climbers and birders.
properties.title: Tieton River Nature Trail

properties.description: The short route  to Meeks Table goes through some forest then begins a moderately steep and short climb to a ridgeline, eventually continuing along the ridge, where you will walk through a myriad of wildflowers.
properties.title: Meeks Table

properties.description: In the 19th century, Whitman Mission was the site of a tragic clash of cultures, disease and violence. Today, walking trails provide a calm space for thoughtful reflection among peaceful fields, hills and streams.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Whitman Mission National Historic Site

properties.description: Spanning the Wenatchee Mountains and offering views of the backside of the Enchantment Peaks, the Beverly Turnpike trail (named for the two creeks it parallels) offers a straightforward out-and-back hike to a pass, or a more rugged thru-hike into the Ingalls Creek drainage. It also can be used to create loop hikes, or access nearby peaks. Hikers share this trail with mountain bikes and horses, and it isn’t uncommon to see occasional evidence of them along the way.
properties.title: Beverly Turnpike

properties.description: Convert the popular out-and-back Norse Peak hike into a lollipop loop through the open terrain along the PCT and back along the Goat Lake Trail. While it has fewer views, it provides a longer, more secluded return to the trailhead.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Norse Peak Lollipop via Goat Lake Trail

properties.description: This 1.6-mile section of trail is located in the Tiger Mountain State Forest. It is popular with mountain bikers and hikers.
properties.title: Inside Passage

properties.description: This paved urban trail follows along SW Spokane Street. Take a walk or ride your bike over the East Waterway, across Harbor Island and over the West Waterway.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: West Seattle Bridge Trail

properties.description: Formerly known as the McLane Nature Trail, the Ralph Munro Trail was re-named in June of 2018 to honor the man who established the McLane Forest Committee. The trail starts near the McLane Elementary School and goes along Evergreen Pkwy NW towards the Evergreen State College.
properties.title: Ralph Munro Trail

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Luna Peak

properties.description: The Tracy Hill Loop at Catherine Creek is a popular route, but the eastern-most portion of it crosses a parcel of tribal land not open to the public. Visitors are encouraged to use the WTA-built Catherine Creek loop, which starts and ends from the main parking area for Catherine Creek.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Catherine Creek - Tracy Hill Loop

properties.description: This old road is managed for snowmobilers, cross-country skiers and snowshoers, and it's a great way to enjoy a long, 8-mile snowshoe, or a shorter hike to views and history of the area.
properties.title: Old Blewett Pass Highway

properties.description: A short, flat trail in the Mora campground winds through classic Olympic forest to a small frog pond.
properties.title: James Pond Loop

properties.description: This mountain bike trail makes a nice spring or fall hike. The trail gradually climbs up the mostly forested Middle Fork Beaver Creek valley. In late spring, the sparse flowers are blooming and the sound of the creek fills the valley. In fall, the upper half is in a mixed forest that includes golden larch.
properties.title: Middle Fork Beaver Creek

properties.description: This route is the perfect gateway to Mount Adams' spectacular high country on its less-visited western side. It climbs through dense forests, past a small lake, then across Riley Meadows (great campsites!) before joining the PCT. From there, you can continue on to Sheep Lake or head off-trail to check out Crystal Lake at the edge of the tree line.
properties.title: Riley Camp

properties.description: A short hike near the Staircase area of Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Four Stream

properties.description: Witness the destructive force and the restorative power of nature on this hike in the blast zone of Mount St. Helens’ 1980 eruption. The rocky ash and treeless areas are testaments to the devastation caused by the explosion, while wildflowers and shrubs signal the return of vegetation to the denuded landscape.
properties.title: Norway Pass

properties.description: A route-finding bushwhack to beautiful views and berries in the summertime in the North Cascades
properties.title: Squire Creek

properties.description: Also known as Little Navaho, this scramble is best attempted in winter, as the rock in summer  makes for class 2 or 3 climbing. In any season, climbing experience and equipment recommended.
properties.title: Freedom Peak

properties.description: Dalles Ridge is the primary way that hikers access the popular Noble Knob Trail and Ranger Creek. It provides hikers with a beautiful ridge walk after a steady climb from the trailhead.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Dalles Ridge

properties.description: The trail to Stirrup Lake is a road less traveled and a moderate hike through second-growth forest to a serene alpine lake tucked between Big Muffin and Meadow Mountain, paying tremendous dividends for lovers of huckleberries, wildflowers, and riparian fauna.
properties.title: Stirrup Lake

properties.description: The Deceiver Trail is a hiker-only trail in the southern reaches of Cougar Mountain. It is a connector trail so it does not have its own devoted trailhead but can be reached on foot from the multiple trails in the park.
properties.title: Deceiver

properties.description: Hike a rugged trail through second-growth forest and across lively creeks to a high alpine lake.
properties.title: Dingford Creek-Myrtle Lake

properties.description: A moderate, year round loop trail in the Issaquah Alps that is popular with hikers, dog walkers and trail runners.  Entering the large parking area at the Red Town trailhead (one of several in this 3,100-acre regional park) it’s hard to imagine that what is today a lush green forest was once a busy coalmine operation. Now all that remains are nearly forgotten place names, a few carefully preserved artifacts and caution signs warning of the hazards of travel off established trails.
properties.title: Wildside Trail-De Leo Wall

properties.description: A scramble to Fortune Peak via the Esmerelda Basin hike.
properties.title: Fortune Peak via Esmeralda Basin (Esmerelda)

properties.description: Tatoosh Lakes are not open to camping any more, but they are much easier to get to than they used to be, and still a good bet for solitude and the peaceful sounds of nature.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Tatoosh Lakes

properties.description: The trail to Big Huckleberry Mountain passes some of the best wildflower shows in the Gorge, and takes visitors to two former fire lookout sites, which means you'll get a workout and views for miles. It's a wonderful way to spend a day, provided you're OK with a rough road approach.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Big Huckleberry Mountain

properties.description: The Radio Peak Trail travels for just under half a mile in the northern reaches of Cougar Mountain. It is part of the vast trail network in the park and does not have its own devoted trailhead.
properties.title: Radio Peak

properties.description: On this hike, you'll get your heart rate going under intense UV rays and a whole lot of dust in your nose/shoes/socks, so pack your trekking poles, sunscreen, buff, an extra pair of socks and lots of water! But for braving the elements, you’ll be rewarded with a rainbow of wildflowers (think balsamroot, desert-parsley, phlox, lupine and so much more), incredible views of the town of Chelan, and perhaps best of all, the massive lake that the town shares its name with.
properties.title: Chelan Butte

properties.description: Traverse across beautiful Chuckanut Mountain in Larrabee State Park. Enjoy views of Puget Sound, as well as Mount Baker along this high trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Larrabee State Park - Chuckanut Ridge Trail

properties.description: A hike named after Nawang Gombu, Jim Whittaker's partner in his first ascent of Everest. Connect it with the Whittaker Wilderness Peak trail for a long loop with historical significance.
properties.title: Gombu Wilderness Cliffs

properties.description: An abandoned trail in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
properties.title: Red Pass

properties.description: Krause Ridge Trail offers a textbook example of a Pacific Northwest forest nearing succession climax. Whether you are a jaded forest trekker or an ecologist, this is a classical forest with big trees towering as a sunshade with a lush understory and an easy day hike.
properties.title: Kraus Ridge

properties.description: The walk to Frazer Homestead Preserve is mellow and straightforward, an easy hike through forests and small meadows. Here, you can spot old homesteads along the hillsides, including the site of the infamous pig fatality that started the otherwise bloodless Pig War.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Frazer Homestead Preserve

properties.description: This forested park, a wilderness with glimpses of Issaquah below, has miles of winding trails alongside bubbling creeks and narrow ravines. There are several trail loop options on this 2,024-foot-high mountain. With multi-use trails and a natural area, hikers have plenty to explore in this quiet sanctuary outside of Issaquah.
properties.title: May Valley Loop

properties.description: Wildlife is often difficult to spot in the North Cascades, but McAlester Pass is an exception to this. Take a multi-day backpack from Highway 20 into the tiny town of Stehekin, where you can rest easy and gorge yourself on treats from the renowned bakery before making the multiple mile trek out.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Bridge Creek - McAlester Pass to Stehekin

properties.description: This Bainbridge Island park is popular with horseback riders and hikers due to its proximity to the main highway.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Manzanita Trail

properties.description: Jungle Creek Trail is a 4-mile long trail from FS 9701/Jungle Creek Road to Johnson Media Trail #1383. The saddle at 2.1 miles from the trailhead is the highest point of the trail at 4,500 feet in elevation. In spring there are a lot of flowers along the trail. When the weather is good, there are good views of peaks in Stuart Range at the saddle.
properties.title: Jungle Creek

properties.description: A popular climbing route in the North Cascades. Proper gear and expertise is required.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Sahale Glacier

properties.description: The Bayview Loop trail fittingly follows the perimeter of the Bayview Campground along the west bank of Baker Lake. It's a short and relatively flat hike great for all ages.
properties.title: Bayview Loop Trail

properties.description: A 2.8 mile trail in the Columbia River Gorge, the Wahkeena Trail can be connected with the Larch Mountain trail and the Return Trail to create a 6 mile loop. It also connects with many other trails in the area to create many other routes longer loops or traverses.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Wahkeena Falls

properties.description: Experience a quiet woodland walk while camping at one of Olympic National Park's many campgrounds. Add it on to a day of exploration on the coast, or simply meditate in the cool forest with your morning coffee before heading out for the day.
properties.title: Quillayute River Slough

properties.description: Arch Rock is not an arch, but a rocky point on the ridge to the west of Arch Rock Spring in the Norse Peak Wilderness Area. The trip to the rock involves a 5.4-mile hike mainly on the Pacific Crest Trail along a forested ridge to Arch Rock Spring, followed by a 0.6-mile boot trail to Arch Rock.  From the top, the expansive views of the South Cascades are dominated by Mount Rainier, 20 miles to the southwest.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Arch Rock

properties.description: This wildlife area is considered one of the best places in northwest Washington to view falcons, short-eared owls, and shorebirds.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Welts-Samish Restoration Site

properties.description: The name Tamanous derives from local Native American's who initiated their young in their area by sending them on vision quests, called "Ta-mah-no-ous."
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Tamanous Trail

properties.description: A summit of a mountain in the Entiat. Route-finding experience required.
properties.title: Stormy Mountain Summit

properties.description: Little Beacon Trail is a short spur trail off the Hadley Trail in Beacon Rock State Park over moss covered talus to the base of Little Beacon Rock and a view of Beacon Rock.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Beacon Rock State Park - Little Beacon Trail

properties.description: Utilizing a historic network of forest roads, hike to an expansive viewpoint of the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Valley that lies below the summit of Green Mountain.
properties.title: Last Chance Promontory

properties.description: The relentless but scenic climb up to Paddy-Go-Easy Pass is often used to access scrambling routes on nearby peaks, or further adventures beyond the pass. On its own, the Paddy-Go-Easy Pass trail offers views of Tucquala Lake and Mount Daniel as well as The Cradle and mountain ranges to the east.
properties.title: Paddy-Go-Easy Pass

properties.description: This route started as a pedestrian- and bike-friendly route along the Spokane River, coinciding with the Washington State Centennial celebration, hence the name. Now, users can follow the Spokane River from Riverside State Park west of Spokane all the way to the Idaho border.
properties.title: Spokane River Centennial State Park Trail

properties.description: This grind of a hike is one of the most strenuous hikes in the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Mount Defiance (Oregon)

properties.description: An unofficial bootpath that connects Dirty Harry's Balcony with the Ira Spring Trail. This route requires route-finding skills and the ability to hike cross-country.
properties.title: Ira Spring Connector Trail

properties.description: Beaver Loop is a pleasant, level outing which is easy to follow and and has many distractions for younger hikers. There is ample opportunity for wildlife and best of all it is close to town.
properties.title: Beaver Loop

properties.description: The trail to Ferguson Lake is an offshoot of a now mostly abandoned loop trail that skirted Wildcat Mountain and followed Eureka Creek. Fortunately, the route to Ferguson Lake, which includes the Ferguson Lake Trail is still maintained.
properties.title: Ferguson Lake Trail

properties.description: While there is not a trail all the way around the lake proper, it’s possible to do a loop hike around this lovely little lake just across the road from Mount Erie and Sugarloaf in the Anacortes Community Forest Lands. Formerly a state park, this area was transferred to the City of Anacortes in 2002, and now the trails that loop and bend around this little lake are accessible to residents and visitors without requiring a Discover pass.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Anacortes Community Forest Lands - Heart Lake

properties.description: A short connector trail between Bullitt Fireplace Trail and West Access Trail in the Squak Mountain trail system.
properties.title: Coal Mine

properties.description: A trip to Ring Hill Forest gives visitors an opportunity to observe a working forest in action as King County implements its Forest Stewardship Plan which is focused on creating a diverse, vigorous, and healthy forest that provides habitat as well as revenue.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ring Hill Forest

properties.description: The Olallie Trail in Olallie State Park is a new (as of Fall 2017) trail dedicated to mountain bikers, but open to all forms of non-motorized recreation such as hiking and horseback riding. It takes recreators up the slopes of Mount Washington above the I-90 corridor. Stop at multiple viewpoints on your way up that look north across I-90 towards the rest of the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.
properties.title: Olallie State Park - Olallie Trail

properties.description: With nearly 300 acres and a mile and a half of shoreline along Boundary Bay, Lily Point Marine Park & Reserve is an excellent coastal retreat for adults and children alike.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Lily Point Marine Park and Reserve

properties.description: Located eleven miles east of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho at exit 28 off I-90, Fourth of July Pass Recreation area provides a fun place to play in the winter.
properties.title: Fourth of July Pass Recreation Area

properties.description: This snowshoe route follows Forest Road 38 at the end of the Middle Fork Nooksack Valley.
properties.title: Middle Fork Nooksack River Snowshoe

properties.description: Access several loop options at the north side of Cougar Mountain with the Red Cedars Trail.
properties.title: Red Cedars

properties.description: A quiet hike through a still old-growth forested gully near Lena Lake.
properties.title: Lena Lake - Valley of Silent Men Snowshoe

properties.description: This springtime desert oasis requires some effort to reach, but rewards with wildflowers and, yes — birds!
properties.title: Roza Creek Road to Birdsong Tree

properties.description: Enjoy this rolling 1.25 mile loop hike in a (currently) undeveloped city park. Multi-use hiking and mountain-biking trails are slated for development in 2025.
properties.title: Kaiser Woods Park

properties.description: Follow this trail through the heart of the Pasayten Wilderness. Take in all the sights the Wilderness has to offer, including but not limited to: stunning peaks, refreshing creeks, wildflowers galore, and limitless views from ridges.
properties.title: Larch Creek

properties.description: This is a pleasant, short, lowland forest walk, accessed in Barlow Pass, the popular jumping-off point for locations like Monte Cristo and Gothic Basin.
properties.title: Old Government

properties.description: This short trail allows you a quick escape from the Sunrise parking lot to stunning views of Mount Rainier and the peaks and valley nearby.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Sourdough Ridge

properties.description: Tongue Mountain is one of several craggy peaks in the Dark Divide offering excellent views and a nice walk through forest
properties.title: Tongue Mountain

properties.description: Venture across the Columbia River, just barely into Oregon, and ramble on easy trails where you’ll see and hear a wide variety of birds, mammals and reptiles.
properties.title: McNary Dam Nature Area

properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Shaw Island

properties.description: Explore a rich mixture of blended nature and outdoor sculpture that is in harmony with one another on this seventy two acres of natural restoration. Enjoy trails through various small ecosystems that include bogs, ponds, a forest wildlife and several surprises along the way. You will also be experiencing the early decades of what is to be a five hundred year plan.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Earth Sanctuary

properties.description: With a low-key walk that merges into a steep uphill climb, and an optional extension to visit a fire lookout, the trail to Thorp Lake offers a range of hiking experiences crammed into one 2.6-mile trail.
properties.title: Thorp Lake

properties.description: Take a long, rolling trail deep into quiet forest. Admire enormous trees, see a historic cabin, and find true solitude on the banks of Lillian River.
properties.title: Elwha River and Lillian River

properties.description: Stroll though a remnant of Palouse prairie, wetland and steppe ecosystem.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Rose Creek Nature Preserve

properties.description: This trail uses the old North Pacific Railroad grade as a quiet place for Kirkland residents to stretch their legs, and is a part of the partially-completed 42-mile Eastrail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cross Kirkland Corridor Trail

properties.description: The Queets Campground Loop is a quintessential rainforest experience. At just under three miles, it provides visitors with a generous variety of nature. Giant spruce and hemlock rise above great galleries of fern and oxalis. The wind whispers the memories of abandoned homesteads in the grasses of shrinking meadows. Owls hoot and frogs croak the song of an ancient melody. One stands here often and wonders.
properties.title: Sam's River Loop (Queets Campground)

properties.description: A rugged trail that offers stunning views and access to several beautiful backcountry lakes.
properties.title: Lost Creek Ridge

properties.description: Explore the links between the Columbia River and Vancouver’s historic past and vibrant future on this paved accessible trail.
properties.title: Columbia River Renaissance Trail

properties.description: The hike involves a circumnavigation of Umatilla Rock, a narrow rock blade that passes below Dry Falls. This area lies midway along the 50-mile Grand Coulee—one of the longest and most spectacular chasms carved out by up to 100 gargantuan Ice Age floods.
properties.title: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park - Umatilla Rock via Monument Coulee

properties.description: Try this backcountry ski or snowshoe trail through deep forest, past lakes and with access to Windy Pass and Mount Catherine.
properties.title: Nordic Pass - Hyak

properties.description: Within a residential neighborhood of south Everett, tucked between expansive public sport fields and a golf course, a network of trails winds through towering trees, thriving native flora and a fragile yet precious wetland ecosystem: Loganberry Lane.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Loganberry Lane at Kasch Park

properties.description: Looking for an early-season backpack featuring craggy, snow-capped peaks, a sapphire-blue lake, a myriad of wildflowers, and a trail that’s regularly maintained by WTA volunteers? The 17-mile thru-hike on the Chelan Lakeshore Trail might be just the thing for you.
properties.title: Chelan Lakeshore Trail

properties.description: Take a leisurely hike on an old logging road to a beautiful waterfall.
properties.title: Big Creek Falls

properties.description: One of many loop hikes offered in the Mount Spokane area. Great for hiking and trail running in the summer, and snowshoeing in the winter.
properties.title: Mount Spokane - Trail 110/140 Loop

properties.description: The Skyline Trail roughly follows the ridgeline up to the summit of Badger Mountain, then back down to meet the Sagebrush Trail and the Langdon Trail at the Triple Junction. The graved path is 3.5 feet wide and popular with hikers, runners, mountain bikers and equestrians. The trail has mostly sagebrush at both ends with native dryland grasses in the middle. Balsamroot and purple sagebrush can be found blossoming in the spring.
properties.title: Badger Mountain - Skyline Trail

properties.description: No less than five picturesque lakes, wide panoramas of South Cascades peaks and oodles of seasonal wildflowers and berries make this an ideal long day hike or weekend backpack.
properties.title: Bird Mountain Loop

properties.description: Church Creek Shelter sits in a delightful clearing near the South Fork of the Skokomish River. The short hike to it was once part of the longer Church Creek Trail that extended from the “Skok” to Satsop Lake. Now just a half mile from the road, the shelter is one of the most easily attained on the Olympic Peninsula.
properties.title: Church Creek Shelter

properties.description: Explore a network of trails through a wooded marshy wetland, sprinkled with poems and quotes on small placards along the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Farrell's Marsh Wildlife Area

properties.description: One of about six former lookout sites in the Stevens Pass area, Poe Mountain boasts two different trails to the summit; Irving Pass was the recommended route, since you spend a significant amount of the hike on the ridge with awesome views both north and south, though the August 2022 fire has caused significant damage, so it is now more of a toss up.
properties.title: Poe Mountain via Irving Pass

properties.description: Near Odessa Craters is this short, flat trail to another crater, this one terminating at an overlook into the crater.
properties.title: Cache Crater Overlook

properties.description: Visit a the site of an old fire lookout, where you'll have views for miles in all directions on a clear day. Along the way, you'll enjoy wildflowers of many varieties, beargrass, and plump huckleberries in the summertime.
properties.title: Observation Peak

properties.description: Hiking Mount Townsend in the winter can be challenging. Depending on how much snow is present, it could require route-finding skills and the ability to evaluate slopes for avalanche risk. Go prepared with gear and a plan B.
properties.title: Mount Townsend - Winter

properties.description: This primitive trail spans over 20 miles through Montane and subalpine ecosystems. From the Low Divide Ranger Station to the Three Lakes campsite, the Skyline trail will take you on a steep journey past lakes and to the top of Kimta Peak.
properties.title: Skyline

properties.description: The North Fork Sol Duc River is a remote wilderness trail teeming with adventure. The trail is seldom maintained all the way to its end, and three river fords complicate the effort. The shoulder season hiker may experience solitude and wildlife, but they will also likely encounter high water, blowdown, and route-finding challenges.
properties.title: North Fork Sol Duc River

properties.description: This little lollipop loop in Riverside State Park is the perfect short walk to experience the north end of Riverside State Park, get a little exercise and a lot of a view.
properties.title: Riverside State Park - Trail 25 Trail 410 Loop

properties.description: Take a short trail from the Lost Lake Trailhead to Clayton Beach, where you'll find nearly a mile of shoreline to explore.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Clayton Beach

properties.description: Hike a trail that connects the beautiful Waptus River trail to the popular Pete Lake trail. Along the way, pass three other trail junctions, leading to further adventures.
properties.title: Waptus Pass

properties.description: Strap on your snowshoes and explore the Marble Mountain trails with a gentle hike to June Lake in the shadow of Mount St. Helens.
properties.title: June Lake Snowshoe

properties.description: Little Giant Pass is home to one of the finest views in Washington State: the sight of the Napeequa River, winding its lazy way through the perfect U-shaped valley left by receding glaciers that cling wearily to the surrounding heights and feed the silver ribbon beneath your feet. It is a rare prize, this view, locked away at the end of a long, 4,000-foot climb that is itself guarded most of the year by an icy river crossing.
properties.title: Little Giant Pass

properties.description: Big Tree Loop is no longer maintained and inaccessible to hikers due to fire damage and a mudslide.
properties.title: Big Tree Loop

properties.description: Mackenzie Reserve property is about 130 acres of former farmland/open space. Part of the original landowner's property was developed, but there is no public access to the beach.
properties.title: Mackenzie Reserve

properties.description: The route to Goode Mountain is a Class 5 and involves exposed climbing. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Goode Mountain

properties.description: This out-and-back hike into a channel of the ice age floods rewards you with stunning vistas, big sky and endless breathing space.
properties.title: Bobs Lakes

properties.description: Take a hike through railroad history. The old tunnels, rusting relics, cement snow sheds and the big red caboose should appeal to kids of all ages, and the complex history of the railroad and those who built it, as well as the avalanche that wiped everything away will appeal to history buffs.
properties.title: Iron Goat Trail

properties.description: Unbeknownst to many, there's a beautiful lake tucked into the forests on the west slopes of Mount Defiance. Thompson Lake provides a great destination for day hikers or overnighters in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. You may even find solitude here, just off the I-90 corridor. But that solitude comes at a price.
properties.title: Thompson Lake via Mount Defiance

properties.description: Climb, climb, climb through several stages of eastern forest to open wildflower filled alpine meadows and inspired views on this abandoned lookout peak.
properties.title: Hall Mountain

properties.description: Reaching the summit of Andrew Peak requires going off trail.
properties.title: Andrew Peak

properties.description: A birder's paradise, this wildlife refuge is the perfect getaway without a long drive. The refuge includes mixed wetlands and pastures with riparian strips lined with cottonwoods and white oak trees. More than 200 species of waterfowl and songbirds have been recorded here, making it the perfect place to slow down and enjoy nature.
properties.title: Steigerwald Lake National Wildlife Refuge

properties.description: The Core Zone of the Enchantments may be one of the most popular destinations in Washington state, but those who venture to Lake Stuart may just get the extra-enchanting reward of relative solitude in a high traffic area. Most hikers heading into the Enchantments use the Lake Stuart trailhead, but make for the Core zone via Colchuck Lake and Aasgard Pass. However, taking the right-hand trail 2.2 miles from the trailhead leads you into an adjacent valley, with a large, shallow lake at the base of the imposing massif of Mount Stuart.
properties.title: Lake Stuart

properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Shark Reef Sanctuary

properties.description: Tiger Mountain Road is a gravel road that starts at the East Tiger Mountain Summit Parking Lot and winds up near the summit.
properties.title: Tiger Mountain Road

properties.description: This short little loop trail is a sweet walk that enhances a camping trip, picnic, or hike at the Eagle Creek Recreation area.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Shady Glen

properties.description: Wapato Lake Park has all the amenities of a big local park, but the draw for hikers will be the loop trail around the lake.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Wapato Lake Park

properties.description: Here's a good training hike to the site of a former fire lookout. You'll get a workout in heading through the tangle of salal, Oregon grape, and imposing rhododenrons. There's not much of a view from the top anymore, since it hasn't been used as a lookout in decades, but it's still worth a visit, particularly if you need a leg-stretcher or you're in the area.
properties.title: Ned Hill

properties.description: The preserve has a short trail that wanders through mature trees along a salmon spawning creek and offers access to this beautiful 24-acre park where visitors are likely to see a variety of bird species.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Coho Preserve

properties.description: Hike a portion of the Pacific Crest Trail through meadows of wildflowers and past sparkling lakes with views of Nelson Ridge, Mount Aix and Mount Rainier. This outing makes for a great day hike or backpacking trip.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: American Lake

properties.description: A steep thigh-burner that doesn't offer much in the way of views, but will give you the workout you're looking for should you be training for Rainier or any other grueling ascents. The Aurora Creek trail rises an astonishing 3700 feet in 3.4 miles, from the edge of Hwy 101 to its junction with the Aurora Ridge Trail.
properties.title: Aurora Creek

properties.description: This mountain just outside the town of Richland is nice place for locals and visitors to recreate, with several trails for hiking, biking and equestrian. Views extend in every direction and include mountains as well as agricultural fields.
properties.title: Badger Mountain - Canyon Trail

properties.description: Part hike, part wander, this 20-acre sculpture garden is an outdoor gallery of nature-oriented artwork. There are few paths, but more than 100 pieces of artwork to discover in this special place adjacent to Roche Harbor on San Juan Island and managed by the San Juan Islands Museum of Art.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Westcott Bay Nature Reserve and Sculpture Park

properties.description: The Waterline Trail is part of the extensive trail network in the city of Newcastle. It connects to the May Valley Trail, passes by Lake Boren Park and ends at Newcastle Way with connections on to various other trails.
properties.title: Waterline Trail

properties.description: Get a workout and experience rock work completed by Department of Natural Resources and WTA volunteer crews on this hike. Your reward is a rocky overlook from which you can marvel at Mount Kent, McClellan Butte, and Mount Washington, the behemoths forming the south rim of the west entrance to Snoqualmie Pass.
properties.title: Dirty Harry's Balcony

properties.description: Take a walk around a 17-acre pond at this park, where you'll likely find folks boating and fishing in the warmer months.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: South Lewis County Regional Park

properties.description: A summit accessed via a scramble off of the south side of I-90. Cross country navigation experience and navigation required.
properties.title: Mount Kent

properties.description: A stroll along the sand dunes of Deception State Park's West Beach offers a glimpse into this important geologic feature. The way is easy and interpretive signs provide information about the interesting seaside vegetation unique to this area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Deception Pass State Park - West Beach Sand Dunes

properties.description: A mile-long wide gravel trail connects the Cornwall Park and Irongate neighborhoods of Bellingham.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Squalicum Creek Trail

properties.description: The Greg Ball Trail is a trail envisioned by and honoring one of the greatest trail advocates this state has ever had. Ball was a former board member and director of the WTA. In 1993 he launched the organization’s volunteer trail maintenance program which has since grown into the largest state-based program of its kind. He designed this trail to Wallace Lake and it was finished in his memory by volunteers from WTA and through support from the Spring Trail Trust.
properties.title: Wallace Falls State Park - Greg Ball Trail to Wallace Lake

properties.description: One of the Quincy Lakes, Dusty Lake is further in the backcountry, making for a good long day hike or an overnight.
properties.title: Dusty Lake

properties.description: Hike a trail on the southwest flanks of Mount St. Helens. While mudflows and flooding rendered the land close to St. Helens difficult to negotiate even for two-legged hikers, the Blue Horse trail has been cultivated enough that the way is passable and pleasant for both horses and hikers.
properties.title: Blue Horse Trail

properties.description: Capitol State Forest offers hikers a quick getaway fix and an opportunity to stretch their legs during the winter months.
properties.title: Capitol State Forest - Rock Candy Mountain

properties.description: Fort Simcoe Historical State Park consists of 196 acres in the Yakima Indian Reservation. The Park is closed in the winter from October 1 through March 31.
properties.title: Fort Simcoe Historical State Park

properties.description: China Lake is a small forest escape with a trail that takes you around a quiet lake on a green nature walk. Perfect on a sunny day for a stroll and a picnic or for hiding from the rain under a tree canopy, this trail is just a step away from the bustle of city life nearby.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: China Lake

properties.description: Twisp Pass is a stunner in summer and autumn. Though it is a bit of a drive to get there from almost anywhere in the state, it's well worth it!
properties.title: Twisp Pass

properties.description: This hike is to a beautiful lake basin filled with larch and expansive views of the peaks above.  From a basecamp at the lake, day trips explorations lead to other lakes and views.
properties.title: Cooney Lake

properties.description: There is no formal trail to the summit of Pinnacle Mountain. However, it can be reached by going off trail. Gear and experience is recommended.
properties.title: Pinnacle Mountain

properties.description: A hefty workout, spectacular views, and very little company await you on this summit. Please note access to this trail is via private property. A recreational permit from Hampton Resources, a forest products company, is required.
properties.title: Mount Persis

properties.description: The wide-open trail to Hannegan Pass and Hannegan Peak offers spectacular mountain views, glorious alpine wildflowers, waterfalls and glaciers. Choose to hike to 5050 foot Hannegan Pass (about 8 miles roundtrip) or press on to the 6,200 foot summit of Hannegan Peak — 10.6 miles roundtrip.
properties.title: Hannegan Pass and Peak

properties.description: Hike through some of the Boundary Trail’s best scenery on the 44-mile lollipop loop along the Chewuch River and through majestic Cathedral Pass.
properties.title: Cathedral Pass Loop

properties.description: The more strenuous winter version of this easy summer hike leads to the overlook of Cedar Falls. In winter, the falls are a snow-topped mound of ice with a flowing creek base.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Cedar Falls Snowshoe

properties.description: In 1929, a man bought 40 acres of sagebrush in Wenatchee. Over the decades, his labor of love has turned a portion of desolate, dry rock into a fantasy world of stone pathways, waterfalls, pixie lawns, and stunning views. Today the Ohme (pronounced Oh-Me) family’s verdant imagination has turned this hillside into a playground to wander and explore. Children of all ages will delight in exploring the paths, stairs, pools, and corners.
properties.title: Ohme Gardens County Park

properties.description: The Lake Constance route is not a casual hike to a lake. It's a Class 2 and sometimes Class 3 scramble that requires continuous attention and careful hand work in areas where a mistake could prove fatal. People who have a fear of heights or are less than 100% confident in their climbing skills should avoid this route.
properties.title: Lake Constance

properties.description: Located in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Union Peak is a popular summit in the winter months. Skiers skin up to the summit, enjoying untouched powder for months, even after ski season is over.
properties.title: Union Peak

properties.description: This multi-use trail offers hikers and bikers alike sweeping views of Chikamin Ridge and peaks nearby starting right from the road to the trailhead.
properties.title: Chikamin Tie ORV

properties.description: This easy-to-moderate hike brings you through lush meadows, planted forest trees, and a stump-filled clearing to the monument dedicated to Robert Henry Hauberg, the founder of the Pilchuck Tree Farm. The monument meadow has great views of the valley below plus the Sound and the islands, but be aware that this is on private property and visitors must fill out a release to hike here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Pilchuck Tree Farm

properties.description: A relatively easy hike to a tranquil mountain lake.
properties.title: Crystal Lake

properties.description: Hike good trails though a forested drainage in Burien that has many tall trees and, in season, is very green. In spring look for a few wildflowers. Continue your hike on trails paralleling the beach, both north and south of your trailhead.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Seahurst Park

properties.description: Ramble through some great stands of fir and hemlock and pull in some panoramic views to the south including the north slopes of Mount Appleton.
properties.title: Boulder Lake (Olympics)

properties.description: This little-used trail gets hikers to Cirque Lake in the Goat Rocks Wilderness. Paralleling Tenday Creek, it's a low-key riverside walk to a lovely little lake.
properties.title: Ten Day

properties.description: Hike a 10-mile route connecting Lake Sammamish to Lake Washington. Accessible from a variety of parks along the way, you can make your route as long or as short as you like.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake to Lake Trail

properties.description: When it is hot and dry, escape to this shaded hike through old-growth forest, culminating with views of Washington’s second-deepest lake and its surroundings. But you'll have to cross a precipitous washout 2 miles in to reach the views.
properties.title: Pyramid Mountain / Pyramid Peak

properties.description: Extending from the family-friendly Wetland Wildlife Interpretive Trail at Howard Miller Steelhead Park, the Skagit–Sauk Reach Trail stretches toward the confluence of the Skagit and Sauk Rivers before looping back toward the camping area at the park.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Skagit-Sauk Reach Trail
Trout Lake via West Fork Foss

properties.description: Looking for a long winter snowshoe ramble? The Bumping Lake area has miles of cross country and snowshoe trails to entertain beginners and seasoned snowshoers alike. Keep in mind you'll be sharing the trail with cross country skiers, and the area is open to snowmobilers in some areas, so you may have a soundtrack to keep you company as you walk.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Bumping Lake Ski and Snowshoe Trails

properties.description: Chambers Creek Canyon is a deeply incised, forested stream corridor between Lakewood and University Place in the South Puget Sound region.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Chambers Creek Canyon

properties.description: This is a snowshoe up a Forest Road before continuing through to a lake basin just off I-90.
properties.title: Twin Lakes Snowshoe

properties.description: The Grand Valley Loop is a great option, combining a ridge walk with sections along both Grand Creek Valley and Badger Valley.
properties.title: Grand Valley Loop

properties.description: A broad expanse of meadow blooms with a lovely waterfall, while the Goat Rocks loom overhead and Mount Adams feels close enough to touch to the south.
properties.title: Snowgrass - Cispus Basin - Nannie Ridge Loop

properties.description: A 30.5 mile long paved trail follows a historic rail line through Snohomish to Skagit county. Take a short walk, use it to connect to another trail, or undertake the whole thing in a day!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Centennial Trail

properties.description: The Wilderness Creek Trail starts from a parking area along Highway 900 and ascends up the slopes of Cougar Mountain to a junction where hikers have the choice of three other trails that take off into the expanse of the Cougar Mountain Regional Park.
properties.title: Wilderness Creek

properties.description: Formerly in the Department of Natural Resources trail system, Sedum Point has been taken out of their inventory. Visitors here may have difficulty finding the trail, but if you can, you'll be rewarded with a good day hike, and the possibility of connecting to the Pacific Crest Trail at the top end of the trail.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Sedum Ridge

properties.description: When it comes to resplendent alpine meadows, the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness can't be beat. And when it comes to the finest flower romps within that wild area named for the longtime Washington senator and champion of conservation, Cady Ridge ranks supreme. A multitude of blossoms proliferate along this mile-high ridge. But it's the lupines that dominate, transforming Cady into a purple mountain majesty. And views! From the inspiring Poet Peaks, to the emerald-cloaked summits along the Cascade crest, to cloud-piercing, snow-catching, ice-harboring, horizon-dominating Glacier Peak!
properties.title: Cady Ridge

properties.description: Trails offer many different experiences to all types of users. This tail is no different. It can be a colorful place to avoid on boating days, it can be a wonderful short trail for youngsters to explore, or it can be a link in a much larger and longer network of trails in and around the University of Washington Campus.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Washington Ship Canal Waterside Trail

properties.description: Sesqualitchew Creek is a fantastic find in the middle of DuPont. Transition from urban to forest and back over a short trail that provides a great distraction from the buzz of urban life -- and all possible on your lunch break!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Sequalitchew Creek

properties.description: The Long View Peak Trail is a connector trail on Cougar Mountain. The most direct route for reaching this trail is to hike from the Jim Whittaker Wilderness Peak Trailhead. The eastern end of the Long View Peak Trail connects to the Wilderness Creek Trail.
properties.title: Long View Peak

properties.description: This trail is a narrow, paved trail to a lookout on a ledge overlooking Liberty Bell Mountain. This area is worth the trip from the west side, because of spectacular views, and the myriad hiking trails in the area.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Washington Pass Overlook

properties.description: Disregarding the apocryphal stories about their name, the Damfino Lakes are noteworthy only to distinguish this route from two other routes. The lakes pale in comparison to these magnificent destinations: Excelsior Pass, the High Divide and Excelsior Peak.
properties.title: Excelsior Peak via Damfino Lakes Trail

properties.description: This short trail guides hikers through open forest to a junction with the Kachess Ridge Trail, where you can continue on to Thorp Lookout or just a little longer wander along the ridge.
properties.title: French Cabin Creek

properties.description: Hike a trail on top of an elevated berm that leads into a newly restored tidal marsh on Leque Island. Enjoy sights and sounds of hawks, ducks, and other birds, in addition to breathtaking views of the Olympics and North Cascades.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Leque Island - Stanwood Levee Trail

properties.description: If you like rugged, primitive trails, creek crossings with no bridges and finding a great view at the end of the trail, this hike is for you.
properties.title: East Fork Lewis River

properties.description: Green Mountain is the Kitsap Peninsula's go-to after work destination. Whether you're mountain biking, trail running, or hiking, you can get a quick workout by hiking the Gold Creek Trail up to the summit of Green Mountain.
properties.title: Green Mountain State Forest - Gold Creek Trail

properties.description: This 4.8 mile trail runs from upper Quartz Creek Trail to Boundary Trail. This is an access route to the Boundary Trail (above Forest Road 9341) and to the Quartz Creek Trail #5 below the road.
properties.title: Snagtooth Mountain

properties.description: See some sequoias and stare out over Lake Washington at Leschi Park. The 18-acre park was named after Chief Leschi of the Nisqually tribe.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Leschi Park

properties.description: Cascade Rock used to be accessible from the backyard of many sites at the Elwha Campground, but with the removal of the Elwha Dam, this campground has flooded multiple times and the campground is closed. Luckily though, you can still hike Cascade Rock, and its such a secret trail, you're likely to have it to yourself.
properties.title: Cascade Rock

properties.description: Hike this little-used trail on the east side of Cougar Mountain past an enormous glacial boulder left over from the last ice age.
properties.title: Bear Ridge

properties.description: Hike shoreline trails in both directions from this Anacortes trailhead. Take in views of distant islands, ferries, seabirds, eagles, historic displays. All on good trails suitable for all ages.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Guemes Channel and Ship Harbor

properties.description: Visit a sweet little state park on the Satsop River, where you can picnic, fish, float and do a little hiking.
properties.title: Schafer State Park

properties.description: This pair of back-to-back urban parks just west of Shoreline Community College offers some very tall trees, small creeks, and a network of (mostly) good trails with a few ups and downs. Wildflowers, ferns, moss, birds: they are all here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Shoreview and Boeing Creek Parks

properties.description: Hike a re-built trail adjacent to the Wild Sky Wilderness. The Beckler Peak trail opened in September of 2011, and with it, the Jennifer Dunn trailhead. The trail takes you through an old-growth forest to summit views of Glacier Peak, Baring, Index, the Monte Cristo Range, and Evergreen Mountain. It's easy to get to and provides great rewards for your effort. The trail has a gentle grade, it is well built, and suitable for kids. Be sure to take water with you, because there is no reliable water along the trail.
properties.title: Beckler Peak

properties.description: Enjoy fantastic views of the Blue Mountains from this cozy retreat on the edge of the Umatilla National Forest.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Wenatchee Guard Station

properties.description: Take a mellow walk on a trail that wanders among large old trees and huge mossy boulders. The trail alongside Baker River takes you on a path of gentle up and downs, splashing your way through stream crossings and past open areas filled with young alder, huckleberry and salmonberry. On a quiet spring day, your chances of seeing wildlife are excellent.
properties.title: Baker River

properties.description: A Downtown Seattle walk featuring stairways, art, architecture, history, and views of Puget Sound.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: City Hall to Pike Place

properties.description: Erinswood is an ADA-accessible that meanders through a variety of ecosystems over its short length. Meditate to the sound of rushing streams as you pass through riparian, deciduous, and evergreen habitats that form the backdrop of a 0.7-mile sojourn under the shadow of Heybrook Ridge.
properties.title: Erinswood

properties.description: This park sits at the southern end of Lake Washington in Renton. With a network of paved trails, it is a wonderful place to enjoy the lake and get some miles in.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Gene Coulon Memorial Beach Park

properties.description: Hike up through mountain meadows to the top of Chewelah Peak, home of 49 Degrees North mountain resort, for spectacular views.
properties.title: Chewelah Peak

properties.description: Imagine that you are looking through a telephoto lens at one of those iconic images of Mount Rainier taken from the south. Now zoom out to a wider view of the entire mountain, the thick forests below timberline, the enormous brown gash of the Nisqually River Valley, and beside it the verdant parkland that became known as Paradise. This is the view from the Pinnacle Saddle trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Pinnacle Saddle

properties.description: Tucked into the heart of Seattle's Capitol Hill neighborhood, Cal Anderson is a bustling hub of activity year round. There is about a mile of trail to walk here, but it's also a great place to exercise your dog, meet up with a friend, or just hang out in the sun.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Cal Anderson Park

properties.description: The middle section of the Burnt Bridge Creek trail extends from Devine Road to Leverich Park. In this section of the trail, the character becomes more urban and passes close to houses and soccer fields. Nonetheless, the trail passes through some open grassy areas where you may spot a raptor looking for lunch.
properties.title: Burnt Bridge Creek - Middle Section

properties.description: Hiking the Boundary Trail is an adventure on many a hikers’ bucket list. The trail spans the width of the Pasayten Wilderness and is part of the much larger Pacific Northwest National Scenic Trail. The combination of stunning scenery and lack of crowds is one of the BT’s most enticing aspects especially in autumn, when colors are changing, temperatures are cooling and bugs are gone. A number of places along the trail are so special that you’ll have the images etched into your memory for years to come.
properties.title: Boundary Trail - Pasayten

properties.description: Reynolds Creek is an unmaintained trail within the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.
properties.title: Reynolds Creek

properties.description: A few different trails wind through this forest, so visitors can make any number of loop hikes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Beaver Lake Park

properties.description: Take a rugged trek through creek canyons, down a four-wheeling road, over a remote pass, and back down through a multi-use trail to complete a challenging loop hike. You may have equestrians, mountain bikers, and ORV users for company, but any type of user can appreciate the views you’ll get along the way.
properties.title: Esmeralda Peak Loop

properties.description: Take a nice retreat to a couple of trails winding through a mossy forest to a beach and tidal inlet where you can continue exploring along the sand.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Anderson Island

properties.description: Here's a remote forest trail 1.9 miles long that descends through a pristine old-growth forest to Quartz Creek and connects to Quartz Creek Trail #5. It's a steep descent, and you'll have to make it up on the way back out, but the cool forest makes it a great shelter from the sun in the summer.
properties.title: Quartz Creek Butte

properties.description: Featuring a 1.3 mile lollipop loop, this preserve takes visitors through a forest of Douglas fir and salal to an open meadow.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Del Fairfax Preserve
