properties.description: This pleasant trail is shared by hikers, backpackers, mountain bikes and dirt bikes. All visitors will ultimately reach Mad Lake and its pretty surrounding meadows.
properties.title: Mad Lake

properties.description: The South Climb (or Lunch Counter Approach) of Mount Adams is the one that requires the least amount of technical expertise. However, ice axes, trekking poles, and crampons or microspikes (depending on the season) are required to summit. Hikers who put this investment in will be rewarded with stunning views on a clear day, as well as the satisfaction of having made it up one of Washington's five volcanoes.
properties.title: Mount Adams South Climb

properties.description: West Foster Creek offers a restored shrub-steppe environment for idle meandering, bird watching, or simply enjoying the out-of-doors.
properties.title: Foster Creek Wildlife Area

properties.description: Just a short drive from Spokane, this easy-going river hike is perfect for beginners or kids. Keep your eyes out for the deer, bald eagles, bird, ducks, herons and turkeys that make this forest their home.
properties.title: Little Spokane River Natural Area - Little Spokane River

properties.description: Mount Spokane State Park’s Trail 182 offers park visitors a new beautifully forested singletrack trail option on the western side of the park. The main access point for Trail 182 is via Day Mountain Road, located near Greenbluff, making this the perfect trail to enjoy before visiting the nearby farms and breweries.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 182

properties.description: The Black River Riparian Forest and Wetland hosts more than 50 species of birds in this habitat area. A bird-watcher's dream, it also provides a wonderful place to stretch your legs and enjoy a shot of nature within Renton's city limits.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Black River Riparian Forest and Springbrook Trail

properties.description: Hike around a paved trail in a former cattle ranch at the base of the core of an ancient volcano.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Che-che-op-tin Trail

properties.description: A trail wide enough for a stage coach, which was its original and still permitted use, Old Stage Trail No. 75 serves as the main feeder trail to the Kettle Crest National Recreation Trail for access to nearby Copper Butte.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Old Stage

properties.description: This waterfront park is only a few minutes of a drive away from the Lopez Island Ferry Terminal.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Odlin County Park

properties.description: A very rocky hike with breaks of sandy beach along a beautiful coast that's full of marine life between the towns of Oak Harbor and Coupeville on Whidbey Island.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Monroe Landing Low Tide Trail

properties.description: The Green Lantern Trail mostly follows the shores of Silver Lake in South Everett, perfect for those looking to stretch their legs and experience the outdoors without having to leave the city. With a multitude of attractions including passing through three parks with water access this trail is ready to please! Disc golfers, beach-goers, kids, birders and fishermen alike may all find something here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Green Lantern Trail

properties.description: This early or late-season hike takes you for a ridge walk high above Coldwater Lake, which was not a standing body of water prior to the massive eruption of Mount St. Helens in 1980. You'll walk through a serene willow forest, marvel at the power of nature when you encounter twisted hulks of logging machinery, and see plenty of gnarled stumps where tall evergreens once stood.
properties.title: South Coldwater Trail

properties.description: Rowena Crest is a fabulous place to pull off the road and enjoy the sweeping views of the Columbia River. Grasslands, basalt cliffs, and scrub oak forests form the landscape you'll hike through on a trail that climbs steadily with ever-increasing views.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - OR
properties.title: Rowena Plateau and Tom McCall Point

properties.description: A short and steep trail that offers hikers access to the Pacific Crest Trail or a longer loop with Fog City trail.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Bear Gap

properties.description: A no-longer-maintained trail that heads towards Mount St. Helens from Weyerhauser timber land.
properties.title: Castle Lake

properties.description: In the wake of the 2017 Norse Peak Fire, the Union Creek area is charred and stark, and yet strangely beautiful at the same time. Walking through the destruction, the signs of life and renewal are plainly seen. But trail washouts restrict passage, and demand caution.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Union Creek

properties.description: Walk along an old Forest Road to a lake tucked away off the Mountain Loop Highway.
properties.title: Canyon Lake

properties.description: Mount Kit Carson Trail 160 begins at Saddle Junction and climbs a short, steep route to the summit of its namesake peak, second tallest of the main peaks within Mount Spokane State Park. While it may lack the elevation of Mount Spokane, it more than makes up for it with superior views; pack a picnic lunch and take advantage of the outstanding vista.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Mount Kit Carson Trail

properties.description: The Bells Mountain trail is a non-motorized, multi-use trail constructed by the Chinook Trail Association (CTA) and managed by the Washington State Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It is part of a 30-mile stretch of the Chinook Trail that was awarded National Recreation Trail Status in 2005.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Yacolt Burn State Forest - Bells Mountain

properties.description: Enjoy a flat, sandy stroll to the mouth of Willapa Bay on the Long Beach Peninsula.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - Leadbetter Point

properties.description: The Connelly Creek Nature Area features a short 1-mile backbone trail through some of the largest Sitka spruce trees in Bellingham.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Connelly Creek Trail

properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Yakima Peak

properties.description: Bearhead Mountain is a moderate, well-marked trail through the forest that carries you to an old fire lookout site with a bold and brassy Rainier view.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NW - Carbon River/Mowich
properties.title: Bearhead Mountain

properties.description: Blag Mountain can be reached via the network of mountain roads.. There are many abandoned services roads in the area, so navigating can be tricky.
properties.title: Blag Mountain

properties.description: Famous for its wildlife, the 4-O Ranch portion of the Chief Joseph Wildlife Area provides hikers with access to the Grand Ronde River in the Blue Mountains. Walk over rolling hills and through ponderosa pine woodlands as you search for numerous species that call the area home.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Chief Joseph Wildlife Area - 4-O Ranch

properties.description: A popular trail with great views of the Sauk and Skagit river valleys, Cascade mountain peaks, and on a good clear day, the Olympics and San Juan Islands. There will also be plenty of wildflowers to please photographers and hiking plant nerds alike.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Sauk Mountain

properties.description: Lake Clarice, surrounded by granite cliffs, is located in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness near Marmot Lake. The lake is accessible from the Deception Creek trailhead in the north or the Tucquala trailhead from the south.
properties.title: Lake Clarice

properties.description: With views of Crater and Jack Mountains, the Jackita Ridge trail takes you up a challenging incline to the top of a ridge above the timberline. It features wildflowers and unobstructed views. Many hikers use it to connect to the Devil's Dome loop or to reach Crater Mountain.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Jackita Ridge

properties.description: Green, mossy old growth trees and miles of level hiking are the main attractions at Federation Forest State Park. More than 12 miles of trails wind through the forest and hikers can put together loops to fit their hiking needs.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Federation Forest State Park

properties.description: The trail winds its way above the Suiattle River through old-growth forest and some mature forest recovering from an old burn from the 1920’s. The vegetation in the upper Suiattle watershed includes a wonderful mixture of west-of-the-crest/east-of-the-crest species.
properties.title: Suiattle River Trail

properties.description: Despite its intermediate difficulty, hikers flock to Mount Pilchuck for its historic restored fire lookout with grand panoramic views of Mount Baker, Mount Rainier and the Olympics.
properties.title: Mount Pilchuck

properties.description: Hike a trail that traverses Nason Ridge. Along the way, you'll enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding summits, as well as access to an old fire lookout.
properties.title: Nason Ridge

properties.description: The Kachess Lake Shore trail is a short, one-mile jaunt along Kachess Lake, good for campers in the summer or a short snowshoe in winter.
properties.title: Kachess Lake

properties.description: Take a beautiful, very short hike to a lovely waterfall off the beaten path.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Panther Creek Falls

properties.description: A hike which starts in high alpine forests of pines and larches, opening up to beautiful mountain vistas in the Chelan Sawtooth range.
properties.title: Summer Blossom

properties.description: The Elliott Bay Trail is a 5-mile multi-use paved trail for walkers and cyclists that hugs the Elliott Bay shoreline, running from S King Street near Lumen Field to Smith Cove Park in Magnolia.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Elliott Bay Trail

properties.description: Scramble to the top of this peak from Headlee Pass, located off the Mountain Loop Highway.
properties.title: Sperry Peak

properties.description: Take a pleasant hike up a spectacular canyon with towering basalt formations, a rushing creek, and a chance to see bighorn sheep. Whether you go in spring or fall, the canyon is filled with brilliant color.
properties.title: Umtanum Creek Canyon

properties.description: This is an easy loop trail, wandering nearly one mile through a forest of bigleaf maple and cedars on the shores of Carr Inlet in Gig Harbor.  With less than fifty feet of elevation gain and plenty of picnic tables, it makes the perfect destination for families with small children.
properties.title: Kopachuck State Park Trail

properties.description: Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park is the largest “urban wild land” in the United States, with more than 3,000 acres of forest riddled with 38 miles of hiking trails. The Licorice Fern Trail is a great choice for Cougar Mountain veterans looking for a fresh approach to Far Country Falls.
properties.title: Licorice Fern Trail

properties.description: Roughouse Mountain is the unofficial name for this peak in southwestern Chelan County. This relatively easy-to-climb peak is great for beginners or for those looking for non-technical snowshoeing in the off-season.
properties.title: Roughhouse Mountain

properties.description: With a trailhead so easily accessible, there's no excuse not to visit Snoquera Falls. Best in early spring, this lush, forested trail features a pretty fantail cascade plunging down a sheer, rocky wall.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Snoquera Falls Loop

properties.description: This popular multi-sport park provides trail access to the Beacon Hill trail network.
properties.title: John C. Shields Park (Minnehaha)

properties.description: This is a great trail near the Bainbridge ferry dock that offers visitors quick and easy beach access.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Hawley Cove Park

properties.description: Scramble to a scenic high point in the upper Enchantments.
properties.title: Little Annapurna

properties.description: An easy walk around a small urban lake and wetland area.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Scriber Lake

properties.description: A short, beautiful, but very steep unofficial bootpath to Lake Laura and Lake Lillian, this route gets you there in a quarter of the time, but breathing just as hard.
properties.title: Lake Laura Backdoor

properties.description: Beezley Hills can boast silence and solitude like few other locations in Washington can. Apart from occasional air traffic or the distant sound of farm machinery, the breeze rustling through the shrub-steppe and bird song will rule the day. Wildflowers will abound with an April or May visit while a late summer trip will encourage you to visit earlier or later in the day to beat the afternoon heat.
properties.title: Beezley Hills Preserve

properties.description: Perched high on a hill in the Issaquah Highlands, Grand Ridge Park offers hiking opportunities for both residents of the neighborhood and visitors.
properties.title: Grand Ridge Park - Water Tower Loop

properties.description: The Big Tree Trail is a short (0.5 mile) trail on Tiger Mountain's Tradition Plateau. It passes one of the largest Douglas firs still standing in the Tigers, and also passes a short section of some of the best true swamp you will find in the area, with lots of hanging moss and standing water.
properties.title: Big Tree Trail

properties.description: Far-off views of the Napeequa River are coveted among Cascade hikers, and rightly so. Actually reaching and hiking the Napeequa River Trail is, for most, a multi-day adventure in a remote corner of the Glacier Peak Wilderness that will leave memories of deep glacier-scoured walls, musical waterways, and meadows abuzz with life.
properties.title: Napeequa River

properties.description: Hike through the forest on this small trail system near Yale Lake and Amboy.
properties.title: Frasier Creek and Ridgeline Trail

properties.description: Visit a rare remnant of Garry Oak Prairie in the state at this small but mighty park in Tacoma.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Oak Tree Park

properties.description: If you need to take a break before braving the traffic coming back into Seattle on a Sunday evening, or if you want to stretch your legs on the way over the pass to adventures in Leavenworth, the Skyline Lake Trail is just the thing.
properties.title: Skyline Lake

properties.description: Waptus Pass Trail connects Pete Lake Trail with the Waptus River Trail, climbing steeply out of the Salmon La Sac area to Pete Lake and Waptus Lake to reach Waptus Pass.
properties.title: Quick Creek Camp

properties.description: Hike a short way or a little longer -- either to a lakeside or an overlook. Wherever you choose, you'll enjoy a route that passes through the Pacific Crest Trail's famous "Green Tunnel"; the tree canopy and foliage that makes up the iconic trail's character in southwest Washington.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Gillette Lake and Greenleaf Overlook

properties.description: This hike takes you through a lush area of the Chuckanuts that offers solitude and an experience of primal setting getting you away from the old logging roads turned trails that are close by. Going to the crest via the Salal trail is enhanced by thick undergrowth of Oregon grape, a variety of ferns and mosses and of course salal. The route winds through huge glacial erratics and an overstory of cedar, Douglas fir, hemlock, red maple and bigleaf maple.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Madrone Crest Trail

properties.description: Table Mountain's dramatic south face and pyramid profile beckon the adventurous hiker ready for a strenuous climb that is good training for summer summit attempts to come. The top features one of the best panoramas of the Columbia River Gorge, as well as views of Mount St. Helens, Rainier, Hood and Adams. Carry a guidebook with good route information as there are a couple of options to the summit and signage may be lacking.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Table Mountain

properties.description: Sometimes, taking the back door is better. At 9 miles and 3600 feet of elevation gain, the back way to the Rock Mountain Lookout is less steep, more scenic, and two miles shorter than the more frequently used route from Rock Lake. Try this as a key swap or a thru-hike if you want to get both sides of this gorgeous hike.
properties.title: Rock Mountain via Snowy Creek

properties.description: Climb to the top of Little Huckleberry Mountain, where you will be greeted with excellent views of Mount Adams and other Cascade peaks. Though steep at times, the summit and the huckleberries you’ll find along the way make this hike worthwhile.
properties.region: Southwest Washington > Columbia River Gorge - WA
properties.title: Little Huckleberry Mountain

properties.description: Enjoy a short but sweet stroll on a wide, flat trail to the pebble beaches of Belfair State Park. For those with younger children, you can also spend time on the delightful playground next to the large picnic shelter.
properties.title: Belfair State Park

properties.description: A section of the longer Palouse to Cascades Trail.
properties.title: Palouse to Cascades Trail - South Cle Elum Trailhead

properties.description: The Alpine Lakes Wilderness may be reached from numerous trail heads along the I-90 corridor. This little trail-gem sparkles, hidden in Snoqualmie Pass. It varies in terrain from abandoned logging road, through clear cut, all the way up to pristine alpine lake(s) nestled into a glacier scoured cirque. Seasonal changes make this medium difficulty hike worth returning to time and time again.
properties.title: Lake Lillian

properties.description: A fairly well used climber's trail goes straight up, and up, and then up Mount Baring. The trail requires moderate navigational skills and possibly climbing equipment in bad weather.
properties.title: Mount Baring

properties.description: This wheelchair-friendly small section of Spokane’s 40-mile Centennial Trail passes through Riverside State Park and additionally showcases some regional history at the site of a former Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) camp.
properties.title: Spokane River Centennial State Park - Wilbur Trailhead to Trail 211

properties.description: Chinese Reconciliation Park is a small park on the Tacoma waterfront. There are trails, both gravel and paved, winding throughout.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Chinese Reconciliation Park

properties.description: Independence Peak is the unofficial name of the peak towering above Independence and North Lakes.
properties.title: Independence Peak

properties.description: Why drive to the top when you can hike? Try this day hike as an introduction to Mount St. Helens for visitors who’ve never been here, or if they haven't been in a long time.
properties.title: Hummocks Loop

properties.description: The Inter Glacier is part of the standard Mount Rainier climbing route. While it may appear to be just a steep snowfield, it is a glacier with crevasses and other hazards. Glacier travel experience and equipment is required.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Inter Glacier

properties.description: A conveniently accessed, easy walk through historical and picturesque downtown Issaquah and surrounding forests.
properties.title: Rainier Trail - Issaquah

properties.description: Although this gently rolling creekside ramble is one continuous trail, an adventure in three parts awaits. The first few miles are a quiet walk through a classic fern-dotted, mossy forest. In the second section, hikers find Siouxon Creek and fellow waterfall seekers, and the final miles offer more solitude and small narrow canyons with more waterfalls to enjoy.
properties.title: Siouxon Creek

properties.description: This estuary at the saltwater edge of the Skagit River delta is eight miles long and three miles across, and you can travel along a portion of it. This hike can be enjoyed in any season. The easy flat trail make this an ideal hike for many hikers. Birders will definitely want to bring the binoculars! Before you start, be sure to check out the large tree on the road to the trailhead, there is a pair of bald eagles that sometimes hang out here.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Padilla Bay

properties.description: This less-than-a-mile boardwalk hike is a lovely way to get outside and enjoy a little forest time in a cathedral of trees.
properties.title: Boyd Creek Interpretive Trail

properties.description: Explore ancient caves and view a wide array of wildlife, all near a large lake in Washington's Coulee Country.
properties.title: Lenore Lake Caves

properties.description: Get away from the crowds and explore miles of trails through meadows and groves along the lower Snake River. Watch and listen for songbirds, waterfowl, raptors, deer, coyotes, wildflowers, tall grass, and sage.
properties.title: Big Flat Habitat Management Unit

properties.description: The High Lakes Ramble connects Chain of Lakes to Horseshoe Lake along a rough and tumble, multi-use trail. This corner of the Gifford Pinchot National Forest draws hikers, dirt bikers, and horseback riders alike. The trail offers views along the lake shores, including Mount Adams, and dips into the shaded canyon of Adams Creek about halfway between the lakes.
properties.title: High Lakes Ramble

properties.description: Hike a loop around this exceptional wetland. In season, view a variety of waterfowl. And marvel at the close-up views of beaver dams.
properties.title: Hazel Wolf Wetlands

properties.description: A temperate rainforest saunter up from the Quinault River valley floor to a fauna rich lake within the Olympic National Park
properties.title: Irely Lake

properties.description: Like so many lakes in the William O Douglas Wilderness, Shellrock Lake has peaceful solitude and plentiful wildlife including resident elk which graze in the meadows nearby.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Shellrock Lake

properties.description: Paradise provides a gateway to Washington's most iconic mountain, trails to get your heart pumping or just stretch your legs, and in winter, fantastic snowshoe and skiing opportunities for people of all ages.
properties.title: Paradise

properties.description: Access to Mount Gardner has been closed by a gate and a washout.
properties.title: Mount Gardner

properties.description: The Sumner Link Trail offers the chance to experience the valley along the White River including river views, wildlife, and native vegetation as well as agriculture and industry. Linking to the Interurban trail and Lakeland Hills Trail on the north and the Foothills trail and river walk to the south, this is also a great commute option.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Sumner Link Trail

properties.description: The hike to Deer Lake is a great day hike, or beginners overnight.
properties.title: Deer Lake

properties.description: The Copper Ridge Trail forms part of the popular and iconic Copper Ridge Loop. The trail climbs to a ridge with stunning views before dropping down to the Chilliwack River Valley.
properties.title: Copper Ridge

properties.description: There may be an easier way to reach the summit of Rock Mountain but if you are looking to earn your ascent in a shorter amount of time, this approach offers you alpine meadows and stunning views of peaks within the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest via this lesser-traveled but steeper route right off Highway near Stevens Pass.
properties.title: Rock Mountain (Rock Lake)

properties.description: A very short trail rewards visitors with views of a lovely waterfall, accessible in the early season. Look for trillium along the trail in spring, and enjoy the sounds of rushing water year-round.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: Camp Creek Falls

properties.description: This is an old lookout site that towers nearly 3000 feet above Lake Pend Oreille. The trail is mixed use and open to motorcycles and offers splendid views from the top.
properties.title: LIttle Blacktail Mountain

properties.description: Lost Lake is a beautiful gem along the trail to Manastash Lake, and is a sweet destination for people who want a shorter hike with less vertical ascent.
properties.title: Lost Lake (Manastash Lake)

properties.description: Visit a trio (yes, trio) of waterfalls just off I-90 on this sure-to-please short trail, perfect for families.
properties.title: Twin Falls

properties.description: A hike to two lakes situated in a remote hanging valley in the Entiat, this beautiful hike is ideal for adventurous backpackers in the autumn who are looking for larches.
properties.title: Larch Lakes (Entiat)

properties.description: Bruni's Snow Bowl Hut is named for Brunhilde (Bruni) Wislicenus, a passionate mountaineer and wilderness skier who donated a substantial portion of the funds to rebuild the hut after a fire in 2007 burnt the original to the ground. Snow Bowl, High Hut and the Yurt are all accessible for a summer hike or bike, in addition to the winter snowshoe and ski. Depending on conditions and logging trucks, the upper parking lot may be open, shaving off nearly a mile or more each way of this hike.
properties.title: Bruni's Snow Bowl Hut

properties.description: The White River Trail is a great year-round option to hike a gradual trail through the forest northeast of Mount Rainier National Park.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: White River

properties.description: This connector trail links Avondale Road to Hartman Park, Perrigo Heights Open Space Park, and connects to a trail that leads to Nike Neighborhood Park.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Ashford Trail

properties.description: At 6254 feet, Blue Lake sits quietly a little over two trail miles from Highway 20. With towering granite peaks, forests, meadows, wildflowers, and of course the beautiful mountain lake surrounded by granite that reaches for the sky, this short hike is easily a classic and should be on your must-hike list. With only 1050 feet of elevation gain this hike is doable for almost everyone. If you’re driving over Highway 20 and don’t have all day, stop for this mountain gem.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Blue Lake

properties.description: This short connector trail goes to Deception and Fisher creeks, which lead to Deception Lakes, the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT), and Deception Pass. The trailhead also provides alternative access to other area highlights such as Tonga Ridge and Fisher Lake.
properties.title: Deception Creek Cutoff

properties.description: The South Tiger Summit Trail starts on the South Tiger Traverse Trail, passes the south summit of South Tiger Mountain and ends at the north summit. The trail was built in 2023 after the area was logged in years 2018 and 2019.
properties.title: South Tiger Summit

properties.description: Get ready for 28 miles of very scenic hiking on the Pacific Crest Trail. This is a great intro to backpacking route: Four days, seven to eight miles per day of relatively flat backpacking. The trail is well marked, there are abundant camp sites and many stopping points along the way.
properties.region: South Cascades > White Pass/Cowlitz River Valley
properties.title: White Pass to Chinook Pass

properties.description: A loop hike to the base of Mount Baker or a rugged alternate route to Park Butte; take your pick. Along the way, soak in sweeping views of the North Cascades, gaze at Koma Kulshan’s glistening glaciers, munch on an inexhaustible supply of berries and marvel at old-growth western hemlock forest.
properties.title: Scott Paul Trail

properties.description: This trail is a staircase of switchbacks that march ever upward through thick forest to deliver hikers to an iconic ridge walk in the North Cascades.
properties.title: Excelsior Pass via Nooksack River

properties.description: The trail climbs sharply through a forest of Douglas fir for a mile to a view of the Goat Rocks, Sawtooth Mountain, Mount Rainier, and Mount Adams. From this viewpoint you get a great view of Mount Adams and the Goat Rocks. It's worth bringing a camera for this one.
properties.title: Cultus Creek

properties.description: On Park Butte, hike to an historic fire lookout and come face-to-face with Koma Kulshan. Along with unobstructed panoramic views of Mount Baker, the Twin Sisters, and the rest of the North Cascades, the route to Park Butte offers dedicated campsites, wildflower-filled alpine meadows and a stunning variety of mushroom species.
properties.title: Park Butte

properties.description: WTA helped build this trail on the Republic Ranger District of the Colville National Forest. Open to hikers and bikers, it offers big views of the surrounding area, as well as quiet places to camp.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Gibralter Mountain

properties.description: This is a lovely little trail tucked behind the North Cascades Visitor Center outside of Newhalem. Learn about the area by exploring inside the Visitor Center, and then see some of the natural wonders for yourself by wandering down the River Loop Trail to the Skagit River.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Skagit River Loop Trail

properties.description: At the highest Sno-Park in the state, you find a nice loop route with suberb snowshoe opportunities.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Okanogan Highlands/Kettle River Range
properties.title: Sherman Pass Snowshoe Loop

properties.description: Walk through coastal forest for an expansive view of Willapa Bay and the opportunity to observe large numbers of bird species.
properties.title: Willapa National Wildlife Refuge - South Bay Trail

properties.description: This summit is off the south side of I-90. Route finding experience required.
properties.title: Scout Patrol Peak

properties.description: Teddy Bear Cove encompasses more than nine acres and 1,430 feet of shoreline along beautiful Chuckanut Bay. Explore two small beaches for sea critters, fascinating Chuckanut sandstone formations and views out over Chuckanut Bay to the the San Juan Islands. A headland hike topped with cedars and twisted madronas offers views of both beaches from a high perspective. This is a fine all-season hike for a bit of seclusion in the winter months.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Teddy Bear Cove

properties.description: The overlook at Faraway Rock is a short jaunt along the Mazama Ridge Trail up from Stevens Canyon Road and Reflection Lakes along the Wonderland Trail. This viewpoint showcases glistening Lake Louise below and the towering Tatoosh Ridge to the south.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Faraway Rock

properties.description: This route is in the Crystal Spring Sno-Park. It is along both a motorized and non-motorized groomed trail.
properties.title: Dandy Pass Road Snowshoe

properties.description: Hike towards the base of Klawatti and Austera Peaks along Newhalem Creek on this unmaintained North Cascades National Park trail. Years of blowdowns and overgrowth make this trail difficult to hike and navigate, but Newhalem Falls and the views of the mountains cannot be beaten. It's a great way to get into the North Cascades in the winter and still avoid the snow.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Newhalem Creek

properties.description: Far to the north, between the Strait of Georgia and the waters surrounding the San Juan Islands is a funny-shaped little island with a wealth of hiking trails on its relatively small square acreage.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Sucia Island State Park

properties.description: The classic approach (via Sunrise) to this sea of meadows and wildflowers at the base of Mount Rainier is long and tough, putting Grand Park out of reach for most casual dayhikers. Instead, try this "backdoor" approach via Lake Eleanor to enjoy this stunning destination.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > NE - Sunrise/White River
properties.title: Grand Park via Lake Eleanor

properties.description: A short trail through a burn area that leads to Tronsen head and some beautiful larch and ponderosa forest views. This is a great option to see some fall color near Blewett Pass and create a loop link up with nearby other trails.
properties.title: Table Mountain

properties.description: The Potholes Wildlife Area is enclosed in the nearly 40,000-acre Potholes Reservoir Unit near Moses Lake. Part of the Columbia Basin Irrigation Project, anyone who has driven cross-state has zipped through this enormous irrigation project, but few stop to enjoy the wide variety of wildlife it supports.
properties.title: Potholes Wildlife Area

properties.description: The Pete Lake trail is a mild-mannered path with something to offer for hikers, campers, children, birders, wildlife enthusiasts, and aquaphiles. This even-tempered route follows the Cooper River 4.5 miles to its headwater, passing through a diverse old-growth forest and terminating at an alpine lake sitting in the shadows of Big Summit Chief and Chimney Rock.
properties.title: Pete Lake

properties.description: A 2 mile loop through one of Seatle's seven hills, exploring a section of the redlining heritage trail.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redlining Heritage Trail - First Hill and Little Saigon

properties.description: A nice break from in-town shopping, the Tammi Wilson Memorial Trail is a short, ADA-accessible trail in Burlington.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Bellingham Area
properties.title: Tammi Wilson Memorial Trail

properties.description: Mazama Ridge at Mount Rainier's Paradise area offers an especially scenic intermediate-level snowshoe route in the midst of snow-covered alpine meadows.
properties.title: Mazama Ridge

properties.description: Walk along the Puyallup River on a nature walk without ever leaving the city.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Puyallup Riverwalk Trail

properties.description: The hike to Halfway House follows the first five miles of the North Fork Quinault River along the same route taken by the Press Expedition of 1890. The trail passes through superb lowland rainforest before entering the canyon of the Quinault. Halfway House makes a good picnic spot for day hikers and is also a great camp site for backpackers on a longer journey.
properties.title: North Fork Quinault River and Halfway House

properties.description: Snowshoe trail that starts just below the Selkirk Lodge (Nordic ski area) and goes down to the Condo Road.
properties.title: Mount Spokane State Park - Trail 260 (Snowshoe)

properties.description: Backpack on primitive trails to Dodger Point Camp in the heart of Olympic National Park for unparalleled views of high, snowy peaks towering above deep forested valleys.
properties.title: Dodger Point

properties.description: The Langdon Trail runs along the south side of Badger Mountain above a large apple orchard. This is the least traveled trail in the system. It is popular with trail runners and mountain bike riders because of its meandering route as it goes in and out of gullies.
properties.title: Badger Mountain - The Langdon Trail

properties.description: The Ring Road Trail is part of the Cougar Mountain trail system. It can only be reached on foot and does not have its own trailhead. Hikers can connect to the Ring Road Trail From the Long View Peak Trail in the southern reaches of this vast park.
properties.title: Ring Road

properties.description: Start at the junction with the White River Trail 1199 and climb through old growth timber. At mile .5 find a spur trail to left with a view of the White River Valley. Come to another scenic view of Mt. Rainier and the valley at mile 3.6. The junction with Noble Knob Trail 1184 is just ahead at mile 4.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > Chinook Pass - Hwy 410
properties.title: Deep Creek

properties.description: A lengthy and difficult hike up an iconic peak inside the Enchantments. Climbing gear and expertise required.
properties.title: Dragontail Peak

properties.description: Can't decide between walking along an ocean bluff with water stretched out for miles before you or wandering through forest under the drooping branches of moss-covered cedars? The Kettles Trail System on Whidbey Island offers you an opportunity to do both!
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Whidbey Island
properties.title: Kettles Trail System

properties.description: The Arboretum Loop Trail is a short interpretive trail within the Indian Creek Community Forest.
properties.title: Indian Creek Community Forest - Arboretum Loop Trail

properties.description: A beach, forests, wetlands, and the potential to spot wildlife; Lake Sammamish State Park has it all. And people have been appreciating what the area has to offer for generations -- the land around the lake is culturally significant as a gathering place for several Native American tribes.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Lake Sammamish State Park

properties.description: This brushy but scenic river bottom trail accesses the Wildhorse Creek Trail within the Alpine Lakes Wilderness of the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest.
properties.title: White Pine Creek

properties.description: This short section of the much longer Boundary Trail (which spans the Dark Divide between Mount St. Helens and Mount Adams) provides a nice day hike amid the unique geology of the St. Helens area.
properties.title: Boundary West

properties.description: Lightning Peak is a Class 3 and involves exposed scrambling. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.title: Lightning Peak

properties.description: Short forested lollipop trail in the Renton Highlands that crosses a creek and has several access points.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Maplewood Heights Park

properties.description: A peak scramble on the east side of the Cascades.
properties.title: Sentinel Mountain

properties.description: Explore 800 acres of wooded area right in Redmond’s backyard.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Redmond Watershed Preserve

properties.description: This trail is short and steep with great views. The rocky, arid climate of eastern Washington is on full display as this crumbly-at-times trail snakes up through cliff bands and rock gardens.
properties.title: Alta Lake State Park

properties.description: Cascade Lake provides recreation opportunities for every kind of outdoor enthusiast. The main day-use area offers a picnic area, kitchen shelters, boat launches and rentals, a swimming beach, and fishing. One of the main attractions though is the loop trail that circles the lake. Walk along the shore of the lake and enjoy secluded viewpoints and tall trees.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Moran State Park - Cascade Lake

properties.description: On this hike, you’ll experience the renewal of life after a devastating fire as you climb a canyon through bunch grasses, wildflowers and regenerating stands of aspen to panoramic views of the surrounding countryside and the distant Cascades.
properties.title: Black Canyon

properties.description: Explore one of the quieter Olympic Peninsula river valleys. Quiet, that is, if you don't count the Duckabush River's constant belching, crashing, and churning as it tumbles over giant boulders and squeezes through narrow rocky clefts.
properties.title: Duckabush River

properties.description: Visit this sweet wheelchair-friendly trail outside Twisp for lovely mountain views and a placid lake.
properties.title: Black Pine Lake

properties.description: This backpack loop starts low where water and trees abound, then climbs high to take in the views on the Mount Misery trail's open ridges. An easy one- or two- night backpack trip, give some thought to campsite locations to take advantage of the few springs that are available in the high country.
properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Tucannon River - Rattlesnake Loop

properties.description: Just adjacent to the equally popular Horse Lake Reserve, the Sage Hills is home to great trails for hiking, running, or mountain biking. The rolling hills found at Sage Hills offer wonderful views of the Columbia River, the Wenatchee Valley and the North Cascades. Springtime brings vibrant color to the area with wild sage, yellow arrowleaf balsamroot, Indian paintbrush and purple lupine abound.
properties.title: Sage Hills

properties.description: The Aurora Divide Trail branches off the Barnes Creek Trail and steeply climbs to Aurora Ridge. Aurora Ridge offers sweeping views of Lake Crescent, Mount Baker, and more.
properties.title: Aurora Divide

properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > San Juan Islands
properties.title: Goldstream Provincial Park: Grand Loop

properties.description: Explore this network of trails through riparian wetlands and sagebrush along the Yakima River.
properties.title: Chamna Natural Preserve

properties.description: The route to Lamont Mountain is a Class 3 and involved exposed scrambling. Gear and experience recommended.
properties.title: Lamont Mountain

properties.description: Follow a short, ADA-accessible path around Picture Lake, home to one of the most photographed vistas in America. Featuring a backdrop of craggy Mount Shuksan and a foreground of wilflowers ringing a sparkling lake in summer, Picture Lake is pretty as, well, a picture.
properties.title: Picture Lake

properties.description: The name "Laughingwater Creek" conjures up a nice stroll alongside a bubbling creek, but this trail mostly keeps hikers far above any running water. At several spots early in the hike, it is possible to hear the creek, but not to see it.
properties.region: Mount Rainier Area > SE - Cayuse Pass/Stevens Canyon
properties.title: Three Lakes via Laughingwater Creek

properties.description: Take a few minutes to pull off the highway and do the short hikes at the euphoniously named Sweet Creek Falls rest area. You’ll be glad you did!
properties.title: Sweet Creek Falls Interpretive Trail

properties.description: The way to Lake Augusta is rough. It's a steep and brushy trail that doesn't see much maintenance. But the destination is worth it; the lake is gorgeous, set in a basin at the bottom of Big Jim Mountain. It's a wonderful spot for wildflowers and backpacking trips late into the season.
properties.title: Lake Augusta

properties.description: An unofficially named, seldom-visited peak above Wagonwheel Lake on the border of Olympic National Park.
properties.title: Cub Peak

properties.description: This park, in the middle of West Seattle, has 1.7 miles of hiking trails in a natural forest setting, and offers the opportunity to see old growth conifers that once were common in Puget Sound forests.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Schmitz Preserve Park

properties.region: Eastern Washington > Palouse and Blue Mountains
properties.title: Lakes Basin Loop (Oregon)

properties.description: A primitive trail that climbs steeply to connect the Trapper Creek Trail (#192) to the Observation Trail (#132).
properties.title: Sunshine Trail

properties.description: Explore this loop that begins and ends at the popular Paradise Ranger Station on Mount Rainier. Hike a little more than 5 miles around and through a myriad of delightful lakes at the base of Washington's tallest volcano.
properties.title: Lakes Loop

properties.description: This trail offers a more intimate view of the Nisqually Glacier Valley, and connects to the Moraine Trail from the Paradise parking area.
properties.title: Deadhorse Creek

properties.description: Named after and built in honor of an Ellensburg wrestling coach, this trail provides the sought-after combination of great workout and big views. But its exposed; you'll want to be up here in spring or fall, because the direct sun of summer and lack of water can make this one a burner (literally).
properties.title: Manastash Ridge - Westberg Trail

properties.description: This North Idaho interpretive trail is easily accessible from I-90 and is not-to-be missed for its rich history of the 1910 fires.
properties.title: Pulaski Tunnel Trail

properties.description: Coal Creek Falls is a wonderful destination for any day hiker looking for an easy and/or family friendly trail with a picturesque culmination at Coal Creek Falls. It’s a well maintained trail that meanders beneath a thick canopy and a dense understory with many wildflower species in the spring.
properties.title: Coal Creek Falls

properties.description: A local part in Port Orchard, Square Lake has a fishing pond, picnic opportunities and the chance to get a breath of fresh air close to home.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Square Lake Park

properties.description: The Stiletto Spur Trail is a connector trail between the McAlester Lake/Twisp junction and the Pacific Crest Trail near Highway 20.
properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Stiletto Spur Trail

properties.description: This urban gem features 4.5 miles of paved trail connecting Jefferson Park and Kubota Gardens, with expansive views all along the way.
properties.region: Puget Sound and Islands > Seattle-Tacoma Area
properties.title: Chief Sealth Trail

properties.region: North Cascades > North Cascades Highway - Hwy 20
properties.title: Boston Basin
